## EP-05-S3: System can limit a karigar's reads to their own jobs

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S3
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can limit a karigar's reads to their own jobs
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every read a karigar session makes to be filtered to jobs whose `karigarId` equals the `karigarId` on that user, and to the reference images of those jobs only
- **So that:** a karigar never sees another karigar's work, or any price, customer, lead or stock record (FR-05-4, BR-05-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Lakshmi Devi signed in as a karigar user linked to KG-04, when she requests a job assigned to KG-01, then the server returns `not_found` and no field of that job (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the same session, when she lists her jobs, then only jobs with `karigarId` KG-04 are returned.
  3. Given the same session, when she requests the reference image of a KG-04 job, then it is returned; when she requests the reference image of a KG-01 job, then the server returns `not_found`.
  4. Given the same session, when she calls any list or read operation on customers, leads, stock or parcels, then the server returns `forbidden`.
  5. Given a karigar job record returned to her, when the response is inspected, then it carries no customer name, customer phone or price field.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The filter is applied in the query on the server, not after loading. Another karigar's record is answered with `not_found`, not `forbidden`, so its existence is not revealed. A karigar user with no `karigarId` gets an empty job list. Price fields are never in the karigar response shape.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads change nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the karigar scope filter to the read path; jobs and images themselves come in EP-19 and EP-09.
- **UI reference:** No screen in this story. The karigar job list is EP-20 (route `k-jobs`); the NEVER SEES list is on `docs/ux/mockups/11-roles-and-permissions.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: another karigar's job returns not-found, not the record (epic section 13). Personal data: customer data never reaches a karigar phone.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S2, EP-02-S3, EP-02-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S4: Owner can add a user with name, phone and role

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S4
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can add a user with name, phone and role
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to fill in Name, Phone (the number they sign in with), Email and the role picker (Staff or Karigar) on the Add a staff member screen and press "Add this staff member", and to resend the activation email if it was lost
- **So that:** the new person gets an activation email, sets their own password, signs in with their own phone and lands on their role's home (FR-05-5, FR-05-6, FR-05-17, BR-05-2, BR-05-11, BR-05-12)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth signed in as Owner on route `staff-new`, when he enters Name "Deepak Rao", Phone "+91 90030 71145", Email "deepak.rao@example.com", picks Staff and presses "Add this staff member", then a user with role `staff`, status `pending_activation` and Sanjay's shop ID is created, its id is returned, and an activation email goes to that address (EP-04-S10) (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Deepak Rao was just added, when he opens the activation link, sets a password and then signs in with "+91 90030 71145" and that password, then he lands on route `today` (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given an active user already has phone "+91 90030 71145", when the owner adds another user with the same phone, then the server returns `validation` with field `phone` and no user is written.
  4. Given Rajesh Verma signed in as Staff, when he calls the add-user operation directly, then the server returns `forbidden` with "Only the owner can add staff or change a role." (FR-05-6).
  5. Given an empty Name, an empty Email or a phone of "12345", when the form is submitted, then the field shows an error and the server, if reached, returns `validation` with the field name.
  6. Given Deepak is still `pending_activation`, when Sanjay taps "Resend activation email", then a new link is sent and the earlier link stops working; given Deepak is already active, the action is not offered and the server refuses it.
  7. Given Sanjay picks Owner in the role picker, when he saves, then the server refuses with "The shop already has an owner." (EP-05-S9).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may call Create User and Resend activation. Name and email are required; email must be a valid address. Phone is normalised to E.164 and must be unique within the shop among users who are not deactivated (D4). Role must be `staff` or `karigar`; `owner` is refused because the shop has exactly one owner (EP-05-S9). The shop ID is taken from the owner's session, never from the request (D7). No password is set or emailed; the activation link is issued through EP-04-S10. The create runs in one transaction with its audit entry and uses an idempotency key so a double tap creates one user (EP-03-S8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes (through EP-05-S14): actor, time, entity user (new id), action `user_added`, after (name, masked phone, masked email, role); on resend, action `activation_link_sent`.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `users` with shop ID, email and status `pending_activation`; inserts into `password_links` through EP-04-S10. Prototype `StaffMember` rows for owner and staff merge into `users`; prototype ids such as `ST-01` are kept as a reference column (epic section 16 risk). Migration adds `created at`, `deactivated at` and `version` to `users` if EP-02-S3 did not.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/25-onboard-staff.svg`, route `staff-new`. The add and edit user flow for all three roles is not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: the phone is personal data and shown only to the owner. Concurrency: two parallel adds with the same phone create one user. Personal data: the email is personal data and shown only to the owner. D4 is decided: the form has an email field and phone numbers are unique, so two users cannot share one phone. D7 is decided: no branch field; the "Which counter / branch" field on mockup 25 is not used for a branch.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S2, EP-04-S3, EP-04-S6, EP-04-S10, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-02-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S5: Owner can edit a user's name and phone

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S5
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can edit a user's name and phone
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to open a user from the directory and change their Name, Phone or Email and save
- **So that:** a typing mistake or a new phone number does not lock the person out (FR-05-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Deepak Rao at version 1 with phone "+91 90030 71145", when the owner changes the phone to "+91 90030 71146" and saves, then the user row has the new phone and version 2.
  2. Given the phone changed, when Deepak next signs in, then his password works with "+91 90030 71146" and not with the old number.
  3. Given the owner saves with version 1 while another owner already saved version 2, when the server handles it, then it returns `conflict` with "Someone else changed this user. Reload and try again." and nothing changes.
  4. Given a new phone already held by another active user, when the owner saves, then the server returns `validation` with field `phone`.
  5. Given a Staff session, when it calls Update User profile, then the server returns `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may call Update User profile. The update checks `version` (EP-02-S14). Phone uniqueness within the shop and the email format are checked as in EP-05-S4. Role and status cannot be changed through this operation.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes (through EP-05-S14): actor, time, entity user, action `user_edited`, before and after (name, masked phone, masked email).
- **Data changes:** Updates `users.name`, `users.phone`, `users.email`, `users.version`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (edit user, MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3). Fields follow `docs/ux/mockups/25-onboard-staff.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: version check stops two owners overwriting each other. Personal data: old and new phones are masked in the audit entry. Open question: whether existing sessions survive a phone or email change; proposed: they do, because the password did not change.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S4, EP-05-S11, EP-02-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S6: Owner can change a user's role

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S6
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can change a user's role
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to pick a different role (Staff or Karigar) for an existing user and save
- **So that:** a promotion or a change of job takes effect without creating a new account (FR-05-8, BR-05-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Deepak Rao with role `staff` and a linked Karigar record, when the owner changes his role to `karigar`, then the user row has role `karigar`, the version goes up by 1, and "User deactivated or role changed" is emitted after commit.
  2. Given that change, when Deepak's next request arrives with his old session, then it is refused as `unauthenticated` and his next sign-in lands on route `k-jobs` (EP-04-S13).
  3. Given a staff user changed to `karigar`, when the change is saved without a linked Karigar record, then the server refuses with "Link this user to a karigar record first." (FR-05-15).
  4. Given a Staff session, when it calls Update User role, then the server returns `forbidden` with "Only the owner can add staff or change a role.".
  5. Given a change of any user to `owner`, or of the owner to another role, when it is saved, then it is refused by EP-05-S9, because the shop has exactly one owner.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may call Update User role. The new role must be `staff` or `karigar`. The role update, the one-owner guard, the session end (EP-04-S13) and the audit entry run in one transaction. A role change to `karigar` needs a `karigarId`; a change away from `karigar` clears it.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "User deactivated or role changed" (through EP-05-S10).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes (through EP-05-S14): actor, time, entity user, action `role_changed`, before role, after role.
- **Data changes:** Updates `users.role`, `users.karigarId` where needed, `users.version`; ends rows in `sessions`.
- **UI reference:** Role picker on `docs/ux/mockups/25-onboard-staff.svg` ("WHAT ROLE · THIS SETS EVERYTHING ELSE"). The edit-role screen is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the old role's access ends at once. Concurrency: version check plus the one-owner guard in the same transaction. D7: one shop has exactly one owner, so no role change involves the owner role.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S4, EP-05-S9, EP-05-S10, EP-05-S13, EP-04-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S7: Owner can deactivate a user

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can deactivate a user
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** a "Deactivate" action on a user that stops them signing in and ends their open sessions
- **So that:** a person who leaves the shop loses access at once while their past sales and audit history stay (FR-05-9, BR-05-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma is active and signed in on the shop device and his own phone, when the owner deactivates him, then his status is `deactivated`, `deactivated at` is set, and both devices return to sign-in within about 1 second once EP-07 delivers the event (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given Rajesh is deactivated, when he signs in with his phone and the right password, then the response is the same as for a wrong password and no session is created (EP-04-S3).
  3. Given Rajesh is deactivated, when the directory is read, then his row is still listed with status Deactivated and his user id is still the actor on his past audit entries.
  4. Given the owner tries to deactivate himself, the shop's only owner, when it is saved, then it is refused by EP-05-S9.
  5. Given a Staff session, when it calls Update User status, then the server returns `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may deactivate. A user row is never deleted. Deactivation, the one-owner guard, Delete All sessions (EP-04-S13) and the audit entry run in one transaction. Deactivating an already deactivated user is refused with "This user is already deactivated.".
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "User deactivated or role changed" (through EP-05-S10).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes (through EP-05-S14): actor, time, entity user, action `user_deactivated`, before status `active`, after status `deactivated`, reason if given.
- **Data changes:** Updates `users.status`, `users.deactivated at`, `users.version`; ends rows in `sessions`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (deactivate and reactivate, MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: deactivation ends sessions within about 1 second through the live event (epic section 13). Time: `deactivated at` in UTC. Concurrency: a request in flight is either completed before the change or refused.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S9, EP-05-S10, EP-05-S11, EP-04-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S9: System can refuse to remove the last active owner

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S9
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can refuse to remove the last active owner
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a guard that keeps exactly one active owner per shop, checked inside the same transaction as any add, deactivation or role change, refusing a change that would leave the shop with no owner or with two
- **So that:** the shop is never left with nobody who can manage users or clear mismatches, and the rule "one shop has one owner" holds (FR-05-11, BR-05-13)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth is the shop's owner, when he changes his own role to `staff`, then the server refuses with "The shop needs its owner." and his role stays `owner` (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given the same, when he deactivates himself, then the same refusal is returned and nothing changes.
  3. Given the shop has an owner, when Sanjay adds a user with role `owner` or changes Deepak Rao's role to `owner`, then the server refuses with "The shop already has an owner." and nothing changes (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  4. Given two requests at the same moment that would each make a user `owner`, when both are handled, then both are refused and the shop still has exactly one owner.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The count of active owners in the shop and the update run in one transaction with a row lock or serialisable isolation, so two parallel changes cannot both pass; a unique constraint on (shop ID) for active owners backs it up. The guard runs on Create User, Update User role and Update User status. The first owner is created only by EP-04-S1 through the setup wizard (EP-45).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. A refused change emits nothing.
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused change writes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The refusal sentence shows on the edit-user screen, which is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the one-owner guard runs inside the same transaction (epic section 13). D7 is decided: one shop has exactly one owner and an owner has exactly one shop. Open question: how ownership is handed over if the owner changes (not in v1).
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S4, EP-03-S6, EP-02-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S10: System can end a user's sessions live when they are deactivated or re-roled

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S10
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can end a user's sessions live when they are deactivated or re-roled
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** deactivation and role change to call Delete All sessions (EP-04-S13) in the same transaction and to emit "User deactivated or role changed" with the user id and reason after commit
- **So that:** EP-04 ends the sessions, EP-07 drops the user's subscriptions and EP-20 signs the karigar phone out, all within about a second (FR-05-12, BR-05-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the owner deactivates Vijay Kumar, when the transaction commits, then exactly one "User deactivated or role changed" event is emitted with user id, reason `deactivated` and time.
  2. Given the transaction rolls back, when the change fails, then no event is emitted and no session ends.
  3. Given Deepak Rao's role changes from `staff` to `karigar`, when the event is emitted, then it carries reason `role_changed` and the new role, and his sessions have `end reason` `role_changed`.
  4. Given the live channel from EP-07 is not yet built, when the event is emitted, then the user's next request is still refused as `unauthenticated` because the sessions have ended.
  5. Given the event payload, when it is inspected, then it holds no phone number or name.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The event is emitted only after commit, never inside a transaction that may roll back. Ending sessions and the user change share one transaction. Only the server emits this event.

- **UI reference:** No screen. The signed-out state is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: access ends at once. Performance: open screens return to sign-in within about 1 second once EP-07 is live (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1). Personal data: the payload carries ids only. D1 is decided (Option C): the event goes through the Node API's live channel (EP-07).

- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S11: Owner can see the user directory with role and status

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S11
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can see the user directory with role and status
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** the `staff-directory` screen to list every user with name, phone, email, role and status (Awaiting activation, Active, Locked or Deactivated), with a way to open one user and an "Unlock" action on a locked account
- **So that:** I can see who has access, pick a person to edit, re-role, deactivate or reactivate, and let a locked-out person back in without waiting 15 minutes (FR-05-14, FR-05-18)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth signed in as Owner, when he opens route `staff-directory`, then every user is listed with name, phone, role (Owner, Staff or Karigar) and status, loaded from the server.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma signed in as Staff, when he opens `staff-directory` or calls List Users, then the screen is not shown in his rail and the server returns `forbidden`.
  3. Given more than one page of users, when the list is scrolled, then the next page loads with a cursor (EP-03-S9).
  4. Given the directory is loading, when the server has not answered, then a loading state shows; given the server fails, then an error message with a retry shows.
  5. Given a deactivated user, when the list is shown, then the row says Deactivated and offers Reactivate instead of Deactivate.
  6. Given Deepak Rao is locked after 5 wrong passwords, when Sanjay opens the directory, then Deepak's row says "Locked until 11:42" and offers Unlock; when Sanjay taps Unlock, then Deepak can sign in at once (EP-04-S8), and a Staff session calling Unlock gets `forbidden`.
  7. Given a user who has not activated, when the list is shown, then the row says Awaiting activation and offers "Resend activation email" (EP-05-S4).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may call List Users and Unlock. List Users returns only users of the owner's shop (D7). Karigar users appear with their linked karigar id. Sorting is by name. Unlock clears the lock through EP-04-S8.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "User deactivated or role changed", to update a row while the directory is open, once EP-07 delivers it.
- **Audit entry written:** No for reading the directory. Unlock writes `account_unlocked` with the owner as actor (through EP-04-S14).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database.
- **UI reference:** Route `staff-directory` (`src/components/people/StaffDirectory.tsx`). The user list with status is not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: full phones and emails are shown to the owner only (epic section 13). Performance: the directory loads under 2 seconds. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; the list shows the shop's users only.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S2, EP-05-S4, EP-03-S9, EP-04-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S12: User can open an account menu that replaces the role switcher

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S12
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** User can open an account menu that replaces the role switcher
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** the chip at the foot of the rail to open an account menu with my name, my role and "Sign out", and nothing that lets me become someone else
- **So that:** each person acts only as themselves on a shared device (FR-05-13, BR-05-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma signed in as Staff, when he opens the account menu, then it shows "Rajesh Verma", "Staff" and a "Sign out" item, from Read Current user.
  2. Given any signed-in user, when the app is searched, then no screen offers an identity switch; `RoleChip` no longer lists other identities and `StoreProvider.switchIdentity` is removed (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  3. Given Rajesh taps "Sign out", when it completes, then his session on that device ends and the sign-in screen shows (EP-04-S11).
  4. Given Sanjay Seth signed in as Owner, when he opens the menu, then it shows "Sanjay Seth" and "Owner" with no "switch" label (the "Owner · switch" text on mockup 25 is replaced).
  5. Given Read Current user, when it is called, then it returns user id, name, role, landing route and the role's permission list from EP-05-S1, which the web uses to hide buttons.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Current user returns data for the session's user only and accepts no user id parameter. The permission list sent to the web is for display; the server still checks each call (EP-05-S2).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "User deactivated or role changed", so the menu and screens return to sign-in when the user's own account changes.

- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Removes `switchIdentity` and the identity list from the web.
- **UI reference:** `src/components/ui/RoleChip.tsx` at the rail foot; account menu not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: no identity switch reachable from any route. Performance: the menu opens without a server round trip after the first Read Current user.
- **Depends on:** EP-04-S6, EP-04-S11, EP-05-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S13: Owner can link a karigar user to a karigar record

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S13
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can link a karigar user to a karigar record
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to set the `karigarId` of a user with role `karigar` to one Karigar record, such as KG-04
- **So that:** the karigar sees exactly their own jobs when they sign in on the job portal (FR-05-15)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a karigar user Lakshmi Devi and Karigar record KG-04, when the owner links them, then `users.karigarId` is KG-04 and her job list shows only KG-04 jobs.
  2. Given KG-04 is already linked to another active user, when the owner links a second user to it, then the server refuses with "This karigar already has an account."
  3. Given a user with role `staff`, when a link to a karigar record is attempted, then the server refuses with "Only a karigar user can be linked to a karigar record.".
  4. Given a Karigar record id that does not exist, when the link is saved, then the server returns `not_found`.
  5. Given a Staff session, when it calls the link operation, then the server returns `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only role `owner` may link. A karigar user links to exactly one Karigar record, and one Karigar record to at most one active user. The link uses the user's `version`. Prototype ids such as `KG-04` stay as the karigar reference.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes (through EP-05-S14): actor, time, entity user, action `karigar_linked`, before and after `karigarId`.
- **Data changes:** Updates `users.karigarId` and `users.version`; uses the foreign key from `users.karigarId` to `karigars` (EP-02-S4).
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The karigar onboarding screen is `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg` (EP-16).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: a wrong link would show one karigar another's jobs, so the link is owner-only and audited. Open question: whether linking happens in one step with karigar onboarding in EP-16 or in two. D4 is decided: phone numbers are unique, so two karigars cannot share one phone.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S4, EP-05-S3, EP-02-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-05-S14: System can audit every user lifecycle change

- **Story ID:** EP-05-S14
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can audit every user lifecycle change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** add, edit, role change, deactivate, reactivate and karigar link to each write an audit entry with actor, time, user id, action and before and after values, in the same transaction as the change
- **So that:** the owner can later see who gave or took away whose access, and when (FR-05-16)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth adds Deepak Rao at 11:15 IST, when the audit entries are read, then one has actor Sanjay Seth, time 05:45 UTC, entity Deepak's user id, action `user_added` and after values name, role `staff`, masked phone "+91 ••••• 71145" and masked email.
  2. Given Deepak's role changes from `staff` to `karigar`, when the entries are read, then one has action `role_changed`, before role `staff` and after role `karigar`.
  3. Given a deactivation that is refused by the one-owner guard, when the entries are read, then no entry exists for it.
  4. Given each of `user_added`, `user_edited`, `role_changed`, `user_deactivated`, `user_reactivated` and `karigar_linked`, when a test runs the operation, then exactly one entry with that action is written.
  5. Given any of these entries, when it is searched for a full phone number, then none appears.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The entry is written in the same transaction as the change (EP-03-S6), so a rolled-back change leaves no entry. Actor and time come from `Ctx` (EP-03-S3). Entries are append-only. Phones are masked before writing.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity user, action, before, after, reason where given.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). No schema change. The audit reader screen is EP-06.
- **UI reference:** No screen in this story. Entries appear on the audit screen built in EP-06.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every user lifecycle change has before and after values (epic section 13). Personal data: phones masked. Time: stored in UTC.
- **Depends on:** EP-04-S14, EP-02-S11, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-06: Audit log · stories

Epic document: [EP-06 Audit log](../epics/EP-06-audit-log.md)

Role note: stories where the server writes, protects or filters audit entries on its own use "System". Stories that describe reading the Security log use "Owner", the only role allowed to read it.

---

## EP-06-S1: System can store audit entries that cannot be updated or deleted

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S1
- **Status:** Partial: AC5 (grants check run in CI against staging) waits for staging (FU-008, D1a).
- **Title:** System can store audit entries that cannot be updated or deleted
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `audit_entries` table from EP-02-S11 extended with entity type, entity id, before, after, reason and token reference columns, and locked so the application's database role can only insert and select rows
- **So that:** no person, including the owner or a developer with a database tool in production, can change or remove the record of who changed the books (BR-06-1, BR-06-2, FR-06-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `audit_entries` is inspected, then it has id, at (UTC), actor id, actor name, actor role, entity type, entity id, action, summary, before, after, reason, token reference and ref columns, and every column is set at insert.
  2. Given an existing entry, when the application's database role runs an UPDATE or DELETE on `audit_entries`, then the database refuses it with a permission error and the row is unchanged (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given Sanjay Seth signed in as Owner, when he calls an update or delete operation on an audit entry through the API, then no such operation exists in the contract and the server returns `not_found` for the unknown operation, with the row unchanged (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  4. Given an entry with entity type `invoice`, which is not in the list piece, parcel, lead, job, edit, problem, scrap request, stock-out, setting, user, scale, karigar, customer, broadcast, wish, session, when it is inserted, then the database rejects it.
  5. Given a production database, when the grants on `audit_entries` are listed in a CI check against staging, then only INSERT and SELECT are granted to the application role, and no role used by the application or by developers in production has UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Append-only is enforced twice: the contract has no update or delete operation for audit entries, and PostgreSQL grants on the application role allow only insert and select. A correction is a new entry whose ref points at the old entry id; the old entry is never touched (epic section 16 risk). Entity type and actor role are checked against fixed lists.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The audit log pushes no events (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story builds the store; it writes no entries itself.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11): adds `entity type`, `entity id`, `before` and `after` (structured, for example JSON), `reason`, `token reference`; renames `kind` to `action` or keeps `kind` as the column name, matching EP-02 naming; adds an index on (entity type, entity id) and on (actor id, at). Migration revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the table from the application role. The prototype `AuditEntry {id, at, actorName, actorRole, kind, summary, detail, ref}` keeps its fields; `detail` stays as free text, and before and after are empty for entries written before this migration. Entity type `session` is added to the epic's list for the sign-in entries from EP-04-S14.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: append-only by storage permissions as well as by the API (epic section 13). Concurrency: inserts only, so no lock contention on existing rows. D1 is decided (Option C): the lock is a PostgreSQL grant on the role the Node API uses. Open question: whether a hash chain is also needed for tamper evidence; if yes, a `previous hash` column is added here.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S11, EP-03-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-06-S2: System can write an audit entry in the same transaction as every state change

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S2
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can write an audit entry in the same transaction as every state change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a service-layer wrapper that every state-changing operation runs through, which appends exactly one audit entry inside the operation's transaction before it commits
- **So that:** a change without an entry can never be committed, and a failed audit write rolls the change back (FR-06-1, FR-06-2, BR-06-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given lead LD-2026-213 in state `opened`, when Rajesh Verma calls the reference `markLeadLost` (EP-03-S12) with reason "Customer went elsewhere.", then one audit entry with entity type lead, entity id LD-2026-213, actor Rajesh Verma and reason "Customer went elsewhere." is written in the same transaction as the state change.
  2. Given a test that makes the audit insert fail inside a state-changing operation, when the operation ends, then the business row is unchanged and the caller gets an error (epic acceptance criterion 4; the stock-out case with a piece staying `in_stock` is re-run in EP-26 once stock-out exists).
  3. Given an operation that is refused by a rule, by the permission check or by a version conflict, when it ends, then no audit entry is written.
  4. Given an operation registered in the EP-03 contract as state-changing, when it is not wrapped by the audit writer, then a CI test fails and names the operation (epic section 16 risk).
  5. Given two operations committed one after the other, when the log is read, then their entries are in commit order.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The Append Audit entry operation is internal and callable only from service functions, never from a client request. Actor and time come from `Ctx` (EP-03-S3), never from the request body. The entry insert and the business change share the one transaction from EP-03-S6. One state-changing call writes exactly one entry, even when it touches several rows.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. After-commit events from other epics are emitted only once the transaction with its audit entry has committed.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, for every wrapped operation: actor id, actor name, actor role, time, entity type, entity id, action, summary, reason when given.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries`. No schema change beyond EP-06-S1. Adds the audit writer and wrapper to `api`, and a list of state-changing operations to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: entries are written in the operation's transaction, so order matches commit order (epic section 13). Performance: the extra insert adds one row per operation and no extra round trip outside the transaction. D1 is decided (Option C): the wrapper runs in the Node API, inside the operation's transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S3: System can record before and after values for each change

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S3
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can record before and after values for each change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the audit writer to take the row as it was read and the row as it will be saved, and store only the fields that changed in `before` and `after`
- **So that:** the owner can see exactly what each change did, and entries stay small over a year of use (FR-06-3, BR-06-2, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given lead LD-2026-213 in state `opened` with an empty note, when it is marked lost with reason "Customer went elsewhere.", then the entry has before `{state: "opened", note: null}` and after `{state: "lost", note: "Customer went elsewhere."}` and no unchanged field such as the customer name.
  2. Given a create operation, such as adding user Deepak Rao (EP-05-S4), when the entry is written, then before is empty and after holds the created fields, with the phone masked as "+91 ••••• 71145".
  3. Given a change to a field holding a list, such as `notifyChannels {whatsapp, app, email}`, when only `email` changes from false to true, then before and after hold `notifyChannels` with the old and new values.
  4. Given a field named `code`, `token`, `password`, `link`, `secret` or `tokenHash`, when it changed, then it is left out of before and after.
  5. Given any entry, when it is inspected, then no money field is present, because value fields stay off until EP-42.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Before comes from the row read inside the transaction, not from the client. Only changed fields are stored. Secret fields are stripped before writing (shared with EP-04-S14). Phones are masked. A correction is a new entry; before and after of an earlier entry are never rewritten.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: before and after added to the fields written by EP-06-S2.
- **Data changes:** Writes `audit_entries.before` and `audit_entries.after`. No schema change beyond EP-06-S1.
- **UI reference:** No screen in this story. Before and after are shown by EP-06-S11.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every state change records before and after values (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 Auditable). Personal data: customer names may appear in before or after, for example on stock-outs and wishes; listed under gap G22. Performance: storing only changed fields keeps an entry to a few hundred bytes.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S2, EP-04-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S4: System can record a token reference instead of the token value

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S4
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can record a token reference instead of the token value
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** operations that use a one-time token (applying an edit with the owner edit code) to store the id of the hashed token record in `token reference`, and never the 6-digit value
- **So that:** nobody reading the log or a backup can reuse or learn a token, and the habit of writing "Token ${edit.token}" from `applyEdit` is not carried into production (FR-06-5, BR-06-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth applies an edit to TAG-8841 with a valid token, when the operation commits, then the entry has a token reference that points to the hashed token record and the entry contains no 6-digit token anywhere in summary, before, after or reason (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given a test that searches every column of every entry written by the edit-token tests for the 6 digits used, and by the sign-in, activation and reset tests for the passwords and links used, when it runs in CI, then it finds no match.
  3. Given the audit entry type in the shared package, when it is read, then it has a `tokenReference` field and no field that can hold the code value (epic section 16 risk).
  4. Given an operation that used no token, such as marking a lead lost, when its entry is written, then `token reference` is empty.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The writer accepts a token record id only. The value is stripped by the same secret-field filter as EP-06-S3. Summary text is built by the server from field names and values and never from a client string that might include the token.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: token reference added to the fields written by EP-06-S2 when a token was used.
- **Data changes:** Writes `audit_entries.token reference`. The hashed token records themselves come from EP-25 (edit token). Sign-in has no code (D4); passwords and links are never written to audit (EP-04-S14).
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/05-edit-propose-apply.svg` shows the edit and token flow that produces this entry ("Enter the token sent to your WhatsApp"). No screen in this story.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: tokens are never logged in plain text; the reference points to the hashed token record (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5, epic section 13). Audit: the reference lets the owner match an edit to the token sent to his WhatsApp without seeing the token.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S3, EP-04-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S5: System can record weights in entries as integer units of 0.0001 g

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S5
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can record weights in entries as integer units of 0.0001 g
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every weight inside before and after (for example `grossG`, `stoneG`, `lossG`, `gapNetG`, `deltaG`) stored as an integer in units of 0.0001 g using the shared conversion from EP-02-S2, and shown at four decimals
- **So that:** the log never rounds a weight differently from the books, and an edit of 40 mg shows as exactly 0.0400 g (FR-06-6, BR-06-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an edit to TAG-8841 changing gross weight from 48.6500 g to 48.6100 g, when the entry is written, then before has `grossG` 486500 and after has `grossG` 486100 (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given that entry, when it is shown to the owner, then it reads "48.6500 g" and "48.6100 g", with four decimals and no rounding.
  3. Given an accepted loss with `lossG` 0.0350 g, when the entry is written, then it stores 350.
  4. Given the writer is passed a weight as a decimal such as 48.61, when it validates the entry, then it rejects it in tests, because weights must already be integers.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Weight fields in before and after must be whole numbers. Conversion happens once, in the shared package, never in the audit writer.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: weight values inside before and after, as integers.
- **Data changes:** None beyond EP-06-S1. Weight values inside `before` and `after` are integers.
- **UI reference:** No screen in this story. Display at four decimals is used by EP-06-S11.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: weights are integers in units of 0.0001 g and shown to 4 decimals (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Precision: a test confirms that 486500 to 486100 displays a difference of 0.0400 g.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S3, EP-02-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S6: System can record actions taken by the scheduler and integrations

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S6
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can record actions taken by the scheduler and integrations
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a System actor for changes made with no signed-in user, with a name that says which part acted, such as "Scheduler" or "WhatsApp intake"
- **So that:** a lead escalated by the timer or a lead created from an incoming message still has an entry with a clear actor (FR-06-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a background job changes a record with no session, when its entry is written, then actor role is System, actor id is empty or the fixed System id, and actor name is the job's name, for example "Scheduler".
  2. Given an integration such as WhatsApp intake creates a record, when its entry is written, then actor name is "WhatsApp intake" and actor role is System.
  3. Given a client request that sends actor role System in its body, when the server handles it, then the actor is still taken from the session and the request cannot act as System.
  4. Given the owner later reads the log, when he filters by actor System, then these entries are listed (EP-06-S10).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only server-side job and integration code can build a System `Ctx`; no client request can. The actor role list is `owner`, `staff`, `karigar`, System. Each job or integration registers one fixed actor name.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor role System, actor name, time, entity, action, before, after.
- **Data changes:** Migration allows actor role System in `audit_entries` and allows an empty actor id for System rows, or seeds one fixed System user, matching the EP-02-S11 foreign key.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: System context is never built from a request. Time: job time is the server's UTC time at commit.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S2, EP-03-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S7: System can audit lead, job, parcel, problem, edit-proposal and onboarding transitions not audited today

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can audit lead, job, parcel, problem, edit-proposal and onboarding transitions not audited today
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an action kind in the shared action list for every transition that the prototype does not audit, so that each one writes an entry when its feature epic ports it
- **So that:** the log covers every change, not only the 10 kinds the prototype writes today (FR-06-10, BR-06-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the shared action list, when it is compared with the "not audited today" list in epic section 6, then it has one action kind for each of createLead, confirmLead, startWorkingLead, markLeadLost, routeLeadItemToStock, createOrderCopyAndJob, acceptJob, startJob, markJobReady, handOver, parcel arrival, saveTag, qcTick, releaseParcel on an exact match, ownerRecheckTag, raiseProblem, proposeEdit, ownerAgreeEdit, requestScrap, onboarding of customer, karigar and staff, sendWishes, sendBroadcast and upsertScale, and none for releaseHold, because v1 has no holds.
  2. Given the 10 existing kinds `edit_applied`, `edit_refused`, `loss_accepted`, `parcel_sent_back`, `parcel_last_digit`, `problem_cleared`, `scrap_marked`, `scrap_declined`, `stock_out`, `setting_changed`, when the list is read, then they are all still present with the same names, so prototype entries stay readable.
  3. Given the karigar Lakshmi Devi hands over job for KG-04, when the operation commits in EP-19 or EP-20, then an entry exists with actor Lakshmi Devi, actor role `karigar` and the hand-over action (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  4. Given the reference `markLeadLost` from EP-03-S12, when it runs, then its entry uses the lead-lost action kind from this list.
  5. Given a new action kind is added to the list, when the migration runs, then the database accepts entries with it, and a kind not in the list is still rejected.
  6. Given every operation in the EP-03 catalogue, when the CI audit test runs, then each state-changing operation has a test that checks it writes an entry of its kind, and the run fails for any that does not (epic acceptance criterion 6).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The action list lives in the shared package and the database check is generated from it. Each feature epic must use a kind from this list; EP-06-S2 refuses to commit an entry with an unknown kind. A transition removed in v1 (releaseHold) has no kind.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, by each feature epic's operation: actor, time, entity, action, before, after, reason where given.
- **Data changes:** Migration replaces the 10-value check on the action column from EP-02-S11 with the full list. The shared package gains the action list and the label for each kind.
- **UI reference:** No screen in this story. Labels show on the `security` route (EP-06-S9).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every transition writes an entry (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Open question: the final names of the new action kinds are not decided; this story fixes the list of transitions, and the names are set once that question is answered. Until then, working names such as `lead_lost` or `job_handed_over` are used and may change by migration before launch.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S2, EP-06-S6, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S8: System can audit the pricing flag and every other setting change

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S8
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can audit the pricing flag and every other setting change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every setting change, including `pricingEnabled`, to write a `setting_changed` entry with the setting key in ref and the old and new values in before and after
- **So that:** turning pricing on or off is on the record like any other rule change, which the prototype skips today (FR-06-11, BR-06-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given `pricingEnabled` is false, when Sanjay Seth sets it to true, then an entry is written with action `setting_changed`, ref `pricingEnabled`, before `{pricingEnabled: false}` and after `{pricingEnabled: true}`.
  2. Given `leadSlaHours` is 4, when the owner sets it to 6, then an entry is written with before 4 and after 6.
  3. Given the owner sets `leadSlaHours` to 0, when the server refuses with "The lead timer must be at least 1 hour.", then no entry is written.
  4. Given each of `pricingEnabled`, `leadSlaHours`, `requireEditToken`, `notifyChannels`, `lateLeadAudience` and `autoSendWishes`, when a test changes it, then exactly one `setting_changed` entry is written.
  5. Given the owner opens the Rules filter on the Security log, when entries load, then the `pricingEnabled` change is listed.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The setting change and its entry share one transaction. There is no exception for `pricingEnabled`; the `if (a.key === 'pricingEnabled') return st;` skip in `setSetting` is not carried over. Who may change each setting is decided by EP-13 and the G12 question, not here.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story. "Setting changed" is a proposed event (README gap G26) emitted by EP-13.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity setting, entity id the key, action `setting_changed`, before, after.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries`. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** Rules filter on the `security` route; settings screens are EP-13.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: a change to `pricingEnabled` writes an entry like any other setting (FR-06-11). Open question G12: who may change which setting is not settled, so this story audits every change regardless of who makes it.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S9: Owner can list audit entries newest first, one page at a time

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S9
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can list audit entries newest first, one page at a time
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** the Security log on route `security` to load entries from the server newest first, a page at a time, each row showing the kind label, ref, time in Asia/Kolkata, actor name and role, and summary
- **So that:** I can see what changed the books and who did it, even after a year of entries (FR-06-8, BR-06-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth signed in as Owner, when he opens "Security log" in the owner rail, then the screen shows the title "Security log", the subtitle "Everything that changed the books and who did it. Entries are never edited or removed." and the first page of entries newest first, loaded from the server.
  2. Given an entry for the edit applied to TAG-8841 at 09:02 UTC, when it is listed, then the row shows "Edit applied", "TAG-8841", the time as 14:32 IST, "Sanjay Seth (owner)" and the summary.
  3. Given more entries than one page, when the owner scrolls to the end of the list or presses the next-page control, then the next page loads by cursor with no repeats and no gaps (EP-03-S9).
  4. Given the list is loading, when the server has not answered, then a loading state shows; given the server fails, then an error message with a retry shows; given the connection drops, then the screen says it is reconnecting.

- **UI reference:** Route `security` (`src/components/settings/SecurityLog.tsx`); owner rail item "Security log" on `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg`. The Security log list itself is not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: first page under 2 seconds with a year of entries (epic section 13). Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Availability: loading, error and reconnecting states shown. Personal data: rows may show customer names; only the owner sees them.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S2, EP-06-S12, EP-03-S9, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-06-S10: Owner can filter the log by kind group, entity, actor and date

- **Story ID:** EP-06-S10
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Owner can filter the log by kind group, entity, actor and date
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to narrow the Security log by kind group (Everything, Tag edits, Parcels and losses, Problems, Scrap, Stock-out, Rules), by entity such as TAG-8841 or BATCH-2026-044, by actor, and by a date range
- **So that:** I can find every change to one piece or every action by one person quickly (FR-06-8, BR-06-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the owner presses "Tag edits", when the list reloads from the server, then only entries with `edit_applied` or `edit_refused` are shown, and the button shows as pressed.
  2. Given the owner enters TAG-8841 as the entity, when the list reloads, then only entries with that entity id or ref are shown, newest first.
  3. Given the owner picks actor Rajesh Verma and dates 1 to 7 March 2026, when the list reloads, then only Rajesh's entries with `at` from 1 March 00:00 IST to 7 March 23:59 IST are shown, and the range is converted to UTC on the server.

- **UI reference:** Filter group "Kind of entry" on route `security` (`src/components/settings/SecurityLog.tsx`). Entity, actor and date filters are not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3).

# EP-07: Live channel · stories

Epic document: [EP-07 Live channel](../epics/EP-07-live-channel.md)

Role note: stories where the server publishes, filters, buffers or closes connections on its own use "System". The two-browser test harness story uses "Developer". Stories about what a person sees use Owner, Staff or Karigar, or "User" in the candidate title where every role is meant; the "As a" field then names the role used in the example.

---

## EP-07-S1: System can publish an event only after its operation's transaction commits

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S1
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can publish an event only after its operation's transaction commits
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** service functions to record each event they cause in an outbox row inside the operation's transaction, and a publisher to send the event to the live channel only once that transaction has committed
- **So that:** no screen ever shows a change that was rolled back, such as a piece shown as billed when the stock-out failed (FR-07-2, BR-07-6, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the reference `markLeadLost` operation from EP-03-S12 is extended to cause a test event, when the transaction commits, then exactly one event is published to the live channel after the commit and none before it.
  2. Given a test that forces the same operation to fail after the outbox row is inserted, when the transaction rolls back, then the outbox row is gone and no event is published.
  3. Given an operation refused by a rule, a permission check or a version conflict (EP-02-S14), when it ends, then no event is published.
  4. Given the publisher process is stopped while 3 operations commit, when it is restarted, then the 3 events are published in commit order and none is lost or sent twice.
  5. Given a service function that calls the live channel's publish directly instead of writing to the outbox, when the CI check runs, then it fails and names the function.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Publish is internal and callable only from service functions through the outbox, never from a client request (epic section 10). The outbox row and the business change share the one transaction from EP-03-S6. Each outbox row is marked sent once published, so a restart does not resend it.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. This story builds the publish path that every catalogue event in PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 uses.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The audit entry belongs to the operation that caused the event (EP-06-S2); publishing changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** Migration adds an `event_outbox` table: id, event name, entity type, entity id, entity version, audience, created at (UTC), sent at. The publisher reads unsent rows in id order.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: events leave only after commit, so a client never sees a rolled-back change (epic section 13). Availability: unsent rows survive a publisher crash or redeploy. Time: created at is server UTC. D1 is decided (Option C): the outbox and the publisher run in the Node API, which is the live push service. Open decision D3: the transport the publisher writes to is not chosen; the criteria hold for WebSocket or Server-Sent Events.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-07-S2: System can stamp each event with a sequence number, entity id and version

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S2
- **Status:** Partial: AC5 (stock screen shows the refetched piece) needs the piece read of EP-22 and a live stock screen (FU-012, FU-013).
- **Title:** System can stamp each event with a sequence number, entity id and version
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every published event to carry one envelope: sequence number, event name, entity type, entity id, entity version, emitted at (UTC) and audience, and no business values
- **So that:** clients can order events, detect gaps, ignore stale ones, and refetch the real record through a permission-checked read (FR-07-3, FR-07-4, BR-07-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an edit is applied to TAG-8841 and the piece moves from version 6 to version 7, when the event is published, then its envelope has name "Edit applied", entity type `piece`, entity id TAG-8841, entity version 7, emitted at in UTC and a sequence number one higher than the previous event on that stream.
  2. Given two events published on the same stream, when a client receives them, then their sequence numbers are strictly increasing with no duplicates.
  3. Given the envelope of any catalogue event, when it is inspected, then it contains no weight, no money, no customer name and no phone number (epic section 13 Personal data).
  4. Given a client holds TAG-8841 at version 7, when an event for TAG-8841 with version 6 arrives late, then the client does not refetch and keeps version 7.
  5. Given a client receives "Edit applied" for TAG-8841, when it updates the `stock` screen, then it shows the gross weight from the refetched piece, for example 48.6100 g, and never a value from the event (FR-07-4).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The sequence number is assigned by the server at publish time, per stream, from a counter that never goes backwards. Entity version comes from the row's version column (EP-02-S14). The envelope schema is defined once in the shared package (EP-03-S1) and the publisher rejects an envelope with extra fields.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Defines the envelope used by all 10 catalogue events.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The envelope is transport data, not a state change.
- **Data changes:** Adds sequence number and audience to `event_outbox` (EP-07-S1). Adds the envelope type to the shared package. Weights are never carried; clients refetch pieces whose weights are integers in units of 0.0001 g.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: events are ordered by sequence number per stream (epic section 13). Personal data: envelopes carry ids only. Precision: no weight is sent in an event, so no rounding can happen in transit. Time: emitted at is server UTC. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; the envelope carries no branch key, and the server scopes every event to the shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S1, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S3: User can open an authenticated live connection

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S3
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** User can open an authenticated live connection
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** my browser to open one live connection when I sign in, authenticated with my session, and keep it open while any screen is open
- **So that:** changes made by others reach my screen without a refresh, and nobody without a session can listen (FR-07-1, BR-07-1, BR-07-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma signed in as Staff, when the app shell loads on route `today`, then exactly one live connection opens and the server records it with his user id and role `staff`.
  2. Given a connection attempt with no session or with an expired session (EP-04-S12), when it reaches the server, then it is refused as `unauthenticated` and no subscription is created.
  3. Given Rajesh opens a second tab, when it loads, then that tab opens its own connection, and both are listed against his user id.
  4. Given Rajesh signs out (EP-04-S11), when the sign-out commits, then his connections close within about 1 second.
  5. Given the owner Sanjay Seth on a phone and Lakshmi Devi on the karigar app at route `k-jobs`, when each signs in, then each opens one connection with their own role.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The connection is checked against the session store on open, the same check as an API request. The user id and role come from the session, never from the client. A connection whose session ends is closed by the server.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Opening a connection changes no business record; sign-in itself is audited by EP-04-S14.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. The Node API holds a connection record in memory: connection id, user id, role, opened at.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The connection starts from the app shell for every route; the shell's states are built in EP-08.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: an unauthenticated connection is refused (FR-07-1). Performance: the connection is open within 2 seconds of the shell loading on a shop connection. Open decision D3: WebSocket or Server-Sent Events; presence (EP-07-S8) needs two-way, which rules out plain Server-Sent Events unless presence uses API calls. D1 is decided (Option C): the connection is served by the Node API on the shop's own domain. D4 is decided (phone and password); the connection only checks that the Node API session is valid.
- **Depends on:** EP-04-S5, EP-04-S11, EP-04-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S4: System can subscribe a connection to its user and role channels

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S4
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can subscribe a connection to its user and role channels
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each new connection to join its user channel and its role channel automatically, and to join or leave an entity channel (for example one parcel) when the client asks
- **So that:** each event goes only to the streams that need it, matching the audiences in PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 (FR-07-5, BR-07-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma's connection opens, when the server sets it up, then it joins `user:<Rajesh's id>` and `role:staff` and no other channel.
  2. Given Sanjay Seth's connection opens, when it is set up, then it joins `user:<Sanjay's id>` and `role:owner`.
  3. Given Rajesh opens route `parcel-tag` for BATCH-2026-044, when the client subscribes to `parcel:BATCH-2026-044`, then the server adds that channel to his connection after the EP-05 read check passes.
  4. Given Rajesh leaves `parcel-tag`, when the client unsubscribes, then the channel is removed and he receives no more events for BATCH-2026-044 unless his role channel carries them.
  5. Given a client asks to subscribe to `role:owner` while signed in as Staff, when the request arrives, then it is refused as `forbidden` and the connection stays on its own channels.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** User and role channels are assigned by the server from the session; the client cannot choose them. Entity channels are joined only after the EP-05 permission check for reading that entity (EP-05-S2). The list of channel kinds is fixed: user, role, entity.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Joining a channel changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Subscription record per connection: connection id, user id, role, channels joined.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Entity subscriptions are opened by `parcel-tag` and `parcel-match` (`docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, `docs/ux/mockups/04-parcel-match.svg`).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: every subscription is checked against EP-05 permissions (epic section 13). D7 is decided: one shop, so role channels are not split by branch.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S3, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S5: System can filter every event by the receiver's permissions

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S5
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can filter every event by the receiver's permissions
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the channel to check, for each event and each subscribed connection, that the receiving user may read the entity under EP-05 before delivering it
- **So that:** a wrong audience on an event, or a channel joined in error, cannot leak that a lead, customer or piece exists to someone who may not read it (FR-07-5, BR-07-4, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" event for LD-2026-213 addressed to staff and the owner, when it is delivered, then Rajesh Verma (Staff) and Sanjay Seth (Owner) receive it and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar) does not.
  2. Given a test that publishes a "Piece billed by one staff member" event with the karigar role wrongly in its audience, when it is delivered, then no karigar connection receives it, because karigars may not read pieces in stock.
  3. Given a user whose role changed from Staff to Karigar in the same second as an event, when the event is delivered, then the filter uses the role stored on the server at delivery time, not the role the connection opened with.
  4. Given 10 open connections and one event, when it is delivered, then each connection is checked once and the event still arrives within about 1 second of commit.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The filter calls the same permission check as the read API (EP-05-S2) for the event's entity type and id. An event that fails the check for a connection is dropped silently for that connection. Payloads hold ids only, so even a delivered event reveals nothing beyond the id; the client still refetches through a checked read.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Applies to every catalogue event.
- **Audit entry written:** No. A dropped delivery changes no business record. Repeated drops for one user are counted by EP-37.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: every event is filtered by EP-05 permissions (epic section 13). Performance: filtering keeps delivery within about 1 second of commit (BR-07-2). Personal data: envelopes carry ids, not names or phones.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S2, EP-07-S4, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S6: Karigar can receive only events about their own jobs

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S6
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Karigar can receive only events about their own jobs
- **As a:** Karigar
- **I want:** my phone to get live updates only for jobs issued to me and for my own account
- **So that:** my job list stays current without a refresh, and I never learn about other karigars' work, customers, leads, stock or prices (FR-07-6, BR-07-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Lakshmi Devi's phone is connected on route `k-jobs`, when a job assigned to Mahesh Soni changes status, then her phone receives nothing (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given a job assigned to Lakshmi Devi, when staff change its status, then her phone receives "Karigar job status changed" for that job within about 1 second and the job card refetches its status.
  3. Given any "Piece billed by one staff member", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Edit proposed / token sent" or "Metal pool changed" event, when it is published, then no karigar connection receives it.
  4. Given the owner changes Lakshmi Devi's role, when "User deactivated or role changed" is published for her, then her phone receives it on her user channel.
  5. Given a karigar user with no linked karigar record (EP-05-S13), when the phone connects, then it receives only events on its user channel and no job events.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** A karigar connection joins only its user channel and the job channels for jobs whose karigar id equals the karigar record linked to the user (EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13). It never joins `role:staff` or `role:owner`. The EP-07-S5 filter applies on top as a second check.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "Karigar job status changed" (own jobs only), "User deactivated or role changed" (own account only).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Receiving events changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Reads the user to karigar link from EP-05-S13.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: a karigar receives only own-job and own-account events (FR-07-6). Performance: own-job events arrive within about 1 second on a normal connection. D6 is decided: online only, so there is no offline queue; this story covers a connected phone, and catch-up after a long gap falls back to "refetch everything" (EP-07-S7). D5 is decided: the karigar client is a React web app in the phone browser.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S7: User can reconnect and catch up from the last sequence number

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** User can reconnect and catch up from the last sequence number
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** my browser to reconnect on its own after the connection drops, send the last sequence number it received, and get every event it missed in order
- **So that:** a short drop on the shop Wi-Fi does not leave me looking at a piece that someone else already sold (FR-07-8, epic section 13 Availability)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma's browser on `stock` loses its connection for 30 seconds while 4 events are published to his channels, when it reconnects, then it receives all 4 events in sequence order and no others (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the client's last sequence number is older than the replay buffer holds, when it resumes, then the server sends a single "refetch everything" signal and the client reloads its open screen's data from the API.
  3. Given the client already received event 1042 before the drop, when it resumes from 1042, then event 1042 is not sent again.
  4. Given the connection drops, when the client tries to reconnect, then it retries with growing delays up to a fixed maximum and never stops trying while a screen is open.
  5. Given a resume request whose session has expired during the drop, when it arrives, then it is refused as `unauthenticated` and the client goes to sign-in.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Resume checks the session like a new connection (EP-07-S3). Replayed events go through the same permission filter as live ones (EP-07-S5), using the user's current role. The replay buffer keeps events for a fixed window; older gaps get "refetch everything".
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Replays any catalogue event the client missed.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reconnecting changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** Replay buffer: recent events with sequence number, kept as sent rows in `event_outbox` for the retention window. A cleanup removes rows older than the window.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The "Reconnecting" state shown in the shell is built in EP-08.
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: reconnect is automatic and catches up without a full reload when the gap is short (epic section 13). Concurrency: replayed events arrive in sequence order. Security: replay is filtered by the current permissions. Open question: the replay buffer length is not decided; the criteria use "the retention window" and a test value of 5 minutes until it is. D6 is decided: online only. A karigar phone disconnected for hours reconnects and the server answers catch-up by sequence number if the gap is inside the retention window; otherwise the client refetches everything.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S2, EP-07-S3, EP-07-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S8: Staff can see who else is working on the same parcel

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S8
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Staff can see who else is working on the same parcel
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to see the names of the other staff who have the same parcel open on `parcel-tag` or `parcel-match`, updated live as they join and leave
- **So that:** two of us tagging BATCH-2026-044 can split the items and not tag the same one twice (FR-07-9, BR-07-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao both open `parcel-tag` for BATCH-2026-044, when both are present, then Rajesh sees "Deepak Rao" and Deepak sees "Rajesh Verma" in the parcel's presence list (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given Deepak closes the tab without leaving, when no heartbeat arrives from his connection for the timeout, then his name disappears from Rajesh's list within that timeout plus about 1 second.
  3. Given Deepak navigates from BATCH-2026-044 to another parcel, when he leaves, then his name disappears from the BATCH-2026-044 list within about 1 second.
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi signed in as Karigar, when she tries to join presence on BATCH-2026-044, then the server refuses it as `forbidden`.
  5. Given a user's own entry, when the list is shown, then their own name is not listed among the others.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Join and Leave are allowed for roles `staff` and `owner` only (epic section 10). The user name shown comes from the server's user record, not the client. Entries expire after a heartbeat timeout. The server is the only source of the presence list.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from the catalogue. Presence join and leave updates travel on the `parcel:<id>` entity channel and are not business events.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Presence changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Presence record kept by the channel: parcel id, user id, user name, joined at, last seen.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg` (THIS PARCEL panel for BATCH-2026-044), route `parcel-tag`; `docs/ux/mockups/04-parcel-match.svg`, route `parcel-match`. Where the presence names sit on the screen is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: join and leave reach others within about 1 second. Availability: stale entries expire by heartbeat timeout (epic section 16 risk). Open question: whether presence means "has the parcel open" or "is tagging an item now"; the criteria use "has the parcel open" until it is decided. Open decision D3: presence needs a two-way transport. D7 is decided: one shop, so presence is per parcel.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
