## EP-07-S9: User can see rail badge counts update live

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S9
- **Status:** Partial: no rail badge is server-backed yet; each moves to server counts with its screen (FU-012).
- **Title:** User can see rail badge counts update live
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** the counts on the rail items (Decisions, Leads, Parcels in, Showroom stock) to change within about a second of a relevant event, recomputed from server data
- **So that:** I see "Decisions 3" become "Decisions 4" when a parcel is stopped, without refreshing (FR-07-11, BR-07-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth on `decisions` with the Decisions badge at 3, when a "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" event arrives for BATCH-2026-044, then the badge shows 4 within about 1 second.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma on `today` with the Showroom stock badge at 42, when Deepak Rao bills a piece and "Piece billed by one staff member" arrives, then Rajesh's badge shows 41 within about 1 second.
  3. Given the owner's rail, when a lead passes its 8-hour SLA and "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" arrives, then the owner's Leads badge counts late leads and goes up by 1; given a staff rail, then the staff Leads badge counts leads needing a glance.
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi on the karigar app, when any event arrives, then no rail badge is shown, matching `railBadges` returning none for karigar.
  5. Given a burst of 5 events in one second, when they arrive, then the client fetches the counts once after the burst, not 5 times.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Counts come from a permission-checked read of badge counts on the server, using the same rules as `railBadges`: owner gets decisions total, late leads, open parcels and in-stock count; staff get leads needing a glance, open parcels and in-stock count; karigar gets none. The event only triggers the refetch.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "Piece billed by one staff member", "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Edit applied", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Parcel handed over by karigar". Proposed (README gap G26), once accepted: "Parcel released into stock", "Problem cleared", "Scrap requested", "Piece scrapped".
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading counts changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds a badge-count read operation to the shared contract; the `railBadges` selector rules move to the server.
- **UI reference:** Rail on `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg` (Decisions 3) and `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` (Decisions 6, Leads 2), route `decisions`; rail on `docs/ux/mockups/02-staff-home.svg` (Showroom stock 42, Parcels in 2), route `today`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: badges change within about 1 second of the event (FR-07-11); the count read answers in under 2 seconds. Security: counts are computed on the server per role. D7 is decided: one shop; the owner rail's "All branches" label shows the shop name and counts are for the shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S11, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S10: System can close a user's connections when they are deactivated or re-roled

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S10
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can close a user's connections when they are deactivated or re-roled
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the channel to consume "User deactivated or role changed", deliver it to that user's open connections, then close them and drop their subscriptions and presence
- **So that:** a deactivated user stops seeing live data within about a second, and a re-roled user cannot keep the old role's channels (FR-07-10, BR-07-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Vijay Kumar is signed in on two devices, when Sanjay Seth deactivates him (EP-05-S7), then both connections receive the event and are closed by the server within about 1 second (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given Deepak Rao is on `parcel-tag` for BATCH-2026-044 with presence, when his role changes from Staff to Karigar, then his connection closes, his name leaves the presence list, and on reconnect he joins only `user:<id>` and karigar job channels.
  3. Given a deactivated user's client tries to reconnect, when the resume arrives, then it is refused as `unauthenticated` because EP-05-S10 ended the sessions.
  4. Given the event is published, when it reaches other users, then only the affected user's connections receive it.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only the server closes connections (epic section 10, Close: System only). The close happens on the event, not on the next request. The event carries only the user id, the reason (`deactivated` or `role_changed`) and the new role, as set by EP-05-S10.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "User deactivated or role changed" (emitted by EP-05). Delivered to that user's open sessions before closing.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The deactivation or role change is audited by EP-05-S14; closing connections adds no entry.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Removes the user's connection, subscription and presence records from the channel.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The client's return to sign-in is covered by EP-04-S13.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: access ends within about 1 second of deactivation (epic section 13). Concurrency: a connection that opens in the same moment as the deactivation is refused by the session check in EP-07-S3.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S3, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S8, EP-05-S10, EP-04-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S11: System can carry each of the 10 catalogue events to its audience

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S11
- **Status:** Partial: AC4 (stock screen drops a billed piece live) needs the piece read of EP-22 and a live stock screen (FU-012, FU-013).
- **Title:** System can carry each of the 10 catalogue events to its audience
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the 10 catalogue events registered in the shared package with their entity type and audience channels, so that an emitting epic only names the event and the channel routes it
- **So that:** each event reaches exactly the people PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 says must see it, and the emitting epics do not each invent routing (BR-07-3, FR-07-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the shared event list, when it is compared with PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1, then it has exactly these 10 names and audiences: "Piece billed by one staff member" to `role:staff` except the billing user; "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" to `role:owner`; "Edit proposed / token sent" to `role:owner`; "Edit applied" to the proposing staff member's user channel and `role:staff`; "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" to `role:staff` and `role:owner`; "Karigar job status changed" to `role:staff`, `role:owner` and the owning karigar's user channel; "Parcel handed over by karigar" to `role:staff`; "Tag saved on a shared parcel" to `parcel:<id>` except the saving user; "Metal pool changed" to `role:staff` and `role:owner`; "User deactivated or role changed" to that user's channel.
  2. Given a test that emits each of the 10 events once from a stub service function, when it runs against two staff, the owner and two karigars, then each connection receives exactly the events listed for it in criterion 1 and no others.
  3. Given an emitting function that names an event not in the list, when it runs, then the publisher refuses it and the CI test fails.
  4. Given "Piece billed by one staff member" for TAG-8841 billed by Deepak Rao, when it is delivered, then Rajesh Verma's `stock` screen stops showing TAG-8841 as available within about 1 second and Deepak's own screen gets its result from the API response, not the event.
  5. Given a proposed event from README gap G26 such as "Parcel released into stock", when it is accepted into the catalogue later, then it is added to the shared list with its audience and needs no change to the transport.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The audience is set by the registry, not by the emitting function or the client. The EP-07-S5 permission filter still applies after routing. "Metal pool changed" goes to the roles allowed to open `order-copy`; karigars are excluded.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Transports: "Piece billed by one staff member" (EP-26), "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" (EP-23, EP-24), "Edit proposed / token sent" (EP-25), "Edit applied" (EP-25), "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" (EP-28, EP-29, EP-10), "Karigar job status changed" (EP-19, EP-20), "Parcel handed over by karigar" (EP-20), "Tag saved on a shared parcel" (EP-21), "Metal pool changed" (EP-18), "User deactivated or role changed" (EP-05).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Each emitting operation writes its own entry.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the event registry (name, entity type, audience rule) to the shared package.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Screens that react: `today`, `decisions`, `leads`, `stock`, `parcels`, `parcel-tag`, `parcel-match`, `order-copy` and `k-jobs` (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: each event reaches its audience within about 1 second of commit under normal shop load (FR-07-7). Security: audiences match PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 and karigars receive only their own job and account events. Open question G26: which proposed events are added to the catalogue; this story fixes the 10 and leaves room for more. D7 is decided: role channels are for the one shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S1, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-07-S12: Developer can test two browsers receiving each other's events

- **Story ID:** EP-07-S12
- **Status:** Partial: AC1 runs against a stand-in read until the piece read of EP-22 exists (FU-013).
- **Title:** Developer can test two browsers receiving each other's events
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** an automated test that signs in two browsers as different staff on staging, makes a change in one and checks the other receives the event and refetches, plus a short manual demo script
- **So that:** the M1 milestone demo "two browsers receive each other's events live" is proven on every run, not only once (epic acceptance criterion 6, PRODUCTION-SCOPE §7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given two browsers signed in as Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao on `stock`, when Deepak's browser triggers a "Piece billed by one staff member" test event for TAG-8841, then Rajesh's browser receives it and stops showing TAG-8841 as available within 1 second (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the same two browsers, when Rajesh's browser is cut off from the network for 30 seconds while 3 events are published, then after reconnect it has received all 3 in order (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  3. Given both browsers open `parcel-tag` for BATCH-2026-044, when the test runs, then each sees the other's name (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  4. Given a karigar test browser signed in as Lakshmi Devi, when a job of Mahesh Soni changes status, then it receives nothing; and when the owner deactivates the second staff user, then that browser's connection closes within about 1 second (epic acceptance criteria 2 and 5).
  5. Given the test is part of the CI suite (EP-01-S8), when it fails, then the run fails and names which criterion failed.

- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted (by the test stub): "Piece billed by one staff member", "Karigar job status changed", "User deactivated or role changed". consumed: the same, by the test browsers.
- **Audit entry written:** No for the stub test events. Yes for the deactivation step, written by EP-05-S14: actor, time, entity user, action, before, after.

- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the test asserts the 1-second delivery bound (BR-07-2). Security: the stub emitter is absent from production builds. Availability: the reconnect case proves catch-up.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S7, EP-07-S8, EP-07-S10, EP-07-S11, EP-01-S8, EP-02-S13

Copied from the epic's section 17. Not answered here.

- D3: WebSocket or Server-Sent Events? Presence needs two-way. Either way it is built in the Node API (D1, Option C), not taken from a platform. (EP-07-S1, S3, S8)
- D6 is decided: online only. A phone disconnected for hours reconnects, and the server answers catch-up by sequence number if the gap is inside the retention window; otherwise the client refetches everything (EP-07-S6, S7).

# EP-08: Front-end production foundation · stories

Epic document: [EP-08 Front-end production foundation](../epics/EP-08-front-end-production-foundation.md)

Role note: stories about what a person sees use Owner, Staff or Karigar; where the candidate title says "User" every role is meant, and the "As a" field names the role used in the examples. "System" means the browser data layer (API client, query cache and live hooks) acting on its own. "Developer" means the person wiring screens and building releases. This epic adds no server operation, so "Rules enforced on the server" names the server checks from EP-03, EP-04, EP-05 and EP-07 that the client relies on and must not replace.

---

## EP-08-S1: Developer can call every API operation through one typed client built from the contract

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can call every API operation through one typed client built from the contract
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** one API client in `web`, typed from the EP-03 shared contract, that attaches the session, adds an idempotency key to every action, and turns the EP-03 error format into a code and a sentence a person can read
- **So that:** every screen talks to the server the same way and a contract change breaks the build instead of a screen (FR-08-1, BR-08-1, BR-08-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the shared contract defines `markLeadLost` (the EP-03-S12 reference operation), when a developer calls it through the client with a wrong argument type, then `pnpm typecheck` fails in `web` and names the call site.
  2. Given a signed-in Staff session, when the client sends any read or action, then the request carries the session by the method EP-04 chose and the page script never reads the raw token.
  3. Given an action call such as `markLeadLost`, when the client sends it, then the request carries a newly generated idempotency key, and a read call carries none.
  4. Given the server answers with the EP-03 rule-refusal format and the sentence "A converted lead cannot be marked lost.", when the client returns, then the caller gets `{ ok: false, code, message: "A converted lead cannot be marked lost." }` and no thrown exception.
  5. Given the server answers 401 `unauthenticated`, when the client returns, then it reports the session as ended to the shell (used by EP-08-S15) as well as returning the error to the caller.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Every request is validated against the contract at the trust boundary (EP-03-S2). The actor comes from the session, never from a client field (EP-03-S3). Idempotency keys are deduplicated on the server (EP-03-S8). The client adds no rule of its own.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. The client changes no business record; each operation it calls writes its own entry on the server.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the API client module in `web`, built from the shared contract package (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the session token is never stored where scripts from other origins can read it (epic section 13). Concurrency: every action carries an idempotency key. Precision: weights pass through as integers in units of 0.0001 g; the client never converts them to floating point. D1 is decided (Option C): the client is built on the EP-03 contract and calls only the Node API on the shop's own domain; it never connects to the database or storage directly.
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S8, EP-04-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-08-S2: System can cache server reads and share them between screens

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can cache server reads and share them between screens
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a query cache keyed by operation and parameters, so each screen declares the reads it needs (for example "in-stock pieces", "parcel BATCH-2026-044", "Today cards") and screens that need the same read share one request and one result
- **So that:** moving between screens is fast, the same figure is never shown two ways, and the server is not asked for the same data twice at once (FR-08-1, BR-08-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given `today` and the rail both need the in-stock piece count, when both mount at once, then one request is sent and both show the same number, for example 42.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma opened `stock` 20 seconds ago and goes to `today` and back, when `stock` mounts again, then the cached list shows at once and a background refresh runs.
  3. Given a cache entry, when it is inspected in a test, then it holds the query key, data, fetched at, the entity versions seen, and a status of `loading`, `ready`, `failed` or `possibly stale` (epic section 9).
  4. Given a cached piece TAG-8841 at version 7, when a refetch returns version 6 because of a slow replica, then the cache keeps version 7.
  5. Given two reads for the same key with different parameters, such as parcel BATCH-2026-044 and parcel BATCH-2026-043, when they resolve, then each is stored under its own key and neither overwrites the other.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Every read is permission-checked by EP-05-S2, so the cache only ever holds what the server allowed this user to see. Entity versions come from the server's version column (EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story. Invalidation by events is EP-08-S8.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the client query cache in memory: query key, data, fetched at, versions seen, status.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Used by every route in `src/nav.ts`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: cached screens show data at once and refresh in the background (epic section 13). Personal data: the cache lives in memory only, never in local storage, so cached customer data does not survive the tab. Precision: cached weights stay integers in units of 0.0001 g.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S1, EP-02-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S3: User can see a loading state while a screen's data arrives

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see a loading state while a screen's data arrives
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a screen, card or list that is waiting for its first data to show a loading state in place of its content
- **So that:** I never read "nothing here" and decide wrongly while the data is still on its way (FR-08-2, BR-08-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma opens `staff-directory` on a connection slowed to 3 seconds per request, when the read has not returned, then a loading state shows and no "no staff" empty state appears (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given `today` loads its cards and its figures from separate reads, when the figures return first, then the figures show and each card still waiting shows its own loading state.
  3. Given the read returns an empty list, when it arrives, then the screen's existing empty state shows with its sentence, for example on `staff-directory`.
  4. Given a screen reader is running, when a loading state appears, then it is announced once as loading, and text in it is at least 14 px (15 px on the karigar phone `k-jobs`).
  5. Given cached data exists for the screen (EP-08-S2), when the screen mounts, then the cached data shows and no loading state replaces it during the background refresh.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** None beyond the read's own permission check (EP-05-S2). Loading is a display state only.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Display state only.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the cache status `loading` from EP-08-S2.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (loading state, epic section 12). Type scale and colours follow `docs/ux/mockups/01-foundations.svg` (body copy 14 / 400 as the smallest text).
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: a screen shows its first data in under 2 seconds on a shop connection (BR-08-6). Open question: after how long a loading state turns into a read error is not decided; tests use 15 seconds until it is.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S2

## EP-08-S4: User can see a read error with "Try again" when data cannot be loaded

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see a read error with "Try again" when data cannot be loaded
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** an area whose read failed to say what could not be loaded and offer "Try again", while the rest of the screen keeps working
- **So that:** a failed read is never mistaken for "nothing to show", and I can recover without reloading the app (FR-08-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the server is unreachable, when Sanjay Seth opens `security`, then the screen says the security log could not be loaded and shows "Try again" (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given the server is back, when Sanjay presses "Try again", then the log loads and the error goes away without a page reload (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given `decisions` loads its queues from several reads, when only one read fails, then only that card shows the error and "Try again", and the other cards stay usable.
  4. Given a read fails with `forbidden` from EP-05-S2, when the area shows its error, then it says the user may not see this, and "Try again" is not offered.
  5. Given a read is still unanswered after the loading time-out (EP-08-S3), when it times out, then it shows the same read error with "Try again".
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The read returns errors in the EP-03 format (EP-03-S5), with `forbidden` from the permission check (EP-05-S2). The client does not retry `forbidden` on its own.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A failed read changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the cache status `failed` from EP-08-S2.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (read-error state with "Try again", epic section 12). Shown first on route `security` (`src/components/settings/SecurityLog.tsx`).
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: a failed read never leaves an area silently empty. Accessibility: the error is announced to screen readers and "Try again" meets the UX-SPEC §6 touch target. Open question: the loading time-out before a read error is not decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-03-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S5: User can see the server's sentence when an action is refused

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see the server's sentence when an action is refused
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a refused action to show the server's sentence at the place I took the action, and keep what I typed
- **So that:** I know exactly why it did not happen and can fix it without filling the form again (FR-08-4, BR-08-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Deepak Rao has just billed TAG-8841, when Rajesh Verma submits a stock-out for TAG-8841, then the stock-out step shows "TAG-8841 is not in stock." where he pressed the button.
  2. Given Rajesh submits `lead-create` with no customer name, when the server refuses it, then the form shows "Add the customer name." and keeps the items he entered.
  3. Given a refusal arrives, when it is shown, then the submit button is enabled again and the screen does not navigate away.
  4. Given the server returns a refusal with no sentence, when it is shown, then the screen falls back to its existing text, for example "That did not save." in `ScalesRules.tsx`.
  5. Given a `version_conflict` error from EP-02-S14, when it is shown, then the sentence says someone else changed the record and the affected read is refetched.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The rule check and the `DomainError` sentence live on the server (EP-03-S4). The client shows the sentence as text and never decides the refusal itself. Version conflicts are detected on the server (EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused action changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Uses each screen's existing error line, for example `src/components/parcels/TagItem.tsx` ("Could not save the tag.") and `docs/ux/mockups/06-stock-out.svg`, route `stock-out`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the "already taken" and "not in stock" refusals for double-sell are shown as sentences (epic section 13). Accessibility: the sentence is announced to screen readers.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S1, EP-03-S4, EP-02-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S6: User can retry an action after a network failure without applying it twice

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can retry an action after a network failure without applying it twice
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** an action that fails on the network to say it may not have been saved and offer a retry that reuses the same idempotency key
- **So that:** I can safely try again without creating two leads or billing a piece twice (FR-08-5, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma submits `lead-create` and the response is lost after the server committed, when the screen shows the failure, then it says the lead may not have been saved and offers a retry.
  2. Given he retries, when the request reaches the server with the same idempotency key, then one lead exists and the screen shows the id returned by the first request (EP-03-S8).
  3. Given an action is in flight, when he presses submit again, then no second request is sent and the button shows it is working.
  4. Given he changes a field after the network failure, when he submits, then a new idempotency key is used, because it is a different request.
  5. Given a network failure on a non-create action such as a stock-out of TAG-8841, when he retries and the first attempt had committed, then the server's sentence "TAG-8841 is not in stock." or the first result is shown, and the piece is billed once.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Creates are deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Each operation runs in one transaction (EP-03-S6), so a lost response means either all or nothing was saved. State checks refuse a second stock-out of the same piece.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. The audit entry is written once by the operation on the server; the retry writes none.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. The client keeps the pending action's idempotency key in memory until it succeeds or the form changes.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (network-failure message). Shown first on route `lead-create` (`docs/ux/mockups/17-lead-create.svg`).
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: a retry is applied at most once (epic section 13). Availability: the user is never told "saved" before the server answers.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S1, EP-08-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S7: System can refetch the affected reads after the user's own action

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refetch the affected reads after the user's own action
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each action to declare the query keys it affects, and those reads to be refetched after the action succeeds, before the screen shows new values
- **So that:** the person who made the change sees the server's result, not a guess made in the browser (FR-08-6, BR-08-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma bills TAG-8841 on `stock-out`, when the action succeeds, then the in-stock pieces list, the stock totals and the Today figures are refetched, and TAG-8841 no longer appears on `stock`.
  2. Given the action succeeds, when the screen updates, then the values shown come from the refetch and none is computed in the browser from the request.
  3. Given an action that is refused, when the result arrives, then no read is invalidated.
  4. Given the same change also arrives as a live event to the same browser (EP-08-S8), when both happen within the coalescing window, then each affected read is fetched once.
  5. Given a refetch fails after the action succeeded, when the area updates, then it shows the read error with "Try again" (EP-08-S4) and the action is still reported as saved.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The server is the only source of the new state (BR-08-3). Reads are permission-checked (EP-05-S2).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story. The live path is EP-08-S8.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Refetching changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds an "affects" list of query keys to each action wrapper in the client.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the refetched values show within 2 seconds of the action on a shop connection. Precision: refetched weights are shown to four decimals from integers in units of 0.0001 g.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S1, EP-08-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S8: System can keep one live connection per signed-in client and map every catalogue event to reads

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can keep one live connection per signed-in client and map every catalogue event to reads
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the shell to open one EP-07 live connection after sign-in, and one event-to-query map, kept next to the catalogue, that names the query keys each event invalidates
- **So that:** every screen gets live updates the same way, and no event leaves a screen stale because nobody mapped it (FR-08-7, BR-08-5, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma signs in and opens three screens in turn, when the connection count is checked on the server, then his tab has exactly one live connection.
  2. Given the event-to-query map, when it is compared with the 10 events of PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1, then every event has at least one query key, and a unit test fails if an event is added to the shared list without a map entry.
  3. Given "Piece billed by one staff member" arrives for TAG-8841, when the map runs, then it invalidates the in-stock pieces, stock totals, Today cards, sale lists and suggestions reads (epic section 11).
  4. Given "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" arrives for BATCH-2026-044, when the map runs, then it invalidates the parcel, Decisions and Today reads, and only reads that are cached or on an open screen are refetched.
  5. Given 5 events invalidate the same query within 300 ms, when they arrive, then that query is refetched once (epic section 16 risk).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The connection is authenticated (EP-07-S3), channels are assigned by the server (EP-07-S4), and each event is filtered by the receiver's permissions (EP-07-S5). Events carry ids and versions only (EP-07-S2), so the client always refetches.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: all 10 catalogue events: "Piece billed by one staff member", "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Edit applied", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", "Parcel handed over by karigar", "Tag saved on a shared parcel", "Metal pool changed", "User deactivated or role changed". Proposed events from README gap G26 join the map when they are added to the catalogue.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Receiving events changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the event-to-query map in `web` and the live client state: connection status and last sequence number received.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: refetches are coalesced per query so the owner's screens do not storm the API. Security: the client subscribes only to entity channels for screens it has open, and the server checks each (EP-07-S4). Open decision D3: WebSocket or Server-Sent Events from the Node API decides how the hook connects; the map does not change.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S2, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S3, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S9: User can see a screen update by itself when someone else changes something

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see a screen update by itself when someone else changes something
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** my open screen to change within about a second when another person changes data it shows, without me reloading
- **So that:** I never offer a customer a piece that someone else has just sold (FR-08-8, BR-08-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given two browsers signed in as Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao, when Deepak changes data through a migrated screen, then Rajesh's open screen shows the change within about 1 second without a reload (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the owner Sanjay Seth adds a user on `staff-new`, when the add commits, then another owner browser on `staff-directory` shows the new row within about 1 second.
  3. Given Rajesh is filling a form on the screen being updated, when the refetch arrives, then the values he typed are kept and only the read-only parts change.
  4. Given an event for a record Rajesh may not read, when the server filters it (EP-07-S5), then his screen does not change.
  5. Given the refetch returns a version older than the one on screen, when it arrives, then the screen keeps the newer version.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Events go only to permitted receivers (EP-07-S5). The refetch is a permission-checked read (EP-05-S2). The server is authoritative (BR-08-3).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: any catalogue event mapped by EP-08-S8. The demo uses "User deactivated or role changed" for other users' lists and, once their epics wire them, "Piece billed by one staff member" and "Tag saved on a shared parcel".

- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: a change appears on other screens within about 1 second (BR-08-6). Concurrency: an update never overwrites what the user is typing. Time: times on refreshed cards are shown in Asia/Kolkata from server UTC.

- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S10: User can see "Reconnecting…" when the connection drops and catch up when it returns

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see "Reconnecting…" when the connection drops and catch up when it returns
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** every open screen to show "Reconnecting…" and mark its data as possibly out of date when the live connection or the network drops, and to catch up and clear the banner when it returns
- **So that:** a dropped connection never leaves me silently looking at old stock (FR-08-9, FR-08-10, epic section 13 Availability)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma's browser on `stock`, when its network is cut for 30 seconds, then "Reconnecting…" appears within 5 seconds and the list is marked as possibly out of date (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given 4 events were published to his channels during the cut, when the network returns, then the client resumes from its last sequence number, refetches the affected reads, the banner clears, and the screen shows every change made meanwhile (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given EP-07 answers the resume with "refetch everything" because the gap is too old, when it arrives, then every open read is refetched before the banner clears.
  4. Given the session expired during the cut, when the resume is refused as `unauthenticated`, then the shell returns to sign-in (EP-08-S15).
  5. Given "Reconnecting…" is showing, when a screen reader is running, then the change is announced once, and announced again when the connection is back.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Resume checks the session (EP-07-S3) and replays only permitted events in order (EP-07-S7). The "refetch everything" signal is decided by the server.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: any catalogue event replayed by EP-07-S7 after resume.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reconnecting changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the live client state: status `connected`, `reconnecting` or `offline`, and last sequence number received; sets cache status `possibly stale` while reconnecting.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed ("Reconnecting…" banner, epic section 12). Amber means "needs a person: waiting" in `docs/ux/mockups/01-foundations.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: the banner appears within a few seconds and clears after catch-up (epic section 13). Concurrency: replayed events are applied in sequence order. Open decision D3: how a drop is detected depends on the transport. Open question: how long cached data may be shown while reconnecting before the screen hides it; tests keep it shown with the possibly-out-of-date mark until decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S8, EP-07-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S11: User can see an offline state with server actions disabled

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see an offline state with server actions disabled
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** the web app to say it is offline when there is no network, and disable every action that needs the server with a reason
- **So that:** I do not press "Bill" or "Save tag" and believe it worked when nothing reached the server (FR-08-11)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma's browser reports no network, when he is on `stock-out`, then the shell shows the offline state and the submit button is disabled with the reason that the server cannot be reached.
  2. Given he is offline, when he reads the screen, then the data already shown stays visible and is marked as possibly out of date.
  3. Given he is offline, when he tries any staff or owner action, then nothing is queued to send later.
  4. Given the network returns, when the connection is back, then the actions are enabled again and the reconnect catch-up of EP-08-S10 runs.
  5. Given Lakshmi Devi on the karigar app `k-jobs`, when she is offline, then the same offline state shows, her step buttons are disabled with the reason, and nothing is queued (D6 decided: online only).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** None new. With no network nothing reaches the server; every action is still checked there once online.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Nothing is saved while offline.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses live client status `offline`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (offline state, epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: offline is always shown, never a silent failure. Accessibility: the disabled reason is readable at 14 px or more and announced. D6 is decided: online only, with no offline queue anywhere. The web app, staff and karigar alike, is read-only while disconnected, and actions are refused with a reason, not queued.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S15: User can be returned to sign-in when the session ends or is ended

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S15
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can be returned to sign-in when the session ends or is ended
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** the shell to clear every cached read and return me to sign-in when my session expires, or when "User deactivated or role changed" arrives for me
- **So that:** a deactivated person sees none of the shop's data, and a re-roled person starts again with the right screens (FR-08-14, BR-08-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma is signed in on `stock`, when Sanjay Seth deactivates him (EP-05-S7), then his browser returns to sign-in within about 1 second and shows none of the previous data (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given Deepak Rao's role changes from Staff to Karigar, when the event arrives for him, then his cache is cleared and he goes to sign-in; after signing in again he lands on `k-jobs`.
  3. Given an idle session expires (EP-04-S12), when Rajesh's next request returns `unauthenticated`, then the shell goes to sign-in and says the session ended.
  4. Given the cache is cleared, when the browser's memory is inspected in a test, then no customer, lead or piece data from the previous session remains, and the live connection is closed.
  5. Given "User deactivated or role changed" arrives for another user, when Sanjay is on `staff-directory`, then his list is refetched and he stays signed in.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Sessions are ended on the server (EP-04-S13, EP-05-S10) and connections closed (EP-07-S10). Any later request with the old session is refused as `unauthenticated`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "User deactivated or role changed".
- **Audit entry written:** No in this story. The deactivation or role change is audited by EP-05-S14.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Clears the client query cache, session context and live client state.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (session-ended state, epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: access on screen ends within about 1 second of deactivation. Personal data: cached customer data is removed from memory on session end. D4 is decided: the sign-in screen asks for phone number and password.
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S1, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S12, EP-04-S12, EP-04-S13, EP-05-S10, EP-07-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-08-S17: Developer can move a screen from `useStore()` onto the data layer by a documented pattern

- **Story ID:** EP-08-S17
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can move a screen from `useStore()` onto the data layer by a documented pattern

- **So that:** every feature epic from EP-11 to EP-44 wires its screens the same way and the patterns do not drift (BR-08-1, BR-08-2, epic section 16 risk)

  4. Given the pattern, when it describes weights, then it says weights arrive as integers in units of 0.0001 g and are shown to four decimals with the existing display helpers.

- **Audit entry written:** No. Documentation and lint only.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the pattern document in the repository and a lint rule that flags `useStore()` in screens.

- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the pattern forbids converting weights to floating point for storage or comparison (BR-08-10).
- **Depends on:** EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S6, EP-08-S7, EP-08-S9, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11, EP-01-S7

# EP-09: File storage · stories

Epic document: [EP-09 File storage](../epics/EP-09-file-storage.md)

Role note: stories about uploading or seeing a file use Staff, Owner or Karigar. "System" means the file service on the server (upload handling, resizing, signed links, access checks and retention) acting on its own. "Developer" means the person loading the dev seed. This epic has no screen of its own; the screens that show files belong to EP-19, EP-20, EP-21, EP-28 and EP-29, so UI references name the mockups those screens will use.

---

## EP-09-S1: System can store a file in object storage with a database record

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S1
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can store a file in object storage with a database record
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every stored file to be written to a private object storage bucket under a generated storage key, with one StoredFile row in the database that describes it
- **So that:** files live outside the database, can be found by id, and are never reachable by a guessable public URL (BR-09-6, BR-09-1, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a file is handed to the file service, when it is stored, then one object exists in the bucket and one StoredFile row exists with id, storage key, original name, content type, size in bytes, uploaded by, uploaded at and retention class filled in.
  2. Given the storage key, when it is inspected, then it is a random value that contains neither the original name nor the uploader, for example not `necklace-sharma.jpg`.
  3. Given the bucket, when anyone requests the object URL without a signed link, then the request is refused, because the bucket is private (no public bucket by default).
  4. Given the object write succeeds but the database insert fails, when the operation ends, then no StoredFile row exists and the orphan object is removed, so the two never disagree.
  5. Given two files with the same original name `IMG_0412.jpg` are stored, when both finish, then each has its own id and storage key and neither overwrites the other.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only the file service writes to the bucket; the bucket credentials come from environment variables (EP-01-S6) and are never sent to a browser. The uploader is taken from the session, not from a request field (EP-03-S3). The row insert runs in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. File storage emits no catalogue event (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Storing a file changes no business record; attaching it does (EP-09-S7, S8).
- **Data changes:** Adds the StoredFile table (id, storage key, original name, content type, size in bytes, width, height, thumbnail key, display key, uploaded by, uploaded at, retention class, shop ID) by migration (EP-02-S1). Creates the private bucket per environment.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: private bucket, random storage keys, credentials in environment only. Personal data: the bucket is placed in an India region (D10, decided). Availability: the bucket is covered by the backup plan in EP-38. D1 is decided (Option C): the bucket is in the cloud provider's S3-compatible object storage, on the same provider as the database, and only the Node API reaches it, over the provider's private network. Open decision D1a: which provider's storage holds the bucket. D7 is decided: StoredFile carries the shop ID, not a branch key.
- **Depends on:** EP-01-S6, EP-02-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-09-S2: Staff can upload an image and get a file id

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S2
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Staff can upload an image and get a file id
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to upload an image through the API and get back a file id I can then attach to a piece, order copy or lead
- **So that:** the photo I take at tagging or at the counter is kept on the server instead of picked from four bundled pictures (FR-09-1, BR-09-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma is signed in as Staff, when he uploads a 3 MB JPEG taken on the shop phone, then the server returns a file id and the StoredFile row shows him as uploaded by and the server time as uploaded at.
  2. Given Sanjay Seth is signed in as Owner, when he uploads a PNG, then he also gets a file id.
  3. Given no session, when anyone calls Create File, then the server answers `unauthenticated` and nothing is stored.
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi is signed in as Karigar, when she calls Create File without naming a job of her own as the target, then the server answers `forbidden` (bench photos are EP-09-S10).
  5. Given the network drops after the server stored the file and Rajesh retries with the same idempotency key, when the retry arrives, then the same file id is returned and only one StoredFile row exists.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create File is allowed for Staff and Owner (EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2); Karigar only through the bench-photo path. Size and type are checked before storing (EP-09-S3). Creates are deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). The response carries the created id (EP-03-S7).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. An unattached upload changes no business record; the attach step writes the audit entry.
- **Data changes:** Inserts StoredFile rows (EP-09-S1). Adds the Create File operation to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Used by "Add more angles" on `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag`, and "Attach a photo (optional)" on `docs/ux/mockups/17-lead-create.svg`, route `lead-create`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: permission checked on the server for every upload. Concurrency: a retried upload stores one file. Performance: a 3 MB photo uploads and returns an id within 5 seconds on a shop connection.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-09-S3: System can reject files that are too large or of a type not allowed

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S3
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can reject files that are too large or of a type not allowed
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to refuse any upload above the size limit or whose content, read from the file bytes, is not on the allowed type list, with a sentence that names the limit
- **So that:** storage does not fill with huge or unsafe files, and the person uploading knows what to change (FR-09-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a 50 MB file, when it is uploaded, then the server refuses it with a sentence naming the maximum size, and no object or StoredFile row is created (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given a `.exe` file renamed to `photo.jpg`, when it is uploaded, then the server reads the file bytes, finds it is not an allowed type, and refuses it with a sentence listing the allowed types (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  3. Given a JPEG, PNG or WebP image under the limit, when it is uploaded, then it is accepted.
  4. Given a PDF purchase order under the limit, when Staff uploads it as a PO attachment, then it is accepted or refused according to the decided type list, and the tests cover the decided case.
  5. Given an upload that is cut off before the declared size, when the server checks it, then it is refused as incomplete and nothing is stored.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Size is checked while the upload streams, so an oversize file is stopped before it is fully read. Type is decided from the file content, never from the file name or the client's declared type. The refusal uses the EP-03 error format (EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused upload stores nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the size limit and allowed type list as server configuration (EP-01-S6).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The refusal sentence shows on the uploading screen, for example `parcel-tag` (`docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: content-based type check stops renamed executables. Open question: the maximum size and the allowed types (images only, or PDF and other PO formats) are not decided; tests use a limit below 50 MB and the image types JPEG, PNG and WebP until they are.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-01-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-09-S4: System can make thumbnail and display-size copies of an image

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S4
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can make thumbnail and display-size copies of an image
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every stored image to get a thumbnail copy and a display-size copy, with their keys, width and height on the StoredFile row, and an original that stays usable if resizing fails
- **So that:** list screens load small images fast, the full image loads only on demand, and a bad resize never loses the photo (FR-09-3, FR-09-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma uploads a 4000 x 3000 JPEG, when processing finishes, then the StoredFile row has width 4000, height 3000, a thumbnail key and a display key, and both copies exist in the bucket (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given a portrait phone photo with an orientation tag, when the copies are made, then both copies are upright.
  3. Given an image the resizer cannot read, when processing fails, then the original stays stored and served, the row is flagged as not resized, and the failure is logged without the image content.
  4. Given a PDF PO attachment, when it is stored, then no image copies are made and the original is served as is.
  5. Given the copies are made, when they are inspected, then location and camera metadata from the original are removed from the thumbnail and display copies.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Resizing runs on the server only; the client never supplies its own thumbnail. The flag and keys are set by the file service, not by a request field.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Making copies changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** Fills width, height, thumbnail key and display key on StoredFile; adds a "resize failed" flag column by migration (EP-02-S1). Thumbnail and display objects are added to the bucket.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Thumbnails are used by the photo grid on `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg` (route `parcel-tag`) and "Photo at tagging" on `docs/ux/mockups/07-qc-check.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: thumbnails let list screens load in under 2 seconds on a shop connection; full images load on demand (epic section 13). Personal data: location metadata is removed from served copies. Open question: the exact thumbnail and display pixel sizes are not set in the sources; tests check that both copies are smaller than the original.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-09-S2, EP-02-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-09-S5: System can serve a file through a signed, expiring link

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S5
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can serve a file through a signed, expiring link
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Read File link to return a signed link for one file and one size (thumbnail, display or original) that stops working after a set time
- **So that:** a link copied out of the app or left in browser history cannot be used later to open a customer's PO or a piece photo (FR-09-5, BR-09-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma may read piece TAG-9108, when he asks for the display link of its first photo, then he gets a signed link that loads the image.
  2. Given a signed link issued an hour ago, when it is used after its expiry, then the file is refused (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given a signed link, when one character of its signature is changed, then the file is refused.
  4. Given a signed link for the thumbnail, when its path is edited to point at the original, then the file is refused.
  5. Given a list screen shows 20 piece photos, when it asks for links, then it gets 20 thumbnail links in one call and no original is fetched.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** A link is issued only after the access check of EP-09-S6 passes. The expiry time is set by the server. Links are signed with a server secret from environment variables (EP-01-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading a file changes nothing; link requests are logged for security review without the link itself.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the Read File link operation to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Used wherever a photo shows, for example the piece drawer on route `stock` and `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: signed, expiring links only; never public URLs (epic section 13). Performance: links for a page of thumbnails are issued in one request. Open question: the link lifetime is not stated in the sources; tests use 15 minutes until decided. D1 is decided (Option C): the link points at the Node API on the shop's own domain and is signed by the API, which checks it and streams the file from storage; the browser never talks to storage directly.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-09-S4, EP-09-S6, EP-01-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-09-S6: System can check a file request against the owning entity and the caller's role

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S6
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can check a file request against the owning entity and the caller's role
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every link request to find what the file is attached to (piece, order copy, job or lead) and allow it only if the caller's role may read that entity
- **So that:** file access follows the same rules as the records, and nobody sees a customer's PO image they could not see on the lead (FR-09-6, FR-09-7, BR-09-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a PO image attached to a lead, when Rajesh Verma (Staff) asks for its link, then it is issued, because Staff may read leads.
  2. Given the same PO image, when Lakshmi Devi (Karigar) asks for its link, then the server answers not-found, the same answer as for a file id that does not exist (FR-09-7).
  3. Given a file that is stored but not attached to anything, when anyone other than its uploader asks for its link, then the server answers not-found.
  4. Given a file attached to both a lead and an order copy, when a caller may read one of them, then the link is issued.
  5. Given a deactivated user's old session, when it asks for a link, then the server answers `unauthenticated` (EP-04-S13).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The check uses the EP-05 permission list (EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2) and the karigar own-jobs read scope (EP-05-S3). Refusals to karigars are not-found so a karigar cannot learn that a file exists. The check runs on every link request, not once per session.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused read changes nothing; refusals are counted in logs for EP-39.
- **Data changes:** Adds the Attachment table (file id, owner entity type, owner entity id, role, position, attached by, attached at) by migration (EP-02-S1), which the check reads.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: access is checked against the owning entity and role on every link request (epic section 13). Personal data: karigars never reach PO files (BR-09-2, BR-09-3). Performance: the check adds one indexed lookup on Attachment by file id.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3, EP-04-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-09-S7: Staff can attach photos to a piece

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Staff can attach photos to a piece
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to attach uploaded photos to a piece in a set order, and remove one I attached by mistake
- **So that:** each tagged piece carries its own photos instead of one of four bundled pictures (FR-09-4, BR-09-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**

- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: attach and detach are recorded with the piece's audit entry (epic section 13). Concurrency: two staff attaching to the same piece get distinct positions.

## EP-09-S12: System can apply the retention rule to stored files

- **Story ID:** EP-09-S12
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can apply the retention rule to stored files
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an internal Run Retention operation that finds files past the keep period of their retention class and removes the original, thumbnail and display copies together, or keeps them where the rule says so
- **So that:** personal data in PO files is not kept longer than decided, and storage does not grow without limit (FR-09-11, BR-09-3, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a PO file whose retention class keep period has passed, when Run Retention runs, then its original, thumbnail and display objects are removed from the bucket and its StoredFile and Attachment rows are removed or marked removed as decided.
  2. Given a piece photo whose class says keep, when Run Retention runs, then it is untouched.
  3. Given a file removed by retention, when anyone asks for its link, then the server answers not-found.
  4. Given removal of one of the three objects fails, when the run ends, then the file is retried on the next run and is not reported as removed.
  5. Given a run, when it ends, then the number of files removed per retention class is written to the run log.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Run Retention is callable only by the scheduler's system actor; no user session may call it. Keep periods come from server configuration per retention class.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (system, retention run), time, entity (owning piece, order copy, job or lead), action (file removed by retention), before file id.
- **Data changes:** Deletes or marks StoredFile and Attachment rows; deletes bucket objects. Adds retention class configuration.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: PO files are kept only as long as the rule says (epic section 13). Audit: removals by the system are recorded (EP-06-S6). Open question: how long piece photos, reference images and PO attachments are kept is not decided; tests use a short test period per class. The schedule that triggers the run is provided by EP-10 (higher-numbered), so this story delivers the callable operation and a manual trigger for tests. Deletion requests under DPDP are EP-39.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-09-S4, EP-09-S6, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-10: Background jobs · stories

Epic document: [EP-10 Background jobs](../epics/EP-10-background-jobs.md)

Role note: this is a layer A platform epic. Most stories use "System" for the scheduler and its job handlers acting on their own, with no person pressing a button. "Developer" means the person registering jobs in code. Only EP-10-S13 has an end user (Owner). The scheduler's Schedule, Cancel and Run operations are internal and cannot be called from a browser session; only List job runs and Retry job run are exposed, and only to the roles decided in EP-10-S13.

---

## EP-10-S1: System can register and run scheduled and delayed jobs on the server clock

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S1
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can register and run scheduled and delayed jobs on the server clock
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a scheduler that holds JobDefinition records (name, schedule, handler, max attempts) and runs each job at a set time, after a delay, or on a repeat, using the server clock
- **So that:** SLA breaches, overdue jobs, token expiry and 9 am wishes happen without anyone opening a screen (FR-10-1, BR-10-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a job registered with a 5-minute delay, when 5 minutes pass on the server clock, then its handler runs once, within one minute of the due time.
  2. Given a job registered on a repeat of every minute, when 10 minutes pass, then it has run 10 times, each run starting within one minute of its due time.
  3. Given a job registered for a set UTC time, when that time arrives, then it runs, whatever the time zone of the server machine or of any browser.
  4. Given a browser session of any role (Owner, Staff or Karigar), when it calls Schedule, Cancel or Run, then the server refuses it, because these operations are internal.
  5. Given a pending delayed job, when Cancel is called for it by a service function, then it does not run and no JobRun row is created for it.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Schedule, Cancel and Run are callable only from server-side service functions and the scheduler itself, never from a user session (EP-05-S2). Due times are taken from the server clock (EP-03-S3), never from a request field. JobDefinition names are unique.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The scheduler itself emits no catalogue event; the job handlers in EP-10-S5 and EP-10-S7 do.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Registering or running a job changes no business record; changes made by a handler are audited in EP-10-S12.
- **Data changes:** Adds the JobDefinition table (name, schedule as cron-like or delay, handler, max attempts) and a pending-job store (job name, due at UTC, payload, idempotency key) by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: due times stored in UTC. Performance: a due job starts within one minute of its due time (epic section 13). Security: internal operations unreachable from browser sessions. D1 is decided (Option C): the scheduler is a worker process of the Node API, and its pending jobs live in the managed PostgreSQL database.
- **Depends on:** EP-01-S6, EP-02-S1, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-10-S2: System can record a run history for each job

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S2
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can record a run history for each job
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one JobRun row per run, with job name, idempotency key, scheduled at, started at, finished at, attempts, result (ok, retrying, failed) and error text
- **So that:** anyone investigating a missed alert can see when a job ran, how often it was tried and why it failed (FR-10-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the SLA breach job runs and succeeds, when it finishes, then its JobRun row has started at, finished at, attempts 1 and result ok.
  2. Given a run that throws an error, when it ends, then its JobRun row has result retrying or failed and the error text, with no customer phone numbers, passwords, links or token values in that text.
  3. Given a run in progress, when the row is read, then started at is filled and finished at is empty.
  4. Given a run retried twice, when the row is read, then attempts is 3 and scheduled at still shows the original due time.
  5. Given JobRun rows older than the kept period, when the history is read, then the newest runs come first and old rows can be paged with a cursor.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only the scheduler writes JobRun rows. Error text is cut to a fixed length and passed through the same redaction used for logs before it is stored. Times come from the server clock (EP-03-S3).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A JobRun row is operational history, not a business change; business changes are audited in EP-10-S12.
- **Data changes:** Adds the JobRun table (id, job name, idempotency key, scheduled at, started at, finished at, attempts, result, error text) with an index on job name and started at, by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Read by the run list in EP-10-S13.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: all JobRun times stored in UTC. Personal data: no phone numbers, codes or tokens in error text. Performance: the index lets the newest 50 runs of a job be read in under 200 ms.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-02-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-10-S3: System can retry a failed job with backoff and mark it failed after the last attempt

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S3
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can retry a failed job with backoff and mark it failed after the last attempt
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a failed run to be tried again with a longer wait each time, up to the job's max attempts, and then marked failed with its error
- **So that:** a short outage of the database or WhatsApp provider does not lose an alert, and a job that keeps failing stops and is visible (FR-10-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a job with max attempts 3 that fails on attempt 1, when it is retried, then attempt 2 starts after a longer delay than the first retry interval and the JobRun result is retrying.
  2. Given the same job fails on attempt 3, when retries are exhausted, then the JobRun result is failed, attempts is 3 and the last error text is stored (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  3. Given a job that fails on attempt 1 and succeeds on attempt 2, when it finishes, then the JobRun result is ok and attempts is 2.
  4. Given a run marked failed, when the scheduler next ticks, then it does not retry it again by itself.
  5. Given a run marked failed, when it is recorded, then the failure is handed to the alerting hook that EP-37 fills in.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Retry delays grow with each attempt and are capped. Max attempts comes from the JobDefinition. A retry re-uses the same idempotency key, so EP-10-S4 still stops a double effect. Each attempt runs in its own transaction (EP-03-S6), so a failed attempt leaves no partial change.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A failed attempt changes no business record because its transaction is rolled back.
- **Data changes:** Updates JobRun attempts, result and error text. Adds the next-attempt-at column on the pending-job store by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: a short outage of a dependency is ridden out by retries. Concurrency: a retry and a late original run cannot both apply, because they share one idempotency key. Open question: the exact backoff intervals are not set in the sources; tests use max attempts 3 and check that each wait is longer than the last.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S2, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-10-S4: System can act once per idempotency key

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S4
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can act once per idempotency key
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each trigger to carry an idempotency key, such as the lead id plus "sla-breach", that is claimed inside the handler's transaction, so a second run with the same key does nothing
- **So that:** the owner gets one breach alert per lead and a karigar one reminder per day, even with two scheduler workers or a retry (FR-10-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given two scheduler workers pick up the SLA breach run for one lead at the same moment, when both finish, then the lead is marked late once and one "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" event is published.
  2. Given a run that committed its change but crashed before writing finished at, when it is retried with the same key, then it finds the key already claimed and makes no second change.
  3. Given the overdue job for MO-2026-118 runs twice on 2 November 2026, when both finish, then one reminder exists for that job for that day.
  4. Given the key for one lead is claimed, when the breach job runs for a different lead, then it is not blocked.
  5. Given a run whose transaction rolls back, when it is retried, then the key is not left claimed and the retry can act.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The key is claimed by a unique constraint in the same transaction as the handler's change (EP-03-S6), not in a separate step. Keys are built by the handler from the entity id and the trigger name (and the Asia/Kolkata date for daily triggers), never from a request field.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. It stops duplicate "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" events published after commit (EP-07-S1).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Claiming a key changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** Adds a JobKey table (idempotency key unique, job name, claimed at) by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: one effect per key with several workers, checked inside the transaction (epic section 16 risk). Time: daily keys use the Asia/Kolkata date from EP-10-S10.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-07-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S5: System can mark a lead late when its SLA passes and emit the passed-SLA event

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S5
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can mark a lead late when its SLA passes and emit the passed-SLA event
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a delayed job, scheduled when a lead arrives, that checks the lead at `arrivedAt` plus `settings.leadSlaHours` and, if it is still `needs_glance` or `opened`, sets SLA breached at and emits the passed-SLA event
- **So that:** "8 h limit passed · owner told" on `leads` is true, because the owner is actually told (FR-10-5, FR-10-7, BR-10-2, BR-10-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a lead that arrived at 09:00 and is still `needs_glance`, when 8 hours pass, then SLA breached at is set to 17:00 (the time the limit passed), the breach notified flag is set once, and "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" is emitted once (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given a lead in `opened` when the limit passes, when the job runs, then it is marked late in the same way.
  3. Given `settings.leadSlaHours` is changed from 8 to 6 while a lead that arrived 7 hours ago is still `needs_glance`, when the change is saved, then the lead's due time is recalculated and it is marked late within one minute.
  4. Given the job runs at 17:00 for that lead, when the breach is recorded, then the event is published within one minute of 17:00 and staff on `leads` and the owner on `decisions` see "2 leads nobody has opened for over 8 hours" counts update.
  5. Given the due time is worked out, when the code is read, then it comes from one shared function that a shop-hours calendar (EP-13) can replace without changing the job.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The job reads the lead's current state inside its transaction and acts only if it is `needs_glance` or `opened` (`slaRunning`). The breach is claimed with the key lead id plus "sla-breach" (EP-10-S4). SLA breached at is the due time, not the run time. Who is told and on which channel is left to EP-11.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" (the passed-SLA half, on behalf of EP-28). consumed: None.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (System, SLA breach job), time, entity (lead), action (lead marked late), before (SLA breached at empty), after (SLA breached at).
- **Data changes:** Adds SLA breached at (UTC) and breach notified flag to Lead by migration (EP-02-S7 table). Pending-job rows for each lead's SLA timer.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Shown on `docs/ux/mockups/16-lead-inbox.svg`, route `leads` ("8 h limit passed · owner told"), and `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("RUNNING LATE · 2 · THE CLOCK TOLD ME, NOT A PERSON").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: due time stored in UTC. Performance: breach detected within one minute of the limit (epic section 13). Concurrency: one breach per lead with several workers. Open decision A2: whether the 8 hours count shop hours ("shop hours, not clock hours" on mockup 13) or clock hours; tests use clock hours through the replaceable due-time function until decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-02-S7, EP-02-S12, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
