## EP-10-S6: System can cancel a lead's SLA timer when staff start working it

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S6
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can cancel a lead's SLA timer when staff start working it
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the lead's pending SLA job to be cancelled in the same transaction that moves the lead out of `needs_glance` or `opened`
- **So that:** a lead that staff picked up in time is never shown or reported as late (FR-10-6, BR-10-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a lead that arrived at 09:00, opened by Rajesh Verma at 12:00 and moved to `being_worked`, when 17:00 passes, then no SLA breached at is recorded and no passed-SLA event is emitted (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given the cancel happens at 16:59:59 and the breach job is already picked up at 17:00, when the job reads the lead, then it finds `being_worked` and makes no change, because it re-checks the state inside its transaction.
  3. Given a lead moved from `needs_glance` to `opened`, when the move commits, then the timer is not cancelled, because `opened` still runs the clock.
  4. Given the lead transition fails and rolls back, when the transaction ends, then the SLA timer is still pending.
  5. Given a lead already marked late, when it is moved to `being_worked`, then SLA breached at stays as recorded.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The cancel is called by the lead transition service function (EP-28) inside its own transaction (EP-03-S6). The breach job re-checks `slaRunning` before acting, so a lost cancel still cannot cause a false breach.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. The lead state change itself is EP-28's.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Cancelling a timer changes no business record; the lead transition is audited by EP-28 (EP-06-S7).
- **Data changes:** Deletes or marks cancelled the lead's pending-job row.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Affects the "within time · 6 h left" and "being worked" rows on `docs/ux/mockups/16-lead-inbox.svg`, route `leads`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: a cancel racing a due breach never produces a breach for a worked lead.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S5, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S7: System can mark a karigar job overdue past its agreed date

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can mark a karigar job overdue past its agreed date
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a daily job that finds karigar jobs not `handed_over` whose agreed date (`confirmedDate ?? dueDate`) is before today in Asia/Kolkata, sets overdue since, and hands one reminder per job per day to EP-11
- **So that:** "2 karigar jobs past their agreed date · both reminded automatically" is true without staff chasing each karigar (FR-10-8, BR-10-5, BR-10-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given job MO-2026-118 with agreed date 1 November 2026 and status `on_bench`, when the overdue job runs on 2 November 2026, then overdue since is set, last reminder at is set, and one reminder is handed to EP-11 for that day (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given a job with `confirmedDate` 5 November and `dueDate` 1 November, when the job runs on 2 November, then it is not overdue, because the confirmed date wins.
  3. Given a job past its agreed date but `handed_over`, when the job runs, then it is not marked overdue.
  4. Given Mahesh Soni's job is 3 days over, when the job runs again on the same day, then no second reminder is handed over for that day.
  5. Given a job becomes overdue, when the change commits, then "Job passed its agreed date" is published so `decisions` and `k-jobs` update.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The key is job id plus "overdue" plus the Asia/Kolkata date (EP-10-S4). Overdue days are counted in whole Asia/Kolkata days (`jobOverdueDays`, EP-10-S10). Overdue since is set once and not moved by later runs. The reminder audience and channel are EP-11's.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Job passed its agreed date" (proposed in README gap G26, owner EP-19, emitted through EP-10). consumed: None.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (System, overdue job), time, entity (karigar job MO-2026-118), action (job marked overdue or reminder sent), before and after overdue since and last reminder at.
- **Data changes:** Adds overdue since (UTC) and last reminder at to KarigarJob by migration (EP-02-S8 table).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Shown on `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("Mahesh Soni 3 days over · Lakshmi Devi 1 day over · both reminded automatically"), and on `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: day boundary computed in Asia/Kolkata. Concurrency: one reminder per job per day. Open question: whether a karigar is reminded once or every day while overdue; tests cover one per day, the shape FR-10-8 states, until decided. Open question G26: "Job passed its agreed date" is proposed, not yet in the catalogue.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-10-S10, EP-02-S8, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S8: System can expire edit tokens after 10 minutes

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S8
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can expire edit tokens after 10 minutes
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a sweep that runs every minute and sets expired at on every PieceEdit token (the owner edit code) issued more than 10 minutes ago and not yet used
- **So that:** a code entered after 10 minutes is refused even if the check at use were wrong, and the owner's pending list does not show dead tokens (FR-10-9, BR-10-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an edit token issued 11 minutes ago and not used, when the sweep runs, then its expired at is set (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given edit tokens for ED-101 and ED-102 issued 11 and 12 minutes ago, when the sweep runs, then both get expired at, and entering either on `edit-apply` is refused. There is no sign-in OTP to sweep (D4); activation and reset links are refused at use by EP-04 once expired.
  3. Given a token issued 9 minutes ago, when the sweep runs, then it is untouched.
  4. Given a token already used, when the sweep runs, then it is not changed.
  5. Given the sweep has not run yet for a token issued 10 minutes and 30 seconds ago, when the code is entered, then the check at use still refuses it.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The 10-minute limit is `TOKEN_TTL_MS` from the shared package (EP-01-S3, EP-01-S4). The sweep sets expired at only; it never deletes rows. The check at use stays in EP-25 and does not rely on the sweep.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, for edit tokens: actor (System, token sweep), time, entity (piece edit), action (token expired), token reference (never the token value, EP-06-S4). Sign-in uses no code (D4), so nothing else is swept.
- **Data changes:** Adds expired at to PieceEdit (EP-02-S5 table) by migration.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Affects `docs/ux/mockups/05-edit-propose-apply.svg`, route `edit-apply`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: tokens expire after 10 minutes and are single use (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Audit: token reference only, never the value. Performance: the sweep finishes in under 5 seconds with an index on issued at.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S12, EP-02-S5, EP-06-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S9: System can start the 9 am wishes run when auto-send is on

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S9
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can start the 9 am wishes run when auto-send is on
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a daily job at 9 am Asia/Kolkata that reads `settings.autoSendWishes` and, when it is on, hands that day's birthday and anniversary queue to EP-33 once
- **So that:** "Send wishes automatically at 9 am" on `wishes` works without anyone pressing a button (FR-10-10, FR-10-11, BR-10-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given `autoSendWishes` is on, when it is 09:00 Asia/Kolkata on 1 November 2026 (03:30 UTC), then the day's queue, including Priya Malhotra's birthday, is handed to EP-33 once (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given `autoSendWishes` is off, when 09:00 Asia/Kolkata passes, then the job records a run with result ok and hands nothing over.
  3. Given the job runs twice at 09:00 on the same day, when both finish, then the queue is handed over once, because the key is "wishes" plus the Asia/Kolkata date.
  4. Given the server machine's time zone is UTC, when the job is scheduled, then it still fires at 09:00 Asia/Kolkata, not 09:00 UTC.
  5. Given Ravi Shankar is not opted in to WhatsApp, when the queue is handed over, then this job does not decide who is sent; consent is applied by EP-33.

- **Non-functional checks:** Time: 9 am computed in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). Concurrency: one hand-over per day. Availability: a missed 9 am run is caught up the same day (EP-10-S11).

- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S10: System can compute day boundaries and 9 am in Asia/Kolkata

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S10
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can compute day boundaries and 9 am in Asia/Kolkata
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** shared functions that give the start of the day, the date and 09:00 in Asia/Kolkata for any UTC instant, used by the overdue and wishes jobs
- **So that:** "today", "1 day over" and "9 am" mean the shop's day, not the server's or a browser's (FR-10-12, BR-10-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the UTC instant 2026-11-01T18:45:00Z, when the Asia/Kolkata date is asked for, then it is 2 November 2026 (00:15 local).

  4. Given the server's TZ environment variable is set to UTC or to America/New_York, when the tests run, then every result above is the same.

## EP-10-S11: System can run missed jobs after downtime

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S11
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can run missed jobs after downtime
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the scheduler, on start, to run every delayed job whose due time passed while it was down, and to run each missed daily job for today only
- **So that:** an outage does not lose a lead breach or skip today's wishes, and old days are not replayed (epic section 13 availability, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the scheduler is down from 16:30 to 17:20 and a lead's SLA was due at 17:00, when it starts at 17:20, then the lead is marked late with SLA breached at 17:00, not 17:20.
  2. Given the scheduler is down from 08:50 to 09:40 Asia/Kolkata with `autoSendWishes` on, when it starts, then today's wishes run once.
  3. Given the scheduler was down for all of 1 and 2 November, when it starts on 3 November, then the wishes job runs for 3 November only and not for the two missed days.
  4. Given the overdue job missed today's run, when the scheduler starts, then it runs once for today.
  5. Given a lead was moved to `being_worked` during the downtime, when the missed breach job runs, then it makes no change.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Catch-up runs go through the same idempotency keys (EP-10-S4), so a job that did run before the outage is not repeated. Daily jobs catch up only for the current Asia/Kolkata date (EP-10-S10).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. Catch-up runs emit what their handlers emit (EP-10-S5, EP-10-S7).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Catch-up itself changes nothing; the handlers' changes are audited (EP-10-S12).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database beyond JobRun rows.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: missed jobs run on restart, with the recorded breach time being the time the limit passed (epic section 13). Concurrency: catch-up on two workers still acts once per key.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-10-S5, EP-10-S9, EP-10-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-10-S12: System can audit job-made changes with a System actor

- **Story ID:** EP-10-S12
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** System can audit job-made changes with a System actor
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every state change made by a job handler to write an audit entry whose actor is the System actor named after the job, in the same transaction as the change
- **So that:** the owner can tell in the security log that the clock, not a person, marked a lead late or expired a token (FR-10-13)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the SLA breach job marks a lead late, when Sanjay Seth reads the audit log, then the entry shows actor System (SLA breach job), the lead, action lead marked late, and before and after SLA breached at.
  2. Given the overdue job marks MO-2026-118 overdue, when the log is read, then the entry shows actor System (overdue job).
  3. Given the token sweep expires an edit token, when the log is read, then the entry shows a token reference and not the token value.
  4. Given a job's transaction rolls back, when the log is read, then no entry exists for that attempt.
  5. Given the audit log filter by actor, when Sanjay picks System, then only job-made and integration-made entries show.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Handlers write entries through the shared audit writer in the same transaction (EP-06-S2). The System actor comes from EP-06-S6 and cannot be set by a user session.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (System, job name), time, entity, action, before, after, token reference where a token is involved.
- **Data changes:** None beyond AuditEntry rows (EP-02-S11). Registers one System actor per job name.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show on the owner's audit log from EP-06-S9 to EP-06-S11.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every state change by a job is audited with a System actor (epic section 13). Security: entries cannot be updated or deleted (EP-06-S1).
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S4, EP-06-S6, EP-06-S10

- **As a:** Owner

- **So that:** I can check that late-lead alerts and 9 am wishes really ran, and restart one that failed (epic section 10 List and Retry)

Open question: whether the owner or only operations may see run history and retry; criteria assume Owner and the permission can be narrowed without changing the operation.

# EP-11: Notifications engine · stories

Epic document: [EP-11 Notifications engine](../epics/EP-11-notifications-engine.md)

Role note: this is a layer A platform epic. Stories where the service turns events into notifications, picks recipients, routes, escalates or retries on its own use "System". Stories about what a person receives or sees use Owner, Staff or Karigar. EP-11-S10 says "User" in its candidate title because every role has the list; its "As a" field names the role used in the examples. Create Notification and Update Delivery status are internal operations and cannot be called from a browser session.

---

## EP-11-S1: System can store a notification per recipient and channel with a dedupe key

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store a notification per recipient and channel with a dedupe key
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one Notification row per recipient per channel, with kind, group, source event name, entity type and id, template id, variables, channel, status, attempts and a dedupe key built from the source event, the recipient and the channel
- **So that:** every notice has one record whose delivery can be followed, and a redelivered event never produces a second notice (FR-11-1, FR-11-15, BR-11-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the event "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" for BATCH-2026-044 with sequence number 5120, when the service creates notices for Sanjay Seth on the app and whatsapp channels, then two Notification rows exist, each with status queued, attempts 0, group signature and entity type parcel.
  2. Given the same event with sequence number 5120 is delivered again, when it is processed, then no new row is created, because the dedupe key (event 5120, Sanjay Seth, app) and (event 5120, Sanjay Seth, whatsapp) already exist (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  3. Given two workers process event 5120 at the same moment, when both commit, then each recipient still has one row per channel, because the dedupe key is unique in the database.
  4. Given a row is created, when it is read back, then created at is a UTC time from the server clock and sent at and read at are empty.
  5. Given a browser session of any role, when it calls Create Notification, then the server refuses it, because the operation is internal.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Notification is callable only from the notification service, never from a user session (EP-05-S2). The dedupe key is unique and is claimed in the same transaction that creates the row (EP-03-S6). Channel is one of app, whatsapp, email. Status is one of queued, sent, delivered, read, failed. Group is one of signature, stopped, late, info. Times come from the server clock (EP-03-S3).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. Event consumption per kind is in EP-11-S3 to EP-11-S8.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Notification records are operational; delivery status is kept on the notification, not in the audit log (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Adds the Notification table (id, recipient user id, kind, group, source event name, entity type, entity id, template id, variables, channel, status, created at, sent at, read at, attempts, dedupe key unique) with an index on recipient user id and created at, by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the unique dedupe key per event, recipient and channel stops duplicates when events are redelivered (epic section 13). Time: all times stored in UTC. Security: internal create operation unreachable from browser sessions.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S3, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S2, EP-07-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-11-S2: System can render a notification from a template with variables

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can render a notification from a template with variables
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Template per notification kind, with text holding named variables (for example batch id, grams, karigar name), filled from the notification's variables, with the same content used for app, WhatsApp and email
- **So that:** the owner reads the same words wherever a notice reaches him, and wording is changed in one place (FR-11-11, BR-11-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the parcel-stopped template "{batchId} will not weigh up · {shortMg} mg short" and variables batchId BATCH-2026-044 and shortMg 138, when it is rendered, then the text is "BATCH-2026-044 will not weigh up · 138 mg short", as on mockup 13.
  2. Given variables holding weights stored as integers 4471620 and 4473000 units of 0.0001 g, when the template is rendered, then they show as "447.1620 g vs 447.3000 g expected", formatted by the shared gram conversion with 4 decimals.
  3. Given the same notification is sent on app and whatsapp, when both are rendered, then the message text is identical, and the WhatsApp copy carries the template's WhatsApp template reference for EP-12.
  4. Given a template names a variable that the notification does not supply, when it is rendered, then rendering fails, the notification is marked failed with the error "missing variable", and nothing is sent.
  5. Given any template, when it is checked in tests, then it contains no price or rupee variable.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Rendering happens on the server only. Weights are formatted for display from integer units of 0.0001 g by the shared function (EP-02-S2), never stored as text. Variables are escaped for the channel (HTML for email). No template may hold a money field. Templates are seeded by migration; who may edit them is an open question, so no edit operation is exposed in this story.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Rendering changes no record except the notification's own status on failure.
- **Data changes:** Adds the Template table (id, kind, text with variables, per-channel variant if needed, WhatsApp template reference) by migration, seeded with one template per kind used in EP-11-S4 to EP-11-S8.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Template wording follows `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`.

## EP-11-S3: System can pick recipients for each consumed event by role and setting

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can pick recipients for each consumed event by role and setting
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one recipient rule per consumed event kind that picks active users by role (EP-05) and reads `settings.lateLeadAudience`, then passes each recipient to channel routing
- **So that:** the right people hear about each moment, and a karigar never hears about another karigar's job, a customer, a lead or stock (FR-11-1, FR-11-16, BR-11-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the consumed events "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" and "Karigar job status changed", when the service starts, then each has a registered recipient rule, and an event kind with no rule is logged and ignored.
  2. Given "Karigar job status changed" for MO-2026-118 assigned to Vijay Kumar (KG-04), when recipients are picked, then Vijay Kumar is included and Lakshmi Devi and Mahesh Soni are not (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  3. Given "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" for the Sharma wedding enquiry, when recipients are picked, then no user with role Karigar is included.
  4. Given a staff user who was deactivated, when recipients are picked, then that user is not included.
  5. Given `lateLeadAudience` is changed from `staff_then_owner` to `owner_only`, when the next passed-SLA event is processed, then the new value is used, because the setting is read at the time the event is processed.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Recipients are chosen on the server from active users and their roles (EP-05-S1). Karigar recipients are limited to the karigar linked to the job in the event (EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13). Events are consumed only after their transaction commits (EP-07-S1). Settings are read, not written (EP-13 owns them).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", and the proposed "Job passed its agreed date" (README gap G26). emitted: None.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Picking recipients changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Reads users, roles, karigar links and `settings.lateLeadAudience` (EP-02-S12).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: recipients chosen on the server with EP-05 permissions; a karigar's notifications are filtered to their own jobs (epic section 13). Personal data: customer names in lead notices go only to Staff and Owner. Open decision A3: whether staff are warned before the owner; the rule reads `lateLeadAudience` either way.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S1, EP-02-S12, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S3, EP-05-S7, EP-05-S13, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-11-S4: Owner can get notified when a parcel is stopped

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can get notified when a parcel is stopped
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** a notice in the "your signature" group whenever a parcel is stopped on a mismatch or because someone raised a problem
- **So that:** I can clear or reject it quickly, because its pieces are frozen until I act, and a parcel that matches never reaches me (FR-11-2, BR-11-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given BATCH-2026-044 from Mahesh Soni is stopped on a mismatch (447.1620 g against 447.3000 g expected), when the event is consumed, then Sanjay Seth gets one notification in the signature group on each channel enabled in `notifyChannels`, reading "BATCH-2026-044 will not weigh up · 138 mg short" (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Rajesh Verma presses "Tell the owner" on "Stop the line" for BATCH-2026-044 with the note "Parcel is 138 mg under", when the event is consumed, then Sanjay gets a notification in the stopped group that includes the note and Rajesh's name.
  3. Given three parcels match exactly and are released by staff, when their events are processed, then Sanjay gets no signature or stopped notification for them.
  4. Given the in-app channel is on, when the parcel is stopped, then the notification appears in Sanjay's list within about 1 second of the event.
  5. Given a Staff or Karigar user, when the parcel is stopped on a mismatch, then they get no notification from this rule.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only the "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" event triggers this notice; the stop itself and the frozen state are owned by EP-23 and EP-24. Recipient is every active Owner (EP-11-S3). Channels follow EP-11-S9. One notice per event per recipient per channel (EP-11-S1).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)". emitted: none of the catalogue; the new in-app notification is pushed on the owner's user channel (EP-07-S4).
- **Audit entry written:** No. The stop is audited by the epic that stops the parcel; the notification is not audited (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Notification rows only. Seeds the parcel-stopped and line-stopped templates.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` (block "NOTHING MOVES UNTIL YOU ANSWER", card "BATCH-2026-044 will not weigh up · 138 mg short"; staff panel "Stop the line"). The in-app list itself is not yet designed (G21).
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: in-app notice within about 1 second of the event. Precision: grams shown to 4 decimals from integer units. Concurrency: redelivered stop event gives one notice per channel.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S1, EP-11-S2, EP-11-S3, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-11-S7: System can escalate a late-lead notice to the owner after a wait

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can escalate a late-lead notice to the owner after a wait
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an EscalationTimer per late lead that, after the escalation wait, checks the lead's state and notifies the owner only if nobody has acted
- **So that:** a lead staff ignore still reaches the owner, and a lead staff picked up does not bother him (FR-11-5, BR-11-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Staff were notified at 17:00 that the bulk chain order from Erode is late and the escalation wait is W, when 17:00 plus W passes and the lead is still `needs_glance` or `opened`, then Sanjay Seth gets one late-group notification and the timer's escalated flag is set (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh Verma moves the lead to `being_worked` before the wait ends, when the timer fires, then the owner is not notified, because the lead state is checked at the moment it fires.
  3. Given two scheduler workers fire the same timer, when both finish, then Sanjay has one escalation notice per channel.
  4. Given the scheduler was down when the timer was due, when it restarts, then the timer fires once on catch-up with the same state check.
  5. Given `lateLeadAudience` is `owner_only`, when a lead passes its SLA, then no escalation timer is created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The timer runs as a delayed job (EP-10-S1) with the idempotency key lead id plus "escalate" (EP-10-S4). The state check runs inside the job's transaction. Escalate at is stored in UTC. The wait length is a setting value read at scheduling time until decided.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: none directly; the timer is created from the "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" notice in EP-11-S6. emitted: none of the catalogue; the owner's in-app notice is pushed on his user channel (EP-07-S4).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Escalation creates a notification only and changes no business record (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Adds the EscalationTimer table (notification group id, lead id, escalate at UTC, escalated flag) by migration (EP-02-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The result shows on `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("2 leads nobody has opened for over 8 hours · Sharma wedding enquiry (11 h) · bulk chain order from Erode (9 h)").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: escalation wait measured on the server clock, stored in UTC, with any quiet hours computed in Asia/Kolkata. Concurrency: one escalation per lead. Availability: missed timers fire on restart (EP-10-S11). Open question: the length of the escalation wait is not decided; tests use a configured value.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S6, EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-10-S6, EP-10-S11, EP-02-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Karigar can get notified about changes and reminders on their own jobs
- **As a:** Karigar
- **I want:** a notice when the status of one of my jobs changes from the desk side, and a reminder when my job passes its agreed date
- **So that:** I know what the desk expects without phoning, and nobody has to chase me by hand (FR-11-6, FR-11-16, BR-11-7, BR-11-8)

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S9

- **Title:** System can route owner notifications to the channels he enabled
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each owner recipient to get one Notification row per channel switched on in `settings.notifyChannels` (whatsapp, app, email), read when the event is processed

## EP-11-S10: User can see an in-app notification list and mark items read

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** User can see an in-app notification list and mark items read
- **As a:** Staff (also Owner and Karigar, each seeing only their own)
- **I want:** a list of my in-app notifications, newest first, with an unread count, that updates live and lets me mark an item read
- **So that:** I do not miss a stoppage, decision or late item, from any screen (FR-11-8, FR-11-9, BR-11-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma has 3 unread app notifications, when he calls List My notifications, then he gets only his own rows, newest first, 50 per page with a cursor, and an unread count of 3.
  2. Given a new late-lead notice is created for Rajesh, when it commits, then it appears in his open list and the unread count goes to 4 within about 1 second, without a refresh.
  3. Given Rajesh marks one item read, when the update commits, then its status is read, read at is set, and the unread count is 3 on every device where he is signed in.
  4. Given Rajesh calls Update My notification on a notification of Sanjay Seth's, when the server checks it, then it answers `not_found` and nothing changes.
  5. Given the list cannot be loaded, when the screen shows, then it shows the loading state and then the read error with "Try again" from the data layer.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List and Update are limited to the caller's own notifications, by recipient user id from the session (EP-03-S3). Only the recipient may mark read. Read is one-way: a read item cannot go back to unread. Pages use a cursor (EP-03-S9).

- **Audit entry written:** No. Marking a notice read is not a business change (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Updates Notification status and read at. Adds List My notifications and Update My notification to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. No route id for the notification centre exists in `src/nav.ts` (G21); `docs/ux/mockups/10-navigation-map.mmd` shows node NOTIF ("Notification centre · stoppages, decisions, late things") for owner, staff and karigar.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: new in-app notice visible within about 1 second (epic section 13). Security: own notifications only. Open question G21: who owns the notification centre screen and its route id; the operations are built here and the screen is placed once G21 is decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S1, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S9, EP-07-S4, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-11-S12: System can send notifications by email

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can send notifications by email
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an email sender that takes each queued email Notification, renders it from its template, sends it to the recipient's email address and records sent or failed with the time, and that also sends the EP-04 account emails (activation link and password-reset link) to the address on the user record, whatever `notifyChannels` says
- **So that:** the owner can choose email on the rules panel and actually receive mail, and every new user can activate their account and every user can reset a forgotten password in production (FR-11-13, FR-11-17, BR-11-11)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth has email switched on and an email address on his user record, when a queued email notification for BATCH-2026-044 is picked up, then one email is sent with the rendered subject and body, the row's status is sent and sent at is set.
  2. Given the mail provider rejects the message, when the attempt ends, then attempts is 1, status stays queued for retry, and the error is kept without the recipient's address in logs.
  3. Given a recipient with no email address, when an email row would be created, then no row is created and an app row still exists.
  4. Given the mail credentials, when the code and repository are checked, then they come from environment variables only and appear in no file or log.
  5. Given the same email row is picked up by two workers, when both run, then one email is sent.
  6. Given `notifyChannels.email` is off and EP-04 issues an activation link for Deepak Rao, when the account email is queued, then it is still sent to his email address with the subject "Set your JGD password", and the stored row holds no link.
  7. Given production, when EP-04 sends an activation or reset email, then this sender is used and the EP-04-S4 stub is not.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Sends run as background jobs (EP-10-S1) keyed by notification id (EP-10-S4). Credentials come from environment variables (EP-01-S6). The email body uses the same template text as other channels (EP-11-S2), HTML-escaped.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Delivery status is recorded on the notification (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Updates Notification status, sent at and attempts. Reads the user's email address, which is required on every user (EP-02-S3, D4). Registers this sender as the production implementation of the EP-04-S4 account-email interface.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: mail credentials in environment variables only. Personal data: no email addresses in logs or job error text. Concurrency: one send per row. Security: activation and reset links are rendered at send time and never stored in the row, logs or error text. Open decision D4a: the email provider is not chosen; the sender sits behind one interface.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S1, EP-11-S2, EP-11-S9, EP-01-S6, EP-02-S3, EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-04-S4

## EP-11-S13: System can hand WhatsApp notifications to the WhatsApp integration and record status

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can hand WhatsApp notifications to the WhatsApp integration and record status
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** queued whatsapp Notification rows handed to a WhatsApp send interface with the recipient's phone, template reference and variables, and Update Delivery status called from its receipts
- **So that:** the owner gets WhatsApp notices and anyone can see whether a message was sent, delivered, read or failed (FR-11-12, BR-11-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a queued whatsapp row for Sanjay Seth about BATCH-2026-044, when it is picked up, then it is passed once to the WhatsApp send interface with his phone, the template's WhatsApp reference and the variables, and the row's status becomes sent with sent at set.
  2. Given a receipt "delivered" and then "read" for that message, when Update Delivery status is called for each, then the row shows delivered and then read, with read at set.
  3. Given receipts arrive out of order (read before delivered), when both are applied, then the row ends as read and does not move back to delivered.
  4. Given the kind has no approved WhatsApp template, when routing creates the rows, then no whatsapp row is created and the app row still exists.
  5. Given the owner calls Read Notification delivery status for that notice, when it returns, then he sees each channel's status; a Staff or Karigar caller gets `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Update Delivery status is internal and callable only by the WhatsApp integration's receipt handler and the email sender. Status only moves forward: queued, sent, delivered, read; failed is final. Until EP-12 is built, the send interface is a stub that records the call, as EP-04-S4 does for account emails. Read Notification delivery status is Owner only.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Delivery status is recorded on the notification, not in the audit log (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Updates Notification status, sent at, read at, attempts. Adds a provider message id column to Notification by migration. Adds Read Notification delivery status and the internal Update Delivery status to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen. Not yet designed for delivery status.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: WhatsApp message copies kept no longer than needed; phone numbers not logged. Open decision D8: which WhatsApp provider is used and which kinds need approved templates. Open question: quiet hours when WhatsApp notices are held, computed in Asia/Kolkata if decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S1, EP-11-S2, EP-11-S9, EP-03-S1, EP-04-S4, EP-05-S2, EP-10-S1, EP-10-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-11-S14: System can retry failed deliveries and report final failures

- **Story ID:** EP-11-S14
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can retry failed deliveries and report final failures
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a failed WhatsApp or email send to be retried with backoff, and after the last attempt marked failed and passed to the alerting hook that EP-37 fills in
- **So that:** a short provider outage does not lose an alert, and a notice that never got through is visible (FR-11-14)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an email send to Sanjay Seth fails on attempt 1 and succeeds on attempt 2, when it finishes, then the row's status is sent and attempts is 2.
  2. Given a WhatsApp send fails on every attempt up to the maximum, when the last attempt ends, then the row's status is failed and the failure is handed to the EP-37 alerting hook with notification id, channel and error, but no phone number or message text.
  3. Given a whatsapp row for the BATCH-2026-044 stop has failed, when Sanjay opens his in-app list, then the app notification for the same event is still there.
  4. Given a retry and a late original attempt run together, when both finish, then one message is sent, because they share the notification id as idempotency key.
  5. Given a row marked failed, when the scheduler next ticks, then it is not retried again by itself.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Retries use the background job retry and backoff from EP-10-S3, with the notification id as the idempotency key (EP-10-S4). Max attempts per channel is set in the job definition. Failed is a final status.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Delivery attempts are recorded on the notification (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** Updates Notification attempts and status.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: provider outages ridden out by retries; the app channel does not depend on them. Personal data: no phone numbers, email addresses or message text passed to alerting. Open question: retry counts and intervals are not set in the sources; tests check that each wait is longer than the last.
- **Depends on:** EP-11-S12, EP-11-S13, EP-10-S2, EP-10-S3, EP-10-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-12: WhatsApp integration · stories

Epic document: [EP-12 WhatsApp integration](../epics/EP-12-whatsapp-integration.md)

Role note: this is a layer A platform epic. Stories where the integration connects, sends, verifies callbacks, stores messages and receipts or handles opt-out on its own use "System". EP-12-S2 uses "Owner" because the owner registers templates and reads their status. Send Template message and Send Session message are internal operations and cannot be called from a browser session; the inbound webhook accepts only calls signed by the provider.

## EP-12-S1: System can connect to the WhatsApp provider with credentials from environment configuration

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can connect to the WhatsApp provider with credentials from environment configuration
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one internal WhatsApp provider interface with a real provider client that reads its account id, access token, webhook secret, verify token and sender numbers from environment variables only, chosen by the delivery mode variable in place of a development stub that shows messages in the simulated WhatsApp bubble
- **So that:** messages can go out and come in through a real provider without secrets in the code, and the provider can be swapped later behind the same interface (FR-12-1, BR-12-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given staging with the delivery mode set to `whatsapp` and all provider variables set, when the api starts, then the provider client is used for every send and the development stub is not loaded. Sign-in sends no WhatsApp message (D4).
  2. Given production with the provider access token variable missing, when the api starts, then it refuses to start and the log names the missing variable but no value of any variable.
  3. Given a commit that contains a provider access token in a file, when CI runs, then the secret scan fails the run (EP-01-S10).
  4. Given the provider is reachable, when the health check is called, then it reports the WhatsApp provider as up, and when the provider cannot be reached it reports it as down, in both cases without any credential in the response.
  5. Given the sender numbers listed in configuration, when the api starts, then each one exists as a SenderIdentity row with display name, phone number and provider account reference, and a send naming an unknown sender identity is refused.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Provider credentials are read only from environment variables (EP-01-S6) and never written to the database, logs or responses. All provider calls go through one internal interface so the provider chosen under D8 can be replaced. The development stub is refused in production.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Connecting to the provider changes no business record.
- **Data changes:** Adds the SenderIdentity table (id, display name, phone number, provider account reference) by migration (EP-02-S1), filled from configuration. Adds the provider environment variables to each environment's configuration.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: credentials only in environment configuration; health output carries no secret. Availability: health check shows the provider as down so EP-37 can alert. Open decision D8: Meta Cloud API directly or a Business Solution Provider; the interface is written so either fits. D10 is decided (India region); whether the WhatsApp provider also stores message data in India is open. Open question G20: how many sender numbers there are.
- **Depends on:** EP-01-S6, EP-01-S10, EP-02-S1, EP-03-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S2: Owner can register a message template and see its approval status

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can register a message template and see its approval status
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to register a WhatsApp template with a name, purpose, English body with numbered variables, and then see whether the provider has it as pending, approved or rejected
- **So that:** the owner edit code (edit token), alert, wish, broadcast and catalogue messages can be approved early, because messages outside a conversation need approved templates (FR-12-2, BR-12-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth (Owner), when he calls Create Template with name `edit_token`, purpose edit token, language English and body "JGD: confirm edit to {{1}}. Token {{2}}", then it is submitted to the provider, a WhatsAppTemplate row is stored with the provider template id and approval status pending.
  2. Given the provider later reports `edit_token` as approved, when the status update is received, then the row's approval status is approved and updated at is set from the server clock.
  3. Given the provider rejects `wish_birthday`, when the status update is received, then the row's status is rejected and the provider's reason is kept on the row.
  4. Given Sanjay calls List Templates, when it returns, then he sees each template's name, purpose, language, approval status and updated at; Rajesh Verma (Staff) calling it gets `forbidden`.
  5. Given a Create Template request with a language other than English, or a body holding a price or rupee amount, when the server checks it, then it is refused with a sentence saying v1 templates are English only and carry no price.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Template and List Templates are Owner only until the open question on operations access is decided (EP-05-S2). Purpose is one of edit token, alert, wish, broadcast, catalogue; the edit token is registered as an authentication template. There is no sign-in template (D4). Status is one of pending, approved, rejected and changes only from provider status updates. Language is English in v1; other languages belong to EP-44. No template carries a money field (EP-42 owns prices).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (Owner on create, System on provider status change), time, entity (WhatsAppTemplate), action (template registered, approval status changed), before and after status.
- **Data changes:** Adds the WhatsAppTemplate table (id, name unique, purpose, language, body with variables, provider template id, approval status, rejection reason, updated at) by migration. Adds Create Template and List Templates to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: updated at stored in UTC. Open decision D8: template approval lead time; templates are registered early in M1 (epic section 16 risk). Open question: whether operations staff, not only the Owner, may register templates.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S1, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S3: System can send an approved template message with variables

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can send an approved template message with variables
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an internal Send Template message operation that takes a template name, a recipient (user or customer, with phone), a sender identity and variables, sends it through the provider and stores an OutboundMessage with the provider message id
- **So that:** the owner's edit code, alerts, wishes, broadcasts and catalogue links reach the right phone, and each send can be followed (FR-12-3, FR-12-4, BR-12-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the approved `edit_token` template, when Sanjay Seth (Owner) applies Rajesh Verma's proposed edit to TAG-8841 (EP-25), then one message is sent to Sanjay's registered mobile number, an OutboundMessage is stored with recipient type user, the provider message id and status sent, and its stored variables hold no plain code (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given that send, when Sanjay reads it, then his WhatsApp shows "JGD: confirm edit to TAG-8841. Token" followed by the 6-digit token, as on mockup 05.
  3. Given the `wish_birthday` template is still pending, when a send is requested, then it is refused with the sentence "The WhatsApp template wish_birthday is not approved yet, so this message was not sent." and no provider call is made (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  4. Given a send request with fewer variables than the template body needs, when the server checks it, then it is refused and no message is stored as sent.
  5. Given the same send is requested twice with the same idempotency key (for example the EP-11 notification id), when both run, then the provider is called once and one OutboundMessage exists.
  6. Given a browser session of any role, when it calls Send Template message, then the server refuses it, because the operation is internal.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only approved templates may be sent. Send is callable only by EP-11, EP-25, EP-33 and EP-34 server code (not by sign-in, D4), never a user session (EP-05-S2). Sends are deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Customer recipients pass the consent check first (EP-12-S5). Grams in variables are formatted to 4 decimals from integer units of 0.0001 g (EP-02-S2). Secret variables are stored only as references (EP-12-S11).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Sends are requested by internal calls, not live events (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. The OutboundMessage row is the send record; the business action that asked for the send is audited by its own epic.
- **Data changes:** Adds the OutboundMessage table (id, recipient phone, recipient type, recipient id, sender identity id, template id or session flag, variables with secret ones as references, provider message id unique, status queued/sent/delivered/read/failed, failure reason, created at, sent at, delivered at, read at in UTC, source notification id or broadcast id or wish id, idempotency key unique) by migration.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Message wording follows `docs/ux/mockups/05-edit-propose-apply.svg`, route `edit-apply` ("Enter the token sent to your WhatsApp").
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the owner edit code is handed to the provider at once, so delivery does not use up the 10-minute expiry (epic section 13). Precision: grams in variables shown to 4 decimals from integers. Concurrency: one provider call per idempotency key. Security: internal operation only. Open decision D8: provider API shape and template rules.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S1, EP-12-S2, EP-02-S2, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-11-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S4: System can send a session message inside an open conversation window

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can send a session message inside an open conversation window
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an internal Send Session message operation that sends free text, without a template, to a phone whose conversation window is still open according to the latest InboundMessage's "conversation window ends at"
- **So that:** the shop can reply to a customer who has just written, without waiting for a template approval (FR-12-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given +91 90037 44120 sent a message whose conversation window ends at 18:00 tomorrow, when a session message is sent at 11:00 today, then it goes out without a template and the OutboundMessage has the session flag set and no template id.
  2. Given the window for that phone ended at 18:00 yesterday, when a session message is requested, then it is refused with the sentence "The conversation with this number has closed, so only an approved template can be sent." and no provider call is made.
  3. Given the phone belongs to a customer whose `optedIn` is false, when a session message is requested, then it is refused by the consent check (EP-12-S5).
  4. Given a browser session of any role, when it calls Send Session message, then the server refuses it, because the operation is internal.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The window check uses "conversation window ends at" from the latest InboundMessage for that phone and the server clock (EP-03-S3). The window length comes from the provider's rules under D8. Internal callers only (EP-05-S2). Session text carries no price (EP-42 owns prices).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. The OutboundMessage row is the send record.
- **Data changes:** Inserts OutboundMessage rows with the session flag set. Reads InboundMessage "conversation window ends at".
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: window end stored and compared in UTC on the server clock. Personal data: session text is personal data kept only as long as the retention rule says. Open decision D8: the length and rules of the conversation window depend on the provider.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S3, EP-12-S5, EP-12-S7, EP-03-S3, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S5: System can refuse a customer message when consent is off

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse a customer message when consent is off
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every template or session send to a recipient of type customer to read that customer's `optedIn` at the moment of sending and refuse the send when it is false
- **So that:** only customers who agreed get wishes, broadcasts and catalogue links, as the DPDP Act and the shop's promise require (FR-12-6, BR-12-3, BR-12-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra has `optedIn` true and a birthday today, when her wish is sent, then the message goes to her phone.
  2. Given a customer shown on `wishes` as "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send", when a wish is requested for them, then no provider call is made and the send returns the reason consent off (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  3. Given a broadcast to the 86 opted-in VIP Bridal customers, and one of them opts out after the broadcast is queued, when that customer's send runs, then it is refused and the other 85 are sent.
  4. Given a job reminder to Vijay Kumar (Karigar), when it is sent, then no customer consent check applies, because the recipient type is user.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The consent check runs inside the send, on the server, for every customer recipient, using the current `optedIn` value (EP-02-S4). A refused send makes no provider call. The check cannot be skipped by a caller.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused send changes no record; the consent value itself is audited where it changes (EP-12-S10, EP-17).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Reads Customer `optedIn`.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Effects show on `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send"), and `docs/ux/mockups/27-broadcast.svg`, route `broadcast` ("86 customers · all opted in to WhatsApp").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: only `optedIn` customers are messaged and an opt-out applies to the next send at once (epic section 13). Concurrency: consent read at send time, not at queue time.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S3, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S6: System can verify and accept inbound webhook calls

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can verify and accept inbound webhook calls
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one inbound webhook endpoint that checks the provider signature on every call against the webhook secret, answers the provider's subscription check only with the configured verify token, and hands each verified message or receipt to processing
- **So that:** only real provider callbacks become messages, receipts or leads, and forged calls cannot create fake leads (FR-12-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a call whose signature matches the body and the webhook secret, when it arrives, then it is accepted, acknowledged within the provider's timeout and passed to message or receipt processing.
  2. Given a call with a wrong signature, when it arrives, then it is rejected with an authentication error and no InboundMessage, receipt or lead is stored (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given a call with no signature header, when it arrives, then it is rejected the same way.
  4. Given the provider's subscription check with the configured verify token, when it arrives, then the challenge is answered; with any other token it is refused.
  5. Given a rejected call, when it is logged, then the log holds the time, source address and reason, and no body text or phone number.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The signature is checked before the body is parsed or stored. The verified body is validated against the contract (EP-03-S2). The endpoint has no user session and accepts only provider-signed calls. The rate-limit hook applies (EP-03-S11). Processing after acknowledgement runs as a background job (EP-10-S1).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Rejected calls are logged for security; accepted calls are recorded as InboundMessage or receipt rows.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database from this story. Adds the webhook endpoint and the webhook secret and verify token variables.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: signature verified on every call; unsigned calls rejected (epic section 16 risk). Personal data: rejected bodies are not logged. Open decision D8: signature method depends on the provider.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S11, EP-10-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S7: System can store an inbound message once and hand it to lead intake

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store an inbound message once and hand it to lead intake
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each verified inbound message stored as one InboundMessage keyed by its provider message id, with sender phone, text, received at and conversation window ends at, and then handed to the EP-29 intake interface with sender phone, text and media file ids
- **So that:** every PO or broadcast reply becomes a lead exactly once, and nothing a customer sends is dropped (FR-12-8, FR-12-9, BR-12-8, BR-12-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a verified message from +91 90037 44120 with text, when it is processed, then one InboundMessage is stored with the provider message id, sender phone, text, received at in UTC and conversation window ends at, and it is handed to lead intake.
  2. Given the provider delivers the same message id again, when it is processed, then no second InboundMessage is stored and lead intake is not called again, so one lead exists.
  3. Given two workers process the same message id at the same moment, when both commit, then one InboundMessage exists, because the provider message id is unique in the database.
  4. Given a reply to the VIP Bridal broadcast, when it is handed over, then the handoff carries the replied-to OutboundMessage id when the provider supplies it, so EP-29 can mark it a broadcast reply.
  5. Given lead intake returns the new lead id, when the handoff completes, then the InboundMessage "handed to" field holds that lead id.
  6. Given the message text is an opt-out keyword, when it is processed, then it is not handed to lead intake (EP-12-S10).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Deduplication by the unique provider message id and dedupe key (EP-03-S8). Storage and the "handed to" update run in one transaction (EP-03-S6). Intake is an internal interface; until EP-29 exists it is a stub that records the handoff. Actions are recorded with the System actor for WhatsApp intake (EP-06-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. EP-29 creates the lead and emits "Lead arrived / passed its SLA".
- **Audit entry written:** No. The InboundMessage row is the record of receipt; lead creation is audited by EP-29 with the System actor (EP-06-S6).
- **Data changes:** Adds the InboundMessage table (id, provider message id unique, sender phone, text, media file ids, received at, conversation window ends at, replied-to outbound message id, handed to lead id, dedupe key) by migration.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Results show on `docs/ux/mockups/16-lead-inbox.svg`, route `leads` ("from WhatsApp", "Nothing a customer sends is ever dropped").
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: a redelivered webhook creates one InboundMessage and one lead (epic section 13). Personal data: sender phone and text are personal data kept only as long as the retention rule says. Time: received at stored in UTC. Open question G17: whether reply counts for broadcasts are kept here or in EP-34.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S6, EP-02-S7, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S8: System can store inbound media through file storage

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store inbound media through file storage
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each media item on an inbound message downloaded from the provider and handed to EP-09 Create Inbound file, with the returned file id added to the InboundMessage media file ids before the handoff to lead intake
- **So that:** a photo PO, even one the system cannot read, reaches the lead with its original image (FR-12-10, BR-12-9)

## EP-12-S9: System can record delivery, read and failure receipts

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can record delivery, read and failure receipts
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** each verified receipt matched to its OutboundMessage by provider message id, moving its status forward to delivered, read or failed with the time and any failure reason, passed on to EP-11 Update Delivery status for notification messages, and readable through Read Message status
- **So that:** the owner can see whether a token, alert or broadcast got through, and broadcasts show delivered and opened (FR-12-11, BR-12-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a sent message to Sanjay Seth, when the provider reports delivered and then read, then its status shows read with delivered at and read at set (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  2. Given the read receipt arrives before the delivered receipt, when both are applied, then the status ends as read and does not move back to delivered.
  3. Given a failed receipt with the provider's error, when it is applied, then the status is failed with the failure reason, and the failure is reported as in EP-12-S12.
  4. Given the message came from an EP-11 notification, when its status changes, then Update Delivery status is called for that notification (EP-11-S13).
  5. Given Read Message status for a broadcast message, when Rajesh Verma (Staff) who sent the broadcast calls it, then he sees the status; for a message he did not send he gets `forbidden`; Sanjay (Owner) sees any message.
  6. Given a receipt for an unknown provider message id, when it arrives, then it is ignored and logged without phone or text.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Status only moves forward: queued, sent, delivered, read; failed is final. Receipts arrive only through the verified webhook (EP-12-S6). Read Message status is Owner for all messages and Staff for broadcasts they sent (EP-05-S2).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Delivery status is kept on the OutboundMessage, not in the audit log.
- **Data changes:** Updates OutboundMessage status, delivered at, read at, failure reason. Adds Read Message status to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Broadcast tracking shows on `docs/ux/mockups/27-broadcast.svg`, route `broadcast` ("Delivered, opened, and who replied are tracked"), built in EP-34.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: receipt times stored in UTC. Concurrency: out-of-order receipts never move a status back. Open question G17: whether broadcast delivered, opened and replied counts are stored here or in EP-34; this story stores per-message status only.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S3, EP-12-S6, EP-03-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-11-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S10: System can switch off a customer's consent on an opt-out keyword

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can switch off a customer's consent on an opt-out keyword
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an inbound message whose whole text, trimmed and in any letter case, is a configured opt-out keyword to set the matching customer's `optedIn` to false with changed at and changed by System, and to write an audit entry
- **So that:** a customer who asks to stop gets no more wishes or broadcasts from the next send onwards (FR-12-12, BR-12-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra has `optedIn` true and replies "STOP", when the webhook processes it, then her `optedIn` is false, changed by is System, and an audit entry records the change (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given her consent is now off, when the 9 am wishes run reaches her, then no message is sent to her (EP-12-S5).
  3. Given a reply " stop " or "Stop", when it is processed, then it is treated as the keyword; given "please don't stop the order", then it is not, and the message goes to lead intake.
  4. Given a keyword from a phone that matches no customer, when it is processed, then the message is stored and no consent changes.
  5. Given Priya sends "STOP" a second time, when it is processed, then nothing changes and no second audit entry is written.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Matching uses the configured keyword list, defaulting to "STOP" until decided. The consent change and its audit entry run in one transaction (EP-06-S2). Keyword messages are not handed to lead intake. Turning consent back on is owned by EP-17.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (System, WhatsApp intake), time, entity (customer), action (WhatsApp consent switched off by keyword), before `optedIn` true, after `optedIn` false, reason (keyword received, inbound message id).
- **Data changes:** Updates Customer `optedIn`, consent changed at and changed by (EP-02-S4).
- **UI reference:** No screen. The result shows on `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: opt-out honoured at once (epic section 13). Audit: consent change audited with a System actor (EP-06-S6). Open question: which opt-out keywords are recognised, in which languages; v1 is English only.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S5, EP-12-S6, EP-12-S7, EP-02-S4, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S11: System can keep owner edit codes and other secret values out of logs and stored messages

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can keep owner edit codes and other secret values out of logs and stored messages
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** template variables marked secret (the owner edit code, also called the edit token) to be stored on OutboundMessage only as a reference to the token record, and redacted from request logs, provider client logs and error reports
- **So that:** a code cannot leak from our database, logs or audit log and be used to apply an edit (FR-12-14, BR-12-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the edit token "480 913" is sent to Sanjay Seth for TAG-8841, when the OutboundMessage is read back, then its variables hold TAG-8841 and a token reference, and not "480913" or "480 913".
  2. Given an edit code is sent to Sanjay Seth, when the api log, the provider client log and the audit log are searched after the send, then the 6 digits do not appear in any of them.
  3. Given the provider returns an error that echoes the request body, when the error is logged, then the secret variable is replaced by a redaction mark.
  4. Given the audit entry for the edit-token send written by EP-25, when it is read, then it holds the token reference only (EP-06-S4).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Each template's variables are marked secret or not at registration; Edit token variables are always secret. The plain value exists only in memory between generation (EP-25) and the provider call. Logging goes through one redaction step for all provider calls.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No from this story. It makes sure entries written elsewhere hold a token reference only.
- **Data changes:** Adds a secret flag per variable on WhatsAppTemplate. OutboundMessage variables store references for secret variables.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner edit code values never logged or stored in plain text; a test scans logs after a send for the code (epic section 16 risk). Audit: token reference only.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S2, EP-12-S3, EP-06-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-12-S12: System can report failed sends for retry and alerting

- **Story ID:** EP-12-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can report failed sends for retry and alerting
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a send that the provider refuses, times out on, or later reports as failed to be marked failed with its reason, reported to EP-11 so it can retry, and after the last attempt passed to the alerting hook that EP-37 fills in
- **So that:** a provider outage does not silently lose an alert, a token or a wish, and operations hear about it (FR-12-13)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the provider times out on a whatsapp notice to Sanjay Seth about BATCH-2026-044, when the send ends, then the OutboundMessage is failed with reason timeout and EP-11 is told through Update Delivery status, so its retry runs (EP-11-S14).
  2. Given the retry succeeds, when it runs with the same idempotency key, then one message reaches Sanjay and the new OutboundMessage is sent.
  3. Given a send fails on the last attempt, when it ends, then the failure is handed to the alerting hook with message id, template name and error code, and no phone number, text or variables.
  4. Given a failed receipt arrives for a broadcast message (EP-12-S9), when it is applied, then it is reported the same way.
  5. Given the provider refuses because a template was rejected, when the failure is reported, then the reason names the template.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Retries use EP-10 retry and backoff with the source id as idempotency key (EP-10-S3, EP-10-S4). Failed is a final status for that OutboundMessage. The alerting hook receives no personal data.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Failures are recorded on the OutboundMessage and passed to alerting.
- **Data changes:** Updates OutboundMessage status and failure reason.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: a provider outage queues messages for retry (EP-11) and alerts operations (EP-37) (epic section 13). Personal data: no phone, text or variables passed to alerting. Security: secret variables never in failure reports.
- **Depends on:** EP-12-S3, EP-12-S9, EP-10-S3, EP-10-S4, EP-11-S13, EP-11-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-13: Shop settings · stories

Epic document: [EP-13 Shop settings](../epics/EP-13-shop-settings.md)

Role note: stories where the server stores, checks, audits or pushes settings on its own use "System". Stories where a person changes a setting use "Owner". Staff only read settings in these stories; whether staff may change any key is open question G12.

---

## EP-13-S1: System can store shop settings with seed defaults

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store shop settings with seed defaults
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one typed settings record for the shop, keyed by its shop ID, created with the seed defaults when the shop is created (`pricingEnabled` false, `leadSlaHours` 8, `requireEditToken` true, `notifyChannels` WhatsApp on, app on, email off, `lateLeadAudience` `staff_then_owner`, `autoSendWishes` false, `wishSendTime` 09:00, `ageingThresholdDays` empty), and a Read Settings operation that owner and staff screens and background jobs can call
- **So that:** the lead timer, notification rules, wishes run and edit-token flow all read the same stored values instead of an in-memory object that resets on reload (FR-13-1, FR-13-2, BR-13-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an empty database after migrations, when the shop record is created (by the setup wizard, EP-45, through EP-02-S3), then exactly one settings row exists for that shop ID with `leadSlaHours` 8, `lateLeadAudience` `staff_then_owner`, `notifyChannels` {whatsapp: true, app: true, email: false}, `requireEditToken` true, `autoSendWishes` false, `wishSendTime` 09:00, `ageingThresholdDays` null, `pricingEnabled` false and version 1.
  2. Given the settings row already exists, when the api restarts, then no second row is created for the shop and no stored value is reset to its default.
  3. Given Sanjay Seth (Owner) or Rajesh Verma (Staff) is signed in, when either calls Read Settings, then the response holds every key above plus updated at and updated by.
  4. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar) is signed in, when he calls Read Settings, then the server refuses with `forbidden` and returns no values.
  5. Given the settings row cannot be read, when a background job or screen asks for settings, then it gets the seed defaults and the failure is logged, never a record with every switch off (epic section 13, Availability).
  6. Given the shop was created with its default location, when Read Settings is called, then the response also names the one location "Main shop" and its id; no operation to add, rename or remove a location exists (D7).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Settings is allowed for `owner`, `staff` and the System actor and refused for `karigar` (EP-05-S2). Each key has a fixed type: `leadSlaHours` a number of at least 1, `lateLeadAudience` one of `staff_then_owner` or `owner_only`, `notifyChannels` three booleans, `wishSendTime` a local time of day, `ageingThresholdDays` a whole number or null, the rest booleans. Defaults live in one place in the shared package. The row is read for the caller's shop ID from the session, never from the request (D7).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Creating the default row is not a change by any person; later changes are audited in EP-13-S3.
- **Data changes:** Uses the `settings` table from EP-02-S12. Migration adds `wishSendTime`, `ageingThresholdDays` (nullable), updated at, updated by and version columns if EP-02-S12 did not create them. Adds Read Settings to the shared contract (EP-03-S1). Reads the default location "Main shop" from `locations` (EP-02-S3); adds no location table of its own.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: a missing row falls back to the seed defaults, not to "everything off". Performance: Read Settings answers in under 50 ms (proposed target, to confirm) and may be cached until "Setting changed" arrives (EP-13-S14). Time: updated at stored in UTC. D7 is decided (one shop, no branches): one settings row per shop, keyed by shop ID.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S12, EP-02-S3, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
