## EP-13-S2: System can refuse a settings change from a role not allowed to make it

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse a settings change from a role not allowed to make it
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one Update Setting operation that takes a key, a new value and the version the caller last read, checks the caller's role against the permission matrix for that key before anything else, and refuses with "Only the owner can change the shop rules." when the role is not allowed
- **So that:** hiding the rules panel from staff is no longer the only control, and the prototype paths that let any role flip `autoSendWishes` on `wishes` or `pricingEnabled` in the AppShell switch are closed (FR-13-11, BR-13-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Update Setting for `leadSlaHours` with value 6 directly, then the server refuses with code `forbidden` and the sentence "Only the owner can change the shop rules.", and `leadSlaHours` stays 8 (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh, when he calls Update Setting for `autoSendWishes` or `pricingEnabled`, then the server refuses the same way, unless G12 places `autoSendWishes` in the staff list, in which case only that key succeeds.
  3. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar), when he calls Update Setting for any key, then the server refuses with `forbidden`.
  4. Given Sanjay Seth (Owner) sends an unknown key `matchTolerance`, when the server checks it, then it is refused as a validation error, because there is no tolerance setting anywhere (BR-13-4).
  5. Given Sanjay saves `leadSlaHours` with version 3 while the stored version is 4, when the server checks it, then it is refused with "This rule was changed a moment ago. Check and save again." and nothing changes.
  6. Given an accepted change, when it commits, then the version goes up by 1 and updated at and updated by are set from the server clock and the session (EP-03-S3).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The role check per key runs on the server before validation and before any write (deny by default, EP-05-S2). Only known keys are accepted, each validated against its type (EP-03-S2). The version check rejects a stale write (EP-02-S14). Actor and time come from the session and server clock, never from the request. The change runs in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None from this story. The accepted change emits "Setting changed" through EP-13-S14.
- **Audit entry written:** No for a refused change, because nothing changes. Accepted changes are audited by EP-13-S3.
- **Data changes:** Updates the settings row value, version, updated at and updated by. Adds Update Setting to the shared contract and its per-key entries to the permission matrix (EP-05-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The refusal sentence shows on any screen that calls Update Setting through EP-08-S5.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: every settings write checks the role on the server; the AppShell pricing switch and the `wishes` toggle no longer bypass it (epic section 13). Concurrency: two owners saving the same key at once, the second gets "This rule was changed a moment ago. Check and save again." Open question G12: which keys staff may change; the matrix lists all keys as owner-only until it is answered.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S1, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S3: System can audit every settings change with old and new value

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit every settings change with old and new value
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every accepted Update Setting, for every key including `pricingEnabled`, to write a `setting_changed` audit entry in the same transaction, with the key, old value, new value, actor and time, and a List Setting changes operation for the owner that reads those entries
- **So that:** the owner can see who changed which rule and when, and no setting can change without a trace (FR-13-12, BR-13-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth changes `leadSlaHours` from 8 to 6, when the change commits, then one audit entry exists with kind `setting_changed`, ref `leadSlaHours`, before 8, after 6, actor Sanjay Seth and the server time, and its summary reads "leadSlaHours 8 → 6" (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Sanjay switches `pricingEnabled` from false to true, when it commits, then an audit entry is written the same way, with no exception for the pricing key.
  3. Given the audit write fails, when the transaction ends, then the setting is not changed either.
  4. Given Sanjay calls List Setting changes, when it returns, then he sees setting changes newest first, one page at a time, each with key, before, after, actor and time; Rajesh Verma (Staff) calling it gets `forbidden`.
  5. Given a save whose new value equals the stored value, when it is processed, then no audit entry is written and the version does not change.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The setting change and its audit entry share one transaction (EP-06-S2). The `pricingEnabled` skip from the prototype `setSetting` is not carried over (EP-06-S8). List Setting changes is Owner only and reads the append-only audit store (EP-06-S9, EP-06-S12). There is no update or delete path for these entries.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (settings), action (`setting_changed`), ref (setting key), before (old value), after (new value).
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). Adds List Setting changes to the shared contract. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The history is also visible in the security log built in EP-06.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every key, including `pricingEnabled`, writes an append-only entry with old and new value (epic section 13). Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S2, EP-03-S9, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S8, EP-06-S9, EP-06-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S4: Owner can change the lead SLA hours

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can change the lead SLA hours
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to change the number of hours after which a lead counts as late, from the "A lead is late after … hours" field in the rules panel
- **So that:** the shop's lead timer matches how fast the shop wants every enquiry opened (FR-13-3, FR-13-4, BR-13-1, BR-13-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth on `decisions` with `leadSlaHours` 8, when he enters 6 and saves, then the stored value is 6, an audit entry reads "leadSlaHours 8 → 6" with his name, and open lead inboxes recompute lateness within about a second (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Sanjay enters 0.5, when the server checks it, then it refuses with "The lead timer must be at least 1 hour." and the stored value stays 8 (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  3. Given Sanjay enters 0, a negative number or text, when he saves, then the server refuses with the same sentence or a validation error and nothing changes.
  4. Given the value is now 6, when a new lead arrives, then the EP-10-S5 SLA job is scheduled at arrival plus 6 hours.
  5. Given leads already waiting when the value changes, when the change commits, then their lateness is recomputed against 6 hours on open screens; whether their scheduled SLA jobs are also moved is decided with EP-28.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-13-S2). `leadSlaHours` must be a number of at least 1; the refusal sentence is "The lead timer must be at least 1 hour." (prototype `setSetting`). Audited (EP-13-S3).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26) through EP-13-S14.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (settings), action (`setting_changed`), ref `leadSlaHours`, before, after.
- **Data changes:** Updates `settings.leadSlaHours`, version, updated at, updated by.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("THE RULES BEHIND THESE ALERTS", "A lead is late after 8 hours, shop hours, not clock hours"). The shop settings page is not yet designed (EP-13-S13).
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: until A2 is answered the timer counts clock hours and the label must say so; "shop hours, not clock hours" shows only once EP-13-S11 is live. Concurrency: version check from EP-13-S2. Open decision A2: shop hours or clock hours.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-08-S5, EP-10-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S7: Owner can switch auto-send wishes and set the send time

- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to switch "Send wishes automatically at 9 am" on or off on `wishes` and set the daily send time `wishSendTime`, with the change checked and audited on the server
- **So that:** birthday and anniversary wishes go out on their own at the time the shop chooses, and staff can no longer flip the switch without the owner (FR-13-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth on `wishes` with `autoSendWishes` false, when he switches it on, then the stored value is true, an audit entry reads "autoSendWishes false → true", and the next wishes run sends Priya Malhotra's birthday wish.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) on `wishes`, when he taps the switch, then the server refuses with "Only the owner can change the shop rules." and the switch returns to its stored state, unless G12 places `autoSendWishes` in the staff list.
  3. Given Sanjay sets `wishSendTime` to 10:30, when he saves, then the stored value is 10:30 Asia/Kolkata, the label reads "Send wishes automatically at 10:30", and the EP-10-S9 job for the next day runs at 10:30 Asia/Kolkata (05:00 UTC).
  4. Given Sanjay enters 25:00 or text, when he saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error and nothing changes.
  5. Given `autoSendWishes` is switched off at 08:55, when the run time arrives, then no wishes are sent that day (EP-10-S9 reads the value at run time).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only until G12 is answered (EP-13-S2). `autoSendWishes` boolean; `wishSendTime` a local time of day HH:MM between 00:00 and 23:59, stored as Asia/Kolkata local time and converted to UTC when scheduling. Audited.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26) through EP-13-S14.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (settings), action (`setting_changed`), ref `autoSendWishes` or `wishSendTime`, before, after.
- **Data changes:** Updates `settings.autoSendWishes`, `settings.wishSendTime`, version, updated at, updated by.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Send wishes automatically at 9 am"). The send-time field is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: send time is local Asia/Kolkata; the server converts to UTC when scheduling (EP-10-S10). Security: the `wishes` toggle no longer changes the setting without the server check. Open question G12: whether staff may switch auto-send. Open question: whether the send time is changeable at all, or fixed at 9 am as EP-10 says; if fixed, criterion 3 drops and the label stays "9 am".
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-10-S9, EP-10-S10, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S8: Owner can set the ageing threshold for gold sitting too long (G5)

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S8

- **Title:** Owner can set the ageing threshold for gold sitting too long (G5)

- **So that:** the owner's ageing alert on the Decisions home uses his own limit, for example "196.4 g of gold has not moved in 90 days" (FR-13-9)

  3. Given `ageingThresholdDays` is empty, when EP-32 reads settings, then it receives null and shows no ageing alert, rather than using a hidden number.
  4. Given Sanjay enters 0, a negative number or 12.5, when he saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error, because the threshold is a whole number of days greater than 0.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-13-S2). `ageingThresholdDays` is a whole number greater than 0 or null. This epic stores the value only; computing which pieces are old and drawing the alert is EP-32. Audited.

- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (settings), action (`setting_changed`), ref `ageingThresholdDays`, before, after.

- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (shop settings page). The alert it feeds is on `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg`, route `decisions` ("GOLD SITTING TOO LONG", "196.4 g of gold has not moved in 90 days").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: days counted on Asia/Kolkata dates (EP-10-S10). Open question G5: what the threshold is and whether it is one number for all pieces; if per style or category is wanted, this story needs a split.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S1, EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S11: Owner can enter shop hours and holidays for the lead timer

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can enter shop hours and holidays for the lead timer
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to enter an opening and closing time for each weekday, mark a weekday closed, and add holidays with a date and label, through Read Shop hours and Update Shop hours
- **So that:** the 8-hour lead timer counts shop hours, not clock hours, and does not fire overnight or on a holiday (FR-13-14, BR-13-2, BR-13-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given A2 confirms shop hours, when Sanjay Seth sets Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 20:00 and Sunday closed and saves, then seven ShopHours rows are stored in Asia/Kolkata local time and an audit entry records before and after.
  2. Given those hours and `leadSlaHours` 8, when a lead arrives on Monday at 18:00 Asia/Kolkata, then the due time read by the EP-10-S5 SLA job is Tuesday 16:00 Asia/Kolkata (2 hours on Monday, 6 on Tuesday).
  3. Given Sanjay adds the holiday Monday 2026-11-09 "Diwali", when a lead arrives on Saturday 2026-11-07 at 19:00 Asia/Kolkata, then no shop hours are counted on Sunday or on 2026-11-09, and the due time is Tuesday 2026-11-10 at 17:00 Asia/Kolkata.
  4. Given a weekday whose closing time is before its opening time, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error and nothing changes.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Read Shop hours, then he gets the hours; when he calls Update Shop hours, then the server refuses with "Only the owner can change the shop rules."
  6. Given A2 is answered "clock hours", when this story is reviewed, then it is not built and the lead timer label says clock hours.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Shop hours for Owner, Staff and System; Update Shop hours Owner only (EP-05-S2). Times are local Asia/Kolkata and converted to UTC when the due time is computed. One row per weekday; holiday dates unique. Audited in the same transaction.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26) through EP-13-S14, so inboxes recompute lateness.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (shop hours or holiday), action (`setting_changed`), before, after.
- **Data changes:** Migration adds ShopHours (weekday, opens at, closes at, closed flag) and Holiday (date unique, label). Replaces the EP-10-S5 replaceable due-time function with one that reads these tables.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (shop-hours calendar). The label it changes is on `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("shop hours, not clock hours").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: stored local, converted to UTC on the server; day boundaries in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). Open decision A2: shop hours or clock hours, and what the hours and holidays are; the whole story waits on it.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-13-S4, EP-10-S5, EP-10-S10, EP-06-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-13-S14: System can push a changed setting to open screens live

- **Story ID:** EP-13-S14
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can push a changed setting to open screens live
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every accepted settings, shop-hours or holiday change to publish a "Setting changed" event after its transaction commits, carrying the key, the new value and the version, to every open owner and staff connection, and to clear any cached settings read
- **So that:** inboxes recompute lead lateness, the Decisions rules panel refreshes and the pricing sockets appear or hide without a reload (FR-13-13)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma's lead inbox is open, when Sanjay Seth changes `leadSlaHours` from 8 to 6, then the inbox recomputes lateness against 6 hours within about a second without a reload (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Deepak Rao's stock screen is open, when Sanjay switches `pricingEnabled` on, then the value sockets show on its next render without a reload (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given the change transaction rolls back, when it ends, then no "Setting changed" event is published (EP-07-S1).
  4. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar) is connected, when any setting changes, then he receives no "Setting changed" event.
  5. Given a server-side cache of settings, when "Setting changed" is published, then the next Read Settings and the next SLA job read the new value.
  6. Given Rajesh's connection was down during the change, when it reconnects, then he catches up from the last sequence number and sees the new value (EP-07-S7).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Published only after commit (EP-07-S1), stamped with sequence number, entity id and version (EP-07-S2). Delivered to owner and staff roles only (EP-07-S5). Events carry no secret and no money amount.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26); consumers EP-28, EP-31, EP-32, EP-42.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The change itself is audited by EP-13-S3.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds "Setting changed" to the event list and the client event-to-read map (EP-08-S8).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Effects show on `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions`, and on the lead inbox.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: event reaches open screens within about 1 second. Concurrency: the version in the event lets a screen ignore an older value that arrives late. Open question G26: whether "Setting changed" is accepted into the live event catalogue.
- **Depends on:** EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S7, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-14: Scale registry · stories

Role note: stories where the server stores, checks, computes or audits on its own use "System". Stories where a person changes the registry use "Owner", and the picker stories use "Staff". Karigars are not involved in this epic.

## EP-14-S1: System can store scales with readability and capacity as integer weights

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store scales with readability and capacity as integer weights
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `scales` table from EP-02-S4 extended with status (`active` or `retired`), counter key (nullable), shop ID (D7), created at, retired at and version, with readability and capacity kept as integers in units of 0.0001 g, plus a List Scales operation that returns active scales by default and all scales when asked
- **So that:** every weighing in the shop can point at one stored scale whose smallest step and heaviest load are exact and survive a reload (BR-14-1, BR-14-8, FR-14-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when the `scales` table is inspected, then `readability` and `capacity` are integer columns in units of 0.0001 g, `status` accepts only `active` or `retired`, `counter_key` and `retired_at` are nullable, and `version` starts at 1.
  2. Given a scale row with readability `1` and capacity `6000000`, when List Scales returns it, then it reads "reads to 0.0001 g · up to 600.0000 g" in grams with 4 decimals, converted by the EP-02-S2 helpers.
  3. Given an insert with readability `0`, a negative readability, capacity `0` or status `broken`, when it is written straight to the database, then the database check rejects it.
  4. Given one active and one retired scale, when Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls List Scales with no filter, then only the active scale is returned; when Sanjay Seth (Owner) calls it with "include retired", then both are returned with their status.
  5. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar), when he calls List Scales, then the server refuses with `forbidden`.
  6. Given Sanjay Seth registers a scale with a request that also names a location id, when it is stored, then its `location_id` is the shop's default location "Main shop", set by the server, and the client value is ignored.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Scales is allowed for `owner` and `staff` and refused for `karigar` (EP-05-S2). Database checks: readability greater than 0, capacity greater than 0, status enum. Weights are converted only through the shared helpers (EP-02-S2), never with float arithmetic.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage and a read; changes are audited through EP-14-S12.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `scales` (created in EP-02-S4) adds `status` (default `active`), `counter_key` (nullable), `created_at`, `retired_at` (nullable) and `version`. Migration creates `user_scale_preference` (user id, last scale id, updated at) for EP-14-S9. Adds List Scales to the shared contract (EP-03-S1). Uses `scales.location_id` from EP-02-S4 (not null, default location "Main shop").
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: readability and capacity are integers of 0.0001 g; the half-step ceiling unit is settled under G10, not here. Time: created at and retired at stored in UTC. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; the table carries the shop ID (EP-02-S3) and no branch key. Open decision D9: if weights are read from the balance, the registry may later need model, port and serial number; not added in this story.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-14-S2: System can seed the bench balance and platform scale for dev

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can seed the bench balance and platform scale for dev
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the dev and staging seed to create two active scales, "Bench balance" reading to 0.0001 g up to 600 g and "Platform scale" reading to 0.01 g up to 30 kg, with the new registry columns filled
- **So that:** parcel arrival, tagging and the ceiling can be built and demoed against the same two scales mockup 14 shows (epic section 4, seed records)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an empty dev database after migrations, when the seed runs, then `scales` holds "Bench balance" with readability `1` and capacity `6000000`, and "Platform scale" with readability `100` and capacity `300000000`, both `active`, version 1 and no counter key.
  2. Given the seed has already run, when it runs again, then no duplicate scales are created and existing rows are not overwritten.
  3. Given the seeded scales, when Rajesh Verma opens the scale picker on `parcel-arrival`, then it offers "Bench balance · 0.0001 g" and "Platform scale · 0.01 g".
  4. Given a production environment, when the api starts, then this seed does not run, and the real shop scales are loaded by EP-41 instead.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The seed runs only in dev and staging (EP-02-S13), never in production. The seed matches scales by name so a rerun does not duplicate them.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Seed data is loaded by the developer's tooling, not by a person in the product.
- **Data changes:** Inserts two `scales` rows in dev and staging. No schema change.

- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: seed values are written as integers of 0.0001 g, converted from the strings "0.0001", "600", "0.01" and "30000" by the EP-02-S2 helpers. Open question: the real shop scales may differ from these values; the seed is for dev only.

## EP-14-S3: Owner can register a scale

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can register a scale
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to add a scale on `scales` with a name, a smallest step in grams and a heaviest load in grams, through a Create Scale operation that returns the new id
- **So that:** each scale in the shop is named once with its smallest step, and staff never retype it (FR-14-1, FR-14-2, FR-14-3, BR-14-1, BR-14-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth on `scales`, when he adds "Counter 2 balance" reading 0.001 g up to 200 g, then a scale is stored with readability `10`, capacity `2000000` and status `active`, the new id is returned, it appears in the picker on `parcel-arrival`, and an audit entry records it (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the name is empty or only spaces, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with "Name the scale." and nothing is stored.
  3. Given the smallest step is 0, negative or empty, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with "Enter the smallest step the scale reads." and nothing is stored.
  4. Given the heaviest load is 0, negative or empty, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with "Enter the heaviest load the scale can take, in grams." and nothing is stored.
  5. Given a smallest step with more than 4 decimals, such as 0.00005, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error, because it cannot be stored in 0.0001 g units.
  6. Given the same Create Scale request is sent twice with one idempotency key after a network drop, when the server processes it, then only one scale is created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-14-S4). Name required and trimmed. Readability and capacity parsed by the EP-02-S2 helpers and both must be greater than 0. The server sets the id, status `active`, created at and version; the client cannot send them. Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Create and audit in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (scale id), action (`scale_added`), after (name, readability, capacity, status). Written through EP-14-S12.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `scales`. Adds Create Scale to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Route `scales` (owner rail "Scales & rules"). The add scale form is not yet designed; the prototype `ScaleForm` fields and messages are reused until the design pass.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: 0.001 g is stored as `10` and read back as "0.0010 g"; no float multiplication. Security: the form's client checks are only a convenience; the server repeats them.
- **Depends on:** EP-14-S1, EP-14-S4, EP-02-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-14-S4: System can refuse scale changes from anyone but the owner

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse scale changes from anyone but the owner
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Create Scale, Update Scale, Update Scale status and Update Scale assignment to check the caller's role on the server before validation, and refuse every role other than owner with "Only the owner can change the scales."
- **So that:** the readability behind every match ceiling can only be changed by the owner, not by a staff member calling the operation directly (FR-14-4, BR-14-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Create Scale directly, then the server refuses with code `forbidden` and the sentence "Only the owner can change the scales.", and no scale is stored (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh, when he calls Update Scale to change the Bench balance readability from 0.0001 g to 0.001 g, then the server refuses the same way and the readability stays `1`.
  3. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar), when he calls any of the four scale change operations, then the server refuses with "Only the owner can change the scales."
  4. Given Rajesh sends a request that is also invalid, such as an empty name, when the server checks it, then he gets the role refusal, not the validation sentence.
  5. Given Rajesh is refused, when the log is checked, then no audit entry and no change to `scales` exist for that request.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The role check runs before validation and before any write (deny by default, EP-05-S2). The four operations are listed as owner-only in the permission matrix (EP-05-S1). Update My last scale (EP-14-S9) is not a scale change and stays open to staff.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused request changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** Adds the four scale change operations to the permission matrix as owner-only. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The `scales` route is on the owner rail only (EP-08-S13); the refusal sentence shows through EP-08-S5 if reached.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: hiding `scales` from staff is not the control; the server check is.
- **Depends on:** EP-14-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S4, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to open a scale on `scales` and change its name, smallest step or heaviest load, saving with the version I last read
- **So that:** a typo or a corrected readability can be fixed in one place without registering a new scale (FR-14-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth opens "Counter 2 balance" (version 1), when he renames it "Counter 2 bench balance" and saves, then the name changes, the version becomes 2, and an audit entry records before and after names.

  4. Given Sanjay clears the name or enters a smallest step of 0, when he saves, then the server refuses with "Name the scale." or "Enter the smallest step the scale reads." and nothing changes.
  5. Given another owner session saved the scale after Sanjay read it, when Sanjay saves with version 1 while the stored version is 2, then the server refuses as a conflict and nothing changes.

- **UI reference:** Route `scales`. The edit scale form is not yet designed; the prototype `ScaleForm` is reused until the design pass.

## EP-14-S6: System can apply the decided rule when a scale used by open parcels is edited

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can apply the decided rule when a scale used by open parcels is edited
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an Update Scale that changes readability to first find the open parcels (not yet released) with weighings on that scale, and then apply one decided rule: either each weighing keeps the readability it was taken with, or the edit is refused while the scale is in use
- **So that:** correcting a readability never flips the verdict of an open parcel without anyone noticing (FR-14-5, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given parcel BATCH-2026-044 is open with 13 weighings on the Bench balance, when Sanjay Seth changes the Bench balance readability from 0.0001 g to 0.001 g, then the server applies the decided rule, and the result is one of the two in criteria 2 and 3.
  2. Given the decided rule is "keep the old figure", when the edit commits, then each existing weighing on BATCH-2026-044 keeps readability `1` stored on the weighing, its ceiling stays 13 × ½ × 0.0001 g, and only weighings taken after the edit use `10`.
  3. Given the decided rule is "block edits while used", when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with a sentence naming the open parcels that use the scale, for example BATCH-2026-044, and the readability stays `1`.
  4. Given no open parcel has a weighing on the scale, when Sanjay changes its readability, then the edit commits with no further check.
  5. Given a name or capacity change only, when Sanjay saves, then this rule is not applied, because neither affects a ceiling.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The open-parcel check and the edit run in one transaction so a weighing saved at the same moment is either counted or blocked (EP-03-S6). Which rule applies is the open question in this epic's section 17; until it is answered the server uses "block edits while used", which changes nothing that is already stored.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. EP-23 recomputes verdicts when it next evaluates a parcel (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes when the edit commits: actor, time, entity (scale id), action (`scale_edited`), before, after, and the open parcel ids affected. No when the edit is refused.
- **Data changes:** If "keep the old figure" is chosen, migration adds `readability_at_weighing` (integer, 0.0001 g units) to the weighing rows from EP-02-S6 and to `pieces`, filled from the scale at save time. If "block edits" is chosen, no schema change.
- **UI reference:** Route `scales`. The message or confirmation for an edit on a scale in use is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: an edit and a parcel evaluation at the same moment use one consistent version of the scale. Audit: affected open parcels listed in the entry. Open question: when the owner edits the readability of a scale already used by open parcels, do those parcels keep the old figure or take the new one; criteria 2 and 3 are written for either answer.
- **Depends on:** EP-14-S1, EP-02-S6, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- **So that:** the picker lists the scales at a staff member's own counter first and staff are less likely to pick a scale from another counter (FR-14-7)

## EP-14-S10: System can compute the ceiling server-side from the registry

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can compute the ceiling server-side from the registry
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one ceiling function in the shared package, `ceiling = Σ ½ × readability` over every weighing, that reads each weighing's scale from the registry, returns rows per scale with count and subtotal, the total and a plain line, and runs on the server as the authority while the client runs the same code for instant feedback
- **So that:** the exact-match gate in EP-23 uses a ceiling computed only from the scales used, never a configured tolerance, and never from parcel size, piece count or value (FR-14-9, FR-14-10, FR-14-11, BR-14-3, BR-14-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a parcel weighed once and 12 pieces tagged, all on the Bench balance, when the server computes the ceiling, then it is 13 × ½ × 0.0001 g = 0.00065 g, the plain line reads "13 weighings × ½ × 0.0001 g", and the total is shown with the display rounding decided under G10 (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given a 10 kg parcel weighed once on the Platform scale and 300 pieces on the Bench balance, when the ceiling is computed, then it is 0.0200 g and the line shows "300 × 0.00005 + 1 × 0.005" (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given 300 pieces and 20 trays, all on the Bench balance, when the ceiling is computed, then it is 320 × ½ × 0.0001 g = 0.0160 g.
  4. Given a weighing whose scale id is not in the registry, when the server computes the ceiling, then it refuses with "Pick the scale this was weighed on." (FR-14-14).
  5. Given the client and the server compute the ceiling for the same weighings, when the results are compared, then they are identical, and EP-23 uses only the server result.
  6. Given a parcel with 500 weighings, when the server computes its ceiling, then it finishes in under 10 ms.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The function takes only weighings and their scales; it has no tolerance input and no parameter for parcel size, piece count or value. It reads one consistent version of each scale. If EP-14-S6 chooses "keep the old figure", it uses each weighing's stored readability. Arithmetic is integer only. Compute Ceiling is readable by Owner and Staff and refused for Karigar.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. The ceiling is computed, not stored.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the ceiling function to the shared package and Compute Ceiling to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/14-match-rule-any-parcel.svg` ("THE ONLY RULE — IT HAS NO SETTINGS", "ceiling = sum of ( ½ × the scale's smallest step ) for every weighing taken", "0.0007 g", "0.0200 g", "0.0160 g"). The ceiling is shown on the gate screens built in EP-23.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: a half-step of 0.0001 g (0.00005 g) is not a whole number of 0.0001 g units, so the function must stay exact, for example by summing readability units and comparing 2 × gap with that sum; the stored and display unit is settled under G10. Concurrency: one version of each scale per computation. Performance: under 10 ms for 500 weighings (proposed target, to confirm). Open decision G10: the unit and display rounding of 0.00065 g (mockup 14 shows 0.0007 g).
- **Depends on:** EP-14-S1, EP-14-S6, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S6, EP-03-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-14-S12: System can audit every scale change

- **Story ID:** EP-14-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit every scale change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every committed add, edit, retire, reactivate and assignment of a scale to write an audit entry in the same transaction, with actor, time, scale id, action and before and after values
- **So that:** the owner can see who changed a readability and when, because that change alters every future ceiling (FR-14-13, BR-14-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth adds "Counter 2 balance", when it commits, then one audit entry exists with kind `scale_added`, ref the new scale id, after {name "Counter 2 balance", readability 0.0010 g, capacity 200.0000 g, status `active`}, actor Sanjay Seth and the server time.
  2. Given Sanjay changes the Bench balance readability from 0.0001 g to 0.001 g, when it commits, then the entry has kind `scale_edited`, before readability 0.0001 g and after 0.0010 g, written as integer 0.0001 g units (1 and 10).
  3. Given Sanjay retires, reactivates or assigns a scale, when it commits, then entries with kinds `scale_retired`, `scale_reactivated` or `scale_assigned` record before and after values.
  4. Given the audit write fails, when the transaction ends, then the scale change is not saved either.
  5. Given a save whose values equal the stored values, when it is processed, then no audit entry is written and the version does not change.
  6. Given Sanjay opens the security log and filters by entity "scale", then he sees these entries newest first; Rajesh Verma (Staff) reading them gets `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The change and its entry share one transaction (EP-06-S2). Before and after are recorded per field (EP-06-S3), weights as integer 0.0001 g units (EP-06-S5). Entries are append-only (EP-06-S1). Reads are Owner only (EP-06-S12).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (scale id), action (`scale_added`, `scale_edited`, `scale_retired`, `scale_reactivated`, `scale_assigned`), before, after.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). Adds the five scale kinds to the audit kind list. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show in the security log built in EP-06 (EP-06-S9, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S11).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every scale change, including name-only changes, writes an append-only entry. Precision: weights in entries are integer 0.0001 g units. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-14-S3, EP-14-S5, EP-14-S7, EP-14-S8, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S5, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- G10: should the stored unit be 0.0001 g as PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5 says, or a finer unit (the prototype uses 0.00001 g), or a doubled half-step unit, so the ceiling is exact? How is 0.00065 g displayed (mockup 14 rounds it to 0.0007 g)? (EP-14-S1, S10)
- What are the exact readabilities and capacities of the real scales in the shop? (SCOPE-ANALYSIS App. E "Still genuinely open") (EP-14-S2)
- D9: will weights be typed by hand or read directly from the balance, and does that change what the registry stores (model, port, serial number)? (EP-14-S1)
- When the owner edits the readability of a scale already used by open parcels, do those parcels keep the old figure or take the new one? (EP-14-S5, S6, S7)
- Should the registry hold calibration dates and block a scale past its calibration date? (EP-14-S1, S7)
- Is a scale tied to one counter, or can any staff use any scale? (EP-14-S8, S9)

# EP-15: Reference data · stories

Epic document: [EP-15 Reference data](../epics/EP-15-reference-data.md)

Role note: stories where the server stores, checks, generates or audits on its own use "System". Stories where a person maintains a list or the design master use "Owner", and the picker and sold-out stories use "Staff". Karigars only read the words on their own jobs in this epic.

---

## EP-15-S1: System can store categories, styles, purities, inclusion types and specialties as lists

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store categories, styles, purities, inclusion types and specialties as lists
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** five owner-maintained list tables, `categories`, `styles`, `purities`, `inclusion_types` and `specialties`, each entry with id, name, status (`active` or `retired`), sort order, created at and version, plus a List Reference operation that returns active entries in sort order by default and all entries when asked, and references from pieces, manifest rows, order copies, lead items and karigars to these entries in place of free text
- **So that:** "Temple Haram" on a manifest and "Temple haram" on a tag are the same stored entry, and every form reads one source of words (FR-15-1, FR-15-6, FR-15-7, FR-15-8, FR-15-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when the five list tables are inspected, then each has `id`, `name`, `status` accepting only `active` or `retired`, an integer `sort_order`, `created_at` and an integer `version` starting at 1.
  2. Given the `purities` table, when it is inspected, then it also has `label` (for example "22K") and `fineness` as an integer in parts per thousand between 1 and 999, and an insert with fineness `0`, `1000` or `91.6` is rejected by the database (FR-15-8).
  3. Given the `inclusion_types` table, when it is inspected, then it also has `unit` accepting only `g` or `ct`, and an insert with unit `mg` is rejected (FR-15-9).
  4. Given the category "Temple Haram" exists, when an insert of "temple haram" or " Temple Haram " is made in `categories`, then the database rejects it, because names are unique per list after trimming and ignoring case.
  5. Given the migrations have run, when `pieces`, `parcel_manifest_rows`, `order_copies`, `lead_items` and `karigars` are inspected, then they hold `category_id`, `style_id`, `purity_id` or `specialty_id` references to the list tables where they held free text before, and `lead_items` keeps a nullable free-text style beside a nullable `style_id` (FR-15-5).
  6. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls List Reference for styles, then active styles come back in sort order; given Sanjay Seth (Owner) asks with "include retired", then retired styles come back too with their status; given Vijay Kumar (Karigar) calls it, then he receives only entries referenced by his own jobs (EP-05-S3).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Reference is open to `owner` and `staff`; `karigar` reads are limited to entries on own jobs (EP-05-S3). Database checks: status enum, unit enum, fineness range, unique trimmed case-insensitive name per list. References use foreign keys so a stored record cannot point at an entry that does not exist. No entry is ever deleted, because records point at it.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Lists change rarely; pickers reload on next open (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage and a read; changes are audited through EP-15-S12.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `categories`, `styles`, `purities` (with `label`, `fineness`), `inclusion_types` (with `unit`) and `specialties`, each with the shop ID (EP-02-S3, D7). Migration adds `category_id`, `style_id` and `purity_id` to `pieces`, `category_id` to `parcel_manifest_rows`, `purity_id` (and `category_id`, `style_id`) to `order_copies`, nullable `style_id` to `lead_items`, and `specialty_id` to `karigars`; the old text columns are kept until EP-15-S2 (dev) and EP-41 (production) have mapped them. Adds List Reference to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: no weight fields are created here (epic section 9). Performance: all five lists together stay under a few hundred rows and load with the first screen in under 2 seconds (epic section 13). Open question: whether specialties are the same list as styles; if they are, `specialties` becomes a view over `styles` and `karigars.specialty_id` points at a style. D7 is decided: one shop; lists carry the shop ID, set by the server.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S5, EP-02-S6, EP-02-S7, EP-02-S8, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S2: System can seed the lists from the prototype values

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can seed the lists from the prototype values
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the dev and staging seed to fill the five lists from the prototype values and map the seeded free-text kinds, styles and purities on pieces, manifest rows, order copies and karigars to the new list entries
- **So that:** parcel arrival, tagging and the pickers can be built and demoed with the same words the prototype and mockups use (epic section 4, section 6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an empty dev database after migrations, when the seed runs, then `purities` holds 24K (999), 22K (916), 18K (750) and 14K (585) in that order, all `active`, taken from `PURITIES` in `src/components/parcels/util.ts`.
  2. Given the seed runs, when `styles` and `specialties` are read, then each holds Chettinad, Temple, Kundan, Polki, Antique, Jadau and Meenakari in that order, taken from `SPECIALTIES` in `src/components/people/OnboardKarigar.tsx`.
  3. Given the seed runs, when `categories` is read, then it holds every distinct kind in the prototype seed, including Temple Haram, Kundan Choker, Polki Kada, Meenakari Pendant, Temple Nakshi Ring, Kasu Mala, Jadau Emerald Ring, Antique Jhumka, Peacock Ruby Pendant and Meenakari Bangle, and `inclusion_types` holds stones, kemp, lac and pearls with a unit each.
  4. Given the seeded parcel BATCH-2026-044, when its manifest rows are read, then each row's `category_id` points at the matching category, and piece TAG-8841 has `style_id` Kundan and `purity_id` 22K.
  5. Given a seeded text value that matches no entry, such as the style "Nakshi", when the seed runs, then it adds that value as an entry and lists it in the seed output, rather than leaving the reference empty.
  6. Given the seed has already run, when it runs again, then no duplicate entries are created; given a production environment, then this seed does not run, and real lists are loaded by EP-41.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The seed runs only in dev and staging (EP-02-S13). Entries are matched by trimmed, case-insensitive name so a rerun does not duplicate them. Mapping text to entries uses the same name match.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Seed data is loaded by the developer's tooling, not by a person in the product.
- **Data changes:** Inserts rows into the five list tables in dev and staging, and fills the new reference columns from EP-15-S1 on seeded rows. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/20-parcel-arrival.svg`, route `parcel-arrival` (manifest kinds "Temple Haram · Chettinad", "Kundan Choker", "Polki Kada · pair", "Meenakari Pendant"); `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` (purity "22K (916)").
- **Non-functional checks:** Open question: which inclusion types exist and which are weighed in carats; the seed marks stones as `ct` and kemp, lac and pearls as `g` for dev only, to be replaced once answered. Open question: whether specialties are the same list as styles; the seed fills both with the same words either way.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-02-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S3: Owner can add, rename, reorder and retire a list entry

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can add, rename, reorder and retire a list entry
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to add an entry to any of the five lists, rename it, move it up or down, retire it and reactivate it, through Create Reference entry and Update Reference entry, saving with the version I last read
- **So that:** the shop's words are kept in one place by the owner, and a rename shows everywhere without changing what records point at (FR-15-2, FR-15-3, FR-15-6, FR-15-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth adds the category "Vanki", when it commits, then it is stored as `active` at the end of the sort order, the new id is returned, and the next time Rajesh Verma opens the manifest on `parcel-arrival`, "Vanki" is offered (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Sanjay renames the category "Polki Kada" to "Polki Kada pair", when it commits, then piece TAG-8802 and manifest rows that point at it keep the same `category_id` and show "Polki Kada pair" on their next read (FR-15-6).
  3. Given Sanjay retires the style "Antique", when Rajesh next opens the style picker on `parcel-tag`, then "Antique" is not offered, while piece TAG-7914 still shows "Antique" (FR-15-7).
  4. Given Sanjay adds "temple haram" while "Temple Haram" exists, or saves an empty name, when the server checks it, then it refuses with a sentence naming the problem and nothing is stored.
  5. Given Sanjay adds a purity, when he leaves the fineness empty or enters 1000, then the server refuses it; given he adds an inclusion type with no unit, then the server refuses it.
  6. Given Rajesh (Staff) or Vijay Kumar (Karigar) calls Create or Update Reference entry directly, when the server checks the role, then it refuses with `forbidden` and nothing changes (FR-15-3).
  7. Given another owner session saved the entry after Sanjay read it, when Sanjay saves with the older version, then the server refuses as a conflict and nothing changes.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only, checked before validation (EP-05-S2). Name required, trimmed, unique per list ignoring case among active and retired entries. Purity needs label and fineness 1 to 999; inclusion type needs unit `g` or `ct`. Status moves only between `active` and `retired`; there is no delete. Reorder rewrites `sort_order` for the list in one transaction. Stale version refused (EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5). Create is deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Change and audit in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Pickers pick up the change on next open (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (list and entry id), action (`reference_entry_added`, `reference_entry_renamed`, `reference_entry_reordered`, `reference_entry_retired`, `reference_entry_reactivated`), before, after. Written through EP-15-S12.
- **Data changes:** Inserts and updates rows in the five list tables (name, status, sort order, version). Adds Create Reference entry and Update Reference entry to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. No mockup draws a list maintenance screen for the owner (epic section 12); it is to be added to the owner rail in the design pass and uses the EP-08 data layer.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner-only on the server; hiding the screen from staff is not the control. Concurrency: version check on every save; two owners reordering one list at once cannot leave two entries with the same position. Audit: a rename changes what manifests show, so before and after names are always recorded.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S1, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S4: System can reject a stored value that is not an active list entry

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can reject a stored value that is not an active list entry
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one shared server check that every new manifest row, tag and order copy names an active category, style and purity, that keeps a retired entry valid on a record that already holds it, and that lets a lead item hold free-text style until the item is routed
- **So that:** no new record can carry a word that is not on the owner's lists, and retiring an entry never breaks an open parcel (FR-15-5, FR-15-7, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a new tag on BATCH-2026-044 whose `purity_id` points at no purity, when the shared check runs, then the server refuses it with code `validation` and a sentence naming the field, and nothing is stored.
  2. Given the style "Antique" is retired, when a new tag or order copy is saved with style "Antique", then the server refuses it with a sentence saying the style is no longer on the list.
  3. Given the category "Kasu Mala" was retired after it was put on the manifest of BATCH-2026-044, when a staff member saves a tag of kind "Kasu Mala" against that manifest row, then the check accepts it, because the entry is already on the record (epic section 16 risk).
  4. Given a lead item with free-text style "Chettinad nakshi work" and no `style_id`, when the lead is saved, then the check accepts it; when the item is routed to `make`, then the server refuses until a style entry is picked (FR-15-5).
  5. Given a request sends the free text "Temple Haram" in place of a category id, when the contract check runs, then the request is rejected as a validation error, because writes carry ids, not words.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Writes carry list ids only (EP-03-S2). A new record needs active entries; an existing record keeps its entries even if retired, and an update that changes an entry needs an active one. The check is a shared function in the service layer, called by the manifest, tag and order copy operations that EP-19 and EP-21 build. Refusals use the EP-03-S4 code and sentence format.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused write changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the shared active-entry check to the service layer.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The refusal sentence shows through EP-08-S5 on `parcel-arrival`, `parcel-tag`, `order-copy` and `lead-create` once those forms are built.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the picker only offering active entries is a convenience; the server check is the control. Concurrency: an entry retired while a tag is being saved is either accepted before the retire or refused after it, in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S5: Staff can pick categories, styles and purities from server lists on every form

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can pick categories, styles and purities from server lists on every form
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** one shared picker for each list, loaded through the EP-08 data layer from List Reference, that offers active entries in the owner's sort order, shows purities as "22K (916)", and stores the entry id
- **So that:** every form on `parcel-arrival`, `parcel-tag`, `lead-create`, `order-copy` and `karigar-new` offers the same words, and I never type a kind or purity freehand (FR-15-4, BR-15-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma opens the purity picker, when the list arrives, then it offers "24K (999)", "22K (916)", "18K (750)" and "14K (585)" in that order, and picking "22K (916)" sends the purity id, not the text (BR-15-8).
  2. Given Sanjay Seth added the category "Vanki" while Rajesh's screen was open, when Rajesh next opens the category picker, then "Vanki" is offered (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  3. Given a record holds the retired style "Antique", when Rajesh opens it for editing, then the picker shows "Antique" as the current value marked as retired, and does not offer it for any other record.
  4. Given the list is still loading, when Rajesh opens a picker, then it shows the EP-08-S3 loading state; given the read fails, then it shows the EP-08-S4 error with "Try again".
  5. Given the category picker on `parcel-tag` for BATCH-2026-044, when it is opened, then it offers only the kinds on that parcel's manifest with how many are still to tag, for example "Temple Haram · Chettinad · 1 of these still to tag" (BR-15-4).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Reference returns active entries in sort order; the client never adds entries. Whatever the picker sends is checked again by EP-15-S4. The forms themselves are built in EP-16, EP-19, EP-21 and EP-28, which use this picker.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Pickers reload on next open (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Picking an option reads data only.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the shared category, style, purity, inclusion type and specialty pickers to the web app, each reading through the EP-08 cache.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` ("Kind of item", "Temple Haram · Chettinad", "picked from the manifest · 1 of these still to tag", "Purity", "22K (916)"); `docs/ux/mockups/20-parcel-arrival.svg`, route `parcel-arrival` ("SAY WHAT IS INSIDE · MIXED IS FINE", "Add another kind of item"); routes `lead-create`, `order-copy` and `karigar-new` reuse the same pickers.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the lists are cached by EP-08-S2 and load with the first screen in under 2 seconds. Availability: offline, the picker shows the last cached list read-only and saving is disabled (EP-08-S11).
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-15-S2, EP-15-S4, EP-08-S1, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S6: System can generate the next tag number in the decided format without duplicates

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can generate the next tag number in the decided format without duplicates
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Reserve Next tag number operation backed by one counter row that is incremented atomically, formatted by the decided pattern, and never hands the same number to two callers
- **So that:** the tag number on `parcel-tag` is suggested rather than typed, and two staff tagging one parcel at the same moment never get the same number (FR-15-10, BR-15-5, epic section 13 concurrency)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the highest tag number in use is TAG-9107, when Rajesh Verma opens "Tag item 8 of 12" on `parcel-tag`, then "New tag number" is filled with the next number in the decided format, for example TAG-9108 (BR-15-5).
  2. Given Rajesh and Deepak Rao are tagging BATCH-2026-044, when both ask for a suggested tag number at the same moment, then they receive different numbers (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  3. Given a test that sends 50 concurrent Reserve calls, when they finish, then 50 distinct numbers are returned and the counter has moved by exactly 50.
  4. Given Rajesh was given a number and chooses "Save and stop here" without saving the tag, when the next Reserve call is made, then that number is not given to anyone else.
  5. Given the counter is created on a database that already holds pieces, when it is initialised, then it starts above the highest number in use, as `nextTagNumber` does today.
  6. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar) calls Reserve Next tag number, when the server checks the role, then it refuses with `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Reserve is allowed for `owner` and `staff` only (EP-05-S2). The counter is incremented and read in one atomic statement inside a transaction (EP-03-S6). The format pattern is stored on the server, not in the client. A suggested number is still checked for uniqueness at save time (EP-15-S7). The same Reserve request retried with one idempotency key returns the same number (EP-03-S8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Tag progress between staff on one parcel travels on "Tag saved on a shared parcel", which EP-21 owns (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. A suggested number is not a change to shop records until a tag is saved.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `tag_format` (pattern, next number, year if the counter resets yearly, version), initialised from the highest number in `pieces`. Adds Reserve Next tag number to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` ("New tag number", "TAG-9108", "The tag number and HUID are suggested").
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the generator is atomic; two callers never share a number. Time: if the counter resets each year, the year is taken from the server clock in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: format `TAG-NNNN` (prototype, `nextTagNumber`) or `TAG-YYYY-NNNN` (mockup 03 "TAG-2026-8841"), and whether the counter resets each year; criteria 1 to 5 hold for either.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-02-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S7: System can reject a tag number used on another piece

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can reject a tag number used on another piece
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every tag save to check the tag number, trimmed and upper-cased, against all pieces in every parcel and status, and refuse a used one with "`<tag>` is already used on another piece."
- **So that:** a tag number identifies exactly one piece in the shop for its whole life (FR-15-11, BR-15-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given TAG-8841 exists on a piece from BATCH-2026-041, when Rajesh Verma saves a tag on BATCH-2026-044 with TAG-8841, then the server refuses with "TAG-8841 is already used on another piece." and nothing is stored (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh types " tag-8841 ", when the server checks it, then it is trimmed and upper-cased to TAG-8841 before the check and refused the same way.
  3. Given an empty tag number, when Rajesh saves, then the server refuses with "Give the piece a tag number."
  4. Given TAG-7914 belongs to a piece that is `billed` or `scrapped`, when a new tag is saved with TAG-7914, then the server refuses it, because a number is never reused.
  5. Given two saves with the same typed number arrive at the same moment, when both commit, then the unique index lets exactly one succeed and the other gets the same refusal sentence.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Tag numbers are normalised (trim, upper case) and unique across all pieces by a database unique index (EP-02-S5), with the check repeated in the service so the refusal carries the sentence (EP-03-S4). A unique-index violation is mapped to the same sentence, not to a generic conflict.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused save changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** Migration normalises existing tag numbers to upper case and confirms the unique index on `pieces` tag number. No new table.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` ("New tag number"); the sentence shows through EP-08-S5.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: uniqueness holds under simultaneous saves through the index, not only the service check. Open question: if both `TAG-8841` and `TAG-2026-8841` exist after migration, they are different strings to this check; the format decision in EP-15-S6 settles whether one is migrated to the other (epic section 16 risk).
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S6, EP-02-S5, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S8: System can check HUID format and uniqueness

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can check HUID format and uniqueness
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Check HUID operation and the same check on every tag save, which trims and upper-cases the HUID, checks it against the stored HUID rule (6 characters, letters A to Z and digits 0 to 9), and, if HUID uniqueness is confirmed, refuses one already used on another piece
- **So that:** a mistyped hallmark code is caught at tagging, not at QC or sale (FR-15-12, BR-15-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma enters "9X82K" (5 characters), when he saves the tag, then the server refuses it as the wrong format with a sentence giving the rule, for example "A HUID is 6 letters and digits, like 9X82K1." (proposed wording), and nothing is stored (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given Rajesh enters "4t71m9 ", when the server checks it, then it is stored as 4T71M9 and accepted.
  3. Given Rajesh enters "4T71-M9" or "4T71M9X", when the server checks it, then it is refused for the wrong characters or length.
  4. Given HUID uniqueness is confirmed and 9X82K1 is on TAG-2026-8841, when Rajesh saves another piece with 9X82K1, then the server refuses with a sentence naming the piece that holds it.
  5. Given the `parcel-tag` form, when Rajesh leaves the HUID field, then the client runs the same shared check and shows the sentence straight away, and the server repeats it on save.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The HUID rule (length, allowed characters) is stored on the server and shared with the client. Format is checked on every save and in Check HUID; uniqueness is enforced by a unique index on the normalised HUID only once confirmed. Check HUID is allowed for `owner`, `staff` and System callers, refused for `karigar`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A check or a refused save changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `huid_rule` (length 6, allowed characters, unique flag, version). If uniqueness is confirmed, migration adds a unique index on the normalised HUID in `pieces`. Adds Check HUID to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` ("Hallmark HUID", "4T71M9"); `docs/ux/mockups/03-showroom-stock.svg`, route `stock` ("BIS hallmark", "9X82K1"); `docs/ux/mockups/07-qc-check.svg`, route `parcel-qc` ("HUID on the tag", "8H33Z9").
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the client check is a convenience; the server repeats it. Concurrency: if uniqueness is on, two saves with one HUID at once let only one succeed through the index. Open question: the full HUID rule and whether HUID must be unique across all pieces; criterion 4 applies only once uniqueness is confirmed. Open question: whether a HUID is required on every piece is not settled here, so an empty HUID passes this check.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-02-S5, EP-03-S4, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S9: System can record an inclusion's unit as grams or carats

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can record an inclusion's unit as grams or carats
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** itemised inclusion rows on a piece, each pointing at an inclusion type, holding its weight as an integer in units of 0.0001 g and, for types recorded in carats, the carat figure stored alongside the gram figure
- **So that:** "Emerald 3.100 cts" is kept as the karigar wrote it while the match gate still works only in grams (FR-15-9, BR-15-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the inclusion type "stones" has unit `ct`, when an inclusion "Emerald 3.100 cts" is stored on TAG-9110 with a gram figure of 0.6200 g, then the row holds carats `3100` (thousandths of a carat) and weight `6200` (0.0001 g units), and reads back as "Emerald 3.100 cts · 0.6200 g".
  2. Given the inclusion type "lac" has unit `g`, when "Lac and foil 1.150 g" is stored, then the row holds weight `11500` and no carat figure.
  3. Given a carat figure is sent for a type with unit `g`, or a type with unit `ct` is sent with no carat figure, when the server checks it, then it refuses the row as a validation error.
  4. Given a gram figure with more than 4 decimals, such as 0.62005 g, when the server checks it, then it refuses it, because it cannot be stored in 0.0001 g units.
  5. Given the piece with five inclusion rows, when it is read, then the rows come back in stored position order, matching "Weight breakdown · 5 inclusions" on `stock`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Inclusion type must be an active list entry for new rows (EP-15-S4). Unit `ct` requires a carat figure; unit `g` forbids one. Grams are parsed by the EP-02-S2 helpers, never by float arithmetic. Whether the rows must add up to the piece's stone weight is checked by EP-21, not here. Only the gram figure is used by the match gate (EP-23).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Inclusion rows are written as part of a tag save, audited by EP-21.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `piece_inclusions` (piece id, position, inclusion type id, label, weight integer in 0.0001 g units, carats integer in 0.001 ct units nullable). No money fields.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/21-tag-one-item.svg`, route `parcel-tag` ("Stones, kemp, lac on this piece", "itemise →"); `docs/ux/mockups/07-qc-check.svg`, route `parcel-qc` ("Emerald 3.100 cts · Polki 2.400 cts", "Lac and foil 1.150 g"); `docs/ux/mockups/03-showroom-stock.svg`, route `stock` ("Weight breakdown · 5 inclusions"). The itemise form is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: grams stored as integers of 0.0001 g and shown to 4 decimals; carats stored as integers of 0.001 ct. Open question: how stone carats are converted to grams and to how many decimals; until answered, the gram figure is entered with the carat figure and no conversion is done on the server; once decided, the conversion must produce integer 0.0001 g units.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-15-S4, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S10: Owner can keep a design master that pieces point to (G3)

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can keep a design master that pieces point to (G3)
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to create, rename and retire designs, each with a name, a category, a style, an optional maker karigar and reference images, and to set which design a piece belongs to
- **So that:** "Sold out" and "Asked for 4 times since July" can be counted per design, and EP-19 can reorder a sold-out design from its maker (FR-15-14, BR-15-6, gap G3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth creates the design "Peacock Ruby Pendant" with category Meenakari Pendant, style Antique, maker Vijay Kumar (KG-04) and one reference image, when it commits, then the design is stored as `active`, the new id is returned and the image is linked by its file id.
  2. Given piece TAG-7914 "Peacock Ruby Pendant", when Sanjay sets its design to "Peacock Ruby Pendant", then `pieces.design_id` points at the design, and the piece's own category and style are unchanged.
  3. Given a design with category "Temple Haram", when a piece of that design is tagged on `parcel-tag`, then no gross, stone or net weight is filled in from the design (FR-15-13, BR-15-1).
  4. Given Sanjay renames or retires a design, when it commits, then pieces keep their `design_id`, a retired design is not offered for new pieces, and an audit entry records before and after.
  5. Given the decided rule lets only the owner create designs, when Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Create Design, then the server refuses with `forbidden`; Update Design is refused for staff and karigars in every case.
  6. Given a design's category or style is not an active list entry, when Sanjay saves it, then the server refuses it (EP-15-S4).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Design is allowed for Owner, and for Staff only if the G3 decision allows it; Update Design is Owner only (EP-05-S2). Name required and trimmed. Category and style must be active entries; maker must be an existing karigar or empty; reference images must be file ids the caller may attach (EP-09-S6). A design has no weight fields. No design is deleted. Stale version refused; create deduplicated by idempotency key.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (design id), action (`design_added`, `design_edited`, `design_retired`, `piece_design_set`), before, after. Written through EP-15-S12.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `designs` (id, name, category id, style id, maker karigar id nullable, status, created at, version) and `design_images` (design id, position, file id). Migration adds nullable `design_id` to `pieces` and, if G3 counts asks per design, to `lead_items`. Adds Create, Read and Update Design to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. Mockup `docs/ux/mockups/03-showroom-stock.svg`, route `stock`, shows the design's facts ("Peacock Ruby Pendant", "Made by", "Reordered before 3 times") but no design form is drawn.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: no weight is stored on a design (BR-15-1). Security: image links follow the EP-09 signed-link and role checks. Open question G3: what a design is (same name and style, or an explicit record), and who creates it; criteria 1 to 6 assume an explicit record. Risk: keep the design to the fields needed for "Sold out" and reorder (epic section 16).
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S1, EP-15-S4, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-09-S1, EP-09-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-15-S11: Staff can see a design marked sold out when none is in stock (G3)

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see a design marked sold out when none is in stock (G3)
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** Read Design to return, per design, the count of pieces in stock, pieces billed and times asked for, and to derive "Sold out" when no piece of the design is in stock, plus a count of sold-out designs for the stock screen
- **So that:** "Sold out" is a fact about a design that the server computes, not a piece state someone sets (FR-15-15, BR-15-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the design "Peacock Ruby Pendant" has one piece TAG-7914 with status `billed` and no piece with status `in_stock`, when Rajesh Verma reads the design, then it returns in stock 0, billed 1 and sold out true (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  2. Given a new piece of that design is released into stock with status `in_stock`, when the design is read again, then sold out is false and in stock is 1.
  3. Given nine designs have no piece in stock, when the stock screen asks for the sold-out count, then the server returns 9, matching "Sold out · 9" on `stock`.
  4. Given the decided way of counting asks, when the design is read, then times asked for is returned, for example "Asked for 4 times since July", counted on the server from the decided source.
  5. Given a design with no pieces at all, when it is read, then it is not counted as sold out, because it has never been in stock.
  6. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar), when he calls Read Design, then the server refuses with `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Counts are computed on the server from `pieces.status` and `design_id`; no "sold out" flag is stored on a piece or a design. Read Design is Owner and Staff only (EP-05-S2). The showroom filter and its card are built in EP-22 on top of this read.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story. EP-22 refreshes the stock counts when a piece's state changes.
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story reads and counts only.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database beyond the `design_id` columns from EP-15-S10. Adds the counts to Read Design and a Count Sold-out designs read to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/03-showroom-stock.svg`, route `stock` ("Sold out · 9", "Sold out", "Peacock Ruby Pendant", "Asked for 4 times since July", "Order another from Vijay"). The filter and the reorder action are built in EP-22 and EP-19.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the sold-out count over all designs returns in under 500 ms for a shop with a few thousand pieces (proposed target, to confirm). Open question G3: how "Asked for 4 times since July" is counted (lead items pointing at a design, or name matching), and whether a design with no pieces yet can be sold out; criteria 4 and 5 are written neutrally.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S10, EP-02-S5, EP-02-S7, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
