## EP-15-S12: System can audit changes to reference lists

- **Story ID:** EP-15-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit changes to reference lists
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every add, rename, reorder, retire and reactivate of a list entry, every change to the tag format or HUID rule, and every design change to write one audit entry in the same transaction, with before and after values
- **So that:** the owner can see who renamed a category and when, because a rename changes what every manifest shows (epic section 13 audit)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth adds the category "Vanki", when it commits, then one audit entry exists with kind `reference_entry_added`, ref the category id, after {list "categories", name "Vanki", status `active`}, actor Sanjay Seth and the server time.
  2. Given Sanjay renames "Polki Kada" to "Polki Kada pair", when it commits, then the entry has kind `reference_entry_renamed`, before name "Polki Kada" and after name "Polki Kada pair".
  3. Given Sanjay retires, reactivates or reorders an entry, or changes a design, when it commits, then entries with kinds `reference_entry_retired`, `reference_entry_reactivated`, `reference_entry_reordered`, `design_added`, `design_edited`, `design_retired` or `piece_design_set` record before and after values.
  4. Given the audit write fails, when the transaction ends, then the list change is not saved either.
  5. Given a save whose values equal the stored values, when it is processed, then no audit entry is written and the version does not change.
  6. Given Sanjay opens the security log and filters by entity "reference list", then he sees these entries newest first; Rajesh Verma (Staff) reading them gets `forbidden`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The change and its entry share one transaction (EP-06-S2). Before and after are recorded per field (EP-06-S3). Entries are append-only (EP-06-S1). Reads are Owner only (EP-06-S12).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (list and entry id, or design id), action (`reference_entry_added`, `reference_entry_renamed`, `reference_entry_reordered`, `reference_entry_retired`, `reference_entry_reactivated`, `tag_format_changed`, `huid_rule_changed`, `design_added`, `design_edited`, `design_retired`, `piece_design_set`), before, after.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). Adds the reference list and design kinds to the audit kind list by migration. No other schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show in the security log built in EP-06 (EP-06-S9, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S11).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every list change, including a reorder, writes an append-only entry. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-15-S3, EP-15-S6, EP-15-S8, EP-15-S10, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-16: Karigar master · stories

Epic document: [EP-16 Karigar master](../epics/EP-16-karigar-master.md)

Role note: stories where the server stores, checks, computes or audits on its own use "System". Stories where a person keeps karigar records or reads the directory and scorecard use "Owner", the picker story uses "Staff", and the profile story uses "Karigar".

---

## EP-16-S1: System can store karigar records with code, phone, location, specialties, language and allowance

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store karigar records with code, phone, location, specialties, language and allowance
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `karigars` table from EP-02-S4 extended with workshop location, status (`active` or `deactivated`), deactivated at, wastage allowance as an integer in basis points, language with default `English`, open since and version, a `karigar_specialties` child table so one karigar can hold several specialties, and a counter that hands out the next `KG-NN` code
- **So that:** each karigar is one stored record the order copy, the parcel forms, the portal and the scorecard can all point at, with an allowance that is exact and survives a reload (FR-16-2, FR-16-14, BR-16-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `karigars` is inspected, then it has `id` (`KG-NN`), shop ID, `name`, `phone`, `email` (not null), `workshop_location`, `language` accepting only `Tamil`, `Hindi` or `English` with default `English`, `wastage_bp` as an integer, `status` accepting only `active` or `deactivated`, nullable `deactivated_at`, `open_since` and an integer `version` starting at 1.
  2. Given an insert with `wastage_bp` 59 or 121, or a value such as 0.7 that is not an integer, when it is written straight to the database, then the database check rejects it, and 60 to 120 (0.60% to 1.20%) are accepted (BR-16-1).
  3. Given the migrations have run, when `karigar_specialties` is inspected, then it holds `karigar_id` and `specialty_id` referencing the EP-15 `specialties` list, with one row per pair, and the single `karigars.specialty_id` column added by EP-15-S1 has been moved into it.
  4. Given the seeded karigars KG-01 Lakshmi Devi (0.7%), KG-02 Mahesh Soni (0.8%) and KG-04 Vijay Kumar (0.8%), when the migration has run, then they hold `wastage_bp` 70, 80 and 80, status `active`, and their prototype language values (Tamil, Hindi, Hindi) unchanged.
  5. Given the highest code ever issued is KG-04, when the code counter is initialised, then its next value is 5, so the next code is KG-05 and the gap at KG-03 is never filled (FR-16-2).
  6. Given 20 concurrent requests for the next code, when they finish, then 20 distinct codes are returned and the counter has moved by exactly 20.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Database checks: `wastage_bp` between 60 and 120, status enum, language enum, name not empty. The code counter is incremented and read in one atomic statement inside a transaction (EP-03-S6); codes are never reused, even after deactivation. Codes are two digits up to KG-99 and grow to three digits after that. The account link is kept once, as `users.karigarId` with a unique index (EP-02-S3, EP-05-S13), and is not duplicated on `karigars`. No weight or money column is added to `karigars`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage; changes are audited through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `karigars` (EP-02-S4) adds `workshop_location`, `status` (default `active`), `deactivated_at`, `wastage_bp` (converted from the prototype percentage), sets the `language` default to `English`, and adds `version` if missing. Migration creates `karigar_specialties` (karigar id, specialty id) and `karigar_code_counter` (next number), initialised above the highest code in use. Adds `email` (required, D4). Each table has the shop ID (EP-02-S3); `id` and `phone` are unique per shop (D7).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the allowance is an integer in basis points (0.70% = 70), never a float (epic section 13). Personal data: `phone` and `workshop_location` are personal data and are returned only to the owner and to the karigar themself. Open question: whether the workshop location is free text or an address with a map pin; this story stores free text. D7 is decided: one shop; records carry the shop ID set by the server, never from the request.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S3, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S6, EP-15-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S2: System can refuse karigar changes from anyone but the owner

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse karigar changes from anyone but the owner
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Create Karigar, Update Karigar details, Update Karigar wastage, Update Karigar status and Update Karigar account link to check the caller's role on the server before validation, and to refuse every role other than owner with "Only the owner can add a karigar or change their wastage allowance."
- **So that:** the allowance every job is judged against, and the record a karigar signs in with, can only be changed by the owner (FR-16-5, BR-16-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Create Karigar directly with "Ravi Achari", then the server refuses with code `forbidden` and the sentence "Only the owner can add a karigar or change their wastage allowance.", and nothing is stored (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh, when he calls Update Karigar wastage to move KG-02 Mahesh Soni from 0.8% to 1.2%, then the server refuses the same way and `wastage_bp` stays 80.
  3. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar, KG-04), when he calls Update Karigar details on his own record to change his phone, then the server refuses with the same sentence and the record is unchanged.
  4. Given Rajesh sends a request that is also invalid, such as an empty name, when the server checks it, then he gets the role refusal, not the validation sentence.
  5. Given Rajesh calls Read Karigar scorecard for KG-02, when the server checks the role, then it refuses with `forbidden`.
  6. Given any refused request above, when `karigars` and the audit log are checked, then neither has changed for that request.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The role check runs before validation and before any write (deny by default, EP-05-S2). The five change operations and Read Karigar scorecard are listed as owner-only in the permission matrix (EP-05-S1). List Karigars stays open to staff in its picker shape (EP-16-S8), and Read My karigar profile stays open to the karigar for their own record (EP-16-S12).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused request changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** Adds the five change operations and the scorecard read to the permission matrix as owner-only. No schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Routes `karigars` and `karigar-new` are on the owner rail only (EP-08-S13); the refusal sentence shows through EP-08-S5 if reached. The sentence is the one printed on `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: hiding `karigar-new` from staff is not the control; the server check is (epic section 13).
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S4, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S3: Owner can add a karigar with the 0.6% to 1.2% allowance check

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can add a karigar with the 0.6% to 1.2% allowance check
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to add a karigar on `karigar-new` with name, phone, email, workshop location, one or more specialties and a wastage allowance, through a Create Karigar operation that assigns the next `KG-NN` code and returns it
- **So that:** each artisan I issue gold to is recorded once, with the allowance their jobs will be judged against (FR-16-1, FR-16-2, FR-16-3, FR-16-4, BR-16-1, BR-16-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth on `karigar-new` with KG-01, KG-02 and KG-04 stored, when he adds "Ravi Achari" with a phone, the email "ravi.achari@example.com", Temple and Kundan, and 0.9%, then the record KG-05 is stored with `wastage_bp` 90, status `active` and language `English`, the code is returned, and an audit entry records it (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the name is empty or only spaces, when Sanjay chooses "Add this karigar", then the server refuses with "Add the karigar name." and nothing is stored.
  3. Given no specialty chip is picked, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with "Pick at least one thing they are best at." and nothing is stored.
  4. Given Sanjay sets the allowance to 1.5% or 0.5%, when he saves, then the server refuses with "The wastage allowance is between 0.6% and 1.2%." and nothing is stored (epic acceptance criterion 3); given 0.705%, then it is refused as a validation error because it is not a whole basis point.
  5. Given the allowance is 0.70%, when the form shows the worked example, then it reads "On a 160 g job, that means up to 1.1200 g lost", computed from 1,600,000 units × 70 ÷ 10,000 = 11,200 units, with the 4-decimal display in place of the mockup's "1.120 g".
  6. Given the same Create Karigar request is sent twice with one idempotency key after a network drop, when the server processes it, then only one karigar and one code are created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-16-S2). Name required and trimmed. At least one specialty, each an active EP-15 specialty entry (EP-15-S4). Allowance converted to basis points and checked 60 to 120. Phone required and normalised to +91 and 10 digits. The server sets id, status, language default, open since and version; the client cannot send them. Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Create, code assignment and audit run in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_added`), after (name, phone, workshop location, specialties, wastage allowance, status). Written through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `karigars` and `karigar_specialties`; moves `karigar_code_counter`. Adds Create Karigar to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg`, route `karigar-new` ("Add a karigar", "Name", "Code", "Phone · their job portal logs in with this", "Workshop location", "What they are best at", "ALLOWED LOSS", slider 0.6% to 1.2%, "On a 160 g job, that means", "Add this karigar", "Cancel"). The "Language for their phone" chips (தமிழ் / हिन्दी / English) are not shown in v1; EP-44 adds them.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the worked example is computed from integers of 0.0001 g and basis points through the EP-02-S2 helpers, never with float percentages. Personal data: the phone entered here is shown back only to the owner. Security: the slider's client limits are a convenience; the server repeats the range check. D4 is decided: one phone per karigar (phone numbers are unique) and an email is required; an empty email is refused as a validation error.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-02-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7, EP-15-S4, EP-15-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S4: Owner can edit a karigar's details

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can edit a karigar's details
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to change a karigar's name, phone, workshop location and specialties through Update Karigar details, saving with the version I last read
- **So that:** the record stays correct when a karigar moves workshop, changes phone or takes up new work, without retyping the karigar (FR-16-6, BR-16-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-01 Lakshmi Devi in Kanchipuram, when Sanjay Seth changes her workshop location to "Kumbakonam" and adds the specialty Temple, then both are stored, her version goes up by one, and her code, allowance and status are unchanged.
  2. Given KG-04 Vijay Kumar is linked to a karigar user, when Sanjay changes his phone, then the linked user's phone changes in the same transaction, so the new number is his portal login (BR-16-3).
  3. Given the new phone is already used by another user, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses with a sentence saying the phone is already used by another account, and neither record changes.
  4. Given Sanjay clears the name or removes every specialty, when he saves, then the server refuses with "Add the karigar name." or "Pick at least one thing they are best at." and nothing changes.
  5. Given another owner session saved KG-01 after Sanjay read it, when Sanjay saves with the older version, then the server refuses as a conflict and nothing changes (EP-02-S14).
  6. Given an edit request that also sends `wastage_bp`, `status` or `id`, when the contract check runs, then it is rejected as a validation error, because those fields change only through EP-16-S5, EP-16-S7 and never.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-16-S2). Same field checks as EP-16-S3. Stale version refused (EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5). A phone change on a linked karigar also updates `users.phone` under the EP-05-S5 rules (phone unique among users) in one transaction with the audit entry (EP-03-S6). A deactivated karigar can still be edited, so the record stays correct for history.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_edited`), before and after for each changed field. A phone change on the linked user is also audited by EP-05-S14. Written through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Updates `karigars` (name, phone, workshop location, version) and rewrites the karigar's `karigar_specialties` rows; may update `users.phone` and `users.version`. Adds Update Karigar details to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The edit form is undrawn (epic section 12); it reuses the `karigar-new` fields from `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg` with the code read-only.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: version check on every save. Personal data: before and after phone values in the audit log are visible only to the owner (EP-06-S12). Open question: workshop location as free text or address with a map pin. D4 is decided: phone numbers are unique, so two karigars cannot share a workshop phone. An email change on a linked karigar also updates `users.email` under the EP-05-S5 rules.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-16-S3, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S5, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S5: Owner can change a karigar's wastage allowance, audited

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can change a karigar's wastage allowance, audited
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** a separate Update Karigar wastage operation that changes a karigar's allowance within 0.6% to 1.2% and records the old and new value, with an optional reason
- **So that:** changing the yardstick for a karigar is a deliberate, visible act, and jobs already issued keep the allowance they were issued under (FR-16-4, FR-16-7, BR-16-1, BR-16-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-02 Mahesh Soni at 0.8%, when Sanjay Seth changes his allowance to 1.0%, then `wastage_bp` becomes 100, his version goes up by one, and an audit entry records before 80 and after 100.
  2. Given Sanjay sets 1.25%, when he saves, then the server refuses with "The wastage allowance is between 0.6% and 1.2%." and `wastage_bp` stays 80.
  3. Given the allowance was changed from 0.8% to 1.0%, when a new job is issued to Mahesh afterwards, then the "allowance in force now" read used by job creation returns 100.
  4. Given Mahesh has job MO-2026-118 issued at 0.8% before the change, when its allowance is read after the change, then it follows the decided rule: either it stays 0.8% (new jobs only) or it moves to 1.0% (open jobs too), and closed jobs never change.
  5. Given Sanjay saves the same value 0.8% again, when the server checks it, then nothing changes and no audit entry is written.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-16-S2). Range 60 to 120 basis points, whole numbers only. Stale version refused (EP-02-S14). The change and its audit run in one transaction (EP-03-S6). The server exposes "allowance in force now" for job creation; EP-19 stores the allowance on each job when it is issued and applies the decided rule to open jobs. A settled job's verdict is never recomputed by an allowance change.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_wastage_changed`), before (`wastage_bp`), after (`wastage_bp`), reason if given. Written through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Updates `karigars.wastage_bp` and `karigars.version`. Adds Update Karigar wastage and the allowance-in-force read to the shared contract. The per-job allowance field is added by EP-19.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The edit form with the "THE WASTAGE YOU ALLOW THEM" panel from `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg` is undrawn for an existing karigar (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: stored and compared as integer basis points. Audit: old and new allowance are always recorded, because the value changes how every future job is judged (epic section 13). Open question: whether a changed allowance applies only to jobs issued after the change or also to jobs already open (criterion 4 is written for either answer).
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-16-S3, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S6, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S6: Owner can link a karigar to a karigar user account

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can link a karigar to a karigar user account
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** from a karigar's record, to link it to a user with role `karigar` (or create that user from the karigar's name, phone and email, which sends the activation email), and to see on the record whether it is linked
- **So that:** the karigar can sign in to the portal with the phone recorded here and see only their own jobs (FR-16-10, BR-16-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-05 Ravi Achari has no account, when Sanjay Seth chooses to give him portal access, then a user with role `karigar`, Ravi's name, phone and email is created with status `pending_activation` and linked to KG-05 in one transaction, an activation email goes to Ravi (EP-04-S10), and the record shows it as linked.
  2. Given an existing karigar user with Vijay Kumar's phone and no link, when Sanjay links it to KG-04, then `users.karigarId` is KG-04, and the link uses the EP-05-S13 rules.
  3. Given KG-04 is already linked to an active user, when Sanjay links a second user to it, then the server refuses with "This karigar already has an account." (one account per karigar).
  4. Given KG-05 is deactivated, when Sanjay tries to link or create an account for him, then the server refuses with a sentence saying the karigar is deactivated.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Update Karigar account link, then the server refuses with "Only the owner can add a karigar or change their wastage allowance." (EP-16-S2).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only. The user side is owned by EP-05: role must be `karigar`, phone unique among the shop's users, email required, one active user per karigar record (EP-05-S4, EP-05-S13). Creating the user and setting the link happen in one transaction with both audit entries (EP-03-S6). The user's phone and email must equal the karigar's, so the login stays the phone recorded here. No password is set or emailed; the activation link comes from EP-04-S10.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_linked`), before and after user id. The user creation and `karigarId` change are audited by EP-05-S14. Written through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Updates `users.karigarId` and `users.version`; may insert into `users`. Adds Update Karigar account link to the shared contract. No column added to `karigars`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. No mockup draws the link step; `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg` labels the phone "their job portal logs in with this".
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: a wrong link would show one karigar another's jobs, so the link is owner-only and audited. D4 is decided: phone and password sign-in, phone numbers unique, so two karigars cannot share one workshop phone. Open question (from EP-05-S13): whether linking happens in one step with adding the karigar.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-16-S3, EP-05-S4, EP-05-S13, EP-05-S14, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S7: Owner can deactivate a karigar with no open jobs

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can deactivate a karigar with no open jobs
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to deactivate or reactivate a karigar through Update Karigar status, with the server refusing deactivation while the karigar has an open job or gold issued and not returned, and naming the jobs
- **So that:** a karigar who stops working for the shop is no longer offered or able to sign in, without gold being left untracked with them (FR-16-8, FR-16-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-04 Vijay Kumar has the open job MO-2026-118, when Sanjay Seth tries to deactivate him, then the server refuses with a sentence naming MO-2026-118 and nothing changes (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given a karigar with no open job but 0.4000 g of gold out on the EP-18 ledger, when Sanjay tries to deactivate them, then the server refuses with a sentence giving the gold still with them.
  3. Given KG-05 Ravi Achari has no open job and no gold out and is linked to a user, when Sanjay deactivates him, then the karigar status is `deactivated` with `deactivated_at` set, the linked user is deactivated in the same transaction, and his open portal sessions end through EP-05-S7.
  4. Given a job is being created for KG-05 at the same moment as the deactivation, when both commit, then exactly one succeeds: either the job exists and the deactivation is refused, or the karigar is deactivated and the job is refused (epic section 13 concurrency).
  5. Given KG-05 is deactivated, when Sanjay reactivates him, then the status is `active`, `deactivated_at` is cleared, and his user account stays deactivated until Sanjay reactivates it through EP-05-S8.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (EP-16-S2). Deactivation reads open jobs and gold with the karigar inside the same transaction, holding a lock on the karigar row, and job creation (EP-19) checks the karigar's status under the same lock through the EP-16-S8 check. Status moves only between `active` and `deactivated`; deactivating an already deactivated karigar is refused. The record is never deleted. Stale version refused (EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "User deactivated or role changed" for the linked user, through EP-05-S10.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_deactivated` or `karigar_reactivated`), before and after status, reason if given. The linked user's deactivation is audited by EP-05-S14. Written through EP-16-S13.
- **Data changes:** Updates `karigars.status`, `karigars.deactivated_at` and `karigars.version`; may update `users.status` and end `sessions` rows. Adds Update Karigar status to the shared contract. Reads `karigar_jobs` and the metal pool ledger (EP-02-S8, EP-02-S9).
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The deactivate action is undrawn (epic section 12); it belongs on the karigar record opened from `karigars`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: deactivation and a new order copy for the same karigar cannot both succeed. Precision: the gold-out figure is an integer of 0.0001 g shown to 4 decimals. Security: a deactivated karigar's sessions end within about 1 second through the live event. Open question: whether a karigar with open jobs can be deactivated once the owner takes the gold back first.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-16-S6, EP-02-S8, EP-02-S9, EP-02-S14, EP-05-S7, EP-05-S8, EP-05-S10, EP-04-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S8: Staff can pick only active karigars on the order copy and parcel forms

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can pick only active karigars on the order copy and parcel forms
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a karigar picker on `order-copy` and `parcel-arrival` that lists only active karigars with name, code, specialties and allowance, and no phone, location or scorecard, plus a shared server check that refuses an inactive or unknown karigar on those forms
- **So that:** I can send work to the right karigar without seeing figures meant for the owner, and no job or parcel is recorded against someone who no longer works for the shop (FR-16-9, BR-16-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-01, KG-02, KG-04 active and KG-05 deactivated, when Rajesh Verma opens the karigar picker on `order-copy`, then it offers Lakshmi Devi · KG-01, Mahesh Soni · KG-02 and Vijay Kumar · KG-04, and not Ravi Achari.
  2. Given the picker list, when the response is inspected, then each row carries id, name, specialties and allowance (for example "Chettinad specialist · 0.7% loss") and no phone, workshop location, metal loss, days late, rating or parcel gaps.
  3. Given KG-05 was deactivated after Rajesh's picker loaded, when Rajesh sends an order copy for KG-05, then the server refuses with a sentence saying the karigar is no longer active, and nothing is stored.
  4. Given a parcel arrival names a karigar id that does not exist, when the server checks it, then it refuses with "Say which karigar it came from."
  5. Given the picker is loading or the read fails, when Rajesh opens it, then it shows the EP-08-S3 loading state or the EP-08-S4 error with "Try again".
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Karigars returns the picker shape to `staff` and only `active` karigars (epic section 10). The shared "karigar is active" check takes a lock on the karigar row and is called inside the job-creation and parcel-arrival transactions that EP-19 and EP-21 build. A karigar caller is refused List Karigars with `forbidden`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The picker reloads on next open; a stale choice is caught by the server check.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Picking reads data, and a refused save changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the picker shape of List Karigars and the shared active-karigar check to the service layer, and the karigar picker to the web app through the EP-08 cache.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("Who makes it", "Lakshmi Devi · KG-01", "Chettinad specialist · 0.7% loss · always on time"); `docs/ux/mockups/20-parcel-arrival.svg`, route `parcel-arrival`. The "always on time" phrase is a scorecard figure and is left out until G4 says whether staff see it.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: staff never receive karigar phone or workshop location. Concurrency: a deactivation and an order copy at the same moment cannot both succeed (EP-16-S7). Availability: offline, the picker shows the last cached list and sending is disabled (EP-08-S11). Open question G4: whether staff see any scorecard figure, such as "always on time".
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S7, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S1, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S11, EP-15-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S10: System can compute loss %, days late and last six parcel gaps from real data (G4)

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can compute loss %, days late and last six parcel gaps from real data (G4)
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a scorecard computation per karigar that derives metal loss %, days late, finished jobs and the last six parcel gold gaps from settled jobs, agreed dates and released parcels, and keeps the rating empty until its formula is decided
- **So that:** every figure the owner judges a karigar by is measured from what happened, not seeded (FR-16-12, FR-16-13, BR-16-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given KG-02 has two settled jobs with gold issued 447.3000 g and 160.0000 g and loss 6.3000 g and 2.3000 g, when the scorecard is computed, then metal loss is (63,000 + 23,000) × 10,000 ÷ (4,473,000 + 1,600,000) = 141.6, rounded half up to 142 basis points and shown as 1.42%, computed from integers.
  2. Given three parcels released for KG-02 with gold gaps of 0.0280 g, 0.0330 g and 0.1380 g, when the owner reads the scorecard, then the last gaps are exactly those three, newest first, as integers 280, 330 and 1,380 (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  3. Given KG-02 has eight released parcels, when the scorecard is computed, then only the six most recent gaps are returned.
  4. Given a job confirmed for 17 Nov 2026 and handed over on 20 Nov 2026, when days late are computed, then that job counts 3 days late, using dates in Asia/Kolkata; a job handed over early counts 0.
  5. Given the rating formula is not decided, when the scorecard is read, then `rating` is null and no screen shows a rating.
  6. Given the migration has run, when `karigars` is inspected, then the seeded `metal_loss`, `late_days`, `rating` and `finished_jobs` columns are gone and no scorecard figure is read from them (epic acceptance criterion 6).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Figures are computed only from stored rows: job settlement and agreed dates in `karigar_jobs` (written by EP-19), ledger entries (written by EP-18) and parcel gaps on released parcels (written by EP-23). All arithmetic is on integers of 0.0001 g and basis points, with rounding stated once (half up to whole basis points). Unsettled jobs are not counted in loss %. The cached scorecard, if kept, is recomputed in the same transaction that settles a job or releases a parcel, so it is never stale. Until EP-18, EP-19 and EP-23 exist, tests use fixture rows in those tables.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The scorecard changes when EP-19 and EP-23 settle jobs and release parcels (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. A derived figure is not a change to shop records; the job and parcel changes behind it are audited by their own epics.
- **Data changes:** Migration drops the seeded `metal_loss`, `late_days`, `rating`, `finished_jobs` columns from `karigars` and stops reading `karigar_gap_history` as seed data; the last six gaps are read from released parcels. Migration creates `karigar_scorecards` (karigar id, metal loss bp, days late, finished jobs, last six gaps as integers of 0.0001 g, rating nullable, computed at) if a cache is used.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The figures appear on `karigars` (EP-16-S9, EP-16-S11) and on `parcel-clear` ("His last six parcels, gold gap", `docs/ux/mockups/22-owner-clear-mismatch.svg`), which EP-23 builds.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: percentages computed from integers, never stored floats (epic section 13). Time: day boundaries for days late in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). Open question G4: the rating formula, the period for loss % and days late, and whether days late is a sum or an average. Open question G23: whether reconciliation B is settled per job or per period, which decides what "settled job" means in criterion 1.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S6, EP-02-S8, EP-02-S9, EP-03-S6, EP-10-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

  2. Given the same session, when Read My karigar profile is called, then the server uses the `karigarId` on his user and accepts no karigar id from the request.
  3. Given the same session, when he calls a read for KG-02's record or scorecard, then the server returns `not_found` and no field of that record (EP-05-S3).
  4. Given the profile response, when it is inspected, then it carries no rating, no other karigar's figures, and no customer, price or stock field.
  5. Given a karigar user with no linked record, when they open "Me", then the server returns an empty profile and the screen says the account is not linked yet, with no error.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Karigar role only, own record only, keyed from the session (EP-03-S3, EP-05-S3). Read only; changes go through the owner (EP-16-S2). The language field is not returned in v1.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading a profile changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read My karigar profile to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs`, "Me" tab ("Vijay Kumar · KG-04", "0.8% wastage allowed", "Finished jobs", "14 delivered this year"). The हिन्दी toggle is not shown in v1 (EP-44). The full "Me" tab is built in EP-20; this story provides its data.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: another karigar's record returns not-found, so its existence is not revealed. Personal data: the karigar sees only their own phone and location. Open question G4: whether a karigar sees their own loss % or days late; this story shows neither.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S1, EP-16-S6, EP-16-S10, EP-03-S3, EP-05-S3, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S12, EP-08-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-16-S13: System can audit every karigar change

- **Story ID:** EP-16-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit every karigar change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every add, edit, wastage change, account link, deactivation and reactivation of a karigar to write one append-only audit entry in the same transaction, with before and after values
- **So that:** the owner can see who changed a karigar's record or allowance, when, and from what to what (FR-16-15, epic section 13 audit)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth adds KG-05 Ravi Achari, when the create commits, then one entry exists with actor Sanjay, server time, entity KG-05, action `karigar_added` and the stored fields as after.
  2. Given Sanjay changes KG-02 from 0.8% to 1.0%, when it commits, then one entry exists with action `karigar_wastage_changed`, before `wastage_bp` 80 and after 100.
  3. Given an edit that fails after the karigar row was updated, when the transaction rolls back, then neither the change nor the audit entry is stored.
  4. Given a refused request, such as Rajesh Verma calling Create Karigar, when the log is checked, then no karigar entry exists for it.
  5. Given Sanjay filters the security log by entity KG-02, when the results come back, then they list the karigar entries newest first with before and after values (EP-06-S10, EP-06-S11).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Audit entries are written in the same transaction as the change (EP-06-S2) and cannot be updated or deleted (EP-06-S1). Actor comes from the session and time from the server clock (EP-03-S3). Audit reads are owner-only (EP-06-S12).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (karigar id), action (`karigar_added`, `karigar_edited`, `karigar_wastage_changed`, `karigar_linked`, `karigar_deactivated`, `karigar_reactivated`), before, after, reason where given.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). Adds the karigar kinds to the audit kind list by migration. No other schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show in the security log built in EP-06 (EP-06-S9, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S11).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every karigar change writes an append-only entry, and a wastage change always holds old and new value. Personal data: phone values in before and after are visible only to the owner. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-16-S3, EP-16-S4, EP-16-S5, EP-16-S6, EP-16-S7, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S7, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-17: Customer master · stories

Epic document: [EP-17 Customer master](../epics/EP-17-customer-master.md)

Role note: stories where the server stores, checks, matches, hides or audits on its own use "System". Stories where a person adds, edits, searches or records consent for a customer use "Staff", because mockup 11 gives staff "Add a customer and send wishes"; the owner can do everything staff can. The deletion story uses "Owner".

---

## EP-17-S1: System can store customers with normalised phones and nullable value sockets

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store customers with normalised phones and nullable value sockets
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `customers` table from EP-02-S4 extended with a normalised phone, optional address, status (`active` or `erased`), created at, created by and version, a shared phone normaliser that turns any typed phone into digits with the country code, and the budget and spend columns kept nullable with no default
- **So that:** each buyer is one stored record that leads, POs, wishes and broadcasts can find by phone, and the value sockets are ready for pricing without a later migration (FR-17-2, FR-17-12, BR-17-1, BR-17-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `customers` is inspected, then it has `id` (`CU-NNN`), `name`, `phone` (normalised), `city`, nullable `address`, `group`, nullable `dob`, nullable `anniversary`, `notes`, `status` accepting only `active` or `erased`, `created_at`, `created_by`, an integer `version` starting at 1, and nullable `budgetINR` and `spentINR` with no default.
  2. Given the typed phones "+91 98840 21107", "98840 21107", "098840 21107" and "+91-9884021107", when each is passed to the shared normaliser, then each returns "+919884021107".
  3. Given a typed phone with fewer than 10 digits, such as "98840 211", when it is normalised, then the normaliser returns a refusal and no value, so no store or match can use it.
  4. Given a birthday of 14 Mar with no year, when it is stored, then `dob` holds the ISO date `2000-03-14`, the placeholder year the prototype `dayMonthToIso` uses, and it reads back as "14 Mar".
  5. Given the seeded customers such as Meera Iyer and Priya Malhotra, when the migration has run, then their phones are rewritten in normalised form, their status is `active`, their `budgetINR` and `spentINR` are null, and no other field has changed.
  6. Given an insert that writes a non-null `budgetINR` while EP-42 is not built, when the server's customer service writes it, then the write is refused (the database column stays nullable for EP-42; the service guard is in EP-17-S11).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Database checks: `name` not empty, `status` enum, `group` enum (the four type values `VIP Bridal`, `High net worth`, `Regular`, `Wholesale` until G19 is settled), `dob` and `anniversary` are dates, not timestamps. The phone is always stored after normalisation through the one shared function in the shared package, so add, edit and match use the same form. The server sets `id`, `status`, `created_at`, `created_by` and `version`. Ids are handed out by an atomic counter and never reused.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage; changes are audited through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `customers` (EP-02-S4) adds `address`, `status` (default `active`), `created_at`, `created_by`, `version` if missing, and rewrites existing `phone` values in normalised form. Migration creates `customer_id_counter`, initialised above the highest `CU-NNN` in use. `budgetINR`, `spentINR` and `customer_history` stay as EP-02-S4 made them. Each table has the shop ID (EP-02-S3, D7).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: `name`, `phone`, `address`, `dob` and `anniversary` are tagged as personal data under the DPDP Act, 2023, for EP-39 export and erasure. Precision: no weight column is added; history grams stay integers of 0.0001 g (EP-02-S4). Open question G19: which groups exist and whether they become an EP-15 reference list; the enum here is the type's four values. D7 is decided: customers belong to the one shop and carry its shop ID, set by the server. Open question: how phones outside India (not +91) are normalised; this story treats a 10-digit number as Indian and keeps any number already starting with a country code.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S2: System can store consent as events with time, source and recorder

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store consent as events with time, source and recorder
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a `consent_events` table where each row is one opt-in or opt-out with its source, the user who recorded it and the server time, the customer's current consent derived from the latest event, and the existing `optedIn` column kept as a copy of that latest event, written in the same transaction
- **So that:** the shop can prove when and how a customer agreed to WhatsApp messages, and the send-time consent check in EP-12-S5 keeps working unchanged (FR-17-6, BR-17-2, BR-17-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `consent_events` is inspected, then it has `id`, `customer_id` referencing `customers`, `kind` accepting only `opt_in` or `opt_out`, `source` accepting only `counter`, `whatsapp_reply`, `form` or `import`, `recorded_by` (a user id, or System), and `at` in UTC.
  2. Given Meera Iyer has an `opt_in` event at 10:02 and an `opt_out` event at 16:40 on the same day, when her current consent is read, then it is opted out and `customers.optedIn` is false.
  3. Given a new consent event is inserted, when the transaction commits, then `customers.optedIn` matches the new event's kind; if the transaction rolls back, neither the event nor the copy changes.
  4. Given a seeded customer with `optedIn` true and no events, when the migration runs, then one `opt_in` event with source `import`, recorded by System, at the migration time is written for them, and customers with `optedIn` false get no event.
  5. Given an attempt to update or delete a row in `consent_events`, when it reaches the database, then it is refused, because consent history is append-only.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Consent events are only inserted, never updated or deleted, except by the erase action in EP-17-S13, which keeps the rows and holds no personal value in them. `optedIn` is written only by the consent service, in the same transaction as the event (EP-03-S6); no other operation may set it. `recorded_by` comes from the session, or is System for the WhatsApp keyword path and the migration (EP-03-S3, EP-06-S6). Time comes from the server clock.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage; consent changes are audited through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `consent_events` (id, customer id, kind, source, recorded by, at) with an index on customer id and `at`, and backfills `import` events for seeded opted-in customers. `customers.optedIn` stays as a maintained copy. Rows carry the shop ID (D7).
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent is stored with time and source (epic section 13, DPDP Act, 2023). Time: `at` stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Concurrency: two consent events for one customer in the same second are both kept and ordered by `at` then `id`, so "latest" is always one row.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-02-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S3: Staff can add a customer at the counter

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can add a customer at the counter
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to add a customer on `customer-new` with name, phone, city, optional address, group, birthday, anniversary and notes, through a Create Customer operation that returns the new `CU-NNN` id
- **So that:** a buyer is recorded once at the counter and their wishes, leads and pieces can attach to them (FR-17-1, FR-17-2, FR-17-5, BR-17-3, BR-17-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma on `customer-new`, when he adds Meera Iyer, "+91 98840 21107", Chennai, VIP Bridal, birthday 14 Mar and chooses "Add this customer", then a customer is stored with phone "+919884021107", status `active`, `created_by` Rajesh and server time, and the new id is returned (epic acceptance criterion 1, consent part in EP-17-S6).
  2. Given the name is empty or only spaces, when Rajesh chooses "Add this customer", then the server refuses with "Add the customer name." and nothing is stored.
  3. Given the phone "98840 211" with 9 digits, when Rajesh saves, then the server refuses with "Add a phone number with at least 10 digits. It is also the WhatsApp number." and nothing is stored.
  4. Given a birthday day of 14 with no month, when Rajesh saves, then the server refuses with "Give both the day and the month of the birthday, or neither."; the same check on the anniversary gives "Give both the day and the month of the anniversary, or neither.".
  5. Given a day that does not exist in the month, such as 31 Feb, when Rajesh saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error on `dob`.
  6. Given the same Create Customer request is sent twice with one idempotency key after a network drop, when the server processes it, then only one customer and one id are created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the add-customer permission (staff and owner per mockup 11, EP-05-S1; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). Name required and trimmed. Phone normalised through the EP-17-S1 function and refused under 10 digits. Day and month required together for each date, and the date must exist. Group must be one of the allowed groups. The duplicate phone check from EP-17-S4 runs before the insert. The client cannot send `id`, `status`, `created_by`, `version`, `budgetINR` or `spentINR`. Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Insert, id assignment and audit run in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_added`), after (the stored fields). Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `customers`; moves `customer_id_counter`. Adds Create Customer to the shared contract and moves `customer-new` off `useStore()` onto the EP-08 data layer.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg`, route `customer-new` ("Add a customer", "WHO THEY ARE", "Name", "Phone · also the WhatsApp number", "City", "Address (optional)", "Group", "WHEN TO WISH THEM", "Birthday", "Anniversary", "Add this customer", "Cancel"). The group chips on the mockup (VIP Bridal, High net worth, Festive collector) follow G19.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: the form collects only the fields in epic section 9; nothing is written to logs except the customer id. Security: client-side checks in `OnboardCustomer.tsx` are a convenience; the server repeats every check. Open question: who may add a customer, staff (mockup 11) or owner only (mockups README); criteria are written for staff and change only the permission entry if the answer is owner only. Open question G19: which groups appear on the form.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7, EP-08-S17
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S4: System can warn about a duplicate phone on add and edit

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can warn about a duplicate phone on add and edit
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Create Customer and Update Customer to compare the normalised phone with every active customer, and when it matches, to return a `duplicate_phone` warning naming the existing customer instead of writing, unless the decided duplicate rule allows the save
- **So that:** one buyer does not end up as two records with split history and double wishes (FR-17-3, epic section 13 concurrency)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer is stored with phone "+919884021107", when Rajesh Verma adds a new customer "M. Iyer" with phone "98840 21107", then the server writes nothing and returns `duplicate_phone` with Meera Iyer's id, name, city and group, and the screen offers to open her record (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given Rajesh edits Priya Malhotra's phone to "+91 98840 21107", when he saves, then the server returns the same warning naming Meera Iyer and Priya's phone is unchanged.
  3. Given Rajesh edits Meera Iyer and keeps her own phone, when he saves, then no duplicate warning is raised.
  4. Given two staff add a customer with "98840 21107" at the same moment and no customer has it yet, when both requests commit, then exactly one customer exists with that phone and the other request gets `duplicate_phone` naming it.
  5. Given a customer with that phone has status `erased`, when a new customer is added with it, then no warning is raised, because an erased record no longer holds the phone.
  6. Given the decided rule allows family members to share a phone, when Rajesh confirms the save after the warning, then the second customer is stored and both records keep the phone.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The check uses the normalised phone (EP-17-S1). It runs inside the create or update transaction. If the decided rule is one phone per customer, a unique index on shop ID and `phone` among `active` customers enforces it in the database, so the race in criterion 4 cannot produce two records. If shared phones are allowed, the save needs an explicit confirm flag on the request after the warning, and the index is not unique. The warning is a refusal with code `duplicate_phone`, in the EP-03-S4 format.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A warned request writes nothing; a confirmed save is audited by EP-17-S3 or EP-17-S5.
- **Data changes:** Migration adds an index on `customers.phone` filtered to `status = 'active'`, unique only if the decided rule is one phone per customer. Adds the `duplicate_phone` code to the shared error list.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The duplicate warning is undrawn (epic section 12); it shows on `customer-new` (`docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg`) and on the edit form.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: two staff adding the same phone at once produce one customer when the rule is one phone per customer (epic section 13). Personal data: the warning returns only id, name, city and group of the existing customer, not their dates, address or history. Open question: can two customers share a phone (family members)? Criterion 6 applies only if they can.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S5: Staff can edit a customer's details

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can edit a customer's details
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to change a customer's name, phone, city, address, group, birthday, anniversary and notes through Update Customer, saving with the version I last read
- **So that:** the record stays correct when a buyer moves, changes number or gives a date they did not give at first, without adding them again (FR-17-4, FR-17-5)

  2. Given Rajesh clears her name, when he saves, then the server refuses with "Add the customer name." and nothing changes.
  3. Given Rajesh enters an anniversary month with no day, when he saves, then the server refuses with "Give both the day and the month of the anniversary, or neither." and nothing changes.
  4. Given Rajesh changes her phone to a number that belongs to another active customer, when he saves, then the EP-17-S4 duplicate warning is returned and nothing changes.
  5. Given another staff member saved Meera Iyer after Rajesh opened her, when Rajesh saves with the older version, then the server refuses as a conflict and nothing changes (EP-02-S14).
  6. Given an edit request that also sends `optedIn`, `status`, `budgetINR`, `spentINR` or `id`, when the contract check runs, then it is rejected as a validation error, because consent changes only through EP-17-S6 and EP-17-S7 and the others never through this operation.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the edit-customer permission (staff and owner; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). Same field checks as EP-17-S3. Phone normalised and checked for duplicates (EP-17-S4). Stale version refused (EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5). An erased customer cannot be edited and returns `not_found`. Update and audit run in one transaction (EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_edited`), before and after for each changed field only. Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Updates `customers` (changed fields and `version`). Adds Update Customer to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The edit form is undrawn (epic section 12); it reuses the `customer-new` fields from `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg` and is opened from the customer drawer on `customers`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: version check on every save. Personal data: before and after values of personal fields in the audit entry are visible only to the owner (EP-06-S12). Open question G19: which groups may be chosen.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S3, EP-17-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S6: Staff can record a customer's WhatsApp consent

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can record a customer's WhatsApp consent
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** ticking "Send wishes on WhatsApp" when adding a customer, or choosing to record consent on an existing customer, to write an `opt_in` consent event with source, my user and the server time, through Create Consent event
- **So that:** wishes and broadcasts go only to customers who agreed, and the shop can show when and how each one agreed (FR-17-6, BR-17-2, BR-17-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma adds Meera Iyer on `customer-new` with "Send wishes on WhatsApp" ticked, when the add commits, then one `opt_in` event exists for her with source `counter`, recorded by Rajesh and the server time, in the same transaction as the customer, and `optedIn` is true (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the box is left unticked, when the add commits, then no consent event is written and `optedIn` is false.
  3. Given Ravi Shankar is stored as "not opted in to WhatsApp", when Rajesh records consent for him with source `form`, then an `opt_in` event is written and his next birthday is eligible for the 9 am auto-send.
  4. Given Meera Iyer is already opted in, when Rajesh records consent again, then the server writes nothing and returns her current consent, so the history holds no repeated event.
  5. Given a request with source `whatsapp_reply` or `import` from a user session, when the server checks it, then it is refused as a validation error, because those sources are set only by the system.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the record-consent permission (staff and owner; System for the WhatsApp path; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). Staff may only use sources `counter` and `form`. The event and the `optedIn` copy are written in one transaction (EP-17-S2). The customer must be `active`. Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. EP-33 and EP-34 read consent at send time on the server (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_consent_recorded`), before (opted out) and after (opted in), source. Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `consent_events`; updates `customers.optedIn` and `version`. Adds Create Consent event to the shared contract; Create Customer accepts an optional consent flag and source.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg`, route `customer-new` ("Send wishes on WhatsApp"). Recording consent on an existing customer and the consent history are not yet designed (epic section 12). `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg` shows the result ("opted in · will auto-send at 9 am unless you send now", "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent stored with time and source (DPDP Act, 2023); a professional review of the wording shown at the counter belongs to EP-39. Time: event time stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: who may add a customer, which decides whether staff record the first consent on add.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S2, EP-17-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S7: Staff can record a customer's opt-out

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can record a customer's opt-out
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to record that a customer withdrew consent, through Create Consent event with kind `opt_out`, effective at once, and the WhatsApp opt-out keyword path from EP-12-S10 to write the same event with source `whatsapp_reply` and recorder System
- **So that:** a customer who says stop gets no more wishes or broadcasts from the next send on (FR-17-7, BR-17-2, BR-17-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra is opted in with a birthday today, when Rajesh Verma records her opt-out at the counter at 08:30, then an `opt_out` event with source `counter`, recorded by Rajesh, is stored, `optedIn` is false, and the 9 am wishes run sends her nothing (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given Priya is opted out, when a broadcast to VIP Bridal is sent afterwards, then she is skipped by the send-time consent check (EP-12-S5).
  3. Given Priya replies "STOP" on WhatsApp, when EP-12-S10 processes it, then an `opt_out` event with source `whatsapp_reply`, recorded by System, is written through this operation, and `optedIn` is false.
  4. Given Priya is already opted out, when an opt-out is recorded again, then the server writes nothing and returns her current consent.
  5. Given Priya is opted out, when the `wishes` screen lists her birthday, then she is still shown with "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send" so staff can reach her another way.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the record-consent permission (staff and owner, or System for the keyword path; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). The event and the `optedIn` copy are written in one transaction (EP-17-S2). Sends read consent at the moment of sending, not at queue time (EP-12-S5), so an opt-out recorded at 08:59 stops a 9:00 send. Only the consent service sets `optedIn`; EP-12-S10 calls it instead of writing the column itself.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Consent is read at send time on the server (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (user or System), time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_opted_out`), before (opted in) and after (opted out), source. Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `consent_events`; updates `customers.optedIn` and `version`. The EP-12-S10 keyword handler is changed to call this operation.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The opt-out action and consent history are undrawn (epic section 12); they belong in the customer drawer on `customers`. `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes`, shows the result ("not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send", "Call instead").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: opt-out is honoured from the next send (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Concurrency: the send-time check reads the committed `optedIn`, so an opt-out and a send at the same moment never deliver after the opt-out commits. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S2, EP-17-S6, EP-12-S5, EP-12-S10, EP-03-S6, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S8: Staff can search and filter the customer directory

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can search and filter the customer directory
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** the `customers` screen to load customers from the server through List Customers, search by name, phone (spaces ignored) or city, filter by group, and page through long results
- **So that:** I can find a buyer at the counter in a few keystrokes, even with thousands of customers (FR-17-9, BR-17-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer of Chennai is stored, when Rajesh Verma types "iyer", "98840 21107", "9884021107" or "chennai" into "Search name, phone or city", then her row is in the results each time.
  2. Given the group filter is set to "VIP Bridal", when the search is empty, then only VIP Bridal customers are listed, and choosing "All" lists every active customer.
  3. Given the search "zzz" matches nobody, when the results come back, then the screen reads "Nobody matches that. Clear the search or add them as a new customer.".
  4. Given 10,000 customers, when Rajesh opens `customers`, then the first page loads in under 2 seconds, and further pages load by cursor as he scrolls (EP-03-S9).
  5. Given a customer with status `erased`, when the directory is listed or searched, then that record does not appear.
  6. Given the read is loading or fails, when Rajesh opens `customers`, then the screen shows the EP-08-S3 loading state or the EP-08-S4 error with "Try again".
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the list-customers permission (staff and owner; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). Search runs on the server: name and city case-insensitive contains, phone matched on digits only. Only `active` customers are returned. Results are paged with a cursor and a page size cap (EP-03-S9). Each row carries id, name, phone, city, group, consent and piece count, and no budget or spend value while pricing is off (EP-17-S11).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The list refetches after the user's own add or edit (EP-08-S7).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading the directory changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database beyond indexes. Migration adds indexes for name and city search and for group. Adds List Customers to the shared contract and moves `customers` off `useStore()` onto the EP-08 data layer.
- **UI reference:** Route `customers` (staff and owner rails, "Customers"). Not yet designed: the directory has no mockup (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3); the prototype `Customers.tsx` screen ("Search name, phone or city", group filter, drawer) is reused until the design pass.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: under 2 seconds for 10,000 customers (epic section 13). Personal data: the list is held in memory only on the client (EP-08-S2) and never sent to the karigar portal. Availability: loading, error and offline states shown (EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S11). Open question G19: which groups the filter offers. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; staff see the shop's customers.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-03-S9, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S7, EP-08-S11, EP-08-S13, EP-08-S17
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S9: Staff can see a customer's piece history by tag and grams

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see a customer's piece history by tag and grams
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to open a customer from `customers` and see, through Read Customer, their details, current consent and the pieces they have taken home, each with piece name, tag, pure gold grams and date, newest first, with the count and total grams taken home
- **So that:** I know what a buyer already owns by weight, without any price (FR-17-10, BR-17-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer has history rows "Chettinad Haram · TAG-7521" with pure gold 784,000 units in Oct 2026 and "Polki Kada pair · TAG-6690" with 574,900 units in Feb 2026, when Rajesh Verma opens her, then they show as "Chettinad Haram · TAG-7521 · 78.4000 g · Oct 2026" and "Polki Kada pair · TAG-6690 · 57.4900 g · Feb 2026", newest first.
  2. Given her six history rows add up to 1,358,900 units, when the detail is shown, then it reads "6 pieces in all" and "135.8900 g taken home", summed from integers on the server.
  3. Given a customer with no history rows, when the detail is shown, then the history area says nothing has been taken home yet and the total is not shown.
  4. Given the detail response, when it is inspected, then it carries no price, value, budget or spend figure while pricing is off (EP-17-S11).
  5. Given an unknown or erased customer id, when Read Customer is called, then the server returns `not_found`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the read-customer permission (staff and owner; refused for karigar by EP-17-S12). History rows are read from `customer_history` and returned as integers of 0.0001 g; the total is computed on the server from integers. Rows are ordered by date descending, then tag. The source of new history rows is open (G13); this story reads whatever rows exist and writes none.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading a customer changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Customer to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg` ("WHAT THEY HAVE TAKEN HOME · BY WEIGHT, NOT PRICE", "6 pieces in all · their history ties to the same tags and grams the system already tracks", "135.890 g taken home", shown here to 4 decimals). The customer detail itself is not yet designed (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3); the prototype drawer on `customers` is reused until the design pass.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: grams are integers of 0.0001 g, summed as integers and shown to 4 decimals; the mockup's "78.400 g" and "135.890 g" read "78.4000 g" and "135.8900 g". Personal data: details are shown only to staff and owner. Open question G13: where piece history comes from, given stock-out records no customer today; until EP-26 decides, history holds only seeded or imported rows.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S2, EP-17-S8, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S4, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can match a phone to a known customer for leads and POs (G7)

Returns only id, name, city and group.

- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: under 200 ms (proposed target in epic section 13, to confirm; PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5 sets none). Personal data: the response holds only the fields needed to recognise the customer. Open question G7: when a lead's phone matches a customer but the name differs, which wins and who confirms the match. Open question: can two customers share a phone; criterion 6 applies only if they can.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S4, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-05-S2

## EP-17-S11: System can keep budget and spend dark behind the pricing switch

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can keep budget and spend dark behind the pricing switch
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the customer service to refuse any write to `budgetINR` or `spentINR`, the customer responses to carry them only as null, and every screen to render them only through `ValueSlot`, which draws nothing while the pricing flag is off
- **So that:** the sockets exist from day one and fill when EP-42 turns pricing on, and no amount is stored or shown before then (FR-17-12, BR-17-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given pricing is off, when Rajesh Verma or Sanjay Seth opens Meera Iyer's detail, then no budget or spend figure is shown, no empty space is left for it, and `budgetINR` and `spentINR` are null in the database (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given a Create Customer or Update Customer request that includes `budgetINR: 800000`, when the contract check runs, then it is rejected as a validation error and nothing is stored.
  3. Given `customer-new`, when the form is shown with pricing off, then the "COMES LATER · WITH PRICING" panel with "Budget" and "Spend so far" shows no input and accepts no value.
  4. Given the List Customers, Read Customer and Find Customer by phone responses, when they are inspected, then none carries a non-null budget or spend value.
  5. Given pricing is switched on by the owner (EP-13-S9), when the customer detail is opened, then the `ValueSlot` sockets render, still empty, because only EP-42 fills them.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** No operation in this epic reads or writes an amount. The shared contract for Create Customer and Update Customer has no budget or spend field. The pricing flag is read from shop settings (EP-13-S9); this epic adds no price logic.

- **Audit entry written:** No. Nothing changes; the pricing flag itself is audited by EP-13-S9.

- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the server refuses amount fields; hiding them in the form is not the control. Open decision: money is deferred to EP-42; nothing here computes, stores or shows rupees.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S3, EP-17-S5, EP-17-S9, EP-03-S2, EP-13-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-17-S13: Owner can carry out an approved deletion request on a customer

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can carry out an approved deletion request on a customer
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** an Erase Customer personal data operation that, for an approved deletion request, clears the customer's name, phone, address, birthday and anniversary, sets status `erased`, and keeps their piece history by tag, grams and date without the personal fields
- **So that:** the shop can honour a deletion request under the DPDP Act, 2023, and still keep its stock and weight records whole (FR-17-13, BR-17-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer has an approved deletion request, when Sanjay Seth carries it out, then her `name` reads "Erased customer", and `phone`, `address`, `dob` and `anniversary` are null, her status is `erased`, and her version goes up by one (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  2. Given her history rows TAG-7521 and TAG-6690, when the erase commits, then the rows remain with tag, piece name, pure gold grams and date, linked to the erased record and to no name or phone.
  3. Given her consent events, when the erase commits, then the rows stay as proof of consent and an `opt_out` state applies, so she cannot receive a wish or broadcast.
  4. Given she is erased, when the directory is searched or her old phone is matched, then she is not found (EP-17-S8, EP-17-S10).
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) or a request with no approved deletion request, when Erase is called, then the server refuses and nothing changes.
  6. Given Meera Iyer is already erased, when Erase is called again, then the server refuses with `not_found` and nothing changes.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only, or System when EP-39 carries out an approved request. The request must reference an approved deletion request; until EP-39 builds the request flow, the operation takes a deletion request reference and a reason from the owner. All fields are cleared, the consent copy set to false, and the audit entry written in one transaction (EP-03-S6). The erased record is never deleted, so history foreign keys stay valid. Stale version refused (EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_erased`), the deletion request reference, and the names of the erased fields only, never their values (G22). Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Updates `customers` (personal fields cleared, `status` `erased`, `optedIn` false, `version`). Keeps `customer_history` and `consent_events` rows. Adds Erase Customer personal data to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. No mockup draws the deletion step; it belongs with the EP-39 request flow.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: deletion supported under the DPDP Act, 2023; legal obligations verified with a professional (EP-39). Audit: the erase entry holds no erased value. Open question G22: how earlier audit entries that already hold the customer's name are handled, given the log is append-only. Open question: how long the anonymised history is kept. Open question: whether `city` and `notes` are erased too; FR-17-13 names only the five fields above.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S2, EP-17-S8, EP-17-S10, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
