## EP-17-S14: System can audit customer changes without copying erased values

- **Story ID:** EP-17-S14
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit customer changes without copying erased values
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every add, edit, consent change and erase of a customer to write one append-only audit entry in the same transaction, with before and after for changed fields, and the erase entry to name the erased fields without their values
- **So that:** the owner can see who changed a customer record or their consent, when and how, and an erased customer's details do not survive in a new log entry (FR-17-14, epic section 13 audit)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma adds Meera Iyer, when the create commits, then one entry exists with actor Rajesh, server time, entity type customer, entity her id, action `customer_added` and the stored fields as after.
  2. Given Rajesh changes her city from Chennai to Coimbatore, when it commits, then one entry exists with action `customer_edited`, before `{city: "Chennai"}` and after `{city: "Coimbatore"}`, and no unchanged field.
  3. Given Priya Malhotra replies "STOP", when the opt-out commits, then one entry exists with actor System, action `customer_opted_out` and source `whatsapp_reply`.
  4. Given Sanjay Seth erases Meera Iyer, when it commits, then the entry with action `customer_erased` lists the field names name, phone, address, dob and anniversary, and its text contains neither "Meera Iyer" nor "9884021107".
  5. Given an edit that fails after the customer row was updated, when the transaction rolls back, then neither the change nor the audit entry is stored.
  6. Given Sanjay filters the security log by entity type customer, when the results come back, then they list the customer entries newest first (EP-06-S10).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Audit entries are written in the same transaction as the change (EP-06-S2) and cannot be updated or deleted (EP-06-S1). Actor comes from the session or is System, time from the server clock (EP-03-S3, EP-06-S6). Before and after hold only changed fields (EP-06-S3). The erase entry is built from field names only. Audit reads are owner-only (EP-06-S12). A refused request writes no entry.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_added`, `customer_edited`, `customer_consent_recorded`, `customer_opted_out`, `customer_erased`), before, after, source for consent, deletion request reference for erase.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `audit_entries` (EP-02-S11). Adds the customer action kinds to the audit kind list by migration. No other schema change.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show in the security log built in EP-06 (EP-06-S9, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S11).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every customer change writes an append-only entry. Personal data: personal values in before and after are visible only to the owner; the erase entry copies no erased value. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question G22: how a deletion request applies to earlier entries that already hold the customer's name.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S3, EP-17-S5, EP-17-S6, EP-17-S7, EP-17-S13, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S6, EP-06-S7, EP-06-S10, EP-06-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-18: Metal pool ledger · stories

Epic document: [EP-18 Metal pool ledger](../epics/EP-18-metal-pool-ledger.md)

Role note: stories where the server posts, refuses, locks or pushes on its own use "System". Issue and recovery entries are posted by the system inside the job creation of EP-19 and the scrap decision of EP-27; this epic ships the posting function and tests it with a test caller until those epics exist. The owner records the opening balance, returns and adjustments; staff only read the balance.

---

## EP-18-S1: System can store pool entries and a balance as integer weights

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store pool entries and a balance as integer weights
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `metal_pools` and `pool_entries` tables from EP-02-S9 extended so each entry has a kind from `opening`, `issued`, `returned`, `recovered` and `adjustment`, a signed integer delta in units of 0.0001 g, a note, a reference type and id, an actor and a server time, with one shared posting function that inserts an entry and moves the balance in the caller's transaction
- **So that:** every movement of gold is one row with a reference, and the balance always equals the sum of the rows (FR-18-9, FR-18-10, FR-18-12, BR-18-6, BR-18-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `pool_entries` is inspected, then `kind` accepts exactly `opening`, `issued`, `returned`, `recovered` and `adjustment`, `deltaG` is a signed integer in units of 0.0001 g, and each row has `note`, `ref_type` (`job`, `piece` or none), `ref_id`, `actor` and `at` in UTC.
  2. Given the seed, when it is loaded, then `metal_pools.balanceG` is `8125800` (812.5800 g) and equals the sum of all seeded `deltaG` values; after the seeded scrap of TAG-7701 Temple Haram (net 784,000 units) the balance is `8909800` (890.9800 g).
  3. Given the posting function is called with kind `issued`, delta `-1624000` and job MO-2026-118, when the caller's transaction commits, then one entry is stored and the balance has dropped by exactly 1,624,000 units; when the caller's transaction rolls back, neither the entry nor the balance has changed.
  4. Given an attempt to update or delete a row in `pool_entries`, when it reaches the database, then it is refused, because a mistake is corrected by a new entry (FR-18-10).
  5. Given any state of the ledger, when the consistency check sums `deltaG` over all entries and compares it with `metal_pools.balanceG`, then they are equal, and a mismatch fails the check with both numbers (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  6. Given any posting to the pool, when the entry is stored, then it carries `location_id` set by the server to the shop's default location "Main shop"; the balance is still one per shop, and no transfer between locations exists (D7).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The balance is changed only by the shared posting function, never by a direct update, and the function writes the entry and the new balance in the same transaction (EP-03-S6). The function requires an open transaction from its caller and refuses to run outside one. `actor` comes from the session or is System (EP-03-S3, EP-06-S6); `at` comes from the server clock. Weights are converted only through the EP-02-S2 helpers; a delta with more than 4 decimals is refused, not rounded. Database checks: `balanceG` may not be below 0 (BR-18-1), `kind` enum, `ref_type` and `ref_id` both set or both empty. Updates and deletes on `pool_entries` are blocked by a database rule or trigger.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The posting function hands each committed entry to EP-18-S12, which emits "Metal pool changed".
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage and the posting function; each posting story states its own audit entry.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `pool_entries` (EP-02-S9) widens the `kind` enum with `returned` and `adjustment`, renames `ref` to `ref_type` and `ref_id`, and adds `actor` if missing. Migration adds a check that `metal_pools.balanceG >= 0` and a rule that blocks update and delete on `pool_entries`. Adds the posting function and the consistency check to the `api` service layer. One pool row per shop (D7). Each `pool_entries` row carries `location_id` (EP-02-S9), set by the posting function, never from the request.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: all deltas and the balance are integers of 0.0001 g; the seed balance is summed from integers, not floats. Concurrency: `metal_pools.version` exists for EP-18-S5. Time: `at` stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open decision G10: the prototype uses 0.00001 g units (`UNITS_PER_G = 100000`); this story stores 0.0001 g units as PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5 says, and must be settled before launch. D7 is decided: one pool per shop. Open question: one pool or one per purity (22K and 18K); if per purity, a `purity` column is added to both tables before EP-19.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S9, EP-02-S13, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S2: Owner can record the opening balance

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can record the opening balance
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to record the pool's opening balance once, in grams to 4 decimals with a note, through Create Opening entry
- **So that:** the ledger starts from the gold the shop already holds, and every later movement is measured from that figure (FR-18-1, FR-18-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an empty pool with no entries, when Sanjay Seth records an opening balance of 812.5800 g with the note "Gold in the safe, 1 Nov 2026", then one `opening` entry with delta `8125800`, actor Sanjay and server time is stored, and the balance reads 812.5800 g.
  2. Given an opening entry already exists, when Sanjay records a second opening balance, then the server refuses with code `opening_exists` and a sentence telling him to use an adjustment instead, and nothing changes (FR-18-1).
  3. Given Rajesh Verma, a staff user, or a karigar user sends Create Opening entry, when the server checks the permission, then it is refused and nothing changes (FR-18-8).
  4. Given an opening amount of -10.0000 g, 0.0000 g or 812.58001 g, when Sanjay saves, then the server refuses it as a validation error and nothing is stored.
  5. Given the same Create Opening entry request is sent twice with one idempotency key after a network drop, when the server processes it, then only one opening entry exists.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the post-pool-entry permission, which only the owner role has (EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2). Allowed only while the pool has no entries at all, checked under the EP-18-S5 lock so two openings at once cannot both pass. Amount must be more than 0 and have at most 4 decimals (EP-02-S2). Posted through the EP-18-S1 function with no reference. Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8). Entry and audit in one transaction (EP-03-S6, EP-06-S2).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted: "Metal pool changed" (through EP-18-S12).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (metal pool), action (`pool_opening_recorded`), before (balance 0), after (balance and delta in integer units), reason (the note).
- **Data changes:** Inserts one row into `pool_entries` and updates `metal_pools.balanceG` and `version`. Adds Create Opening entry to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The pool balance and ledger page is undrawn (MOCKUP-COVERAGE §3); the opening action belongs on it.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the typed grams string is converted with the EP-02-S2 helper and shown back as "812.5800 g". Audit: the entry stores weights as integer units (EP-06-S5). Security: owner only, checked on the server. Open question (App. B sub-question 1): does the pool already exist in the owner's books and what is the figure; the launch migration in EP-41 may post the opening entry instead of the owner. Open question: who may post an opening entry besides the owner.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S5, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S3: System can post an issue entry inside job creation

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can post an issue entry inside job creation
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Post Issue function that the job-creation operation of EP-19 calls inside its own transaction, which posts an `issued` entry with a negative delta equal to the gold handed over and the job id as its reference
- **So that:** a job never exists without its gold leaving the pool, and gold never leaves the pool without a job (FR-18-2, BR-18-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a balance of 812.5800 g, when a job for Lakshmi Devi · KG-01 is created with "Pure gold issued to Lakshmi" 162.4000 g, then an `issued` entry with delta `-1624000` and reference job id is stored in the same transaction, and the balance is 650.1800 g (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the job creation fails after Post Issue has run, such as a refused karigar, when the transaction rolls back, then no `issued` entry exists and the balance is still 812.5800 g.
  3. Given Post Issue is called with no job id, when it runs, then it refuses and posts nothing, because every issue must reference its job.
  4. Given Post Issue is called outside a caller's transaction, when it runs, then it refuses and posts nothing.
  5. Given a client request that tries to call Post Issue directly, when it reaches the API, then it is refused, because the operation is not in the public contract.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Post Issue is internal: it is not exposed as an endpoint and is callable only from the job-creation service (System, EP-19). It requires the caller's open transaction and a job reference. The amount must pass EP-18-S4 (positive, at most 4 decimals, not above the balance) and is posted under the EP-18-S5 lock. The actor is the user creating the job. Uses the EP-18-S1 posting function.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted: "Metal pool changed" after the job's transaction commits (through EP-18-S12).
- **Audit entry written:** No separate entry. The ledger row is the append-only record of the movement (actor, time, kind, delta, job reference); the job creation's own audit entry from EP-19 covers the job and names the gold issued.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `pool_entries`; updates `metal_pools.balanceG` and `version`. Adds Post Issue to the internal service layer. Until EP-19 exists it is exercised by a test caller.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The gold figure comes from `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("Pure gold issued to Lakshmi", "160 g target + her 0.7% wastage, from the metal pool"), which EP-19 builds; v1 shows it as "162.4000 g".
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: delta is the negative of the issued integer, with no rounding. Concurrency: posted under the EP-18-S5 lock. Open question Q5b / G23: how the issue is settled against the karigar's allowance at reconciliation belongs to EP-19; this story only records the issue. Open question: one pool or one per purity; the mockup issues 22K (916) gold.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-02-S8, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S4: System can refuse an issue above the balance

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse an issue above the balance
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Post Issue to refuse an amount larger than the current balance with "The metal pool does not have that much gold to issue.", and to refuse a negative or zero amount, so that the job creation that called it fails and changes nothing
- **So that:** the pool is never negative and staff are told plainly why the order copy did not go (FR-18-3, FR-18-4, BR-18-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a balance of 150.0000 g, when Rajesh Verma sends an order copy issuing 162.4000 g, then the server refuses with code `pool_insufficient` and the sentence "The metal pool does not have that much gold to issue.", no job and no entry are stored, and the balance is still 150.0000 g.
  2. Given a balance of 162.4000 g, when an issue of exactly 162.4000 g is posted, then it succeeds and the balance is 0.0000 g.
  3. Given an issue of -5.0000 g or 0.0000 g, when it reaches Post Issue, then it is refused as a validation error on the gold field and nothing changes (FR-18-4).
  4. Given an issue of 162.40001 g, when it reaches the server, then it is refused as a validation error and never rounded (EP-02-S2).
  5. Given the refusal reaches the `order-copy` screen, when it is shown, then the sentence appears through the EP-08-S5 refusal display next to "Send the order copy".
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The balance is compared with the amount as integers of 0.0001 g, after the EP-18-S5 lock is taken, so the comparison uses the committed balance. Amount must be more than 0. A refusal is returned in the EP-03-S4 format with the sentence above, and the caller's whole transaction is rolled back (EP-03-S6). The database check `balanceG >= 0` from EP-18-S1 is a second guard.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. A refused issue commits nothing, so no event is sent.
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused request changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the `pool_insufficient` code and its sentence to the shared error list.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("Pure gold issued to Lakshmi", "Send the order copy"). The refusal state is not drawn; it uses the EP-08-S5 pattern.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: integer comparison only. Concurrency: the check runs after the lock in EP-18-S5. Security: the client may warn early from the EP-18-S10 balance, but the server check is the authority.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S3, EP-02-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S5: System can stop two issues overdrawing the pool

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can stop two issues overdrawing the pool
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every posting that lowers the balance to take a row lock on the pool row, or to update it with a version check, before reading the balance, so that two postings at the same moment are applied one after the other
- **So that:** two staff sending order copies at once cannot together issue more gold than the pool holds (FR-18-11, BR-18-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a balance of 100.0000 g, when two issues of 60.0000 g arrive at the same moment, then one succeeds, the balance is 40.0000 g, and the other is refused with "The metal pool does not have that much gold to issue." and leaves no job and no entry (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given a balance of 100.0000 g, when two issues of 40.0000 g arrive at the same moment, then both succeed one after the other and the balance is 20.0000 g.
  3. Given an issue and a negative adjustment that together exceed the balance arrive at the same moment, when both are processed, then only one commits and the other is refused.
  4. Given 20 concurrent issues of 10.0000 g against a balance of 150.0000 g in a test, when they all finish, then exactly 15 succeed, 5 are refused, and the ledger sum equals the balance of 0.0000 g.
  5. Given a version-check conflict is lost by a request, when the server handles it, then it retries the read and check once inside the request, or returns the conflict error in the EP-03-S5 format; it never posts on a stale balance.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Every call of the EP-18-S1 posting function takes the PostgreSQL row lock (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) or performs a conditional update on `metal_pools.version` before computing the new balance. The lock is held only for the caller's transaction. Lock order is fixed (pool row before job or piece rows) so job creation and scrap cannot deadlock each other.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. The committed posting emits "Metal pool changed" through EP-18-S12.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The postings it protects write their own records.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Changes the EP-18-S1 posting function to lock or version-check; adds a concurrency test to the `api` test suite.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the second of two overdrawing issues fails with the sentence above (epic section 13). Performance: the lock is held for one transaction only; a proposed target, to confirm, is no issue waits more than 1 second for the lock with 10 staff working. D1 is decided (Option C): the Node API owns this transaction and takes the row lock or version check on the managed PostgreSQL database; either way it must pass criteria 1 to 4.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-18-S4, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S6: System can post a recovery entry inside a scrap decision

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can post a recovery entry inside a scrap decision
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Post Recovery function that the scrap decision of EP-27 calls inside its own transaction, which posts a `recovered` entry equal to the piece's net gold with the piece id as its reference
- **So that:** scrapping closes the piece but not the gold, which goes back into the pool to be issued again (FR-18-5, BR-18-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given TAG-7701 Temple Haram with net 78.4000 g and a balance of 812.5800 g, when the owner scraps it, then a `recovered` entry with delta `784000` and reference piece TAG-7701 is stored in the same transaction, and the balance is 890.9800 g (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the scrap decision fails after Post Recovery has run, when the transaction rolls back, then no `recovered` entry exists and the balance is unchanged.
  3. Given a piece already has a `recovered` entry, when Post Recovery is called for it again, then it refuses and posts nothing, so one piece is recovered once.
  4. Given Post Recovery is called with no piece id or with a net of 0 or less, when it runs, then it refuses and posts nothing.
  5. Given a client request that tries to call Post Recovery directly, when it reaches the API, then it is refused, because the operation is not in the public contract.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Post Recovery is internal and callable only from the scrap service (System, EP-27). It requires the caller's open transaction and a piece reference. The amount is the piece's stored net (gross units minus stone units), read on the server, not sent by the client. One `recovered` entry per piece, enforced by a unique index on (`kind`, `ref_id`) for `recovered`. Posted under the EP-18-S5 lock through the EP-18-S1 function. The actor is the owner making the scrap decision.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted: "Metal pool changed" after the scrap transaction commits (through EP-18-S12).
- **Audit entry written:** No separate entry. The ledger row is the append-only record (actor, time, kind, delta, piece reference); the scrap decision's own audit entry from EP-27 covers the piece.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `pool_entries`; updates `metal_pools.balanceG` and `version`. Migration adds a unique partial index on `pool_entries` (`ref_id`) where `kind = 'recovered'`. Adds Post Recovery to the internal service layer. Until EP-27 exists it is exercised by a test caller.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The rule is drawn on `docs/ux/mockups/12-state-lifecycles.svg` ("The owner marks the piece as scrap, the piece closes, and its gold goes back into the metal pool to be issued again.").
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the net is computed in integers through EP-02-S2. Concurrency: the unique index stops two scrap decisions on one piece both crediting the pool. Open question (App. B sub-question 2): is stone weight recovered from scrap and tracked, or written off; this story credits net gold only.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-18-S5, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S5, EP-03-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S10: Staff can see the pool balance on the order copy screen

- **So that:** I know how much gold I can hand over before I send the order copy (FR-18-13, BR-18-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**

  2. Given Rajesh enters 900.0000 g as pure gold issued, when the field is checked on the client, then a warning shows that the pool holds 812.5800 g, and sending is still checked by the server (EP-18-S4).

  4. Given a karigar user calls Read Pool balance, when the server checks the permission, then it is refused.
  5. Given the balance read fails or the device is offline, when `order-copy` is open, then the balance area shows the EP-08-S4 error with "Try again" or the EP-08-S11 offline state, and "Send the order copy" is disabled offline.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the read-pool-balance permission (owner and staff, EP-05-S2). The response holds the balance in integer units, its display string and the pool version, and nothing about karigars or entries. The client warning is a convenience; the server check in EP-18-S4 decides.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Metal pool changed" (EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading the balance changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Pool balance to the shared contract and a pool balance component to the web app, used on `order-copy` and on the `stock` pool card.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("THE DUE DATE AND THE GOLD YOU HAND OVER", "Pure gold issued to Lakshmi", "from the metal pool", "Send the order copy"). The balance line and the warning are not drawn; the mockup shows "162.400 g", which v1 shows to 4 decimals as "162.4000 g". The rest of the screen is EP-19.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: proposed target, to confirm, of a balance read under 100 ms; the screen loads within 2 seconds. Precision: shown to 4 decimals from integers. Availability: offline and reconnecting states shown (EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11). D7 is decided: one shop, one pool, and staff see it.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S1, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S11: Owner can see gold with each karigar and a custody summary

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can see gold with each karigar and a custody summary
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** a Read Custody summary operation that returns the gold in the pool, with each karigar on open jobs (issued less returned), in parcels not yet released, in stock and gone, and a Read Gold with karigar operation that the owner can call for any karigar and a karigar can call only for themselves
- **So that:** I can answer where all my gold is right now, and each karigar sees only the gold they hold (FR-18-13, BR-18-4, BR-18-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Vijay Kumar · KG-04 has two open jobs issued 152.4000 g and 34.0000 g with no returns, when Sanjay Seth reads gold with Vijay, then it is 186.4000 g across 2 jobs.
  2. Given 7 open jobs across all karigars holding 612.0000 g in total, when Sanjay reads the custody summary, then "with karigars" is 612.0000 g with 7 open jobs and a per-karigar list, alongside the pool balance, gold in unreleased parcels, gold in stock (net of `in_stock` pieces) and gold gone (net of stocked-out pieces).
  3. Given Vijay Kumar is signed in on the karigar portal, when he reads gold with karigar for himself, then he gets 186.4000 g; when he asks for KG-01 Lakshmi Devi, then the server refuses (EP-05-S3).
  4. Given Rajesh Verma, a staff user, reads the custody summary, when the server checks the permission, then it is refused.
  5. Given a job is closed or settled, when the figures are read again, then its gold no longer counts as with the karigar.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Custody summary is owner only; gold with karigar is owner, or the karigar linked to that karigar record (EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13). All figures are computed on the server from stored integers: open jobs' `goldIssuedG` less their `returned` entries; net of pieces in unreleased parcels, in `in_stock` and stocked out. No money figure and no other karigar's data is returned to a karigar. Open jobs are the statuses EP-19 defines as not closed.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Metal pool changed" refetches the summary while it is open (EP-08-S9).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading figures changes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Custody summary and Read Gold with karigar to the shared contract, replacing the prototype selector `goldWithKarigar` in `src/store/selectors.ts`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg`, route `decisions` ("WHERE THE GOLD IS RIGHT NOW", "Gold on the floor 1,847 g · 42 pieces, ready to sell", "Gold with karigars 612 g · 7 open jobs"); the tiles are built in EP-32 from this read. `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs` ("GOLD WITH ME 186.400 g", "across 2 jobs"), built in EP-20 and shown to 4 decimals. A full custody page is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: sums of integers, shown to 4 decimals. Security: a karigar reads only their own figure (epic section 13). Performance: the summary reads within the 2-second screen budget for 50 karigars and 10,000 pieces. Open question Q5b / G23: whether a settled job's loss is shown here or only in the EP-16 scorecard. Open question (App. B sub-question 2): whether stone weight from scrap is tracked in custody. D7 is decided: figures are shop-wide.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-18-S7, EP-02-S5, EP-02-S6, EP-02-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13, EP-08-S2, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S9, EP-16-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-18-S12: System can push the balance live after a change

- **Story ID:** EP-18-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can push the balance live after a change
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to emit "Metal pool changed" after every committed pool entry, carrying the new balance, the pool version and the entry kind, to owner and staff connections only
- **So that:** the order copy screen and the pool card always show the gold available to issue without a reload (FR-18-14)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth has the `stock` pool card open and Rajesh Verma has `order-copy` open, when an issue of 162.4000 g commits, then both screens show 650.1800 g within about a second (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  2. Given the posting transaction rolls back, when it ends, then no "Metal pool changed" is sent (EP-07-S1).
  3. Given Vijay Kumar is connected on the karigar portal, when any pool entry commits, then he receives no "Metal pool changed" event.
  4. Given two entries commit in a row, when a screen receives the events out of order, then it keeps the figure with the higher pool version.
  5. Given Rajesh's connection drops while an entry commits, when he reconnects, then he catches up from his last sequence number and shows the current balance (EP-07-S7, EP-08-S10).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The event is published only after the transaction commits (EP-07-S1), with sequence number, entity id and version (EP-07-S2). The audience is the roles allowed to open `order-copy`, owner and staff; karigars are excluded by the EP-07 registry and permission filter (EP-07-S5, EP-07-S11). The payload holds the balance, version and entry kind, not the reference, actor or note.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted: "Metal pool changed".
- **Audit entry written:** No. Each posting writes its own record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Wires the EP-18-S1 posting function to the EP-07 publisher and adds "Metal pool changed" to the client event-to-read map for the pool balance, ledger and custody reads (EP-08-S8).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Effects show on `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy`, and on the pool card inside route `stock`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: event reaches open screens within about a second (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1). Concurrency: version in the payload lets a screen drop an older value. Security: no event to karigars.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S1, EP-18-S10, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S4, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S7, EP-07-S11, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9, EP-08-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-19: Order copy and karigar jobs · stories

Epic document: [EP-19 Order copy and karigar jobs](../epics/EP-19-order-copy-and-karigar-jobs.md)

Role note: stories where the server creates, refuses, derives, schedules or pushes on its own use "System". The karigar's phone screens are EP-20; stories here give the karigar the server operations and the job payload that EP-20 shows. Parcel release is EP-23; the settlement in EP-19-S12 ships as a function called by the release and is tested with a test caller until EP-23 exists.

## EP-19-S1: System can store order copies, jobs and settlements with integer weights

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store order copies, jobs and settlements with integer weights
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `order_copies` and `karigar_jobs` tables from EP-02-S8 extended with the fields this epic needs, and a new `job_settlements` table, with every weight an integer in units of 0.0001 g
- **So that:** an order copy can exist with or without a lead, a job carries its own title, purity and dates, and a settlement can be stored once per job (FR-19-1, FR-19-12, BR-19-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migrations have run, when `order_copies` is inspected, then it has `leadId` and `leadItemId` nullable, a nullable `designId` referencing the EP-15-S10 design master, `brief`, `qty`, `purity`, `targetGrossG`, `targetNetG`, `toleranceG`, `goldIssuedG` as integers in units of 0.0001 g, `allowanceBp` (basis points, for example 70 for 0.7%), `karigarId`, `dueDate`, `createdBy` and `createdAt`.
  2. Given an order copy for 2 pieces of 22K (916) with "Finished piece should weigh" 80.000 g, "Allowed to be off by" ± 500 mg and gold issued 162.4000 g, when it is stored and read back, then `targetGrossG` is `800000`, `toleranceG` is `5000` and `goldIssuedG` is `1624000`.
  3. Given the migrations have run, when `karigar_jobs` is inspected, then it has `orderCopyId`, `title`, `style`, `qty`, `purity`, `karigarId`, `status`, `sentAt`, `dueDate`, `confirmedDate`, `stopped`, `parcelId`, `benchNote`, `settledAt`, `cancelledAt` and `version`.
  4. Given the migrations have run, when `job_settlements` is inspected, then it has `jobId` (unique), `issuedG`, `netReturnedG`, `lossG` as signed integers in units of 0.0001 g, `allowanceBp`, `allowedLossG`, `flagged` (boolean) and `settledAt`, and a second settlement row for the same job is rejected by the database.
  5. Given an order copy row with a weight of 80.00005 g or a negative `goldIssuedG`, when it is written through the EP-02-S2 helpers, then it is refused, and no row is stored.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Weights pass only through the EP-02-S2 conversion helpers; more than 4 decimals is refused, never rounded. Database checks: `targetGrossG > 0`, `goldIssuedG >= 0`, `toleranceG >= 0`, `qty >= 1`, `allowanceBp >= 0`. `job_settlements.jobId` is unique. `purity` and `style` must be active list entries (EP-15-S4). Due and confirmed dates are stored as calendar dates read in Asia/Kolkata. No money column on any of the three tables.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Storage only.
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story creates storage; EP-19-S14 and the writing stories state their audit entries.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `order_copies` adds `designId` (nullable, foreign key to designs), `allowanceBp`, and makes `leadId` and `leadItemId` nullable if not already. Migration on `karigar_jobs` adds `title`, `style`, `qty`, `purity`, `sentAt`, `cancelledAt` and `settledAt` where missing. Migration creates `job_settlements` with a unique index on `jobId` and a foreign key to `karigar_jobs`. Reference images stay as attachment rows (EP-09-S8). Overdue columns come from EP-10-S7.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: all weights integers of 0.0001 g; `allowanceBp` is an integer so no percentage is stored as a float. Time: `sentAt`, `settledAt`, `cancelledAt` in UTC; due and confirmed dates are Asia/Kolkata dates. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; jobs carry the shop ID (EP-02-S3) and no `branchId`. Open decision G10: the stored unit must match EP-02 and EP-18.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-02-S8, EP-02-S14, EP-09-S8, EP-15-S4, EP-15-S10, EP-18-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S2: System can issue gold and create a job in one transaction

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can issue gold and create a job in one transaction
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one Create Order copy and job operation that, inside a single transaction, checks the inputs, takes the EP-18 pool lock, creates the order copy and a job in `sent`, posts the `issued` pool entry through EP-18-S3 and writes the audit entry
- **So that:** a job never exists without its gold leaving the pool, and gold never leaves the pool without a job (FR-19-2, FR-19-3, FR-19-5, BR-19-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a pool of 812.5800 g, when Rajesh Verma creates an order copy for Lakshmi Devi · KG-01, 2 pieces, 80.0000 g each, gold issued 162.4000 g, then order copy OC-2026-NNN and job MO-2026-NNN in `sent` exist, an `issued` entry of -162.4000 g references the job, and the pool reads 650.1800 g (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given a pool of 100.0000 g, when Rajesh issues 162.4000 g, then the server refuses with "The metal pool does not have that much gold to issue.", and no order copy, no job and no pool entry exist (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given no karigar is picked, when the request reaches the server, then it refuses with "Pick who makes it."; given a target gross of 0.0000 g, then it refuses with "Enter the weight the finished piece should have."; given gold issued of -1.0000 g, then it refuses with "Gold issued cannot be negative." (FR-19-2).
  4. Given the karigar KG-05 was deactivated after the form loaded, when Rajesh sends, then the server refuses through the EP-16-S8 active-karigar check and nothing is stored.
  5. Given the same request is sent twice with one idempotency key after a network drop, when the server processes it, then one order copy, one job and one pool entry exist, and the second call returns the same ids.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Caller must hold the create-order-copy permission (Owner and Staff, EP-05-S2). Inputs validated against the contract (EP-03-S2). The karigar must be active (EP-16-S8). The job id is the next `MO-YYYY-NNN` and the order copy id the next `OC-YYYY-NNN`, generated without duplicates. `allowanceBp` is copied from the karigar record at send time, so a later allowance change does not alter this job. Order of locks: pool row, then karigar row (EP-18-S5). Pool entry, order copy, job and audit commit or roll back together (EP-03-S6, EP-06-S2). `createdBy` and `createdAt` come from the session and server clock (EP-03-S3). Deduplicated by idempotency key (EP-03-S8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted after commit: "Karigar job status changed" (job sent, through EP-19-S7) and "Metal pool changed" (through EP-18-S12).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (order copy and job id), action (`order_copy_sent`), after (karigar, qty, purity, target gross, target net, tolerance, gold issued in integer units, due date, lead id or none). Written here and listed in EP-19-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `order_copies`, `karigar_jobs` and `pool_entries`; updates `metal_pools.balanceG` and `version`. Adds Create Order copy and job to the shared contract and ports `createOrderCopyAndJob` from `src/store/transitions.ts` as a server service function.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Called from `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("Send the order copy").
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: issue and job creation share one transaction with EP-18's lock; two sends against a pool that holds enough for only one leave one job. Precision: integer comparison against the pool. Audit: create is audited in the same transaction (epic section 13). D1 is decided (Option C): this is a Node API endpoint, and the Node API holds issue, job creation and audit in one transaction.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S7, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S5, EP-16-S8, EP-18-S3, EP-18-S4, EP-18-S5, EP-18-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S3: Staff can build an order copy without a lead

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can build an order copy without a lead
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to open `order-copy` with no lead and fill in reference images, the brief, how many, purity, "Finished piece should weigh", the gold inside after stones, and "Allowed to be off by", then press "Send the order copy"
- **So that:** I can send work to a karigar today without first creating a lead, and the lead path from EP-30 reuses the same screen later (FR-19-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma opens `order-copy` from the Parcels in or karigar area with no `leadId` or `itemId` params, when the screen loads, then it shows the builder with empty fields and the heading "Order copy to a karigar", and no "From the … lead" line.
  2. Given Rajesh adds 3 images through "Add a photo", types the brief "Chettinad long haram, Goddess Lakshmi centre", picks 2 pieces, 22K (916), 80.0000 g, ± 0.5000 g, Lakshmi Devi · KG-01, 17 Nov 2026 and 162.4000 g, when he presses "Send the order copy", then the order copy is created through EP-19-S2 with `leadId` empty, and the screen confirms with the job number.
  3. Given Rajesh types "80.000" in "Finished piece should weigh", when the field loses focus, then it shows "80.0000 g", and a value with 5 decimals is refused with a validation message.
  4. Given the server refuses the send, for example with "Pick who makes it.", when the refusal returns, then the sentence shows next to "Send the order copy" through EP-08-S5 and the typed values stay on the form.
  5. Given the device is offline, when the screen is open, then "Send the order copy" is disabled with the EP-08-S11 offline state, and a send retried after a drop is not applied twice (EP-08-S6).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The same rules as EP-19-S2. Purity and style must be active list entries (EP-15-S4). Reference images must be files the caller uploaded or may read (EP-09-S6, EP-09-S8). The brief is trimmed and limited to 1,000 characters (proposed limit, to confirm). The server never pre-fills a weight from a design or category (BR-19-8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted through EP-19-S2: "Karigar job status changed" and "Metal pool changed". Consumed: "Metal pool changed" for the balance line (EP-18-S10).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, through EP-19-S2 (`order_copy_sent`). Attaching or detaching a reference image is recorded on the order copy's audit entry (EP-09-S8).
- **Data changes:** None beyond EP-19-S2. Moves `src/components/leads/OrderCopyBuilder.tsx` off `useStore()` onto the EP-08 data layer and makes the `leadId` and `itemId` route params optional.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("WHAT YOU SEND · IMAGES AND THE BRIEF", "Add a photo", "The brief, in your words and theirs", "THE TARGETS AND WHO MAKES IT", "How many", "Purity", "Finished piece should weigh", "Allowed to be off by", "Send the order copy"). The mockup shows the lead path; the direct path without the "From the Sharma lead" line is not drawn. Weights show to 4 decimals in v1.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: typed grams converted with the EP-02-S2 helper; "± 500 mg" is entered and shown as "± 0.5000 g" or the mg wording decided in the design pass. Availability: loading, error, offline and reconnecting states (EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11). Performance: the screen loads within 2 seconds (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Open question: whether the brief and target net are required fields.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S2, EP-09-S2, EP-09-S8, EP-15-S5, EP-08-S1, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S6, EP-08-S11, EP-08-S13, EP-08-S17, EP-18-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S4: Staff can pick a karigar and due date with suggested gold shown

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can pick a karigar and due date with suggested gold shown
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to pick "Who makes it" from active karigars, set the "Due date", and see a suggested gold figure (target plus the karigar's allowance) under "Pure gold issued to …" as a hint, while I type the issued figure myself
- **So that:** I hand over the right amount of gold and give the karigar a date that leaves time for QC (FR-19-4, BR-19-2, BR-19-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma picks Lakshmi Devi · KG-01 with allowance 0.7% and enters 2 pieces at 80.0000 g, when Read Suggested gold runs, then the hint reads "161.1200 g suggested · 160.0000 g target + her 0.7% wastage", computed as 1,600,000 × 10,070 ÷ 10,000 = 1,611,200 units.
  2. Given the hint shows 161.1200 g, when Rajesh leaves "Pure gold issued to Lakshmi" empty and presses send, then the server refuses with a validation message on the gold field, because the hint is never copied into the issued figure on its own (FR-19-4).
  3. Given Rajesh types 162.4000 g, when he sends, then 162.4000 g is issued and stored, even though it differs from the hint.
  4. Given Rajesh picks a due date of 14 Nov 2026, when the field is shown, then the note "3 days before the customer needs it, for QC" is shown as guidance, and a due date before today in Asia/Kolkata is refused by the server.
  5. Given the karigar picker opens, when it loads, then it lists only active karigars with name, code, specialty and allowance, such as "Lakshmi Devi · KG-01 · Chettinad specialist · 0.7% loss" (EP-16-S8).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Suggested gold is Owner and Staff only (EP-05-S2) and returns qty × target gross × (10,000 + allowance basis points) ÷ 10,000, in integer units, rounded half up to 1 unit. It changes nothing. The due date must be today or later in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). The karigar must be active (EP-16-S8). The issued figure is required and is whatever staff typed, checked by EP-19-S2.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Metal pool changed" so the balance next to the gold field stays current (EP-18-S10).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading a suggestion changes nothing; the issued figure is audited on send (EP-19-S2).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Suggested gold to the shared contract and the karigar picker and date field to `order-copy`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy` ("Who makes it", "Lakshmi Devi · KG-01", "Chettinad specialist · 0.7% loss · always on time", "THE DUE DATE AND THE GOLD YOU HAND OVER", "Due date", "17 Nov 2026", "3 days before the customer needs it, for QC", "Pure gold issued to Lakshmi", "160 g target + her 0.7% wastage, from the metal pool").
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: suggestion computed in integers. Time: due date is an Asia/Kolkata date. Open question: the mockup shows "162.400 g" for 160 g plus 0.7%, but 160 g plus 0.7% is 161.1200 g; the source figure needs confirming, and this story uses the arithmetic. Open question: whether the suggestion is based on target gross (as the mockup's "160 g target" implies) or target net, since the gold issued is pure gold. Open question: whether the "3 days before" rule is a guide only or enforced against a customer date when the order copy comes from a lead.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S3, EP-16-S1, EP-16-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-10-S10, EP-18-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S5: Karigar can receive the sent job

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Karigar can receive the sent job
- **As a:** Karigar
- **I want:** a job sent to me to appear in my job list and be readable with its reference images, brief, quantity, purity, targets, tolerance and due date, with a notice that it has arrived
- **So that:** I know what to make and by when without a phone call from the desk (FR-19-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given job MO-2026-119 is sent to Lakshmi Devi · KG-01, when Lakshmi, signed in as the karigar user linked to KG-01, lists her jobs, then MO-2026-119 is returned in `sent` with title, "2 pieces · 22K", "Finished piece must weigh 80.0000 g", "Allowed to be off by ± 0.5000 g", the due date 17 Nov 2026 and the brief.
  2. Given the job payload returned to Lakshmi, when it is inspected, then it has no customer name, customer phone, lead id, price or other karigar's data (epic section 13).
  3. Given Vijay Kumar · KG-04 is signed in, when he asks for MO-2026-119, then the server returns `not_found` (EP-05-S3).
  4. Given the job is sent, when the transaction commits, then Lakshmi gets one notification naming the job (EP-11-S8) and her open job list updates live (EP-07-S6).
  5. Given Lakshmi opens the job, when its reference images load, then she sees only that job's reference images through signed, expiring links (EP-09-S9).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List My jobs and Read Job for a karigar are filtered in the query to `karigarId` equal to the session user's linked karigar (EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13). Owner and Staff may read any order copy. The karigar response shape is a fixed allow-list of fields that excludes lead, customer and money fields. Images are served per EP-09-S6 and EP-09-S9.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Karigar job status changed" (job sent) on the karigar's own channel.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading a job changes nothing.

Open question G14: if one hand-over can carry several jobs, the list may group jobs; this story returns one row per job.

## EP-19-S6: System can enforce the job state order and the stopped guard

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can enforce the job state order and the stopped guard
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** Update Job state operations for accept (with a confirmed date), start, mark ready and hand over that allow only `sent` → `accepted` → `on_bench` → `ready` → `handed_over`, refuse any move on a stopped job, and use a version check
- **So that:** a job's state always means the same thing, and a stopped job stays still until the owner clears the problem (FR-19-6, FR-19-7, BR-19-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given MO-2026-119 in `sent`, when Lakshmi Devi accepts it with confirmed date 16 Nov 2026, then it is `accepted` with `confirmedDate` 16 Nov 2026; a second accept is refused with "This job has already been accepted."
  2. Given a job in `accepted`, when "mark ready" is sent, then the server refuses with "Mark it as being worked on first."; given a job in `sent`, when "start" is sent, then it refuses with "Accept the job first."; given a job in `on_bench`, when "hand over" is sent, then it refuses with "Mark the job ready before handing it over."
  3. Given MO-2026-118 has `stopped` true, when Vijay Kumar tries to start, mark ready or hand it over, then the server refuses with "This job is stopped. Only the owner can start it again." and nothing changes (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  4. Given Vijay Kumar · KG-04 sends any state change for a KG-01 job, when the server checks it, then it returns `not_found` and nothing changes.
  5. Given two state changes on one job arrive with the same version, when both are processed, then one commits and the other gets the EP-03-S5 conflict error.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Accept, start and mark ready may be called by the karigar linked to the job (EP-05-S3); Owner and Staff may not move a karigar's state for them unless the decided rule allows it. Hand over is called by the EP-20 hand-over operation, which creates the parcel in the same transaction. Only the transitions listed are allowed; a `cancelledAt` job cannot move. The confirmed date must be today or later in Asia/Kolkata. The stopped flag is set and cleared only by EP-24; this story only reads it. Each change checks `version` (EP-02-S14) and writes the audit entry in the same transaction.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted after commit: "Karigar job status changed" (through EP-19-S7).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (job id), action (`job_accepted`, `job_started`, `job_ready`, `job_handed_over`), before and after status, confirmed date on accept, bench note if given (EP-06-S7).
- **Data changes:** Updates `karigar_jobs.status`, `confirmedDate`, `benchNote`, `parcelId` and `version`. Adds the four Update Job state operations to the shared contract and ports `acceptJob`, `startJob`, `markJobReady`, `handOver` and `stoppedGuard` from `src/store/transitions.ts`.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The rail is drawn on `docs/ux/mockups/12-state-lifecycles.svg` ("Sent to him", "Accepted, date set", "On the bench", "Ready", "Sent to the store"); the buttons ("Gold received", "Working on it", "Ready for checking", "Sent to the showroom") are on `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs`, built in EP-20.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: version check on every transition. Security: a karigar moves only their own jobs. Audit: every transition audited, which the prototype does not do (epic section 13). Open question G14: if one hand-over carries several jobs, hand over moves each job in one transaction with one parcel. Open question: whether staff may move a job's state on the karigar's behalf, for example when the karigar has no phone.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S2, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S3, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S7, EP-10-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S9: System can flag overdue jobs and remind the karigar

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can flag overdue jobs and remind the karigar
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the EP-10-S7 overdue job to run against the real `karigar_jobs` table, every job read to return its agreed date and days over, and each overdue job to hand one reminder per day to the karigar through EP-11-S8
- **So that:** a late job is visible and the karigar is reminded without anyone chasing by hand (FR-19-9, FR-19-10, BR-19-4, BR-19-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given MO-2026-121 for Mahesh Soni · KG-02 with due date 30 Oct 2026, no confirmed date and status `on_bench`, when the overdue job runs on 2 Nov 2026 in Asia/Kolkata, then the job reads "3 days over", `overdueSince` is set, and Mahesh gets one reminder for that day.
  2. Given a job with due date 1 Nov and confirmed date 5 Nov, when the job runs on 2 Nov, then it is not overdue, because the confirmed date wins (BR-19-5).
  3. Given a job in `sent` that was never accepted, when its due date passes, then it is overdue in the same way, because the rule applies from send.
  4. Given an overdue job is handed over, when the hand-over commits, then it reads 0 days over and the next run sends no reminder.
  5. Given a job becomes overdue, when the change commits, then "Job passed its agreed date" is published to owner and staff and to that karigar only, and the reminder text has no customer, lead or price detail.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** A job is overdue from the day after its agreed date until handed over or cancelled (FR-19-9). Days over are whole Asia/Kolkata days (EP-10-S10). One reminder per job per day, keyed by job id, "overdue" and date (EP-10-S4). A stopped job is still counted overdue but its reminder says it is stopped, so the karigar is not told to hurry a job only the owner can restart. Reminder audience and channel are EP-11's.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted: "Job passed its agreed date" (proposed, gap G26, through EP-10-S7). Consumed: "Karigar job status changed" to stop counting a handed-over job.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, through EP-10-S12: actor System, time, entity (job id), action (`job_overdue`), after (`overdueSince`). Reminders are notification rows, not audit entries.
- **Data changes:** Uses `overdueSince` and `lastReminderAt` from EP-10-S7. Adds agreed date and days over to the job read shapes, replacing `agreedDate` and `jobOverdueDays` in `src/store/selectors.ts`.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. The rule is drawn on `docs/ux/mockups/12-state-lifecycles.svg` ("Past the agreed date the job joins the overdue tracker, the karigar is reminded and the owner sees it on Decisions."); the karigar sees it on `k-jobs` (EP-20).
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: dates and days over computed in Asia/Kolkata. Availability: a missed run after downtime runs once on recovery (EP-10-S11). Open question (compare A3): which channel carries the overdue reminder and how often; this story sends once a day until decided. Open question: whether a stopped job's reminder is suppressed.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S6, EP-19-S7, EP-10-S4, EP-10-S7, EP-10-S10, EP-10-S11, EP-10-S12, EP-11-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S11: Staff can cancel a job and return the gold

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can cancel a job and return the gold
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to cancel a job that is not handed over, with a reason, so that it closes and its gold goes back to the pool in one `returned` entry through EP-18
- **So that:** gold issued for work that will not be made is back in the pool and no longer counted as with the karigar (FR-19-11)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given MO-2026-119 in `sent` with 162.4000 g issued and no returns, when Rajesh Verma cancels it with the reason "Customer changed the design", then `cancelledAt` is set, a `returned` entry of +162.4000 g references the job, and the pool rises by 162.4000 g.
  2. Given the cancelled job, when it is cancelled again, then the server refuses and no second `returned` entry is posted.
  3. Given a job in `handed_over`, when Rajesh tries to cancel it, then the server refuses and nothing changes.
  4. Given a job in `accepted`, `on_bench` or `ready`, when Rajesh tries to cancel it, then the server applies the decided rule; until the rule is decided it refuses with code `cancel_rule_pending` and nothing changes.
  5. Given a reason shorter than 3 characters, or a karigar user sending cancel, when the server checks it, then it refuses and nothing changes.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Cancel is Owner and Staff (EP-05-S2). Allowed in `sent`; other non-handed-over states follow the open rule. A stopped job may be cancelled only by the owner (proposed, to confirm). The returned amount is the job's `goldIssuedG` less its earlier `returned` entries, read on the server, never sent by the client. The return is posted as an internal System entry inside the cancel transaction through the EP-18-S1 posting function under the EP-18-S5 lock, with one cancel return per job enforced by a unique index. Job update, pool entry and audit commit together. Version check on the job.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Emitted after commit: "Karigar job status changed" (job cancelled, through EP-19-S7) and "Metal pool changed" (through EP-18-S12).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (job id), action (`job_cancelled`), before (status), after (`cancelledAt`, gold returned in integer units), reason.
- **Data changes:** Updates `karigar_jobs.cancelledAt` and `version`; inserts one `returned` row into `pool_entries` and updates `metal_pools.balanceG`. Migration adds a unique partial index on `pool_entries` (`ref_id`) for cancel returns. Adds Cancel Job to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. No mockup draws cancel; it belongs on the tracker card or the job detail.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the unique index and job version stop a double return (epic section 16). Audit: cancel is audited (epic section 13). Precision: integer arithmetic for the returned amount. Open question: can a job be cancelled after it is accepted, and if so is the full issued gold returned or only what the karigar hands back and is weighed. Open question: can an order copy be edited after send; edit before accept is listed in the epic's API surface but has no candidate story, so it is not built here.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S6, EP-19-S7, EP-18-S1, EP-18-S5, EP-18-S7, EP-18-S12, EP-02-S14, EP-03-S4, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S12: System can settle a job when its parcel is released (G23)

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can settle a job when its parcel is released (G23)
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a Settle Job function that the parcel release of EP-23 calls inside its own transaction, which records gold issued, net returned, the allowance in force, the allowed loss and the loss, sets `settledAt`, and flags a loss above the allowance
- **So that:** each job is reconciled against the karigar's wastage allowance, apart from the parcel's exact-match check in EP-23 (FR-19-12, FR-19-13, BR-19-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given MO-2026-119 issued 162.4000 g with no returns, allowance 70 basis points, and its released parcel holds pieces with net 160.9000 g in total, when settlement runs, then a `job_settlements` row stores issued `1624000`, net returned `1609000`, loss `15000` (1.5000 g), allowed loss `11368` (1.1368 g) and flagged true (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given the same job with net returned 161.5000 g, when settlement runs, then loss is 0.9000 g, which is within 1.1368 g, and flagged is false.
  3. Given the job had a `returned` pool entry of 2.0000 g before release, when settlement runs, then the returned gold is subtracted from issued before the loss is computed.
  4. Given a job is already settled, when Settle Job is called again, then it refuses and nothing changes, because the settlement row is unique per job.
  5. Given the parcel release rolls back after Settle Job ran, when the transaction ends, then no settlement row exists and `settledAt` is empty.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Settle Job is internal, callable only from the release service (EP-23) and a test caller until then. It requires the caller's open transaction. Net returned is the sum of stored net (gross less stone, in integer units) of the job's pieces in the released parcel, read on the server. Loss = issued − earlier returns − net returned, which may be zero or negative; a negative loss is stored and not flagged. Allowed loss = (issued − earlier returns) × `allowanceBp` ÷ 10,000, rounded down to 1 unit, using the allowance copied onto the order copy at send. The settlement is kept apart from the EP-23 exact-match check (reconciliation B here, A there).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. The release that calls it emits its own events in EP-23. The owner reads the flag through Read Job settlement; showing it on Decisions is EP-32.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (the user releasing the parcel, or System), time, entity (job id), action (`job_settled`), after (issued, net returned, loss, allowed loss in integer units, flagged).
- **Data changes:** Inserts one row into `job_settlements`; sets `karigar_jobs.settledAt`. Adds Settle Job to the internal service layer and Read Job settlement (Owner only) to the shared contract. Replaces the prototype `finishRelease` stamp and its append to `Karigar.gapsMg`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The settlement is named on `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg` ("settled against this job when the parcel is reconciled"); no screen shows the settlement or the flag.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: all figures integers of 0.0001 g. Audit: settlement audited (epic section 13). Security: Read Job settlement is Owner only; a karigar does not see the flag. Open question G23: when settlement is computed, who sees the flag, and whether loss is booked against the karigar ledger; criteria use the allowed-loss formula above until decided. Open question Q5b: whether intake is only reconciliation A with wastage handled here. Open question G14: if one parcel carries several jobs, how net returned is split per job. Open question G4: which settlement figures feed the EP-16 scorecard.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S1, EP-19-S2, EP-18-S1, EP-18-S7, EP-02-S5, EP-02-S6, EP-03-S6, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S5, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

  3. Given Rajesh completes the draft and sends it, when it commits through EP-19-S2, then the order copy stores `designId` and `leadId` empty.
  4. Given Vijay Kumar has been deactivated since, when the draft opens, then the karigar field is empty with a note that Vijay is no longer active, and Rajesh picks another.
  5. Given Rajesh leaves the draft without sending, when he returns later, then nothing was created on the server and no gold was issued.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Reorder draft is Owner and Staff (EP-05-S2) and only returns a draft; it stores nothing. It reads the design from EP-15-S10, refuses a design that is not sold out per EP-15-S11 with a validation message, and never returns weights. The suggested karigar is the maker of the most recent piece of the design, returned only if active (EP-16-S8). Sending is EP-19-S2 with its full checks.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None for the draft. Sending emits through EP-19-S2.
- **Audit entry written:** No for the draft, which stores nothing. The send writes `order_copy_sent` with `designId` (EP-19-S2).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database for the draft. Adds Create Reorder draft to the shared contract and a `designId` route param to `order-copy`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/03-showroom-stock.svg`, route `stock` ("Sold out", "Peacock Ruby Pendant", "TAG-7914 · 22K · Antique", "Asked for 4 times since July", "Order another from Vijay"), opening `docs/ux/mockups/19-order-copy-builder.svg`, route `order-copy`. The stock card is built in EP-22.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the draft returns no customer or price data. Open question G3: what "Order another from Vijay" copies from the sold piece, such as photos as reference images, the brief or the quantity; this story copies design, category, style and karigar only until decided.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S3, EP-19-S4, EP-15-S10, EP-15-S11, EP-16-S8, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-19-S14: System can audit order copy and job changes

- **Story ID:** EP-19-S14
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit order copy and job changes
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every write on order copies and jobs to write one audit entry in its own transaction, with fixed action names `order_copy_sent`, `job_accepted`, `job_started`, `job_ready`, `job_handed_over`, `job_cancelled`, `job_overdue` and `job_settled`, and a test that fails if any job write has none
- **So that:** the owner can see who sent, moved, cancelled or settled each job and what changed, which the prototype does not record (epic section 13)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma sends MO-2026-119, when Sanjay Seth filters the audit log by entity MO-2026-119, then he sees `order_copy_sent` with actor Rajesh, the karigar, the targets and gold issued 162.4000 g.
  2. Given Lakshmi Devi accepts, starts and marks the job ready, when the log is read, then three entries show actor Lakshmi, before and after status and the confirmed date.
  3. Given the overdue job marks the job late and the parcel release settles it, when the log is read, then `job_overdue` shows actor System and `job_settled` shows the settlement figures in integer units.
  4. Given any job write rolls back, when the transaction ends, then no audit entry for it exists.
  5. Given the test suite runs, when each job operation in the contract is exercised, then each one writes exactly one audit entry with its action name, and the test fails if one writes none.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Audit entries are written through EP-06-S2 in the same transaction as the change, with before and after values (EP-06-S3) and weights as integer units (EP-06-S5). System actions name the System actor (EP-06-S6). Audit entries cannot be updated or deleted (EP-06-S1). Reads stay Owner only (EP-06-S12).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (order copy or job id), action, before, after, reason (cancel only), for each action listed above.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database beyond `audit_entries` rows. Adds the eight action names to the shared audit kind list under the job kind group (EP-06-S10) and the coverage test to the `api` test suite.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries show in the owner's audit log from EP-06-S9 to EP-06-S11.
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: create, cancel and settlement audited as the epic requires, plus every transition (EP-06-S7). Precision: weights in entries as integers. Personal data: entries carry no customer data, because jobs have none.
- **Depends on:** EP-19-S2, EP-19-S6, EP-19-S9, EP-19-S11, EP-19-S12, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S5, EP-06-S6, EP-06-S7, EP-06-S9, EP-06-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-20: Karigar portal · stories

Epic document: [EP-20 Karigar portal](../epics/EP-20-karigar-portal-pwa.md)

Role note: stories where the server filters, creates, replays or pushes on its own use "System". The job state rules and the job payload come from EP-19; this epic builds the karigar's phone on `k-jobs` and the karigar-side operations. Parcel weighing and tagging are EP-21, send-back is EP-23, and clearing a raised problem is EP-24. Where those epics are not built yet, the stories here are tested with seeded parcels, jobs and problems. v1 is English only, so the "हिन्दी" chip on mockup 09 is not built in any story here (EP-44).

## EP-20-S1: System can limit every karigar read to the signed-in karigar's jobs

- **Story ID:** EP-20-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can limit every karigar read to the signed-in karigar's jobs
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every karigar-callable operation in this epic (List My jobs, Read My job, the state changes, Create Hand-over, Create Job media, Update Job note, Read Gold with me, Create Raised problem) to filter by the karigar record linked to the session user, and to return a fixed allow-list of fields
- **So that:** a karigar sees only the jobs issued to him and never sees prices, margins, invoices, customers, leads, stock or another karigar's work (FR-20-2, FR-20-11, BR-20-1, BR-20-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Vijay Kumar · KG-04 is signed in, when he calls Read My job for MO-2026-119, a job of Lakshmi Devi · KG-01, then the server returns `not_found`, the same response as for a job id that does not exist (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Vijay is signed in, when he calls Create Hand-over, Create Job media, Update Job note or Create Raised problem with the id of a KG-01 job, then each returns `not_found` and nothing changes.
  3. Given a karigar user whose account has no linked karigar record (EP-05-S13), when he calls List My jobs, then the server returns an empty list and every job read returns `not_found`.
  4. Given the contract test suite runs, when the response of each karigar operation is checked against its allow-list, then the test fails if any response has a field for price, margin, invoice, customer name, customer phone, lead id, piece stock status or another karigar's id (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  5. Given a Staff or Owner session, when it calls List My jobs, then the server refuses with the EP-05-S2 permission error, because the desk reads jobs through the EP-19 shapes.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The karigar id comes from the session user's link (EP-05-S13), never from the request. The filter is part of the query, not a check after the read (EP-05-S3). A job of another karigar and a job that does not exist return the same `not_found` (EP-03-S5). Karigar response shapes are allow-lists defined once in the shared contract (EP-03-S1). Only the Karigar role may call these operations (EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The live filter for karigars is EP-07-S6.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads change nothing, and refused writes store nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the karigar response shapes and the allow-list contract test to the shared package and the `api` test suite.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The rule is drawn on `docs/ux/mockups/11-roles-and-permissions.svg` ("See the jobs issued to him, and only those", "NEVER SEES", "Prices, margins or invoices", "Customers, leads or stock", "Any other karigar's work or scorecard").
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: every karigar request is filtered on the server; other jobs return not-found (epic section 13). Personal data: the phone receives only the karigar's own jobs. D4 is decided: phone numbers are unique, so each session names one karigar.
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S1, EP-03-S5, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3, EP-05-S13, EP-16-S6, EP-19-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-20-S2: Karigar can sign in on the phone

- **Story ID:** EP-20-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Karigar can sign in on the phone
- **As a:** Karigar
- **I want:** to sign in on my phone with the method EP-04 provides, land on "My jobs" (`k-jobs`), stay signed in at the bench, and be signed out at once if the owner deactivates me
- **So that:** only I can see and move my jobs from my phone (FR-20-1, FR-20-16, BR-20-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Vijay Kumar's phone number is on an active karigar user linked to KG-04, when he completes sign-in on a 5-inch phone, then he lands on `k-jobs` with the heading "My jobs" and "Vijay Kumar · KG-04", with no role switcher and no desk rail (EP-04-S6, EP-08-S12).
  2. Given the sign-in screen on the phone, when it is measured, then every button and input is at least 56 px tall and no text is below 15 px (BR-20-3).
  3. Given Vijay types a wrong or expired code, when the server answers, then the phone shows the EP-04-S7 sentence in at least 15 px text and lets him ask for a new code.
  4. Given Vijay is signed in on the phone, when the owner deactivates his user, then the phone is returned to sign-in within about a second if connected, and any later request with the old session is refused (EP-04-S13, EP-05-S10, EP-08-S15).
  5. Given Vijay presses "Sign out" on the Me tab, when the request completes, then the session ends and the phone shows sign-in (EP-04-S11).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Sign-in, code checks, lockout and rate limits are EP-04's. Only a user with role Karigar and a linked karigar record lands on `k-jobs` (EP-05-S13). Deactivation ends every session of the user at once (EP-04-S13). Idle expiry follows EP-04-S12.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "User deactivated or role changed" to close the connection and return to sign-in (EP-07-S10).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, through EP-04-S14: actor, time, action (sign-in, failure, lockout, sign-out), with no code value.
- **Data changes:** None beyond EP-04 sessions. Moves `KarigarPhone.tsx` off the demo identity (`Identity.karigarId` and "Sign in as a karigar from the switcher") onto the real session.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed for the phone sign-in. Landing is `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs` ("Vijay Kumar · KG-04", "My jobs").
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: no demo role switcher in the build (EP-08-S19); deactivation ends sessions at once (BR-20-8). D4 is decided: phone and password, phone numbers unique, so a karigar cannot sign in on a shared phone number. D5 is decided: the karigar app is a React web app opened in the phone browser. D6 is decided: online only.
- **Depends on:** EP-04-S3, EP-04-S5, EP-04-S6, EP-04-S7, EP-04-S11, EP-04-S12, EP-04-S13, EP-04-S14, EP-05-S10, EP-05-S13, EP-07-S10, EP-08-S12, EP-08-S15, EP-08-S19
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
