## EP-31-S5: Staff can see parcels waiting to be weighed, tagged or matched

- **Story ID:** EP-31-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see parcels waiting to be weighed, tagged or matched
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** one card for each `open` parcel, saying whether it has not been weighed, how many pieces are still untagged, or that it is fully tagged and ready to match, with an action that opens the right intake step
- **So that:** parcels move through intake without someone having to check the parcels-in list (FR-31-5, FR-31-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given BATCH-2026-046 from Lakshmi Devi is `open` with no weighing, when Rajesh Verma opens `today`, then a `gold` card reads "BATCH-2026-046 from Lakshmi Devi has not been weighed" with detail "Weigh the whole parcel before anything is tagged." and the action "Weigh it" opens `parcel-arrival` for that parcel.
  2. Given BATCH-2026-043 is weighed, expects 21 pieces and has 12 tagged, when `today` loads, then a `wait` card reads "9 pieces still untagged in BATCH-2026-043" with detail "Lakshmi Devi's parcel · arrived 1 day ago. Tag them to finish reconciling the parcel weight." and "Tag pieces" opens `parcel-tag`.
  3. Given BATCH-2026-043 then has all 21 pieces tagged, when `today` is read, then the card reads "BATCH-2026-043 is fully tagged and ready to match" with detail "Lakshmi Devi's parcel · 21 pieces. Check it and release it to the showcase." and "Match and release" opens `parcel-match`.
  4. Given BATCH-2026-043 is released into stock, when `today` is read, then no card for it is returned.
  5. Given a parcel with 1 piece untagged, when the card is built, then it reads "1 piece still untagged", using the singular.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** One card per `open` parcel, never two. "Not weighed" means no weighing row (EP-21-S3). The expected and tagged counts come from the parcel manifest and saved tags (EP-21-S1). Stopped and released parcels are not open and get no card here. The action route follows the parcel's next step, as the prototype `parcelTarget` does.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story; EP-31-S11 consumes "Parcel handed over by karigar", "Tag saved on a shared parcel" and "Parcel released into stock" (proposed, G26) to refresh these cards.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Builds the `parcel_unweighed`, `parcel_untagged` and `parcel_ready` cards inside Read Today cards; ports `parcelTarget` from `src/components/parcels/util.ts`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/02-staff-home.svg` ("9 pieces still untagged in BATCH-2026-043", "Chettinad parcel from Lakshmi Devi · arrived yesterday", "Tag them to finish reconciling the parcel weight.", "Tag pieces"), route `today`. The "not weighed" and "ready to match" cards are not drawn; they reuse the same card.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: "arrived … ago" from the server `arrivedAt` in UTC, shown relative to Asia/Kolkata now. Concurrency: counts come from committed tags only, so two staff tagging the same parcel see the same count.
- **Depends on:** EP-31-S1, EP-21-S1, EP-21-S2, EP-21-S3, EP-21-S6, EP-21-S10, EP-23-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-31-S8: Staff can see the showcase figures in grams and counts

- **Story ID:** EP-31-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see the showcase figures in grams and counts
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** one Read Showcase figures operation that returns pure gold on the floor, pieces I can sell today, pieces held back from the floor, pieces out today and gold out today, as integer sums and counts, shown under "THE SHOWCASE RIGHT NOW" and in "GOLD OUT TODAY"
- **So that:** I know how the showcase stands in grams and pieces without any money figure (FR-31-10, BR-31-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given 42 `in_stock` pieces whose pure gold sums to `18472000` units, when Rajesh Verma opens `today`, then "Pure gold on the floor" reads "1,847.2000 g" and "Pieces you can sell today" reads 42.
  2. Given 14 pieces are in `draft`, `with_owner` or `stopped`, when `today` loads, then "Held back from the floor" reads 14, and `billed` and `scrapped` pieces are not counted.
  3. Given 11 pieces carrying `2124000` units of pure gold were stocked out since midnight Asia/Kolkata, when `today` loads, then "Pieces out today" reads 11, "GOLD OUT TODAY" reads "212.4000 g", and the line under the figures reads "Pieces out today carry 212.4000 g of pure gold." (EP-26-S13).
  4. Given a stock-out at 23:50 on 31 October and one at 00:10 on 1 November, Asia/Kolkata, when `today` is read on 1 November, then only the 00:10 pieces are counted in pieces out today and gold out today.
  5. Given the response is inspected, when its fields are read, then it holds only counts and integer weights in units of 0.0001 g, and no field named or holding a rupee value.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Showcase figures is Staff and Owner only (EP-05-S2). Sums are integer sums on the server over `pieces.status` and stock-outs (EP-22-S10, EP-26-S13); the browser does not add weights. "Today" starts at midnight Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). No value field is returned.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story; EP-31-S11 consumes "Piece billed by one staff member", "Edit applied" and "Parcel released into stock" (proposed, G26) to refresh these figures.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Showcase figures to the shared contract; replaces the browser selectors `pureGoldOnFloor`, `inStockPieces`, `heldBackPieces`, `piecesOutToday` and `goldOutToday` in `src/store/selectors.ts` with the server read.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/02-staff-home.svg` ("THE SHOWCASE RIGHT NOW", "Pure gold on the floor 1,847.2 g", "Pieces you can sell today 42", "Held back from the floor 14", "Pieces out today 11", "GOLD OUT TODAY 212.4 g"), route `today`. Weights show to 4 decimals in v1.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: every weight is an integer sum in units of 0.0001 g, formatted to 4 decimals only for display. Time: the day boundary is midnight Asia/Kolkata. Performance: the figures return in under 2 seconds. D7 is decided: the figures cover the shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-31-S3, EP-22-S1, EP-22-S10, EP-26-S13, EP-10-S10, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-31-S9: Staff can see today's birthdays and anniversaries

- **Story ID:** EP-31-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see today's birthdays and anniversaries
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a List Wishes due today read that returns customers whose `dob` or `anniversary` day and month fall on today in Asia/Kolkata and who have not been wished today, each with name, group, kind and "last bought" or purchase count, shown under "SAY HAPPY BIRTHDAY" with a "Message" action
- **So that:** no regular customer's birthday or anniversary passes unnoticed at the counter (FR-31-11)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra (VIP Bridal) has `dob` 1 November and last bought a Polki kada, when Rajesh Verma opens `today` on 1 November 2026, then a row reads "Priya Malhotra · birthday today" with "VIP Bridal · last bought Polki kada" and a "Message" button.
  2. Given Arjun & Kavya have `anniversary` 1 November and 4 purchases with no named last item, when `today` loads, then a row reads "Arjun & Kavya · anniversary today" with "High net worth · 4 purchases".
  3. Given two rows are due, when the section is shown, then its heading reads "SAY HAPPY BIRTHDAY · 2"; given none is due, then it reads "No birthdays or anniversaries are left to wish today."
  4. Given a customer has been wished today for that kind, when the list is read, then that customer is not returned for that kind.
  5. Given a customer is `erased` (EP-17-S13), when the list is read, then they are not returned; and each returned row holds only id, name, group, kind and last purchase name or count, with no phone.

Only `active` customers are listed. "Not yet wished" reads the wishes sent today once EP-33 stores them; until then every due customer is listed. The consent rule for sending is enforced at send time by EP-33, not here.

- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.

The "Message" action opens route `wishes`, delivered by EP-33; until that route exists the button is hidden.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: rows show only name, group and last purchase; no phone, birth year or address (epic section 13). Time: "today" is the Asia/Kolkata date. Open question: the source of "last bought" depends on G13 (a stock-out records no customer); until it is answered the last purchase comes from the customer's piece history (EP-17-S9).
- **Depends on:** EP-31-S3, EP-17-S1, EP-17-S9, EP-17-S13, EP-10-S10, EP-05-S2

## EP-31-S11: Staff can see cards and figures update live

- **Story ID:** EP-31-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see cards and figures update live
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** the cards and showcase figures on `today` to refetch within about 1 second when a relevant live event arrives, without a reload, and to catch up after a dropped connection
- **So that:** what I see is what is true now, while other people sell, tag and raise problems (FR-31-13, BR-31-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma is on `today`, when Deepak Rao stocks out a piece with 41.5900 g of pure gold, then within about 1 second "Pure gold on the floor" falls by 41.5900 g, "Pieces you can sell today" falls by 1, "Pieces out today" rises by 1 and "GOLD OUT TODAY" rises by 41.5900 g (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given a karigar hands over a parcel, when "Parcel handed over by karigar" arrives, then a "has not been weighed" card appears (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given Deepak saves a tag on BATCH-2026-043, when "Tag saved on a shared parcel" arrives, then the card changes from "9 pieces still untagged" to "8 pieces still untagged".
  4. Given a lead passes its SLA, when "Lead arrived / passed its SLA" arrives, then its card changes to "past the 8 h limit" and moves to its ranked place; given BATCH-2026-044 is stopped, when "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" arrives, then its card appears.
  5. Given the connection drops for 2 minutes and a parcel is released meanwhile, when it returns, then "Reconnecting…" shows while down, and on return the cards and figures are refetched so the released parcel's card is gone (EP-08-S10, EP-07-S7).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Events reach this user only through the EP-07-S5 permission filter. The client refetches Read Today cards and Read Showcase figures on each event; the card list and ranking always come from the server, never patched from the event payload alone.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Piece billed by one staff member", "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit applied", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", "Parcel handed over by karigar", "Tag saved on a shared parcel"; proposed (G26): "Parcel released into stock", "Setting changed", "Problem raised on a job or piece", "Problem cleared", "Piece scrapped". Emitted: none.
- **Audit entry written:** No. This screen only reads.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the `today` entries to the event-to-read map in the EP-08 data layer (EP-08-S8).
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/02-staff-home.svg`, route `today`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: changes appear within about 1 second of the event (BR-31-8); a burst of tag saves is coalesced into one refetch per short interval so the read is not repeated per event. Availability: "Reconnecting…" and catch-up from the last sequence number (EP-07-S7, EP-08-S10). Concurrency: two staff on `today` see the same cards after the same event.
- **Depends on:** EP-31-S1, EP-31-S8, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S7, EP-07-S11, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9, EP-08-S10, EP-26-S11, EP-21-S11, EP-28-S13, EP-24-S11, EP-24-S12, EP-13-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-32: Owner Decisions home · stories

Epic document: [EP-32 Owner Decisions home](../epics/EP-32-owner-decisions-home.md)

Role note: stories where the server builds, counts or computes on its own use "System". The owner lands on `decisions`; staff and karigars never see it and every read here refuses them. The screen itself only reads; actions taken from a card (clear, apply, decide, chase) write their audit entries and emit their events through their own epics, and the rules panel writes through EP-13. No amount is read or shown. Weights are integers in units of 0.0001 g and shown to 4 decimals, so mockup figures such as "196.4 g", "612 g" and "447.162 g vs 447.300 g" are shown as "196.4000 g", "612.0000 g" and "447.1620 g vs 447.3000 g"; parcel gaps are shown in mg as on the mockups ("138 mg short"). The seed people are Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao (Staff), and the karigars Mahesh Soni · KG-02, Lakshmi Devi · KG-01 and Vijay Kumar · KG-04. The worked example is BATCH-2026-044 from Mahesh Soni, stopped 138 mg short with 12 pieces held back. Routes `broadcast` (EP-34) and the wishes count (EP-33) belong to higher-numbered epics, so the stories here hide or zero what depends on them until those epics ship.

## EP-32-S1: System can build the owner's exception queue on the server

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can build the owner's exception queue on the server
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one Read Owner exception queue operation that returns, in one call, the "blocking" cards (mismatched parcels, open raised problems, one edits card, one scrap card) and the "running late" cards (one late-leads card, one overdue-jobs card), each with a stable key, a kind, a block, a title, a detail line and one action (label, route id and parameters), plus the counts per block and the total
- **So that:** Decisions is built from the server in one call instead of from `ownerQueues` in the browser, and the owner sees only what nobody else may do (FR-32-2, FR-32-3, FR-32-7, BR-32-1, BR-32-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given BATCH-2026-044 is `stopped` with verdict `mismatch` and no open problem, PR-101 is open on job MO-2026-118, 2 edit proposals are open, 1 scrap request is pending, 2 leads are past their SLA and 2 jobs are past their agreed date, when Sanjay Seth calls Read Owner exception queue, then one response holds 4 cards in block `blocking`, 2 cards in block `late`, `blockingCount` 4, `lateCount` 2 and `total` 6.
  2. Given each card in the response, when it is inspected, then it has `key`, `kind` (one of `parcel_mismatch`, `problem`, `edits`, `scrap`, `late_leads`, `overdue_jobs`), `block` (`blocking` or `late`), `title`, `detail` and an `action` with a `label` and a route id from `parcel-clear`, `edit-apply`, `scrap-decision`, `leads`, `karigars` or `stock`.
  3. Given BATCH-2026-045 is `stopped` and has an open raised problem, when the queue is built, then it appears once, as a `problem` card, and not as a `parcel_mismatch` card (FR-32-3).
  4. Given BATCH-2026-046 matched exactly and was released by staff, when the queue is built, then no card for it is returned (BR-32-1).
  5. Given the pipeline holds 40 parcels, 60 leads, 30 open jobs and 10 open problems on staging, when Read Owner exception queue is called, then it answers in under 2 seconds on a shop connection.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Owner exception queue is Owner only (EP-05-S2, EP-32-S13). Cards are built on the server from `parcels`, `problems`, `edit_proposals`, `scrap_requests`, `leads` and `karigar_jobs`; the browser does not decide what is waiting. Counting follows the prototype: each mismatched parcel and each open problem counts 1, all edits count 1, all scrap requests count 1, late leads count 1 and overdue jobs count 1. Each card kind is filled by its own story (EP-32-S3 to EP-32-S6); this story owns the response shape, the counts and the single call. No value or price field is returned.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. This story is the read; live refresh is EP-32-S12.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reading the queue is not audited (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Owner exception queue and the card shape to the shared contract. Ports `ownerQueues(s, now)` and its `blocking` and `late` counts from `src/store/selectors.ts` to the server.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` ("NOTHING MOVES UNTIL YOU ANSWER · 4", "RUNNING LATE · 2"), route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: one aggregated read, under 2 seconds (epic section 13). Security: Owner only on the server. D7 is decided: one shop, no branches; the queue covers the shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S3, EP-05-S2, EP-23-S2, EP-23-S7, EP-24-S1, EP-24-S8, EP-25-S1, EP-25-S4, EP-27-S1, EP-27-S5, EP-28-S8, EP-28-S9, EP-19-S9, EP-19-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-32-S3: Owner can see mismatched parcels with the karigar's recent average

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can see mismatched parcels with the karigar's recent average
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** one blocking card per parcel stopped with verdict `mismatch` and no open raised problem, showing the parcel, karigar, gap in mg, pieces held back, measured against expected pure gold, the stop time and the karigar's average gap over his last six parcels, with "Open it" to `parcel-clear`
- **So that:** I can judge in one look whether this parcel is unusual for this karigar before I open it (FR-32-4, FR-32-7, epic acceptance criterion 1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given BATCH-2026-044 from Mahesh Soni is `stopped` with verdict `mismatch`, a pure gold gap of −1380 units, 12 tagged pieces, measured pure gold 4471620 units against 4473000 expected and `stoppedAt` 09:12 Asia/Kolkata, when Sanjay Seth opens `decisions`, then a card reads "BATCH-2026-044 will not weigh up · 138 mg short" with detail "Mahesh Soni · 12 pieces frozen · 447.1620 g vs 447.3000 g expected · submitted 09:12" (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Mahesh Soni's last six released parcels had gold gaps averaging 310 units, when the card is built, then it adds the line "His last six parcels averaged 31 mg. Staff cannot release this one, only you can."
  3. Given a karigar has only 2 released parcels, when the card is built, then the line reads "His last 2 parcels averaged …"; given he has none, then the line is left out.
  4. Given the card is shown, when Sanjay presses "Open it", then `parcel-clear` opens for BATCH-2026-044, and the badge counts this card as 1.
  5. Given Sanjay sends BATCH-2026-044 back, re-checks a tag or accepts the loss (EP-23-S9 to EP-23-S11), when the queue is read again, then no card for it is returned.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** A mismatch card is built only for `status = stopped`, verdict `mismatch`, no resolution and no open problem on the parcel. Gap, measured and expected pure gold come from the stored EP-23 verdict, never recomputed in the browser. The average comes from the EP-16-S10 last six gaps through Read Karigar recent gaps (EP-23-S13), as an integer mean rounded half up to whole mg. Release, send back and accept loss are not offered on the card; they stay on `parcel-clear`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in this story; EP-32-S12 consumes "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" to add this card.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Builds the `parcel_mismatch` card inside Read Owner exception queue; replaces `Karigar.gapsMg` seed data with the server read of released parcel gaps.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` ("BATCH-2026-044 will not weigh up · 138 mg short", "Mahesh Soni · 12 pieces frozen · 447.162 g vs 447.300 g expected · submitted 09:12", "His last six parcels averaged 31 mg.", "Open it"), `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg` ("PARCEL DOES NOT MATCH", "His last 6 parcels averaged 31 mg loss. This one is four times that."), route `decisions`. The mockup 08 buttons "Release to the floor" and "Send it back" stay on `parcel-clear`; the card offers "Open it" only.

## EP-32-S6: Owner can see late leads and overdue jobs under Running late

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can see late leads and overdue jobs under Running late
- **As a:** Owner

- **So that:** I see what the clock has flagged without anyone having to tell me (FR-32-6, BR-32-3, BR-32-6, BR-32-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the lead SLA is 8 hours and the "Sharma wedding enquiry" has waited 11 hours and the "bulk chain order from Erode" 9 hours without being opened, when Sanjay Seth opens `decisions`, then a card reads "2 leads nobody has opened for over 8 hours" with detail "Sharma wedding enquiry (11 h) · bulk chain order from Erode (9 h)" and "See leads" opens `leads`.
  2. Given Mahesh Soni's job is 3 days past its agreed date and Lakshmi Devi's 1 day, both reminded today, when the queue is built, then a card reads "2 karigar jobs past their agreed date" with detail "Mahesh Soni 3 days over · Lakshmi Devi 1 day over · both reminded automatically" and "See tracker" opens `karigars` (EP-19-S10).
  3. Given a job has `confirmedDate` 28 October and `dueDate` 25 October, when today is 1 November in Asia/Kolkata, then it is 4 days over, using the confirmed date before the due date (BR-32-8).
  4. Given the owner changes the SLA from 8 to 6 hours (EP-13-S4), when the queue is read, then the card text says "over 6 hours" and a lead waiting 7 hours is now listed.
  5. Given no lead is past its SLA and no job is past its date, when the queue is built, then the block heading reads "RUNNING LATE · 0" and neither card is returned.

- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed in EP-32-S12: "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", "Setting changed" and "Job passed its agreed date" (proposed, G26). Emitted: none.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited. Marking a lead late is audited by EP-10-S12.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Builds the `late_leads` and `overdue_jobs` cards inside Read Owner exception queue, replacing `lateLeads` and `overdueJobs` from `ownerQueues`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` ("RUNNING LATE · 2 · THE CLOCK TOLD ME, NOT A PERSON", "2 leads nobody has opened for over 8 hours", "See leads", "2 karigar jobs past their agreed date", "See tracker"), route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: hours waiting from the server clock; days over in Asia/Kolkata calendar days. Open decision A2: whether the SLA counts shop hours or clock hours; the card shows whatever EP-28-S8 returns. Open decision A3: who hears first and how long before the owner; this card shows every lead past the SLA regardless of who was told first.
- **Depends on:** EP-32-S1, EP-28-S8, EP-28-S9, EP-19-S9, EP-19-S10, EP-13-S4, EP-10-S5, EP-10-S7

- **As a:** Owner

- **So that:** I can see the system working without me, and notice when this block is short while the first one is long (FR-32-8, BR-32-4, epic acceptance criterion 2)

  1. Given BATCH-2026-046 matched and was released by Rajesh Verma at 10:15 today, when Sanjay Seth opens `decisions`, then it appears only in this block and has no button, and no card for it is in the other blocks (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given 3 parcels were released today with no loss, holding 35 pieces and 12840000 units of pure gold, when the block is shown, then it reads "3 parcels went live this morning without you" with "35 pieces · 1,284.0000 g pure gold · all three matched, so the staff who tagged them released them".

- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: pure gold is an integer sum in units of 0.0001 g, shown to 4 decimals. Time: "today" starts at midnight Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10); "this morning" is used before 12:00 and "today" after. Performance: under 2 seconds with the queue.

## EP-32-S8: Owner can change the alert rules from the rules panel

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can change the alert rules from the rules panel
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** a "THE RULES BEHIND THESE ALERTS" panel on `decisions` that shows and changes the lead SLA hours, who hears about a late lead ("Staff first, then me" or "Only me"), how it reaches me (WhatsApp, In the app, Email) and the "Code before a tag edit" rule, saving through the EP-13 settings operations, plus the fixed line "A parcel comes to me when it does not match exactly · Nothing for you to set"
- **So that:** I can tune the alerts where I see them, and only I can (FR-32-9, BR-32-5, BR-32-9, epic acceptance criterion 4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given `leadSlaHours` is 8, when Sanjay Seth changes "A lead is late after" to 6 and saves, then Update Setting (EP-13-S4) stores 6, the panel shows 6, and the late-leads card is rebuilt with 6 hours.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls the settings update for `leadSlaHours` directly, when it reaches the server, then it is refused through EP-13-S2 and the value stays 8 (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given `lateLeadAudience` is "staff_first", when Sanjay picks "Only me" and saves, then the stored value changes and the audit entry reads the old and new value (EP-13-S3, EP-13-S5).
  4. Given Sanjay turns Email off and leaves WhatsApp and In the app on, when he saves, then `notifyChannels` holds WhatsApp and in-app only (EP-13-S6); given he tries to turn all three off, then the server's sentence from EP-13-S6 is shown (EP-08-S5).
  5. Given the panel is shown, when the match rule line is read, then it says "Nothing for you to set. Every item tagged, and gross, stone and net all agree, or I see it." and has no control.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Every change is an EP-13 settings update, Owner only (EP-13-S2), validated and audited there (EP-13-S3). `setSetting` without an owner check (G12) is removed. The match rule has no stored setting (BR-32-5). The edit-token switch accepts only the values G18 allows (EP-13-S10). A stale save, made against an older settings version, is refused as a conflict (EP-03-S5).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26), so the panel refreshes when the owner changes a rule on another device. Emitted: none here; "Setting changed" is emitted by EP-13-S14.
- **Audit entry written:** No by this story. Each change is audited by EP-13-S3 with actor, time, setting, before and after.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database by this story; updates `settings.leadSlaHours`, `lateLeadAudience`, `notifyChannels` and `requireEditToken` through EP-13. Moves `RulesPanel` in `OwnerDecisions.tsx` off `setSetting` onto the EP-08 data layer.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` ("THE RULES BEHIND THESE ALERTS", "A lead is late after 8 hours", "shop hours, not clock hours", "A parcel comes to me when it does not match exactly", "Who hears about a late lead · Staff first, then me · Only me", "How it reaches me · WhatsApp · In the app · Email"), `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg` ("YOUR RULE · Code before a tag edit · Staff must get your WhatsApp code first. · On"), route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner check on the server for every rule (BR-32-9, G12). Audit: every change audited by EP-13. Concurrency: version check on save. Open decision A2: the "shop hours, not clock hours" choice is shown only after A2 is decided and EP-13-S11 stores shop hours; until then the panel shows hours only. Open decision G18: whether the edit-token switch can be turned off.
- **Depends on:** EP-32-S2, EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-13-S4, EP-13-S5, EP-13-S6, EP-13-S10, EP-13-S11, EP-13-S14, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

- **So that:** gold tied up on the floor is pushed to customers or remade instead of sitting unnoticed (FR-32-12, FR-32-13, BR-32-11, epic acceptance criterion 5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**

Given `ageingThresholdDays` is 90 and 6 `in_stock` pieces, mostly Temple style, with pure gold summing to 1964000 units have been in stock longer, the oldest 108 days, when Sanjay Seth opens `decisions`, then the card reads "196.4000 g of gold has not moved in 90 days" with "6 pieces, mostly Temple style · tied up on the floor · oldest is 108 days" (epic acceptance criterion 5).

  4. Given `ageingThresholdDays` is empty (EP-13-S8), or no `in_stock` piece is older than it, when `decisions` loads, then no ageing card is shown.
  5. Given a piece is sold or scrapped, when the alert is read again, then it is no longer counted and the total falls by its pure gold.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Ageing alert is Owner only (EP-05-S2). Days in stock are counted on the server in Asia/Kolkata calendar days from the time the piece entered `in_stock` (EP-22-S1, EP-22-S11). Only `in_stock` pieces count. The total is an integer sum. The threshold is the EP-13-S8 setting; no default is assumed. "Mostly <style>" names the style held by the most aged pieces. The alert does not count in the badge or `blockingCount`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed in EP-32-S12: "Piece billed by one staff member", "Setting changed" and "Piece scrapped" (proposed, G26). Emitted: none.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited. Scrap requests started from the card are audited by EP-27-S11.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Read Ageing alert to the shared contract; the prototype has no ageing alert.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg` ("GOLD SITTING TOO LONG", "196.4 g of gold has not moved in 90 days", "6 pieces, mostly Temple style · tied up on the floor · oldest is 108 days", "Push on WhatsApp", "Melt and remake"), route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: total pure gold is an integer sum in units of 0.0001 g, shown to 4 decimals. Time: ageing days in Asia/Kolkata calendar days. Performance: the ageing read is part of the under 2 second load. Open decision G5: the threshold value and whether it is per style or global; the card stays off until the owner sets `ageingThresholdDays`.
- **Depends on:** EP-32-S2, EP-13-S8, EP-22-S1, EP-22-S11, EP-27-S9, EP-10-S10, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-32-S12: Owner can see the badge and cards update live

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can see the badge and cards update live
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** the Decisions rail badge to show the queue `total`, and the cards, the "went through" block, the gold locations, the karigars and the ageing card to refetch within about 1 second when a relevant live event arrives, and to catch up after a dropped connection
- **So that:** a new exception reaches me while the screen is open, without a reload (FR-32-14, epic acceptance criterion 3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Sanjay Seth is on `decisions` with the badge at 3, when Rajesh Verma proposes an edit and "Edit proposed / token sent" arrives, then the edits card appears and the badge shows 4 within about 1 second (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given BATCH-2026-044 is stopped, when "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" arrives, then its mismatch card appears and the badge rises by 1; given a problem is cleared, when "Problem cleared" arrives, then its card goes and the badge falls by 1.
  3. Given Deepak Rao stocks out a piece with 41.5900 g of pure gold, when "Piece billed by one staff member" arrives, then "Gold on the floor" falls by 41.5900 g and "11 pieces went out" becomes "12 pieces went out".
  4. Given the owner is on another screen, when a lead passes its SLA, then the Decisions badge on the rail updates from the server badge-count read (EP-08-S16).
  5. Given the connection drops for 2 minutes and a parcel is stopped meanwhile, when it returns, then "Reconnecting…" shows while down, and on return the queue and badge are refetched so the new card is there (EP-07-S7, EP-08-S10).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Events reach the owner only through the EP-07-S5 permission filter. The Decisions badge is `total` from Read Owner exception queue, served through the badge-count read (EP-07-S9); the browser never adds to it. On each event the client refetches the affected reads; cards are never patched from the event payload alone.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed: "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Edit applied", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", "Metal pool changed", "Piece billed by one staff member"; proposed (G26): "Problem raised on a job or piece", "Problem cleared", "Scrap requested", "Piece scrapped", "Parcel released into stock", "Job passed its agreed date", "Setting changed". Emitted: none.
- **Audit entry written:** No. This screen only reads.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the `decisions` reads to the event-to-read map in the EP-08 data layer (EP-08-S8) and moves the Decisions count in `railBadges` to the server badge-count read.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg` (rail "Decisions 6"), `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg` (rail "Decisions 3"), route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: a new exception appears within about 1 second (epic section 13); a burst of events is coalesced into one refetch per short interval. Availability: "Reconnecting…" and catch-up from the last sequence number (EP-07-S7, EP-08-S10). Concurrency: two owner devices show the same badge after the same event. Open question G21: whether Decisions is the owner's notification centre; this story keeps the badge to cards on this screen only.
- **Depends on:** EP-32-S1, EP-32-S7, EP-32-S9, EP-32-S10, EP-32-S11, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S7, EP-07-S9, EP-07-S11, EP-08-S8, EP-08-S9, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S16, EP-23-S7, EP-24-S11, EP-24-S12, EP-25-S5, EP-26-S11, EP-27-S10, EP-28-S13, EP-18-S12, EP-19-S7, EP-13-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-32-S13: System can refuse the Decisions queue to any role but owner

- **Story ID:** EP-32-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse the Decisions queue to any role but owner
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every Decisions read (Owner exception queue, Went through today, Gold locations, Karigars worst first, Ageing alert, the Decisions badge count and the Decisions updates subscription) to refuse any caller whose role is not Owner, and the `decisions` route not to be offered to them
- **So that:** staff and karigars cannot see the owner's queue, the karigar figures or the gold totals, even by calling the server directly (FR-32-16, BR-32-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Read Owner exception queue directly, when it reaches the server, then it is refused through EP-05-S2 with the refusal format of EP-03-S4 and no card is returned.
  2. Given Vijay Kumar (Karigar) calls Read Gold locations or List Karigars worst first, when it reaches the server, then it is refused and no figure is returned.
  3. Given Rajesh types the `decisions` route, when the app opens it, then the route is not offered and he is sent to `today` (EP-08-S13).
  4. Given Rajesh's live connection, when a "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)" event is published, then he does not receive the Decisions badge count, and his rail shows no Decisions item (EP-07-S5, EP-07-S9).
  5. Given Sanjay Seth's role is changed from Owner to Staff while `decisions` is open (EP-05-S6), when the next read is made, then it is refused and his sessions are ended as EP-04-S13 states.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** All Decisions reads and the subscription are in the Owner-only list of the fixed permission table (EP-05-S1) and checked on every call (EP-05-S2). The role comes from the session, never from the request. Refusals use the shared error format.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None emitted. The subscription filter of EP-07-S5 drops Decisions updates for non-owners.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Refused reads are not audited; reading the queue is not audited (epic section 13).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the Decisions operations to the Owner-only entries of the permission list in the shared package.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The refusal happens on the server; route hiding uses the shell of EP-08-S13.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner-only on the server for every read and the subscription (epic section 13); tests call each operation as Staff and as Karigar and expect refusal.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S6, EP-03-S4, EP-04-S13, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S9, EP-08-S13, EP-32-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-33: Wishes · stories

Epic document: [EP-33 Wishes](../epics/EP-33-wishes.md)

Role note: stories where the server stores, builds, checks, sends or audits on its own use "System"; the 9 am run acts as the System actor "Scheduler" (EP-06-S6). Stories on the `wishes` screen use "Staff", because staff work the queue and the owner can do everything staff can. Choosing the sender identities and editing the templates are Owner only. Karigars are refused every wishes operation. Wishes carry no price and no weight (BR-33-7). The seed people are Sanjay Seth (Owner) and Rajesh Verma (Staff); the seed customers are Priya Malhotra (VIP Bridal, birthday, opted in), Arjun & Kavya (High net worth, anniversary, opted in) and Ravi Shankar (Festive collector, birthday, not opted in). The mockup's second sender "Priya (Manager)" depends on G20, so the stories name the second identity neutrally.

---

## EP-33-S1: System can store wishes, templates and sender identities

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store wishes, templates and sender identities
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `wishes` table from EP-02-S12 extended to hold one row per customer, occasion and year with sender identity, template version, times, provider message id, delivery status, failure reason and who sent it; a `wish_templates` table with one versioned text per occasion; and the EP-12 SenderIdentity table extended so two identities can be marked as wish senders under the owner
- **So that:** wishes, the edited message and the chosen senders survive a reload instead of living in `WishRecord` entries and on-screen text, and the one-per-year rule has a place to live (FR-33-7, FR-33-8, FR-33-9, FR-33-11, BR-33-4, BR-33-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an empty database, when migrations run, then `wishes` has columns id, customer id, occasion (`birthday` or `anniversary`), occasion year, sender identity id, template id, template version, queued at, sent at, provider message id, delivery status (`queued`, `sent`, `delivered`, `failed`), failure reason and sent by (user id or System), with a unique constraint on (customer id, occasion, occasion year).
  2. Given migrations have run, when `wish_templates` is read, then it holds one `birthday` row at version 1 with the text "Happy birthday {name}! Warm wishes from all of us at Jai Gulab Dev. Do visit — we would love to show you something special." and one `anniversary` row at version 1, each with the approved provider template name, edited by and edited at.
  3. Given the SenderIdentity rows from EP-12-S1, when the migration runs, then each row also has a linked user id (nullable), an active flag and a wish-sender slot (1, 2 or empty), and a database check allows at most two rows with a wish-sender slot.
  4. Given a row is inserted into `wishes` with occasion `christmas`, delivery status `read`, or a customer id that does not exist, when it is written, then the database refuses it.
  5. Given the prototype seed (EP-02-S13), when it is loaded, then the existing `WS-` records become `wishes` rows with occasion year from their `at` date in Asia/Kolkata and delivery status `sent`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Enum checks on occasion and delivery status. Foreign keys from wishes to customers, sender identities and wish templates. The unique key (customer id, occasion, occasion year) is the store for the one-wish-per-year rule (EP-33-S10). Times are stored in UTC. The server sets id, queued at and sent by; no client field sets them. No price, amount or weight column on any of these tables (BR-33-7).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Creating tables writes no entry; changes to these rows are audited by EP-33-S13.
- **Data changes:** Migration on `wishes` (EP-02-S12) adds occasion year, sender identity id, template id, template version, queued at, sent at, provider message id, delivery status, failure reason, sent by, and the unique key. Migration creates `wish_templates` (id, occasion, text, version, provider template name, edited by, edited at) and seeds version 1 of each occasion. Migration on SenderIdentity (EP-12-S1) adds linked user id, active and wish-sender slot. Each table has the shop ID (EP-02-S3, D7).
- **UI reference:** No screen.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: `wishes` holds customer ids only, never phones or dates of birth; those stay on `customers` (EP-17-S1). Time: all times in UTC. Open decision G20: whether a sender identity is tied to a user; linked user id is nullable until it is answered. D7 is decided: one shop, so sender identities and templates are per shop.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S12, EP-02-S13, EP-12-S1, EP-17-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S2: System can build today's and tomorrow's wishes queue

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can build today's and tomorrow's wishes queue
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a List Wishes queue operation that returns every active customer whose `dob` or `anniversary` falls today or tomorrow in Asia/Kolkata, one row per customer and occasion, found through a month-and-day index rather than a scan of every customer
- **So that:** birthdays and anniversaries come up on their own each morning, taken straight from the customer profile (FR-33-1, BR-33-1, BR-33-6, BR-33-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given it is 08:30 on 14 March in Asia/Kolkata (03:00 UTC), Priya Malhotra's `dob` is 14 March 1992, Arjun & Kavya's `anniversary` is 15 March 2015 and Ravi Shankar's `dob` is 14 March 1988, when Rajesh Verma calls List Wishes queue, then it returns 3 rows: Priya (birthday, today), Ravi (birthday, today) and Arjun & Kavya (anniversary, tomorrow), and the heading count is "COMING UP · 3".
  2. Given it is 23:45 on 13 March in Asia/Kolkata (18:15 UTC on 13 March), when the queue is read, then "today" is 13 March and "tomorrow" is 14 March, not the UTC dates.
  3. Given a customer has both a birthday and an anniversary today, when the queue is read, then two rows are returned, one per occasion.
  4. Given a customer with `status` `erased` (EP-17-S13) or with no `dob` and no `anniversary`, when the queue is read, then no row is returned for them.
  5. Given 5,000 customers on staging, when List Wishes queue is called, then it answers in under 2 seconds on a shop connection and the query plan uses the month-and-day index.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Wishes queue is Staff and Owner only; karigars are refused (EP-05-S2). Day and month are compared in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10), ignoring the year. Not-opted-in customers are included; consent is shown by EP-33-S3 and enforced at send time by EP-33-S5. Each row carries whether a wish for that customer, occasion and year already exists.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The queue is read on load and refetched after the user's own send (EP-08-S7).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.
- **Data changes:** Migration adds an index on the month and day of `customers.dob` and of `customers.anniversary` (an expression index or stored month-day columns). Adds List Wishes queue to the shared contract (EP-03-S1). Replaces `wishesDueToday` and `isMonthDayToday` in the browser with the server read.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("COMING UP · 3", "Priya Malhotra · birthday today", "Arjun & Kavya · anniversary tomorrow", "Ravi Shankar · birthday today").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: today and tomorrow are Asia/Kolkata dates from the server clock. Performance: under 2 seconds, indexed by month and day (epic section 13). Personal data: the response carries name, group and occasion, not the full date of birth. Open question: whether a 29 February birthday appears on 28 February or 1 March in other years; until answered, it appears only when 29 February exists.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S1, EP-17-S1, EP-17-S13, EP-10-S10, EP-05-S2, EP-03-S1, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S3: Staff can see each customer's occasion and consent state

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see each customer's occasion and consent state
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** each row on `wishes` to show the customer's initials, name and occasion with "today" or "tomorrow", their group, their last purchase or piece count, a consent line that matches the auto-send setting, and the one action that fits the row
- **So that:** I can see at a glance who will be wished on their own, who needs me, and why (FR-33-2, BR-33-1, BR-33-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra is opted in, her birthday is today, she last took home a Polki kada and `autoSendWishes` is true, when Rajesh Verma opens `wishes` before 09:00, then her row reads "Priya Malhotra · birthday today", "VIP Bridal · last took home a Polki kada" and "opted in · will auto-send at 9 am unless you send now", with "Send now".
  2. Given Arjun & Kavya are opted in, their anniversary is tomorrow and they have 4 pieces in their history, when the row is shown, then it reads "High net worth · 4 pieces with us" and "opted in · scheduled for 9 am tomorrow", with "Preview".
  3. Given `autoSendWishes` is false, when the same rows are shown, then Priya's line reads "opted in · auto-send is off" and Arjun & Kavya's reads "opted in · auto-send is off".
  4. Given Ravi Shankar is not opted in and his birthday is today, when the row is shown, then it reads "Festive collector" and "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send" (EP-33-S6 owns the action).
  5. Given List Wishes queue has not answered or fails, when `wishes` is shown, then the loading state (EP-08-S3) or the error with "Try again" (EP-08-S4) appears, not an empty list.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The consent state in each row is the customer's current `optedIn` from the latest consent event (EP-17-S2), read on the server. The last purchase or piece count comes from the customer's piece history (EP-17-S9) by name and count only, never by value. The auto-send state comes from settings (EP-13-S1). The browser does not decide consent or the action.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Consumed indirectly: "Setting changed" (proposed, G26) refreshes the settings read so the consent line follows the switch (EP-13-S14).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Reads are not audited.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds group, last purchase name, piece count, consent state and action to each queue row in the shared contract. Moves `src/components/marketing/Wishes.tsx` off `useStore()` onto the EP-08 data layer.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("VIP Bridal · last took home a Polki kada", "High net worth · 4 pieces with us", "opted in · will auto-send at 9 am unless you send now", "opted in · scheduled for 9 am tomorrow", "Festive collector", "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send"). The "auto-send is off" line follows the prototype and is not drawn on the mockup.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: `wishes` loads under 2 seconds on a shop connection. Personal data: consent shown is the stored state, so an opt-out recorded at the counter shows on the next load. Availability: loading, error, offline and reconnecting states (EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11). Time: "9 am" in the line follows `wishSendTime` if EP-13-S7 makes it a setting.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S2, EP-17-S2, EP-17-S9, EP-13-S1, EP-13-S14, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S4, EP-08-S10, EP-08-S11, EP-08-S13, EP-08-S17
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S4: Staff can send a wish now to opted-in customers

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can send a wish now to opted-in customers
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to press "Send now" on one row, or select several of today's rows and send them together, so the server creates one wish per customer and occasion and sends it through the approved WhatsApp template from the chosen sender
- **So that:** a customer gets their greeting when I choose, without waiting for 9 am (FR-33-3, FR-33-8, FR-33-10, BR-33-1, BR-33-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra is opted in with a birthday today and no wish this year, when Rajesh Verma presses "Send now" with sender slot 1 (Sanjay) selected, then one `wishes` row is created with occasion `birthday`, occasion year 2026, sent by Rajesh, delivery status `queued`, and EP-12-S3 sends the approved birthday template with {name} filled as "Priya".
  2. Given Rajesh selects Priya and Ravi Shankar (not opted in) and sends, when the server answers, then Priya's wish is sent and Ravi's result is "skipped: not opted in to WhatsApp" (EP-33-S5), and the screen shows both outcomes.
  3. Given Arjun & Kavya's anniversary is tomorrow, when a send for them is called directly, then the server refuses with "This occasion is tomorrow. It can be sent on the day." and no row is created.
  4. Given the network drops after Rajesh presses "Send now" and he retries, when the retry reaches the server with the same idempotency key, then no second wish is created or sent (EP-08-S6, EP-03-S8).
  5. Given the send succeeded, when the queue is refetched (EP-08-S7), then Priya's row shows the sent state from EP-33-S12 and "Send now" is no longer offered.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Wish send is Staff and Owner only; karigars are refused (EP-05-S2). Each customer id must have an occasion today in Asia/Kolkata. Each send passes the consent check (EP-33-S5) and the one-per-year rule (EP-33-S10) in the same transaction that creates the row (EP-03-S6). The sender identity must be one of the two active wish senders (EP-33-S7). The text is the latest approved template version (EP-33-S8). Sending goes through EP-12-S3 only; the provider idempotency key is "wish" plus customer id, occasion and year.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Wishes are not in the PRODUCTION-SCOPE §1 catalogue (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, by EP-33-S13: actor, time, entity (wish), action `wish_sent`, customer id, occasion, sender identity, template version.
- **Data changes:** Inserts `wishes` rows. EP-12-S3 inserts OutboundMessage rows with the wish id as source. Adds Create Wish send to the shared contract, replacing `sendWishes` in `src/store/transitions.ts`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Send now", "SENT FROM · Sanjay (Owner)"). Selecting several rows is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: two staff pressing "Send now" for Priya at once create one wish (EP-33-S10). Personal data: consent is checked at the moment of sending (epic section 13). Security: role checked on the server. Open decision D8: the provider and which templates are approved; until a wish template is approved the send is refused with the EP-12-S3 sentence.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S2, EP-33-S3, EP-33-S5, EP-33-S7, EP-33-S8, EP-33-S10, EP-12-S2, EP-12-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S2, EP-08-S5, EP-08-S6, EP-08-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S5: System can refuse a wish to a customer who is not opted in

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can refuse a wish to a customer who is not opted in
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every wish send, from "Send now" or from the 9 am run, to read the customer's current consent at the moment of sending and skip the customer when it is off, with no wish row and no provider call
- **So that:** nobody who has not agreed, or who opted out after the queue was built, gets a WhatsApp message from the shop (FR-33-4, BR-33-3, BR-33-8, epic acceptance criterion 4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Ravi Shankar is not opted in and his birthday is today, when a send for him is requested, then the result is "skipped: not opted in to WhatsApp", no `wishes` row is created and no provider call is made.
  2. Given Priya Malhotra was opted in when the queue loaded at 08:30 and opted out at the counter at 08:45 (EP-17-S7), when the 9 am run reaches her, then she is skipped (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given Priya replied STOP on WhatsApp and EP-12-S10 switched her consent off, when Rajesh Verma presses "Send now" on her row from a screen loaded earlier, then she is skipped and the screen shows "Priya Malhotra is not opted in to WhatsApp, so no wish was sent." (EP-08-S5).
  4. Given Ravi opts in at the counter at 11:00 (EP-17-S6), when Rajesh sends his birthday wish at 11:05, then it is sent, because no row was created for the earlier skip.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The check reads `optedIn` from the latest consent event (EP-17-S2) inside the send transaction, not the value in the queue. EP-12-S5 checks again at the provider boundary, so neither path can skip consent. A skip is a result, not an error, so the other customers in a multi-send still go.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. No message is sent and no wish row changes; the consent change itself is audited by EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Reads `customers.optedIn` and `consent_events`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send"). The skip sentence is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent checked at send time and opt-out honoured at once (epic section 13, BR-33-8). Concurrency: an opt-out committed before the send transaction reads consent is honoured.

## EP-33-S6: Staff can see "Call instead" for customers not opted in

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see "Call instead" for customers not opted in
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a customer who is not opted in to stay in the queue with "Call instead" in place of "Send now", opening the phone dialler with their number, and never to be selectable for a WhatsApp send
- **So that:** I can still greet them another way while the shop never messages them without consent (FR-33-5, BR-33-3, epic acceptance criterion 2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**

  2. Given the row for Ravi, when Rajesh presses "Call instead", then the device dialler opens with Ravi's stored phone, and nothing is written on the server.
  3. Given Rajesh selects several rows to send, when Ravi's row is shown, then it cannot be selected.
  4. Given a not-opted-in customer's birthday is tomorrow, when the row is shown, then it also shows "Call instead", unlike the prototype, which showed it only for today.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The row's action is set by the server from the current consent state (EP-33-S3). The phone is returned only to Staff and Owner (EP-05-S2). Any send attempt for this customer is skipped by EP-33-S5, whatever the screen shows.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Opening the dialler writes nothing.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the customer phone to not-opted-in queue rows only.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Ravi Shankar · birthday today", "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send", "Call instead", "A customer who is not opted in is still shown, so you can reach them another way, but they are never auto-messaged.").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: the phone is shown only on rows where a call is the offered action; opted-in rows do not return it.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S3, EP-33-S5, EP-17-S7, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S7: Owner can choose the two sender identities

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can choose the two sender identities
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to set which two sender identities wishes come from, give each a display name, mark one as the default for the 9 am run, and see both under "SENT FROM" on `wishes`
- **So that:** wishes feel personal because they come from a known name under the owner (FR-33-8, BR-33-4, SCOPE-ANALYSIS Q9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the SenderIdentity rows from configuration, when Sanjay Seth sets slot 1 to "Sanjay (Owner)" and slot 2 to a second identity and saves, then both are stored with their slot and active flag, and "SENT FROM" on `wishes` lists the two names.
  2. Given Sanjay marks slot 1 as the default, when the 9 am run sends, then every wish that day uses slot 1 and the message shows "Sanjay".
  3. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Update Sender identities directly, when it reaches the server, then it is refused with "Only the owner can change the shop rules." and nothing changes.
  4. Given Sanjay tries to set a third slot, or names a sender identity that does not exist, when he saves, then the server refuses and the two stored slots stay as they were.
  5. Given slot 2 is made inactive, when Rajesh opens `wishes`, then only slot 1 is offered under "SENT FROM", and a send naming slot 2 is refused.

Exactly one default when any slot is active. Staff choose between the active slots when sending now; they cannot change them. A stale save against an older version is refused as a conflict (EP-03-S5).

- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (sender identity), action `wish_sender_changed` (new kind, added alongside those in epic section 9), before, after.

- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("SENT FROM", "Two names under the owner can be the sender.", "Sanjay (Owner)", "Priya (Manager)", "Wishes feel personal when they come from a known name."). The editing controls are not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner check on the server. Audit: every change audited. Open decision G20: who "Priya (Manager)" is when only Owner, Staff and Karigar exist, and whether an identity is tied to a user; the second slot is named neutrally until answered. Open decision D8: each identity needs a sending number the provider supports.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S1, EP-12-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-03-S5, EP-06-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S8: Owner can edit the wish template once for all

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can edit the wish template once for all
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to press "Edit the message", change the birthday or the anniversary text keeping {name}, and save it as a new version that every later wish uses once WhatsApp has approved it
- **So that:** I write the greeting once and it applies to all, instead of the edit vanishing on reload (FR-33-9, FR-33-10, BR-33-5, BR-33-9, epic acceptance criterion 5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the birthday template is version 1, when Sanjay Seth changes it to "Happy birthday {name}! From all of us at Jai Gulab Dev." and saves, then version 2 is stored with edited by Sanjay and the server time, and version 1 is kept.
  2. Given version 2 is approved by the provider (EP-12-S2), when the next birthday wish is sent to Priya Malhotra, then it reads "Happy birthday Priya! From all of us at Jai Gulab Dev." and the wish records template version 2 (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  3. Given version 2 is still pending approval, when a wish is sent, then it uses version 1, and the editor shows "Waiting for WhatsApp approval".
  4. Given Sanjay saves a text with no {name}, or with "{nmae}", when it reaches the server, then it is refused with "The message must contain {name} once." and nothing is stored.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Update Wish template, when it reaches the server, then it is refused and the template stays at its version.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Update Wish template is Owner only (EP-05-S2). The text must contain {name} exactly once and no other placeholder. {name} is replaced by the customer's first name at send time. The version increases by one on each save; old versions are kept so each wish shows the text it was sent with. A send uses the latest version with provider status approved. No price or rupee placeholder is allowed (BR-33-7). English only in v1.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, by EP-33-S13: actor, time, entity (wish template), action `wish_template_changed`, occasion, before text, after text, version.
- **Data changes:** Inserts a `wish_templates` row per version. Registers the new text through EP-12-S2 Create Template. Adds Update Wish template to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Edit the message", "THE BIRTHDAY MESSAGE", "Happy birthday {name}! Warm wishes from all of us at Jai Gulab Dev.", "{name} fills in per person · edit once, applies to all"). The anniversary message and the approval state are not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner check on the server. Audit: every edit audited. Open decision D8: whether an edited text needs a new provider approval, which decides how long criterion 3's wait lasts. Open question: one template per occasion or several to choose from; this story stores one per occasion.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S1, EP-12-S2, EP-05-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-08-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S9: System can send wishes automatically at 9 am

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can send wishes automatically at 9 am
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** when the EP-10-S9 job starts at 9 am Asia/Kolkata with `autoSendWishes` on, to send today's wish to every opted-in customer in the queue not already wished this year, from the default sender, as the System actor "Scheduler"
- **So that:** each morning's birthdays and anniversaries go out on WhatsApp without anyone lifting a finger (FR-33-6, BR-33-2, epic acceptance criterion 1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra is opted in with a birthday today and `autoSendWishes` is true, when 09:00 Asia/Kolkata (03:30 UTC) arrives, then one wish is sent to her from the default sender with "Priya" filled in, sent by System (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given Rajesh Verma sent Priya's wish at 08:40, when the 9 am run reaches her, then she is skipped and no second wish is sent (EP-33-S10).
  3. Given Ravi Shankar is not opted in, when the run reaches him, then he is skipped (EP-33-S5); given Arjun & Kavya's anniversary is tomorrow, then they are not sent today.
  4. Given `autoSendWishes` is false at 09:00, when the job starts, then no wish is sent and the run records 0 sends.
  5. Given the run crashes after sending 3 of 5 wishes and EP-10-S3 retries it, when the retry runs, then only the remaining 2 are sent.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The setting is read at run time by EP-10-S9; the run key is "wishes" plus the Asia/Kolkata date (EP-10-S4). Each customer goes through the same send path as EP-33-S4: consent check (EP-33-S5), one-per-year rule (EP-33-S10), latest approved template (EP-33-S8), default sender (EP-33-S7). One customer's failure does not stop the others. A run missed by downtime runs on restart for its own date only (EP-10-S11).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. The job is started by the scheduler, not by a live event.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, by EP-33-S13: one `wish_sent` entry per wish with actor System "Scheduler", time, customer id, occasion, sender identity, template version. The run itself is recorded in the EP-10-S2 run history.
- **Data changes:** Inserts `wishes` rows with sent by System. EP-12-S3 inserts OutboundMessage rows. JobRun and JobKey rows from EP-10.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Send wishes automatically at 9 am", "On, each morning's birthdays and anniversaries go out on WhatsApp without you lifting a finger."). The switch itself is EP-13-S7.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: 9 am Asia/Kolkata, converted to UTC by EP-10-S10. Availability: a failed run retries and never sends twice (epic section 13). Concurrency: a "Send now" racing the run creates one wish. Open question: whether 9 am is fixed or a setting (never per branch, D7); this story uses `wishSendTime` from EP-13-S7, which defaults to 09:00. Open decision G12: who may switch auto-send.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S1, EP-10-S2, EP-10-S3, EP-10-S4, EP-10-S9, EP-10-S10, EP-10-S11, EP-10-S12, EP-13-S7, EP-06-S6, EP-33-S2, EP-33-S5, EP-33-S7, EP-33-S8, EP-33-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S10: System can send at most one wish per customer per occasion per year

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can send at most one wish per customer per occasion per year
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every wish to claim the unique key (customer id, occasion, occasion year) inside the send transaction, so a second request for the same key, from a person or the 9 am run, sends nothing
- **So that:** a customer never gets the same greeting twice, even after a double tap, a retry or a job restart (FR-33-7, epic acceptance criterion 3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a wish was sent to Priya Malhotra for her 2026 birthday this morning, when Rajesh Verma presses "Send now" again, then no second wish is sent and the result is "already wished this year" (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given Rajesh and Deepak Rao send Priya's wish at the same moment, when both reach the server, then exactly one `wishes` row exists and one provider send is made.
  3. Given Priya was wished for her 2026 birthday, when her birthday comes in 2027, then a new wish is allowed with occasion year 2027.
  4. Given Arjun & Kavya were sent an anniversary wish this year, when a birthday wish is due for Arjun & Kavya, then it is allowed, because the occasion differs.
  5. Given a wish row is `failed`, when a retry runs (EP-33-S12), then it reuses the same row and the same provider idempotency key, and no second row is created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The unique key on `wishes` (EP-33-S1) is claimed in the same transaction as the row insert (EP-03-S6); a key clash returns "already wished this year", not an error. Occasion year is the Asia/Kolkata year of the occasion date. The provider send uses idempotency key "wish" plus customer id, occasion and year (EP-10-S4, EP-03-S8). This replaces the prototype's 24-hour window.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused duplicate writes no entry; the one real send is audited by EP-33-S13.
- **Data changes:** None beyond EP-33-S1. Relies on the unique key on (customer id, occasion, occasion year).
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Send now"). The "already wished this year" wording is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: the database constraint, not a read-then-write check, prevents duplicates. Availability: restarts and retries of the 9 am run cannot send twice (epic section 16). Time: year boundaries in Asia/Kolkata.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S1, EP-10-S4, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S12: Staff can see delivery status and failures

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can see delivery status and failures
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** a List Sent wishes read that shows each wish sent today with its sender, time and delivery status (queued, sent, delivered, failed) and, for a failure, the provider's reason, plus the count of wishes sent today for the homes
- **So that:** I know which greetings arrived and which did not, so I can call the customer when one fails (FR-33-11, FR-33-12, epic acceptance criterion 6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Priya Malhotra's wish was sent at 09:00 and the provider reported it delivered at 09:01, when Rajesh Verma opens `wishes`, then her row shows "sent 09:00 · delivered".
  2. Given the provider rejects the wish to Arjun & Kavya with "recipient not on WhatsApp", when the status returns through EP-12-S9, then the wish is `failed`, its row shows "failed · recipient not on WhatsApp" and the failure reason is stored (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  3. Given a wish failed with a temporary provider error, when EP-12-S12 retries it by the EP-10-S3 rule, then the same wish row moves to `sent` or stays `failed` after the last attempt, and no second row is created.
  4. Given 4 wishes were sent today, when Sanjay Seth opens `decisions`, then "Went through without you today" reads "4 wishes sent" (EP-32-S7), and the "SAY HAPPY BIRTHDAY" list on `today` no longer shows those customers (EP-31-S9).
  5. Given a wish is `delivered`, when a late receipt reports `sent`, then the status stays `delivered`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List Sent wishes is Staff and Owner only (EP-05-S2). Wish delivery status is copied from its OutboundMessage receipts (EP-12-S9) and only moves forward: queued, sent, delivered; failed is final for that attempt. Retries follow EP-12-S12 and EP-10-S3 with the wish idempotency key. "Today" is Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Delivery status comes from EP-12 provider callbacks, not a live event (epic section 11); the screen shows the stored status on load and after the user's own action (EP-08-S7).
- **Audit entry written:** No. Status updates come from the provider and are kept on the wish and OutboundMessage rows; the send itself is audited by EP-33-S13.
- **Data changes:** Updates `wishes.delivery status`, sent at and failure reason from OutboundMessage. Adds List Sent wishes and the today count to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes`, has no sent or failed state; the count shows on `docs/ux/mockups/13-notifications-escalation.svg`, route `decisions` ("11 pieces went out · 4 wishes sent").
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: sent and delivered times stored in UTC and shown in Asia/Kolkata. Availability: a provider outage marks wishes failed with a reason rather than losing them (EP-12-S12). Open decision: the retry rule for a failed wish (FR-33-12 "the decided rule"); until decided it is the EP-10-S3 backoff.
- **Depends on:** EP-33-S4, EP-33-S9, EP-33-S10, EP-12-S9, EP-12-S12, EP-10-S3, EP-10-S10, EP-08-S7, EP-31-S9, EP-32-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-33-S13: System can audit wishes, template edits and the auto-send switch

- **Story ID:** EP-33-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can audit wishes, template edits and the auto-send switch
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an append-only audit entry for every wish sent, every template edit and every change to the auto-send switch, written in the same transaction as the change, and the `wishes` toggle routed through the EP-13 settings update so it is checked and audited
- **So that:** the owner can see who greeted whom, from which name and with which text, and who turned auto-send on or off (FR-33-14, FR-33-15, BR-33-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma sends Priya Malhotra's birthday wish, when the send commits, then one `wish_sent` entry exists with actor Rajesh, time, entity wish id, customer id, occasion `birthday`, sender identity slot 1 and template version 1, and no phone or message text.
  2. Given the 9 am run sends 3 wishes, when it commits, then 3 `wish_sent` entries exist with actor System "Scheduler".
  3. Given Sanjay Seth saves birthday template version 2, when it commits, then one `wish_template_changed` entry holds the before text, the after text and version 2.

The prototype `setSetting('autoSendWishes', ...)` call without an owner check is removed; the toggle calls Update Setting (EP-13-S7). Wish entries hold ids, not personal values (EP-17-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor (user or System "Scheduler"), time, entity, action (`wish_sent`, `wish_template_changed`, `setting_changed`), before and after where they apply.
- **Data changes:** Adds the audit kinds `wish_sent` and `wish_template_changed` (and `wish_sender_changed` from EP-33-S7) to the `audit_entries` kind list by migration. No new table.
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Entries are read on the owner's audit log (EP-06-S9); the toggle is on `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("Send wishes automatically at 9 am").
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: append-only, same transaction (epic section 13). Personal data: no phone, date of birth or message body in the entry. Security: the auto-send switch is checked on the server. Open decision G12: who may switch auto-send on or off.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S1, EP-06-S2, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S6, EP-06-S9, EP-13-S2, EP-13-S3, EP-13-S7, EP-17-S14, EP-33-S4, EP-33-S7, EP-33-S8, EP-33-S9

Stories on the `broadcast` and `catalogue` screens use "Staff", because staff do this work and the owner can do everything staff can; EP-34-S15 is Owner only because it starts from `decisions`.
