## EP-36-S11: Staff can scan a tag to add a piece to a stock-out

- **Story ID:** EP-36-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can scan a tag to add a piece to a stock-out
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to scan a tag barcode into "Scan another tag" on `stock-out` and have the piece join "WHAT IS LEAVING THE SHOWCASE" with its photo and name, through Read Piece by scanned tag
- **So that:** I add pieces from what is in my hand without typing, and I can check the scanned piece is the one I hold (FR-36-12, BR-36-6, epic section 16 risk)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given TAG-9040 is `in_stock`, when Rajesh Verma scans it, then "Jadau Emerald Ring · TAG-9040 · 18K · 8H33Z9" joins the list with its photo and pure gold "12.6000 g" (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given TAG-8841 and TAG-9040 are on the list, when the screen totals them, then "LEAVING THE FLOOR" shows "54.1900 g" for 2 pieces.
  3. Given TAG-9040 is already on the list, when it is scanned again, then it stays one row and the field clears.
  4. Given the scanner is unplugged, when Rajesh types "TAG-9040" into the same field, then the piece is added the same way.
  5. Given TAG-9040 is billed by Deepak Rao on another counter while on Rajesh's list, when "Piece billed by one staff member" arrives, then the row is removed as in EP-26-S11.

- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: a scanned tag resolves within about 1 second. Concurrency: two staff scanning the same piece both see it; only one confirm wins (EP-26-S3). Open question: whether scanning also opens a piece in stock search.

# EP-37: Observability · stories

Epic document: [EP-37 Observability](../epics/EP-37-observability.md)

Role note: this is a layer E operations epic with no shop-facing screen. Stories use "System" for the logger, error tracker, uptime checker, metrics and alerting acting on their own, and "Developer" for the operator, the person who runs the system and receives and acknowledges alerts. Who else receives alerts (for example the owner) is an open question, so no story assumes the Owner role reads logs or dashboards. Seed users named in criteria are Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma (Staff) and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar). Operator tools (logs, dashboards, alerts) live in the chosen monitoring tool; which parts come built in depends on the D1a cloud provider.

---

## EP-37-S1: System can write structured logs with a request id across services

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can write structured logs with a request id across services
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every API request, background job run, notification delivery, WhatsApp send and live-channel publish to write structured log lines that share one request id
- **So that:** the operator can follow one counter action from the API through jobs, notifications and the WhatsApp provider when something breaks (FR-37-1, FR-37-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Propose edit on a piece, when the request ends, then exactly one API log line is written with time (UTC), request id, service `api`, operation name, actor id, role `staff`, outcome `ok` and duration in ms.
  2. Given that request causes an edit-token notification and a WhatsApp send, when the logs are searched by its request id, then the API line, the EP-11 notification line, the EP-12 send line and the EP-07 publish line all appear with the same request id.
  3. Given a request is refused by a rule (`DomainError`, for example a stock-out of a piece that is already sold), when it is logged, then the outcome is `refused` with the refusal code, and it is not counted as an error (FR-37-3).
  4. Given an unhandled exception in an operation, when it is logged, then the outcome is `error`, and the line carries the request id that the error report from EP-37-S3 also carries.
  5. Given a scheduled job run with no incoming request (for example the SLA breach job), when it runs, then it gets its own request id and its log lines name service `jobs` and the job name.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The request id is created at the API boundary, or taken from a trusted internal caller, and never from a browser header without validation. Actor id and role come from the session (EP-03-S3), never from the request body. Outcome is one of `ok`, `refused` or `error`.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Publishes of the catalogue events are logged, but their content is not read.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Application logs are not the audit log (EP-06); no business state changes.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds a shared logger in `api` with the log line fields from epic section 9, and passes the request id into job, notification, WhatsApp and live-channel code.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: logging adds less than 5 ms to a request (proposed target, to confirm). Time: every line carries a UTC time (BR-37-7). Precision: log lines carry no business weights; if one ever must, it is an integer in units of 0.0001 g. D1 is decided (Option C): the Node API writes these logs itself and carries the request id in every line. Open decision D1a: which provider log service receives them.
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S3, EP-03-S4, EP-10-S2, EP-11-S13, EP-12-S3, EP-07-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-37-S2: System can redact passwords, links, tokens, phones and names from every log line

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can redact passwords, links, tokens, phones and names from every log line
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the logger itself to remove passwords, activation and reset links, edit tokens, session secrets, phone numbers, email addresses and customer names from every log line, by field name and by pattern, before the line leaves the process
- **So that:** secrets and personal data never reach logs, whatever a developer passes to the logger (FR-37-2, BR-37-2, BR-37-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a staff member signs in with phone and password, and another resets a password from an emailed link, when all logs for those requests are searched for the password and the link, then neither appears (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given Sanjay Seth agrees an edit proposal and an edit token is sent and then applied, when the logs for both requests are searched for the token value, then it does not appear; the line shows the token reference only.
  3. Given a log call that passes an object with fields `phone`, `email`, `password`, `link`, `token`, `sessionSecret`, `customerName` or `name` of a customer, when the line is written, then each of those values is replaced by `[redacted]` and the internal id is kept.
  4. Given a free-text detail that contains a 10-digit Indian mobile number, when the line is written, then the number is replaced by `[redacted]`.
  5. Given the redaction test suite, when it runs in CI, then it fails if any of the above values reaches the log output.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Redaction runs inside the logger, not by convention at each call site (epic section 13). The redacted field list lives in one place in the shared package. Error reports (EP-37-S3) and alerts (EP-37-S5, EP-37-S6) use the same redaction.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. No business state changes.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the redaction list and the redacting step to the logger.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: passwords, links, edit tokens and session secrets never logged in plain text (BR-37-2). Personal data: phones and customer names are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023 and stay out of logs; the internal id is logged instead (BR-37-5).
- **Depends on:** EP-37-S1, EP-04-S14, EP-12-S11, EP-06-S4, EP-01-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-37-S3: System can report web, portal and API errors to error tracking

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can report web, portal and API errors to error tracking
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every unhandled error in the web app, the karigar portal and the API to be reported to error tracking with time, service, release version, request id, message, stack and user role
- **So that:** the operator sees a crash on `parcel-match` or `k-jobs` before the shop phones about it (FR-37-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an unhandled error in an API operation, when it happens, then one error report reaches error tracking with service `api`, the deployed release version, the request id from the matching log line, the message and the stack.
  2. Given Rajesh Verma is on the `stock-out` route and a script error happens, when the web app calls Create client error report, then the report holds service `web`, the release version, the route id `stock-out` and role `staff`, and no name or phone.
  3. Given Lakshmi Devi on the karigar portal `k-jobs` hits an unhandled error, when it is reported, then the report names service `portal` and role `karigar`.
  4. Given a rule refusal shown to the user as the `DomainError` sentence, when it happens, then no error report is created.
  5. Given a caller with no session, when it calls Create client error report, then the server refuses it.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create client error report requires a signed-in session (epic section 10). The server sets time, actor role and release from its own state, not from the payload. Payload size is capped and passed through the redaction from EP-37-S2.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Error reports are operational data, not business changes.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Create client error report to the shared contract (EP-03-S1) and an error-reporting hook in `web`, the portal and `api`. Error reports are stored in the error tracking tool.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Every route reports, including `today`, `decisions`, `parcel-match`, `stock-out` and `k-jobs`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: reports carry user role only, no name, phone or customer data. Security: error tracking is visible only to operators. D10 is decided (India region) for the system's own hosting; whether the error tracking tool must also store data in India is open.
- **Depends on:** EP-37-S1, EP-37-S2, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S4, EP-08-S4, EP-20-S3, EP-01-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S4: System can run uptime checks against the health check

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can run uptime checks against the health check
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an uptime checker outside the main app to call Read Health on staging and production at a set interval and alert the operator after the agreed number of failures in a row
- **So that:** the operator knows the API or database is down even when the app itself cannot send anything (FR-37-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the uptime checker is set for production, when it calls Read Health, then it stores a check result with time, target, status and response time.
  2. Given the API is down, when the uptime check fails the agreed number of times in a row, then the operator is alerted once with the target and the time of the first failure (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  3. Given Read Health reports database `down`, when the check runs, then it counts as a failure.
  4. Given the API recovers after an alert, when the next check passes, then a recovery notice is sent and the alert is marked resolved.
  5. Given the whole app host is down, when the checks fail, then the alert still arrives, because the checker and alert route run outside the main app.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The checker calls only Read Health, which needs no session (EP-03-S10). One alert per outage, not one per failed check. The failure count and interval come from configuration, not code.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A health check changes no state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uptime check results are kept in the monitoring tool. Adds checker configuration for staging and production.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: alerting runs outside the main app so an app outage still raises an alert (epic section 13). Time: alerts carry UTC times and dashboards show Asia/Kolkata. Open question: how many failed uptime checks raise an alert; the criteria use "the agreed number".
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S10, EP-01-S6, EP-01-S12, EP-01-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S5: Operator can receive an alert when a WhatsApp send fails after retries

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Operator can receive an alert when a WhatsApp send fails after retries
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** an alert when a WhatsApp send has failed after its last retry, naming the message kind (edit token, wish, broadcast, alert)
- **So that:** staff are not left waiting at the counter for an owner edit code that never arrives, and a lost alert does not go unnoticed (FR-37-6, BR-37-1, BR-37-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an edit token send that fails after its last retry, when the failure is recorded, then the operator gets an alert naming "edit token", and no phone number or token value appears in the alert or in any log (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the edit token send to Sanjay Seth's registered mobile fails after its last retry, when the failure is reported by EP-12-S12, then the alert names "edit token", the template name and the error code, and severity is high.
  3. Given 30 wish sends fail in the same 9 am run, when they are reported, then the operator gets one grouped alert for "wish" with the count 30, not 30 alerts.
  4. Given a send fails on its first attempt and succeeds on retry, when it ends, then no alert is raised.
  5. Given a broadcast message reported failed by a later receipt (EP-12-S9), when the last retry is used up, then an alert names "broadcast".
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Alerts are raised only for exhausted retries (EP-11-S14, EP-12-S12), never for a first failure. Message kind is one of edit token, wish, broadcast, alert. Sign-in sends no WhatsApp message (D4). Alerts carry message id, template name and error code, and never recipient number, text or variables. Repeats within a short window are grouped.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Business events are not used; the failure report from EP-12-S12 is the input.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The failure is recorded on the OutboundMessage (EP-12) and in the alert.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database unless the tool cannot store alerts; then an Alert record (time, kind, severity, message, acknowledged by, acknowledged at). Adds an alert rule for failed sends.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The alert arrives by the agreed alert route.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: no phone, customer name or message text in alerts. Security: no edit code or token value in alerts (BR-37-2). Availability: the alert route runs outside the main app. Open question: who receives alerts, by which channel and at which hours; the alert route cannot use WhatsApp alone, since WhatsApp may be what failed.
- **Depends on:** EP-37-S1, EP-37-S2, EP-12-S12, EP-11-S14, EP-25-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S6: Operator can receive an alert when a background job fails or does not run

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Operator can receive an alert when a background job fails or does not run
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** an alert when a background job fails after its last retry, and when a scheduled job does not start by its time plus a grace period
- **So that:** a late lead, an overdue karigar job or the 9 am wishes are not missed silently (FR-37-7, FR-37-8, BR-37-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the SLA breach job fails on its last attempt (EP-10-S3), when the run is marked failed, then the operator gets an alert naming the job and the error text.
  2. Given the 9 am wishes job does not run, when the agreed grace period after 9:00 Asia/Kolkata passes with no run recorded, then the operator gets an alert naming the job (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given the token expiry job runs late but succeeds within the grace period, when it ends, then no alert is raised.
  4. Given the overdue karigar job check fails three days in a row, when each failure ends, then each day raises one alert, and repeats on the same day are grouped.
  5. Given the job runner itself is down, when a scheduled time passes, then the missed-run alert still arrives, because the check runs outside the job runner.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** A missed run is judged against the schedule computed in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10) and the JobRun history (EP-10-S2). Alerts are raised only for exhausted retries or missed schedules. Alerts name the job and carry no customer data.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Job runs are already recorded by EP-10; alerts are operational.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database unless the tool cannot store alerts; then the Alert record from EP-37-S5. Adds expected-schedule entries for the SLA breach, overdue jobs, token expiry and 9 am wishes jobs.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Owner-side run history is EP-10-S13.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: schedule and grace period use Asia/Kolkata; stored times are UTC (BR-37-7). Availability: the missed-run check runs outside the main app. Open question: who receives alerts and at which hours.
- **Depends on:** EP-10-S2, EP-10-S3, EP-10-S5, EP-10-S7, EP-10-S8, EP-10-S9, EP-10-S10, EP-37-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S7: System can measure live-event delivery time against the 1-second target

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can measure live-event delivery time against the 1-second target
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to measure the time from publishing each catalogue event to its arrival in a client, and alert when the median passes 1 second over the agreed window
- **So that:** the "live events arrive within about 1 second" target is watched in production, not assumed (FR-37-9, BR-37-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given EP-07 publishes a "Piece sold" event with its publish time and sequence number, when a client receives it, then the client reports arrival through Create client timing with the event name, sequence number and delivery time in ms.
  2. Given client timing reports are sampled, when a busy counter receives many events, then only the sampled share is reported and the screen does not slow down.
  3. Given live events are published, when the median delivery time over the window passes 1 second, then the operator is alerted (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  4. Given a client was reconnecting and catches up from its last sequence number (EP-07-S7), when the caught-up events arrive, then they are reported as catch-up and left out of the median.
  5. Given a delivery time report, when it is stored, then it holds no event content, only name, sequence number, role and time.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create client timing requires a signed-in session. The server compares client arrival with its own publish time; client clock offset is estimated per connection so a wrong device clock does not skew the figure. The epic acts on event timing only, not on content.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** Consumed (timing only): all 10 catalogue events from PRODUCTION-SCOPE section 1 as carried by EP-07. Emitted: none.
- **Audit entry written:** No. Timing is operational data.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds Create client timing to the shared contract and a live-event delivery time metric series in the monitoring tool.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: median delivery under 1 second (BR-37-4); sampling keeps reporting off the screen's critical path. Personal data: reports carry role, not user name. Open question: the length of the agreed window.
- **Depends on:** EP-07-S2, EP-07-S7, EP-07-S11, EP-08-S8, EP-03-S1, EP-37-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S8: System can measure screen load time against the 2-second target

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can measure screen load time against the 2-second target
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the web app and karigar portal to report how long each route takes to show its data on real shop devices, and to show it against the 2-second target
- **So that:** slow screens on the shop connection are found from real use (FR-37-10, BR-37-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma opens the `today` route, when its data has loaded and the loading state from EP-08-S3 ends, then the client reports route id `today`, load time in ms and device type through Create client timing.
  2. Given Lakshmi Devi opens `k-jobs` on her phone, when it loads, then the report names service `portal` and route `k-jobs`.
  3. Given a week of reports, when the operator opens the screen load figure, then it shows the median and 90th percentile per route against the 2-second line.
  4. Given a route whose median passes 2 seconds over the agreed window, when the figure is computed, then the route is marked over target.
  5. Given reporting is sampled, when a screen loads, then the timing call is sent after the screen has shown and does not delay it.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create client timing requires a signed-in session. Route id must be one of the known route ids. Payload carries no names, phones or business values.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Timing is operational data.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds a screen load time metric series in the monitoring tool and the reporting hook in `web` and the portal.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Measured routes include `today`, `decisions`, `parcel-match`, `stock-out` and `k-jobs`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: target under 2 seconds on a shop connection (BR-37-4); reports are sampled. Personal data: role only. Open question: whether a breached screen load target raises an alert or only shows on the dashboard; criteria only mark it over target.
- **Depends on:** EP-37-S7, EP-08-S3, EP-08-S12, EP-20-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S9: Operator can see request, error, job and send dashboards

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Operator can see request, error, job and send dashboards
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** dashboards of request rate, error rate, job runs and send success for the last 24 hours and the last 30 days, for staging and production
- **So that:** I can see whether the system is healthy at a glance and spot a trend before it becomes an outage (FR-37-11)

D10 is decided (India region); whether the monitoring tool must also be in India is open.

## EP-37-S10: Operator can acknowledge an alert

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Operator can acknowledge an alert
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** to list open and recent alerts and acknowledge one, recording who acknowledged it and when
- **So that:** two people do not chase the same failure and an unanswered alert is visible (epic section 10 List alerts, Update alert)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given three open alerts, when the operator lists alerts, then they appear newest first with time, kind, severity and message.
  2. Given an open "edit token" send alert, when the operator acknowledges it, then it records acknowledged by and acknowledged at, and it leaves the open list.
  3. Given an alert that is already acknowledged, when a second operator acknowledges it, then the first acknowledgement is kept and the second is refused or ignored.
  4. Given an alert is not acknowledged within the agreed time, when that time passes, then it is sent again by the alert route.
  5. Given a caller who is not an operator, when it calls List alerts or Update alert, then it is refused.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** List alerts and Update alert are for operators only (epic section 10). Acknowledge is a one-way change from open to acknowledged. Acknowledged at is set from the server clock.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No in the product audit log, since alerts are not business changes; the alert itself keeps acknowledged by and acknowledged at.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database if the monitoring tool keeps alerts; otherwise an Alert record with acknowledged by and acknowledged at.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Alerts are handled in the chosen tool or alert channel.
- **Non-functional checks:** Time: acknowledged at stored in UTC and shown in Asia/Kolkata. Security: operators only. Open question: who receives alerts and at which hours, which decides the resend time.
- **Depends on:** EP-37-S4, EP-37-S5, EP-37-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-37-S11: System can delete logs after the retention period

- **Story ID:** EP-37-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can delete logs after the retention period
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** log lines, error reports, uptime results and client timing data to be deleted once they pass the agreed retention period
- **So that:** operational data does not pile up and is kept no longer than needed (FR-37-12)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the retention period is set in configuration, when a log line becomes older than it, then it is deleted by the tool's retention setting or a scheduled cleanup.
  2. Given logs older than the period, when the operator searches for them, then none are returned.
  3. Given logs within the period, when the cleanup runs, then they are kept.
  4. Given the cleanup, when it runs, then the product audit log (EP-06) is not touched, because it is not an application log.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The retention period comes from configuration (EP-01-S6), one value per environment. Audit entries are append-only and outside this cleanup (EP-06-S1).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Deleting operational logs is not a business change.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Sets the retention period on the logging, error tracking and metrics stores.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: shorter retention limits exposure even though logs hold no personal data by design. Open question: how long logs are kept; criteria use "the agreed retention period". D10 is decided (India region) for the system's own hosting; whether an outside log tool must also store logs in India is open.

# EP-38: Backup and recovery · stories

Epic document: [EP-38 Backup and recovery](../epics/EP-38-backup-and-recovery.md)

Role note: this is a layer E operations epic with no shop-facing screen. Stories use "System" for the backup service, the continuous log and the scheduler acting on their own, and "Developer" for the operator, the person who runs backups, restores and drills with the hosting tools. The Owner approves a production restore and is told what window of work was lost; who exactly approves is an open question, so criteria say "the agreed approver". Seed users named in criteria are Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma (Staff) and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar). The database is managed PostgreSQL (D1, Option C), so its backup and point-in-time features come from the D1a cloud provider; backups stay in an India region (D10, decided).

---

## EP-38-S1: System can take a daily database backup

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S1
- **Status:** Partial: the production daily schedule is the RDS backup window, not built (D1a, FU-018).
- **Title:** System can take a daily database backup
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to take a full backup of the production and staging databases at least once a day on a schedule, and write a backup record for each run
- **So that:** every piece, parcel, weighing, pool ledger entry and audit entry survives a crash, a bad deploy or a lost host (FR-38-1, BR-38-1, BR-38-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given production has run for a day, when the operator calls List backups, then a backup of kind `daily full` from the last 24 hours shows with status `complete`, started at, finished at, size and location (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the daily backup schedule, when the scheduled time passes, then exactly one daily full backup is started for each environment, and a second start for the same day is not made.
  3. Given a daily backup in progress, when Rajesh Verma tags a piece at the counter, then the tag is saved normally and the counter does not wait for the backup.
  4. Given a completed daily backup, when it is restored into an empty staging database, then every table from EP-02 is present with the same row counts as the source at backup time.
  5. Given the backup, when the weight fields of `Piece` and pool ledger entries are compared with the source, then the integers in units of 0.0001 g are identical, and nullable money sockets stay null (BR-38-6).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Backup may be called only by the System schedule or an operator (epic section 10). One daily full backup per environment per day. Backup credentials come from environment configuration (EP-01-S6), never from code.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Backups do not emit business events (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** No. A backup changes no business state; the backup record holds kind, started at, finished at, size, status and location.
- **Data changes:** Adds a Backup record (id, kind `daily full` / `continuous log` / `file storage`, started at, finished at, size, status, location), kept in the hosting tool or in an operations table outside the business schema. No change to business tables.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The operator uses the hosting tools (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: a backup runs every day for production and staging (BR-38-1). Precision: weights copied unchanged as integers in units of 0.0001 g (BR-38-6). Performance: the backup does not lock tables the counter writes to. D1 is decided (Option C): the managed PostgreSQL service has a daily backup built in, so this story means turning it on and confirming its schedule. Open decision D1a: the exact backup options follow the cloud provider.
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-02-S3, EP-02-S4, EP-02-S5, EP-02-S6, EP-02-S7, EP-02-S8, EP-02-S9, EP-02-S10, EP-02-S11, EP-02-S12, EP-01-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-38-S2: System can keep a continuous log for point-in-time restore

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can keep a continuous log for point-in-time restore
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to ship the database's change log continuously to backup storage between daily backups
- **So that:** the database can be rolled back to any moment within the retention window and no more than 1 hour of work is lost in the worst case (FR-38-2, BR-38-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given continuous log shipping is on for production, when the operator calls List backups, then a backup of kind `continuous log` shows with the time of its latest shipped change, and that time is less than 1 hour old.
  2. Given log shipping stops for any reason, when the latest shipped change becomes 1 hour old, then the backup is marked failed so EP-38-S5 can alert.
  3. Given a daily full backup and the continuous log, when any time between the oldest kept daily backup and the latest shipped change is chosen, then that time is accepted as a restore point.
  4. Given a time older than the retention window, when it is chosen as a restore point, then it is refused with the oldest point that can be restored.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The continuous log is written only by the database host, never by application code. Restore points are limited to the retention window. The log is stored apart from the live database (EP-38-S4).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Shipping the log changes no business state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Turns on change-log shipping on the database host and adds Backup records of kind `continuous log`.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: recovery point under 1 hour (BR-38-1). Time: restore points are stored and chosen in UTC and shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open decision D1a: which point-in-time features the chosen provider's managed PostgreSQL includes and at what retention.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

---

## EP-38-S3: System can back up file storage

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S3
- **Status:** Partial: S3 versioning and the copy to another region or account are cloud work (D1a, FU-018).
- **Title:** System can back up file storage
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to copy object storage (piece photos, order copy reference images, PO attachments and bench photos) to backup storage, keeping earlier versions of each file
- **So that:** every file a database row points to at a restore point can be restored with it (FR-38-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma attached a piece photo through EP-09-S7, when the next file storage backup runs, then the photo and its thumbnail and display-size copies are in backup storage.
  2. Given a restored database, when a piece photo referenced at the restore point is opened through a signed link, then the file loads (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  3. Given a file was deleted from live storage after the restore point, when the files are restored to that point, then the file is back, because earlier versions are kept.
  4. Given a restore drill, when every file id in the restored database is checked against restored storage, then the check lists zero missing files, or names each missing one.
  5. Given a file storage backup, when it ends, then a Backup record of kind `file storage` is written with status, size and location.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Backups copy files as stored, without changing their ids. File access after restore still goes through the owning-entity and role check (EP-09-S6). Only System and operators may write to backup storage.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Copying files changes no business state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Turns on versioning or scheduled copy for the object storage bucket and adds Backup records of kind `file storage`.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: database and files can be restored to the same point, so no row points at a missing photo (epic section 16). Security: backup copies are not reachable by signed links meant for live files. Personal data: inbound PO attachments may hold customer details and follow the same region rule. D10 is decided: backup storage is in an India region.
- **Depends on:** EP-09-S1, EP-09-S4, EP-09-S5, EP-09-S6, EP-09-S7, EP-09-S8, EP-09-S10, EP-09-S11, EP-38-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S4: System can encrypt backups and keep them apart from live data

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S4
- **Status:** Partial: India region, operator-only IAM access and credentials that cannot delete backups (AC2-4) are cloud work (D1a, FU-018).
- **Title:** System can encrypt backups and keep them apart from live data
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every database backup, continuous log and file storage copy to be encrypted at rest and stored in a separate location from the live data, in an India region (D10, decided)
- **So that:** losing or breaking into the live host does not also lose or expose the backups, and customer personal data stays in the agreed region (FR-38-4, FR-38-5, BR-38-4, BR-38-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a daily full backup, when its storage settings are read, then encryption at rest is on and the location differs from the live database's location.
  2. Given the backup location, when it is compared with the India region decided under D10, then they match.
  3. Given a user with a shop account only (Sanjay Seth, Rajesh Verma or Lakshmi Devi), when they try to read or download a backup, then access is refused, because only the operator role can read backups.
  4. Given the live database credentials, when they are used against backup storage, then they cannot delete or overwrite a backup.
  5. Given the backup encryption keys and credentials, when the repository is scanned by EP-01-S10, then none are found in code; they live in environment configuration.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Backup storage access is limited to the operator role and the System backup service. Live application credentials have no delete right on backups. Keys and credentials come from environment configuration (EP-01-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Storage settings are infrastructure configuration, not business state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Sets encryption, location and access rules on backup storage.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: backups encrypted; only the operator can read or restore (epic section 13). Personal data: backups hold customer names, phones, birthdays and anniversaries and follow the same region and retention rules (BR-38-5). D10 is decided: backups are stored in an India region; the exact region follows the D1a provider.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S1, EP-38-S2, EP-38-S3, EP-01-S6, EP-01-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S5: Operator can receive an alert when a backup fails

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S5
- **Status:** Partial: the continuous-log alarm (AC3) is cloud, and delivery to a person needs EP-11 and EP-37 (FU-018).
- **Title:** Operator can receive an alert when a backup fails
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** an alert through the EP-37 alert route when a daily backup, the continuous log or a file storage backup fails or does not happen
- **So that:** a broken backup is fixed the same day instead of being found during a restore (FR-38-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the daily backup fails, when the failure is recorded, then the operator is alerted with the environment, backup kind `daily full`, the time and the error text (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given no daily full backup has completed in the last 24 hours plus the agreed grace period, when the check runs, then the operator is alerted that the backup is missing.
  3. Given the continuous log's latest shipped change is 1 hour old, when the check runs, then the operator is alerted with backup kind `continuous log`.
  4. Given a file storage backup fails, when it ends, then the alert names kind `file storage`.
  5. Given the same backup failure is seen again within the grouping window, when it is reported, then the operator gets one alert, not one per check.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The missing-backup check runs outside the main app, so it still alerts when the app host is down. Alerts carry no customer data or credentials.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Alerts are operational; acknowledgement is recorded by EP-37-S10.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds backup failure and missing-backup alert rules to the monitoring tool.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The alert arrives by the agreed alert route.
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: the check runs outside the main app. Time: alert times in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: who receives alerts and at which hours (EP-37 section 17).
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S1, EP-38-S2, EP-38-S3, EP-37-S5, EP-37-S6, EP-37-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S6: Operator can restore staging to a point in time

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S6
- **Status:** Partial: point-in-time restore and the production approver (AC1, AC5) are cloud; screen refetch (AC3, AC4) waits for live screens (FU-012, FU-018).
- **Title:** Operator can restore staging to a point in time
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** to restore the staging database and its files to a chosen point in time, and to use the same procedure for production once the agreed approver has approved
- **So that:** the system can be rolled back to a known good moment after data loss or a bad change, and the procedure is proven before it is needed (FR-38-2, FR-38-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a staging database with known data, when the operator restores it to a time 30 minutes ago, then every row written up to that time is present and no row written after it is present (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given a restore to a point, when the weight totals of pieces in stock and the pool ledger balance are compared with the source at that point, then the integer totals in units of 0.0001 g are equal (BR-38-6).
  3. Given a restore finishes, when Rajesh Verma's open `today` screen reconnects through EP-07, then it refetches state and shows no data from after the restore point.
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi's karigar portal was open on `k-jobs`, when it reconnects after the restore, then it refetches her jobs and shows only state up to the restore point.
  5. Given a production restore is requested without approval from the agreed approver, when the operator tries to start it, then it is refused; with approval, the restore is recorded with who approved it, who ran it and the restore point.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create Restore is for operators only; production also needs the agreed approver's approval (epic section 10). Database and files are restored to the same point. After a restore, connected clients do a full refetch instead of catching up from the sequence number they had cached, because events after the restore point no longer exist (EP-07-S7).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None emitted. After a restore, clients rely on EP-07 reconnect and catch-up to refetch authoritative state (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, for a production restore: actor (operator who ran it), approver, time, entity `database`, action `restore`, restore point, reason. The entry is written after the restore so the restore does not remove it.
- **Data changes:** The whole business database and file storage are replaced with their state at the restore point. No schema change. Adds a restore record (requested by, approved by, run by, restore point, started at, finished at).
- **UI reference:** No screen. The operator uses the hosting tools. Every route reads restored data afterwards.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: weight totals compared before and after (epic section 13). Audit: a production restore is recorded with approver, operator and restore point. Security: only the operator can restore. Availability: the recovery time target is measured in each run. Open decision D1a: the restore steps follow the chosen provider's managed PostgreSQL and object storage tools. Open question: who approves a production restore.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S2, EP-38-S3, EP-38-S4, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S7, EP-08-S10, EP-06-S2, EP-02-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S7: Operator can check that the audit log is whole after a restore

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S7
- **Status:** Done
- **Title:** Operator can check that the audit log is whole after a restore
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a check that compares the restored audit log with the source up to the restore point and reports any missing or changed entry
- **So that:** a restore never breaks the append-only audit trail of who moved which gold (FR-38-9, BR-38-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a restore, when the audit log is compared with the source up to the restore point, then every entry is present and unchanged (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the check, when it runs, then it compares entry count, each entry's id and a checksum of actor, time, entity, action, before, after, reason and token reference.
  3. Given an entry that differs or is missing, when the check finishes, then it names the entry id and fails the drill.
  4. Given the restored database, when anyone tries to update or delete an audit entry, then it is still refused, because the append-only rule from EP-06-S1 is part of the restored schema.
  5. Given an audit entry with weights, when it is compared, then the weights are the same integers in units of 0.0001 g.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The check only reads; it never repairs or rewrites audit entries. The append-only rule (no update or delete path, including for the owner) survives the restore.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. The check only reads; its result is kept on the restore drill record.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds a read-only audit comparison script used in drills.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: no entry altered after a restore (BR-38-2). Precision: weights in entries compared as integers. Personal data: the check prints entry ids, not customer names.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S6, EP-06-S1, EP-06-S3, EP-06-S4, EP-06-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S8: Operator can follow a written restore drill and record its duration

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S8
- **Status:** Partial: go-live sign-off needs staging (AC4) and the drill reminder is cloud work (AC5) (FU-018).
- **Title:** Operator can follow a written restore drill and record its duration
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a written restore drill that names each step, who does it and how long it takes, run in staging before launch and then on the agreed schedule, with each run recorded
- **So that:** a restore is a known, timed procedure rather than a first attempt during an outage (FR-38-7, FR-38-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the drill document, when it is read, then it lists each step (pick restore point, get approval, restore database, restore files, check file references, check audit log, reconnect clients, tell staff), who does it and the expected time.
  2. Given a drill run in staging, when it ends, then the operator calls Create restore drill record with date, environment `staging`, restore point chosen, duration, steps passed, notes and run by.
  3. Given the drill record, when the duration is compared with the recovery time target, then the result is noted as within or over target.
  4. Given launch, when the go-live checklist is checked, then a drill has been run once in staging with its duration recorded and has been signed off (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  5. Given the drill schedule after launch, when the agreed interval passes without a drill record, then the operator is reminded.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create restore drill record is for operators only (epic section 10). A drill record needs every step marked passed or failed. Drills run in staging only, using data seeded from `src/data/seed.ts` through EP-02-S13 or a copy of production.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No in the product audit log. The drill record keeps date, environment, duration and run by.
- **Data changes:** Adds a Restore drill record (date, environment, restore point chosen, duration, steps passed, notes, run by), kept in an operations table or the operations document store.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Availability: recovery time target agreed and measured in each drill (epic section 13). Time: drill dates stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: the recovery time target and how often the drill runs after launch.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S6, EP-38-S7, EP-02-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-38-S9: Operator can list sends made after a restore point for follow-up

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S9
- **Status:** Partial: provider message id, template and status need EP-11 and EP-12; no repeat wish needs EP-33 (FU-018).
- **Title:** Operator can list sends made after a restore point for follow-up
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** to list the WhatsApp messages (including owner edit codes) and account emails sent between the restore point and the restore, from provider logs and receipts, and the work lost in that window
- **So that:** staff can be told what to re-enter, karigars what to resend, and customers who got a wish or broadcast are not sent it twice (FR-38-11)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a restore to 10:00 done at 10:40, when the operator runs the list, then it shows every outbound message sent between 10:00 and 10:40 with message id, kind (edit token, wish, broadcast, alert, activation email, reset email), template name, send time and status from the provider.
  2. Given an edit token sent in that window, when the list shows it, then it shows the token reference only, never the token value.
  3. Given wish sends in that window, when the next 9 am wishes run starts, then customers already wished in the window are not wished again that day.
  4. Given the list, when it is handed to Sanjay Seth, then it names the window of lost work and the kinds of work to re-enter (for example tags, weighings and stock-outs), without customer phone numbers.
  5. Given karigar status updates that Lakshmi Devi sent after the restore point, when the procedure is followed, then she is told to resend them.

- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds a script or procedure step that reads provider logs for a time window.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: no edit code values or links in the list. Personal data: phone numbers are left out of the list given to the shop; the operator sees message ids. Time: window shown in Asia/Kolkata.

## EP-38-S10: System can delete backups after the retention period

- **Story ID:** EP-38-S10
- **Status:** Partial: continuous-log retention (AC3) and S3 noncurrent-version expiry (AC4) are cloud work (FU-018).
- **Title:** System can delete backups after the retention period
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** daily backups, continuous log segments and old file versions to be deleted once they pass the agreed retention period
- **So that:** backups, which hold customer personal data, are kept no longer than agreed (FR-38-12, BR-38-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the retention period is set in configuration, when a daily full backup becomes older than it, then the backup is deleted and its Backup record shows status `deleted`.
  2. Given backups within the period, when the cleanup runs, then they are kept, and the oldest kept backup still allows a restore.
  3. Given continuous log segments older than the oldest kept daily backup, when the cleanup runs, then they are deleted.
  4. Given old file versions past the period, when the cleanup runs, then they are deleted, and current files are not touched.
  5. Given the cleanup, when it ends, then List backups shows no backup older than the retention period.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The retention period comes from configuration (EP-01-S6), one value per environment. Only the System cleanup deletes backups; live application credentials cannot. The live audit log is not touched.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Deleting expired backups is not a business change; the Backup record status shows it.
- **Data changes:** None in business tables. Backup records move to status `deleted`. Sets retention on backup storage.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: backups are kept only for the agreed period (BR-38-5); how a DPDP deletion request affects backups still inside the period is decided with EP-39 (G22). Open question: how long backups are kept. Open decision D1a: retention options of the chosen provider's managed PostgreSQL.
- **Depends on:** EP-38-S1, EP-38-S2, EP-38-S3, EP-38-S4, EP-01-S6, EP-09-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-39: Security and data protection · stories

Epic document: [EP-39 Security and data protection](../epics/EP-39-security-and-data-protection.md)

Role note: stories where the server limits, checks, erases or reminds on its own use "System". Stories where a person records consent or a deletion request at the counter use "Staff"; decisions on deletions, the access review and sign-offs use "Owner". "Developer" means the operator who rotates secrets and works with the penetration testers. Seed users named in criteria are Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao (Staff) and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar); seed customers are Meera Iyer (+91 98840 21107) and Priya Malhotra. Many stories here harden and test mechanisms first built in EP-04, EP-12, EP-17, EP-25 and EP-34; each says which one it builds on. Legal duties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 must be checked with a professional; these stories build the mechanisms only.

---

## EP-39-S1: System can store a consent ledger per customer

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can store a consent ledger per customer
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** the `consent_events` table from EP-17-S2 to become the full consent ledger, with a `channel` column (WhatsApp in v1) and an `evidence_ref` column (the inbound message id for a reply), and a List Consent history operation that returns a customer's entries newest first
- **So that:** the shop can show, for any customer, each grant and withdrawal of WhatsApp consent with time, source and who recorded it, and the current consent is always the latest entry (FR-39-4, FR-39-5, BR-39-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migration has run, when `consent_events` is inspected, then it has `channel` accepting only `whatsapp`, `evidence_ref` (nullable), and the existing `customer_id`, `kind` (`opt_in` or `opt_out`), `source` (`counter`, `form`, `whatsapp_reply`, `import`), `recorded_by` and `at` in UTC.
  2. Given existing rows written before the migration, when the migration runs, then each row gets `channel` `whatsapp` and `evidence_ref` null, and no row is deleted.
  3. Given Meera Iyer has an `opt_in` entry from source `form` at 10:02 and an `opt_out` entry from source `whatsapp_reply` at 16:40 with `evidence_ref` set to the inbound message id, when Rajesh Verma calls List Consent history for her, then both entries come back, the 16:40 one first, with source, recorded by, time in Asia/Kolkata and evidence reference.
  4. Given the same customer, when her current consent is read, then it equals the `kind` of the latest entry by `at` then `id`, and `customers.optedIn` matches it.
  5. Given Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when she calls List Consent history, then the server refuses it and returns no entries.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The ledger is insert-only; update and delete are refused at the database (EP-17-S2). List Consent history is for Staff and Owner only; karigars are refused (EP-05-S2, EP-17-S12). `recorded_by` comes from the session, or is System for the reply path (EP-03-S3). Time comes from the server clock.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. This story extends storage and adds a read; each consent change is audited where it is written (EP-17-S14).
- **Data changes:** Migration adds `channel` and `evidence_ref` to `consent_events` and backfills `channel` for existing rows. Adds List Consent history to the shared contract (EP-03-S1).
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The consent history panel belongs in the customer drawer on `customers` (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent recorded with time and source (BR-39-5). Time: `at` stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Concurrency: two entries in the same second are ordered by `at` then `id`, so the current consent is always one row.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S2, EP-17-S12, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S3, EP-05-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S2: System can rate-limit sign-in, reset-link and edit-token requests and entries

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can rate-limit sign-in, reset-link and edit-token requests and entries
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** one shared rate-limit counter store, keyed by phone, user or address and by operation, that the sign-in and reset-link limits (EP-04-S8, EP-04-S9) and the edit-token limits (EP-25-S9) all use, with the limit values set in configuration, plus an end-to-end review of the D4 password and link rules
- **So that:** nobody can try passwords across accounts, flood an inbox with reset emails, or guess a 6-digit edit token, the limits are checked before any password is compared or any message is sent, and the password, lockout and link rules hold in the built system (FR-39-1, FR-39-2, BR-39-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a phone that has requested reset links up to the configured limit inside the window, when another reset is requested for it, then the server refuses with `rate_limited`, no link is created and no email is sent (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given one address that has tried passwords for many different phones up to the per-address limit, when it tries one more, then the request is refused with `rate_limited` before any password is checked, whichever phone it names.
  3. Given an account with 5 wrong passwords in a row, when the right password is then entered, then it is refused until 15 minutes have passed or the owner unlocks it (EP-04-S8).
  4. Given an edit token for proposal ED-102 that has had wrong entries up to the per-token limit on `edit-apply`, when Sanjay Seth enters any code again, then it is refused with "Too many wrong tokens. Ask for a new one." and the piece is unchanged.
  5. Given the API runs on two instances, when requests for the same phone reach both inside one window, then the counts add up in the shared store and the limit holds across both.
  6. Given the review on staging, when the `users` and `password_links` tables and the logs are inspected after an activation, a reset and a sign-in, then passwords appear only as salted hashes from a modern algorithm, links only as hashes, a used or expired link (activation after 24 hours, reset after 1 hour) is refused, and the forgot-password response is the same for a known and an unknown number.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The limit check runs before a password is compared, a link is created or a token is sent. Counters are kept in a store shared by every API instance, not in process memory. Limits per phone, per address and per code are all applied; a request must pass every one. Refusals for unknown and known phones look the same (EP-04-S9). Counter keys hold a hash of the phone, never the phone in plain text. There is no sign-in OTP to limit (D4).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No for each counted request. A lockout is audited by EP-04-S14 and an invalidated edit code by EP-25-S14, with a token reference only.
- **Data changes:** Adds a RateLimitCounter store (key, operation, window start, count) with expiry at the end of each window. Adds limit values per operation to environment configuration (EP-01-S6).
- **UI reference:** No screen of its own. Refusal messages show on the sign-in and forgot-password screens (EP-04-S3, EP-04-S7) and on route `edit-apply` (EP-25-S8).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: limits apply before any password check or message, per phone, per user and per address (epic section 13); password, lockout and link rules from D4 confirmed end to end. Concurrency: counts are atomic increments, so two requests in the same millisecond cannot both slip under the limit. Personal data: counter keys hold hashed phones. Open question: the actual limit values for sign-in attempts, reset requests and wrong edit-token entries.
- **Depends on:** EP-03-S11, EP-04-S2, EP-04-S8, EP-04-S9, EP-25-S6, EP-25-S9, EP-01-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S3: System can apply a general request limit per user and address

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can apply a general request limit per user and address
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** to fill the rate-limit hook from EP-03-S11 with a general limit on every operation, counted per signed-in user and per address, using the store from EP-39-S2
- **So that:** one script or stolen session cannot overload the API or scrape the stock and customer lists (FR-39-3, BR-39-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma is signed in, when his session sends more requests inside one window than the per-user limit, then the extra requests are refused with `rate_limited` in the standard error format (EP-03-S5) and change nothing.
  2. Given the shop's counter devices share one address, when Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao each stay under the per-user limit, then neither is refused, because the per-address limit is set above the shop's normal combined use (epic section 16 risk).
  3. Given requests without a session from one address, when they pass the per-address limit, then they are refused with `rate_limited`.
  4. Given a refused request, when the response is read, then it says how many seconds to wait before trying again.
  5. Given a public showcase link opened many times a minute from one address, when the per-address limit is reached, then further opens are refused (EP-34-S14b).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The limit runs before validation and before any database work (EP-03-S11). Per-user and per-address counts are both checked. The health check (EP-03-S10) is exempt so uptime checks keep working. Limits come from configuration (EP-01-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. A refused request changes no state; refusal counts go to logs and dashboards (EP-37-S9).
- **Data changes:** None in business tables. Uses the RateLimitCounter store from EP-39-S2 with operation `general`. Adds per-user and per-address limit values to configuration.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The front end shows the refusal through its standard error state (EP-08).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: general limit per user and per address on every operation (FR-39-3). Performance: the limit check adds no more than one round trip to the counter store per request. Availability: limits tuned in staging so a busy counter is never blocked. Open question: the general API limit values.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S2, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S10, EP-03-S11, EP-34-S14b, EP-37-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S4: Staff can record a customer's consent or opt-out at the counter

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can record a customer's consent or opt-out at the counter
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to record a customer's WhatsApp consent or opt-out at the counter, from the "Send wishes on WhatsApp" control on `customer-new` and from the consent panel on `customers`, each write going into the consent ledger with source `counter` or `form`
- **So that:** what the customer said at the counter is on record with who heard it and when, and their next wish or broadcast follows it (FR-39-4, FR-39-7, BR-39-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma adds Meera Iyer on `customer-new` with "Send wishes on WhatsApp" on and presses "Add this customer", then one ledger entry with kind `opt_in`, source `form`, recorded by Rajesh, channel `whatsapp` is written with the customer.
  2. Given he adds a customer with "Send wishes on WhatsApp" off, when it is saved, then no `opt_in` entry is written and the customer is not opted in.
  3. Given Meera Iyer is opted in, when Rajesh records her opt-out from the consent panel on `customers`, then an `opt_out` entry with source `counter` is written and her consent history shows it at the top.
  4. Given Meera Iyer is opted out, when Rajesh records her consent again, then a new `opt_in` entry with source `counter` is written, and the earlier entries stay.
  5. Given Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when she calls Create Consent entry, then the server refuses it and nothing is written.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Staff and Owner may create consent entries; karigars are refused (EP-17-S12). The entry, the `optedIn` copy and the audit entry are written in one transaction (EP-17-S2, EP-06-S2). Recording the state a customer already has writes nothing (EP-17-S7). Whether the box may start ticked is not decided; the server records only the value submitted.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Consent is read on the server at send time (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (customer id), action (`customer_consent_recorded` or `customer_opted_out`), before and after consent, source. Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `consent_events`; updates `customers.optedIn` and `version`. No schema change beyond EP-39-S1.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg`, route `customer-new` ("Send wishes on WhatsApp"). The consent panel on `customers` is not yet designed.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent recorded with time, source and recorder (BR-39-5). Audit: each change appended. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: whether a ticked-by-default consent box is acceptable or staff must ask each time; the prototype starts it ticked (`useState(true)` in `OnboardCustomer.tsx`).
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S1, EP-17-S3, EP-17-S6, EP-17-S7, EP-17-S12, EP-17-S14, EP-06-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S5: System can withdraw consent from a WhatsApp opt-out reply

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can withdraw consent from a WhatsApp opt-out reply
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an inbound WhatsApp message that matches a configured opt-out word to write an `opt_out` ledger entry for the matching customer with source `whatsapp_reply`, recorded by System, and the inbound message id as `evidence_ref`, at the moment it is received
- **So that:** a customer who replies "STOP" gets no further wish or broadcast, and the shop can prove which message withdrew consent (FR-39-6, BR-39-5, BR-39-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer is opted in, when she replies "STOP" to a broadcast, then an `opt_out` entry with source `whatsapp_reply`, recorded by System and `evidence_ref` set to the inbound message id is written, and the next morning's 9 am wishes run skips her (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  2. Given the reply " stop " or "Stop", when it is received, then it is treated as an opt-out; given "please don't stop the order", then it is not, and it goes to lead intake (EP-12-S10).
  3. Given the provider delivers the same "STOP" message twice, when the second copy arrives, then it is recognised by message id and no second entry is written (EP-12-S7).
  4. Given a "STOP" from a phone that matches no customer, when it is received, then the message is stored and no ledger entry is written.
  5. Given Meera Iyer opted out by reply, when Rajesh Verma opens her consent history, then the entry shows source "WhatsApp reply" and the message reference.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Only webhook calls verified by EP-12-S6 can trigger this path. Matching uses the configured opt-out word list, "STOP" until decided. The keyword handler calls the consent service (EP-17-S7) and never writes `optedIn` itself. The entry and its audit entry are written in one transaction. Opt-out messages are not passed to lead intake.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor System (WhatsApp intake), time, entity (customer id), action `customer_opted_out`, before opted in, after opted out, source `whatsapp_reply`, inbound message id. Written through EP-17-S14.
- **Data changes:** Inserts into `consent_events` with `evidence_ref`; updates `customers.optedIn`. Adds the opt-out word list to configuration.
- **UI reference:** No screen. The result shows on `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes` ("not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: opt-out honoured when received (FR-39-6). Audit: written with a System actor (EP-06-S6). Concurrency: an opt-out received during a broadcast send stops the remaining sends to that customer (EP-39-S6). Open question: which reply words count as an opt-out; v1 is English only.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S1, EP-12-S6, EP-12-S7, EP-12-S10, EP-17-S7, EP-17-S14, EP-06-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S6: System can check consent at send time for wishes and broadcasts

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can check consent at send time for wishes and broadcasts
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** every outbound customer message (a wish, a broadcast message or a one-person showcase) to read the customer's current consent from the ledger just before it is handed to the WhatsApp provider, and to skip the send if consent is withdrawn
- **So that:** a customer who opted out after a broadcast was drafted, or partway through its send, gets nothing more (FR-39-5, FR-39-6, BR-39-7, BR-39-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a broadcast to VIP Bridal drafted when 86 customers were opted in, when Meera Iyer opts out before Send is pressed, then the send goes to 85 and she is counted as skipped.
  2. Given that broadcast is sending one message at a time, when Meera Iyer's "STOP" commits after the first 40 messages and before hers, then no message is sent to her and the recipient row is marked skipped with reason "opted out".
  3. Given Priya Malhotra opts out at 08:59 and has a birthday today, when the 9 am wishes run reaches her, then no wish is sent and `wishes` shows her as "not opted in to WhatsApp · will not auto-send".
  4. Given a customer who is not opted in, when a send to them is tried directly through the API, then it is refused by EP-12-S5 and nothing reaches the provider.
  5. Given a broadcast was sent, when its counts are read, then sent plus skipped equals the audience size.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The consent check reads the committed latest ledger entry inside the send step, not at draft or queue time. A send handed to the provider before an opt-out committed is not recalled. The check sits in the WhatsApp send path (EP-12-S5), so no caller can bypass it.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No for each skipped message; the skip and its reason are kept on the recipient row. Broadcasts and wishes are audited by EP-34 and EP-33.
- **Data changes:** None in schema. Recipient rows for wishes and broadcasts get status `skipped` with reason `opted_out`.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/26-wishes.svg`, route `wishes`; `docs/ux/mockups/27-broadcast.svg`, route `broadcast` ("86 customers · all opted in to WhatsApp").
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: consent checked at send time, not draft time (epic section 13). Concurrency: an opt-out that commits during a broadcast stops all remaining sends to that customer (epic section 13). Performance: the check is one indexed read per recipient.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S1, EP-39-S5, EP-12-S5, EP-33-S5, EP-33-S9, EP-34-S2, EP-34-S7, EP-34-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S7: Staff can record a customer's deletion request

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Staff can record a customer's deletion request
- **As a:** Staff
- **I want:** to record a deletion request a customer makes in person, with how it was received and when, so it waits for the owner's decision
- **So that:** no request to delete personal data is lost, and the owner sees each one with who took it (FR-39-7, BR-39-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Meera Iyer asks at the counter to have her details deleted, when Rajesh Verma records it from her customer record on `customers`, then a DeletionRequest with status `open`, received via `counter`, received at the server time and recorded by Rajesh is created and its id is returned.
  2. Given an open request for Meera Iyer, when Rajesh tries to record a second one, then the server refuses with "A deletion request is already open for this customer." and nothing is created.
  3. Given the request is recorded, when Sanjay Seth opens his notifications, then he sees a notice that a deletion request from Meera Iyer is waiting for his decision.
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when she calls Create Deletion request, then the server refuses it.
  5. Given an erased customer, when a deletion request is recorded for them, then the server refuses with `not_found`.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Staff and Owner may create a deletion request; karigars are refused (EP-05-S2). One open request per customer. Recording a request changes no customer data. Who may make a request on the customer's behalf is not decided; the server records received via and recorded by only.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in the catalogue. The owner notice goes through the notifications engine (EP-11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (deletion request id and customer id), action `deletion_request_recorded`, received via. No personal values are copied into the entry.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `deletion_requests` (id, customer id, received via, received at, recorded by, status `open` / `approved` / `refused` / `done`, decided by, decided at, reason, completed at, scope of erasure). Adds Create Deletion request to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The deletion request panel belongs on `customers` (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: deletion requests are recorded (BR-39-5). Audit: entry holds ids, not names. Time: stored in UTC, shown in Asia/Kolkata. Open question: who may make a request on the customer's behalf, and how long a request may take.
- **Depends on:** EP-17-S1, EP-17-S12, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-11-S3, EP-03-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S8: Owner can approve or refuse a deletion request

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can approve or refuse a deletion request
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to see open deletion requests and approve or refuse each one with a reason
- **So that:** every deletion is a recorded owner decision, and an approved one is carried out across all records (FR-39-8, BR-39-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an open request for Meera Iyer, when Sanjay Seth approves it with the reason "Customer asked at the counter", then its status is `approved`, decided by Sanjay, decided at the server time, and the deletion run from EP-39-S9 is started.
  2. Given an open request, when Sanjay refuses it with a reason, then its status is `refused` with the reason, and the customer's data is unchanged.
  3. Given Sanjay presses approve or refuse with no reason, when it is sent, then the server refuses with "Give a reason." and the request stays `open`.
  4. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Update Deletion request, then the server refuses it.
  5. Given a request already `approved` or `refused`, when a second decision is sent, then the server refuses it as a conflict (EP-03-S5).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only (BR-39-1). Allowed transitions: `open` to `approved`, `open` to `refused`. A reason is required for both. The decision, the request version check and the audit entry are written in one transaction (EP-03-S6, EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (deletion request id, customer id), action `deletion_request_approved` or `deletion_request_refused`, before status `open`, after status, reason.
- **Data changes:** Updates `deletion_requests` (status, decided by, decided at, reason, version). Adds List and Update Deletion request to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The deletion request panel on `customers`; open requests may also appear among owner decisions (EP-32).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: both decisions appended with reason. Concurrency: two decisions on one request at once; only one commits, the other is refused on version. Personal data: the decision entry copies no personal value. Open question: how long a deletion request may take.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S7, EP-05-S2, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-02-S14, EP-06-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
