## EP-39-S9: System can erase a customer's personal data across records and files

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can erase a customer's personal data across records and files
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an approved deletion request to run a deletion that calls the customer erase from EP-17-S13, clears the customer's name and phone from leads linked to them, deletes their PO attachments and other stored files, records the scope erased and marks the request `done`
- **So that:** the customer's personal data is gone everywhere the product keeps it, while piece history by tag and grams stays whole (FR-39-9, FR-39-10, BR-39-5, BR-39-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an approved deletion request for Meera Iyer, when the deletion runs, then name, phone, address, birthday and anniversary are gone from her customer record, from every lead linked to her and from file storage, and her piece history by tag and grams remains (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given her history rows TAG-7521 (78.4000 g) and TAG-6690 (57.4900 g), when the run finishes, then both rows remain with tag, piece name, pure gold grams as integers in units of 0.0001 g, and date.
  3. Given a PO attachment and a WhatsApp image linked to her leads, when the run finishes, then the files and their thumbnail and display copies are deleted from storage and their signed links stop working.
  4. Given the run finishes, when the request is read, then status is `done`, completed at is set and scope of erasure lists the record kinds and counts erased (for example customer 1, leads 2, files 3).
  5. Given the run fails partway, when it is retried, then it finishes from where it stopped and does not fail on parts already erased.
  6. Given the run, when the audit log is read, then the new entries name the request and the erased field kinds, and contain neither "Meera Iyer" nor "9884021107"; earlier entries are not updated or deleted.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Runs only for a request with status `approved` (EP-39-S8). Each step is idempotent per request id (EP-10-S4). The audit log stays append-only; how earlier entries that name the customer are treated follows the G22 decision (FR-39-10). The erased customer row is kept so history foreign keys stay valid (EP-17-S13).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor System, time, entity (deletion request id), action `deletion_run_done`, scope of erasure, no personal values. The customer erase writes its own `customer_erased` entry (EP-17-S14).
- **Data changes:** Updates `customers` through EP-17-S13; clears customer name and phone on linked leads; deletes linked file records and objects (EP-09); updates `deletion_requests` (status `done`, completed at, scope of erasure).
- **UI reference:** No screen. The result shows on the deletion request panel on `customers` (not yet designed).
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: deletion covers EP-09 file storage (epic section 13). Precision: piece history weights stay integer units of 0.0001 g, shown as 78.4000 g. Audit: no deleted value copied into new entries. Availability: the written procedure says how deletions are reapplied after a restore (EP-38). Open decision G22: how deletion applies to audit entries that name a customer. D10 is decided (India region) for the system's own hosting; whether outside tools must also keep personal data in India is still open.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S8, EP-17-S9, EP-17-S13, EP-17-S14, EP-09-S1, EP-09-S11, EP-09-S12, EP-28-S1, EP-29-S4, EP-29-S7, EP-10-S4, EP-38-S6
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S10: System can write token references instead of token values in audit

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can write token references instead of token values in audit
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** a check at audit write time that refuses any audit entry whose fields contain an edit-token value, a password or an activation or reset link, plus a test that walks every token and password flow and scans audit entries, logs and stored messages for them
- **So that:** no audit entry, log line or stored message ever holds a usable token, unlike the prototype's `applyEdit`, which wrote `Token ${edit.token}` into the audit detail (FR-39-16, BR-39-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given an edit applied with a token, when the audit log is read, then it shows a token reference and not the six digits (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given a service that tries to write an audit entry containing the token value it holds, when the write is made, then it is refused and the transaction rolls back.
  3. Given a password sign-in, an activation and a password reset, a token request on ED-102 and an edit applied on `edit-apply`, when audit entries, application logs, stored WhatsApp messages and stored email notifications from those flows are searched for the password, the links and the issued codes, then none is found.
  4. Given the token reference in an audit entry, when Sanjay Seth opens it on `security`, then it shows the reference, which cannot be turned back into the code.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Audit entries carry a token reference field only (EP-06-S4). Tokens and links are stored hashed and passwords as salted hashes (EP-25-S6, EP-04-S2, EP-04-S7). Log lines are redacted (EP-37-S2) and stored messages hold no codes (EP-12-S11).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** Yes, as the subject of the story: entries for edit apply and sign-in hold actor, time, entity, action and token reference, never the token value.
- **Data changes:** None in schema. Adds the audit write check and an automated scan test.
- **UI reference:** `security` route (owner audit log, EP-06-S11) shows token references.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: edit tokens, passwords and links never logged in plain text (BR-39-2). Audit: entries stay append-only; the check refuses before insert.
- **Depends on:** EP-06-S4, EP-06-S11, EP-04-S2, EP-04-S14, EP-25-S6, EP-25-S14, EP-12-S11, EP-37-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S12: Owner can run an access review and deactivate users from it

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can run an access review and deactivate users from it
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** an access review list of every active user with name, role, last sign-in and created date, a way to deactivate any of them from the list, a "Mark review done" action that records the review, and a reminder when the next review is due
- **So that:** people who left the shop, and karigars no longer working for it, lose access, and the owner role is held only by the right people (FR-39-11, FR-39-12, BR-39-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given active users Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao (Staff) and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when Sanjay opens the access review, then all four are listed with role, last sign-in in Asia/Kolkata and created date, and users who never signed in show "Never".
  2. Given Deepak Rao has left, when Sanjay deactivates him from the review, then the deactivation goes through EP-05-S7 and Deepak's open sessions end at once.
  3. Given Sanjay presses "Mark review done", when it commits, then an AccessReview record is written with done at, done by, users reviewed 4 and users deactivated 1, and the next due date is set by the review interval.
  4. Given the due date passes with no review done, when the scheduler runs, then Sanjay gets a notice that the access review is due.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls Read Access review, then the server refuses it.
  6. Given Sanjay is the last active owner, when he tries to deactivate himself from the review, then it is refused (EP-05-S9).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Read Access review and Create Access review record are owner only. Deactivation uses EP-05-S7 and its last-owner rule (EP-05-S9). Last sign-in is read from the sign-in audit (EP-04-S14). The reminder runs on the server clock (EP-10-S1).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Deactivation goes through EP-05, which emits "User deactivated or role changed" so that user's open sessions end at once (epic section 11).
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (access review id), action `access_review_done`, users reviewed, users deactivated. Each deactivation writes its own entry through EP-05-S14.
- **Data changes:** Migration creates `access_reviews` (id, due at, done at, done by, users reviewed, users deactivated). Adds a scheduled reminder job. Adds Read Access review and Create Access review record to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The access review list sits near `staff-directory` (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: deactivation ends sessions at once (BR-39-3). Audit: each review recorded. Time: due dates on the Asia/Kolkata calendar (EP-10-S10). Open question: how often the access review is run.
- **Depends on:** EP-05-S7, EP-05-S9, EP-05-S10, EP-05-S11, EP-05-S14, EP-04-S13, EP-04-S14, EP-10-S1, EP-10-S10, EP-11-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S13: Operator can rotate secrets by a written procedure

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Operator can rotate secrets by a written procedure
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a written rotation procedure for each secret (WhatsApp provider token, email provider key, LLM key, file storage keys, database credentials and the session signing key) that swaps the secret without downtime, plus a SecretRotation record of each rotation
- **So that:** a leaked key can be replaced the same day without taking the shop offline, and there is a record of when each secret was last changed (FR-39-13, BR-39-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the procedure document, when it is read, then it lists for each secret where it is stored, how the new value is set in environment configuration, how the old value is retired and who may do it.
  2. Given the WhatsApp provider token is rotated in staging following the procedure, when a wish is sent during and after the change, then both sends succeed and no request fails because of the change.
  3. Given the database credentials are rotated in staging, when Rajesh Verma saves a tag during the change, then the save succeeds.
  4. Given a rotation is done, when the operator calls Create Secret rotation record, then a record with secret name, rotated at and rotated by is stored, and no field holds the secret value.
  5. Given the repository, when it is scanned by EP-01-S10 after a rotation, then no old or new secret value is found in code.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Secrets live only in environment configuration (EP-01-S6, BR-39-4). Create Secret rotation record is for operators only. The record never stores the value. The session signing key rotation accepts the old key until existing sessions expire, so nobody is signed out mid-sale.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No in the product audit log. The SecretRotation record holds secret name, rotated at and rotated by.
- **Data changes:** Adds a SecretRotation record (secret name, rotated at, rotated by) kept in an operations table outside the business schema. Adds the rotation procedure document.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: secrets never in the repo (BR-39-4). Availability: rotation causes no downtime. Open decision D1a: the database and storage credentials come from the cloud provider, so some are rotated in that provider's console or key service; the procedure names those steps once the provider is chosen.
- **Depends on:** EP-01-S6, EP-01-S10, EP-12-S1, EP-04-S5, EP-37-S5
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-39-S15: Owner can accept or close each penetration test finding

- **Story ID:** EP-39-S15
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can accept or close each penetration test finding
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to approve the scope of an external penetration test on staging, have each finding recorded with severity and summary, and mark each one fixed or accept it in writing
- **So that:** the product launches only after an outside tester has tried to break it and every finding has an owner decision (FR-39-17)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the test scope (web app, karigar portal, API, public showcase link, WhatsApp webhook, password sign-in and email links, shop isolation), when Sanjay Seth approves it, then the approval is recorded with date and scope before testing starts.
  2. Given the report is received, when the operator enters its findings, then each PenTestFinding has id, severity, summary and status `open`.
  3. Given a finding fixed on staging, when the fix is retested, then the finding is marked `fixed` with the fix reference, and Sanjay confirms it.
  4. Given a finding the shop will not fix before launch, when Sanjay accepts it, then status is `accepted` with his name, the date and a written reason.
  5. Given any finding still `open`, when the go-live checklist is checked, then launch is blocked; done when the report is received and each finding is fixed or accepted in writing (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  6. Given a test database with a second shop's records, when the tester calls every operation as a user of the first shop, with and without a forged shop ID in the request, then no second-shop record is read or written; any hit is a finding of the highest severity (D7).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Accepting a finding is owner only. A finding needs a written reason to be accepted. The test runs against staging only, never production data.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No in the product audit log. The PenTestFinding record keeps status, decided by and decided at, and the written acceptance is kept with the report.
- **Data changes:** Adds PenTestFinding records (id, severity, summary, status `open` / `fixed` / `accepted`, decided by) kept in the operations document store or an operations table, outside the business schema.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: an external test before launch with each finding fixed or accepted. Personal data: testers use seeded data from EP-02-S13, not real customer data. Open question: who carries out the penetration test, and when.
- **Depends on:** EP-39-S2, EP-39-S3, EP-39-S10, EP-39-S11, EP-39-S14, EP-01-S12, EP-02-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-40: Automated testing · stories

Epic document: [EP-40 Automated testing](../epics/EP-40-automated-testing.md)

Role note: this is a layer E testing epic with no end user. Stories use "Developer" for the person writing and running the tests, and "System" for the CI service acting on its own. "Rules enforced on the server" here means rules enforced by the CI pipeline, the test environment configuration and the product API under test, because the epic's own operations (Create and Delete Test database, Create Test session) exist only in test environments. Fixtures follow the seed from EP-02-S13: scales Bench balance (readability 0.0001 g, capacity 600 g) and Platform scale (0.01 g, 30 kg); parcels BATCH-2026-041 to 046 as seeded; karigars KG-01 Lakshmi Devi, KG-02 Mahesh Soni and KG-04 Vijay Kumar; staff ST-01 Rajesh Verma and ST-02 Deepak Rao; owner Sanjay Seth. All fixture weights are integers in units of 0.0001 g, and all fixture customers are made up.

## EP-40-S1: Developer can run unit tests for the shared package in one command

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run unit tests for the shared package in one command
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** the test runner from EP-01-S8 set up in the shared package and the server service layer, with one command that runs every unit test in one run and exits non-zero on any failure
- **So that:** every domain rule and service function has a single, fast check that CI and developers both use (FR-40-1, BR-40-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the repository root, when a developer runs the unit test command, then every test file under the shared package (the port of `src/domain/**`) and the `api` service layer runs in one process and the summary lists passed, failed and skipped counts.
  2. Given one unit test that fails, when the command finishes, then it exits with a non-zero code and names the failing file and test.
  3. Given all unit tests pass, when the command finishes, then it exits with code 0.
  4. Given a test file marked as focused (only this test) is committed, when the command runs in CI, then the run fails, so a focused test cannot silently skip the rest.
  5. Given a CI run, when the unit step finishes, then a test run record with commit, suite `unit`, passed, failed and duration is kept with the run.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** CI runs the command on its own machines; a local pass does not count (EP-01-S8). Focused and skipped-by-default tests are refused in CI. Unit tests touch no database and no network.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Test results are kept by the CI service as the test run record (epic section 9).
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the unit test configuration to the shared package and `api`, and the test run record to CI output.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: the unit suite finishes inside the time limit the team agrees, so it runs on every push (epic section 13). Open question: which test tooling is used for the web app and the karigar web app.
- **Depends on:** EP-01-S2, EP-01-S3, EP-01-S8, EP-03-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S2: Developer can run weight and ceiling unit tests on integer units

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run weight and ceiling unit tests on integer units
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** unit tests for the shared weight helpers (gram text to integer units and back, net, sum) and for the ceiling function, all asserting integer equality
- **So that:** a change to the unit or the rounding cannot alter a stored weight or the match ceiling without a test failing (FR-40-3, BR-40-4, BR-40-5)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the text "41.5900", when it is converted to units, then the result is exactly 415900, and converting 415900 back gives "41.5900" with 4 decimals.
  2. Given gross 485.5000 g and stones 38.2000 g, when net is computed, then it equals exactly 4473000 units (447.3000 g), checked with integer equality and never with a float tolerance.
  3. Given one parcel weighing and 12 tag weighings, all on the Bench balance, when the ceiling is computed, then it equals 13 half-steps of 0.0001 g, which is 0.00065 g (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  4. Given one weighing on the Platform scale and 300 on the Bench balance, when the ceiling is computed, then it equals 0.0200 g, which is 200 units (FR-40-3, mockup 14).
  5. Given text with 5 decimals such as "1.23456", or a negative weight where the field does not allow it, when it is converted, then the helper refuses it rather than rounding.
  6. Given every weight in the seed fixture, when each is converted to units and back, then each round trip returns the original text.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The tests call the same shared functions the server uses for the gate (EP-02-S2, EP-14-S10, EP-23-S1). No float comparison helper is allowed in weight tests. Expected values are written as integers or exact gram text.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Pure unit tests with no state change.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds unit test files for the weight helpers and the ceiling function.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Expected figures come from `docs/ux/mockups/14-match-rule-any-parcel.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: integer equality only (epic section 13); the half-step case is the G10 check. Open decision G10: 0.00065 g is 6.5 units of 0.0001 g, so the expected value is written in the unit G10 settles (for example 13 half-units); the test is finalised after G10 is answered (epic section 16 risk).
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-14-S10, EP-23-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S3: Developer can run the rewritten match and gate tests (G11)

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run the rewritten match and gate tests (G11)
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** the deleted prototype match assertions rewritten as unit tests on the shared `evaluateParcel` and as service tests on the release and clear rules, using the cases recorded in `.agents/tasks/jgd-redesign/review.md`
- **So that:** the exact-match gate keeps refusing gold that does not add up, as it did in the prototype (FR-40-2, FR-40-3, FR-40-4, BR-40-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the BATCH-2026-044 fixture, when it is evaluated, then the verdict is `mismatch` with a net gap of −0.1380 g (−1380 units) and a ceiling of 0.00065 g (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given the BATCH-2026-046 fixture, when it is evaluated as seeded, then the verdict is `exact`; with a 0.0001 g or 0.0002 g bump on one tag it is `last_digit` against a 5-weighing ceiling of 0.00025 g; with a 0.0003 g bump it is `mismatch` (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given a parcel where saving a tag opens a gap above the ceiling, when the save runs, then the parcel is stopped, and a staff session can neither release it nor re-tag the item.
  4. Given a mismatched parcel, when Rajesh Verma (Staff) or Lakshmi Devi (Karigar) calls clear, send-back, re-check or accept-loss, then each is refused with its `DomainError` sentence, and the same call by Sanjay Seth succeeds.
  5. Given a parcel with an open problem, when Sanjay Seth tries to release it, then it is refused even for the owner.
  6. Given the rewritten list, when it is compared with the cases in section 6 of the epic, then each case has a named test, and the list is reviewed with the owner.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Tests run against the same shared functions and service layer the API uses; no copy of the rule lives in the test. Each `requireOwner` guard in `src/store/transitions.ts` on match and clear has a refusal test for Staff and for Karigar (FR-40-4).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in unit tests. Event publication is tested in EP-40-S9.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The tests assert that the `parcel_last_digit` entry and the clearance entries are written by the services under test (EP-23-S5, EP-23-S11), but write nothing of their own.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds unit and service test files and the BATCH-2026-044 and 046 fixtures in integer units.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Reference figures from `docs/ux/mockups/04-parcel-match.svg`, `14-match-rule-any-parcel.svg` and `22-owner-clear-mismatch.svg` ("485.5000 · 485.3620 · 138").
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: verdicts compared on integer units. Open decision G11: whether 88 or 72 prototype assertions is the authoritative list; this story covers the recorded match cases either way. Open decision Q5d: the expected outcome for the last-digit middle case; criterion 2 follows the prototype (released and logged). Open decision G10: the ceiling unit.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-40-S2, EP-23-S2, EP-23-S4, EP-23-S5, EP-23-S6, EP-23-S7, EP-23-S9, EP-23-S10, EP-23-S11, EP-21-S13, EP-24-S2
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S4: Developer can run the rewritten edit, scrap, stop and stock-out rule tests (G11)

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run the rewritten edit, scrap, stop and stock-out rule tests (G11)
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** the remaining recorded prototype assertions rewritten as unit and service tests: problems and stops, edit tokens, scrap, stock-out, owner-only onboarding and scale changes
- **So that:** every owner signature and every stop rule from the prototype is checked again by machine (FR-40-2, FR-40-4, BR-40-6, BR-40-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a stopped piece, when a stock-out is tried, then it is refused; given a stopped job, when it is advanced, then it is refused (EP-24-S2).
  2. Given an edit token, when it is generated, then it has six digits; given a wrong, an expired (older than 10 minutes) or an already used token, when apply edit is called, then each is refused and the piece is unchanged.
  3. Given TAG-8841 with an open edit proposal, when it is sold, then the proposal is voided; given a billed piece, when an edit is proposed or applied, then it is refused.
  4. Given a scrap request on TAG-7701 Temple Haram (78.4000 g), when it is created, then the piece is at `with_owner`; when Sanjay Seth marks it scrapped, then the pool moves from 812.5800 g to 890.9800 g, compared as 8125800 to 8909800 units.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) and Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when each calls clear problem, agree edit, apply edit, refuse edit, scrap, decline scrap, onboard staff, onboard karigar or change a scale, then each call is refused, and Rajesh's call to send-back, accept-loss, apply edit or scrap gives the server's refusal (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  6. Given Rajesh Verma or Lakshmi Devi, when either raises a problem on a parcel they may see, then it is accepted and the target is stopped.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Tests exercise the service layer that the API calls, so the refusals tested are the server's. Every `requireOwner` transition in `src/store/transitions.ts` has a Staff and a Karigar refusal test (FR-40-4). Token tests use the hashed store from EP-25-S6 and a fixed test clock (EP-03-S3).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None in these tests. Event publication is tested in EP-40-S9.
- **Audit entry written:** No. The tests assert that the services write their own entries; they write none.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds unit and service test files and fixtures for TAG-8841, TAG-7701 and the pool opening balance 812.5800 g.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Reference figures from `docs/ux/mockups/05-edit-propose-apply.svg` and `06-stock-out.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: pool and piece weights compared as integers. Time: token expiry tested with a fixed clock at 9 minutes 59 seconds (accepted) and 10 minutes 1 second (refused). Security: token values in test output are not printed. Open decision G11: the authoritative assertion list.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-40-S2, EP-24-S2, EP-24-S3, EP-24-S9, EP-25-S6, EP-25-S7, EP-25-S8, EP-25-S10, EP-25-S11, EP-26-S2, EP-26-S10, EP-27-S2, EP-27-S4, EP-27-S6, EP-27-S7, EP-14-S4, EP-05-S2, EP-03-S3
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S5: Developer can run API tests against a fresh seeded database

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run API tests against a fresh seeded database
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** an API test suite that creates a fresh test database, runs every migration, loads the fixture seed, signs fixture users in through a test-only session operation, calls each API operation and drops the database afterwards
- **So that:** each operation is checked for success, a validation failure, each rule refusal and the refused roles, through the real API and database (FR-40-5, BR-40-1, BR-40-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a CI run, when the API suite starts, then Create Test database makes a new database, applies all migrations from EP-02-S1 and loads the fixture seed, and Delete Test database drops it when the suite ends, pass or fail.
  2. Given the stock-out operation, when the suite runs, then it has a success test, a validation test (missing invoice number refused with the standard validation error), a rule test ("TAG-8841 is already taken." on a sold piece) and a permission test (Lakshmi Devi refused).
  3. Given each operation in the shared contract (EP-03-S1), when the suite's coverage report runs, then any operation without a success, validation, rule and permission test is listed and the run fails (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  4. Given a production configuration, when the API starts, then Create Test session is not registered and a call to it returns not found; a configuration test fails the deploy if it is enabled (epic section 16 risk).
  5. Given a rule refusal, when the response is read, then it has the code and the `DomainError` sentence in the format of EP-03-S4.
  6. Given a fixed test clock, when the suite signs in Deepak Rao with 5 wrong passwords, then the 6th try with the right password is refused, it is accepted 15 minutes 1 second later, and an owner unlock lets him in at once (EP-04-S8, EP-05-S11).
  7. Given a fixed test clock, when an activation link is used at 23 hours 59 minutes it is accepted, a second use is refused, and a fresh link opened at 24 hours 1 minute is refused; a reset link is accepted at 59 minutes and refused at 61 minutes (EP-04-S7, EP-04-S10).
  8. Given the fixture seed holds a second shop with its own user, piece TAG-8841 and customer, when every list and read operation is called by a user of the first shop, with and without a forged shop ID in the request, then no record of the second shop is returned or changed, and a schema check confirms every business table has a not-null shop ID (D7, EP-02-S3).
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create and Delete Test database are CI only and refuse any connection string that names the production database. Create Test session exists only when the environment is `test`, and is refused in staging and production. Sign-in tests use the real password, lockout and link operations, not the test session. The suite uses the real API, contract validation and transactions (EP-03-S2, EP-03-S6).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None asserted here. Live-event tests are EP-40-S9.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. Audit writes by the operations under test go to the throwaway database and are asserted for each state change.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Creates and drops a throwaway test database per run. Adds the Create Test database, Delete Test database and Create Test session operations to test configuration only.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: the test sign-in path exists only in test environments and is checked to be absent in production (epic section 13). Personal data: fixtures hold made-up customers only; no production data is copied. Performance: the API suite stays within the agreed per-push time. D1 is decided (Option C): the server-side rules live in the Node API, so the suite runs them by calling the API against the throwaway PostgreSQL database; no platform emulator is needed.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-02-S1, EP-02-S13, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S4, EP-03-S5, EP-03-S6, EP-04-S5, EP-01-S6, EP-02-S3, EP-04-S7, EP-04-S8, EP-04-S10, EP-05-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S6: Developer can run permission tests generated from the permission matrix

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run permission tests generated from the permission matrix
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a permission test suite generated from the permission list in the shared package (EP-05-S1), which calls every operation as Owner, Staff and Karigar and checks the result against the matrix, plus a test that an operation missing from the matrix is denied
- **So that:** a new operation or a changed role cannot open a gap that nobody noticed (FR-40-4, FR-40-6, BR-40-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the permission list, when the suite runs, then for every operation and each of the three roles there is one test, and it passes only if an allowed role is not refused for permission and a disallowed role gets the permission refusal.
  2. Given a test-only operation registered in the API but absent from the matrix, when Sanjay Seth (Owner) calls it, then it is denied by default (FR-40-6).
  3. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff), when he calls send-back, accept-loss, apply edit or mark scrapped, then each is refused (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  4. Given Lakshmi Devi (Karigar), when she reads a job of KG-02 Mahesh Soni, then it is refused or returns nothing, and her own KG-01 job is returned (EP-05-S3).
  5. Given a deactivated user's session, when it calls any operation, then it is refused.
  6. Given an operation added to the contract without a matrix row, when the suite runs, then it fails and names the operation.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The matrix in the shared package is the single source for both the server check (EP-05-S2) and the generated tests. Deny by default for any operation not listed. Karigar reads are scoped to their own jobs (EP-05-S3, EP-20-S1).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. Refused calls change no state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the generated permission test file, run against the throwaway database from EP-40-S5.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Reference: `docs/ux/mockups/11-roles-and-permissions.svg` ("Release a parcel whose weights disagree" and "Apply their own edit, or scrap a piece" under Staff CANNOT).
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: every permission is checked on the server (BR-40-9); the suite also covers owner-only settings (EP-39-S11). Performance: the generated tests share one database and one session per role to stay within the per-push time.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-05-S3, EP-05-S7, EP-20-S1, EP-39-S11
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S7: Developer can run concurrency tests for double-sell and double-routing

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run concurrency tests for double-sell and double-routing
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** concurrency tests against the real database engine that send two or more stock-outs of one piece, two lead-line routings of one line, and two owner clearances of one parcel at the same moment from different sessions
- **So that:** two staff can never sell the same piece or route the same line, and a parcel is cleared once (FR-40-7, FR-40-8, BR-40-3)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao each signed in, when both stock out TAG-8841 at the same moment, then exactly one succeeds and the other gets "TAG-8841 is already taken." (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given 20 parallel stock-outs of TAG-8841 from different sessions, when they finish, then 1 succeeded, 19 got the "already taken" refusal, and one stock-out record exists.
  3. Given one lead line, when two staff route it at the same moment (one to stock, one to make), then exactly one succeeds and the other gets "That line has already been routed.", and no order copy is created for the refused one.
  4. Given BATCH-2026-044 stopped on a mismatch, when two owner sessions send accept-loss at the same moment, then one commits and the other is refused as a conflict, and one audit entry exists.
  5. Given the test is run 50 times in a row in CI, when the results are read, then every run gives the same outcome, so the test is not flaky.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Tests run against the real database engine with real transactions, never a mock (epic section 13). Calls are released together from a barrier so they overlap. The locking under test is the server's (EP-26-S2, EP-22-S6, EP-30-S4, EP-30-S5, EP-02-S14).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None asserted here. "Piece billed by one staff member" delivery is asserted in EP-40-S9.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. The test asserts exactly one stock-out audit entry and one clearance entry.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the throwaway database from EP-40-S5.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Reference: `docs/ux/mockups/06-stock-out.svg`, route `stock-out`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: real engine, real transactions, repeated runs (epic section 13, section 16 risk). Precision: the pure gold leaving, 41.5900 g, is counted once in the day's total.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-22-S6, EP-26-S2, EP-26-S3, EP-30-S4, EP-30-S5, EP-23-S11, EP-02-S14
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S8: Developer can run a concurrency test for two staff tagging one parcel

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S8
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run a concurrency test for two staff tagging one parcel
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a concurrency test where two staff sessions save the same tag on a shared parcel at the same moment, and another where a tag save races a release
- **So that:** a shared parcel never gets a duplicate piece and a late tag save cannot slip past the match gate (FR-40-9, BR-40-6)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a parcel shared by Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao, when both save item 7 at the same moment, then one piece exists for item 7, and the second save is refused as a conflict or treated as the same save, never a second piece.
  2. Given both staff save different items at the same moment, when the saves finish, then both pieces exist and the tagged count goes up by 2.
  3. Given a parcel at an exact match, when a release and a tag save that opens a gap arrive at the same moment, then either the release commits first and the save is refused because the parcel is released, or the save commits first and the release is refused on the new `mismatch` verdict (EP-23-S12).
  4. Given the same test run 50 times in CI, when the results are read, then no run creates a duplicate piece.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Tagging rules and the parcel lock are the server's (EP-21-S5, EP-23-S12). Tests run on the real engine with real transactions.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None asserted here. "Tag saved on a shared parcel" is asserted in EP-40-S9.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. The test asserts one tag audit entry per created piece.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the throwaway database from EP-40-S5 with a shared parcel fixture.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Flow under test: route `parcel-tag`, `docs/ux/mockups/04-parcel-match.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Concurrency: real engine and real transactions (epic section 13). Precision: the tagged total equals the sum of saved pieces in integer units.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-40-S7, EP-21-S5, EP-21-S6, EP-23-S12, EP-03-S8
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S9: Developer can run live-event delivery and audience tests

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S9
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run live-event delivery and audience tests
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** tests that open live connections as Owner, Staff and Karigar, trigger each catalogue event's operation, and check the event arrives only after the commit and only to the allowed audience
- **So that:** every screen that relies on a live update gets it, and nobody sees an event they may not see (FR-40-10, BR-40-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the 10 catalogue events ("Piece billed by one staff member", "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit proposed / token sent", "Edit applied", "Lead arrived / passed its SLA", "Karigar job status changed", "Parcel handed over by karigar", "Tag saved on a shared parcel", "Metal pool changed", "User deactivated or role changed"), when the suite runs, then each has a test that triggers it and checks its receivers.
  2. Given an operation that fails and rolls back, when the test listens, then no event is received for it (EP-07-S1).
  3. Given Lakshmi Devi (KG-01) and Mahesh Soni (KG-02) connected, when Mahesh's job status changes, then Mahesh receives "Karigar job status changed" and Lakshmi receives nothing.
  4. Given a staff connection, when an edit token is sent to the owner, then the staff connection receives no token value and the owner's event holds none either.
  5. Given a connection that drops and reconnects with its last sequence number, when events were published in between, then it receives them in order with no gap (EP-07-S7).
  6. Given an event on staging, when the end-to-end run measures it, then it reaches the other browser within about 1 second.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Events are published only after commit (EP-07-S1) and filtered by the receiver's permissions (EP-07-S5, EP-07-S6). Proposed events in gap G26 get tests only once accepted into the catalogue.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: all 10 catalogue events, in tests only. emitted: none in production.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the throwaway database from EP-40-S5 and a test live connection client.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: live events within about 1 second (PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5), measured on staging (EP-37-S7). Security: karigar receives only events for their own jobs. Open question G26: which proposed events get tests.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-07-S1, EP-07-S2, EP-07-S5, EP-07-S6, EP-07-S7, EP-07-S11, EP-07-S12, EP-37-S7
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S10: Developer can run a test that no currency shows while pricing is off

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S10
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run a test that no currency shows while pricing is off
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a rendering test that opens every route with each fixture identity and sample parameters, with the pricing flag off, and fails if any rendered screen contains a currency sign or rupee figure
- **So that:** no rupee figure reaches a screen before pricing exists, as the prototype checked across 2,430 combinations (FR-40-12, BR-40-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the pricing flag off, when every route is rendered for Owner, Staff and Karigar with the sample parameters, then no rendered text contains "₹", "Rs", "INR" or a figure formatted as rupees, and the test lists the combinations checked.
  2. Given a developer adds a raw rupee figure outside `ValueSlot` on route `stock-out`, when the test runs, then it fails and names the route and the identity.
  3. Given `docs/ux/mockups/06-stock-out.svg` shows "total value fills here later", when `stock-out` renders with pricing off, then the value slot is empty or shows that placeholder text.
  4. Given a new route is added, when the test runs, then it is included without editing the test, because routes are read from the route list.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The pricing flag is owner-only on the server (EP-13-S9). The rendering test uses the flag as the server returns it, not a client toggle.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Rendering tests change no state.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the rendering test and the sample-parameter list per route.
- **UI reference:** All routes. Reference: `docs/ux/mockups/06-stock-out.svg`, route `stock-out` ("No prices here").
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: run on deploy if too slow for every push. Pricing on is not tested here; price logic tests wait for EP-42 (epic section 5). Open question: which test tooling is used for the web app and the karigar web app.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-08-S13, EP-08-S19, EP-13-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S11: Developer can run a test that passwords, links and edit tokens never reach logs or audit

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S11
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run a test that passwords, links and edit tokens never reach logs or audit
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** a security test that runs an activation, a password sign-in with one wrong password first, a password reset, an edit token request and an edit apply, captures the passwords used, the links from the account-email stub and the issued codes, and searches audit entries, application logs, error reports and stored messages for them
- **So that:** no log line or audit entry ever holds a usable password, link or code (FR-40-13, BR-40-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given Rajesh Verma activates his account, signs in with one wrong password first and then the right one, and later resets his password, when the audit log and captured log lines are searched for both passwords and both links, then none is found.
  2. Given Sanjay Seth agrees to proposal ED-102 and applies it with the token, when the audit entries for the flow are read, then they hold a token reference and not the six digits.
  3. Given an apply edit call that fails validation with the token in the request body, when the error report and log line are read, then the token is redacted (EP-37-S2).
  4. Given the stored WhatsApp message for the token, when it is read from the message store, then it holds no code (EP-12-S11).
  5. Given a developer adds a log line that prints a password, a link or the edit token, when the test runs, then it fails and names the flow.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Passwords are stored as salted hashes, links and tokens hashed (EP-04-S2, EP-04-S7, EP-25-S6). Audit entries carry a token reference only (EP-06-S4). Log redaction is on in every environment (EP-37-S2). The test reads links only from the account-email stub (EP-04-S4) and codes only from the test WhatsApp stub.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None asserted here.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. The test asserts that the flow's entries hold actor, time, entity, action and token reference only.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Uses the throwaway database from EP-40-S5 and captures log output for the run.
- **UI reference:** No screen. Flow under test: route `edit-apply`, `docs/ux/mockups/05-edit-propose-apply.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: passwords, links and edit tokens never logged in plain text (BR-40-7, PRODUCTION-SCOPE §5). Cross-reference: EP-39-S10 adds the audit write check; this story is the full-flow test across logs, errors and messages. D4 is decided: phone and password sign-in with email links; there is no sign-in OTP to test.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-04-S2, EP-04-S4, EP-04-S7, EP-04-S10, EP-04-S14, EP-06-S4, EP-25-S6, EP-25-S14, EP-37-S2, EP-37-S3, EP-12-S11, EP-39-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-40-S12: Developer can run end-to-end tests of the main flows on staging

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S12
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Developer can run end-to-end tests of the main flows on staging
- **As a:** Developer
- **I want:** end-to-end tests that drive the web app and the karigar portal in real browsers on staging through each main flow in FR-40-11
- **So that:** the whole chain from lead to stock-out works together after every deploy, not only each part alone (FR-40-11, BR-40-1)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given staging, when the suite runs, then it covers: activate an account from the emailed link and sign in with phone and password; issue gold and create a job on `order-copy`; karigar accepts and hands over on `k-jobs`; parcel arrives on `parcel-arrival`, is tagged by two staff on `parcel-tag`, passes `parcel-qc` and matches exactly on `parcel-match`; a mismatched parcel is cleared by the owner on `parcel-clear`; stop the line and clear on `decisions`; edit with token on `edit-propose` and `edit-apply`; stock-out on `stock-out`; scrap to pool on `scrap-decision`; lead to conversion on `lead-create` and `lead-convert` (epic acceptance criterion 6).
  2. Given the tagging flow, when Rajesh Verma saves a tag in one browser, then Deepak Rao's open `parcel-tag` in a second browser shows it within about 1 second.
  3. Given the scrap flow on TAG-7701 (78.4000 g), when Sanjay Seth marks it scrapped, then the pool shown goes up by 78.4000 g.
  4. Given each key screen (`today`, `decisions`, `stock`, `parcels`, `leads`), when it is opened, then it loads in under 2 seconds.
  5. Given a flow fails, when the run ends, then the result names the flow and step and keeps a screenshot, and staging data is reset for the next run.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** End-to-end tests use real sign-in on staging with phone and password, and read the activation link from the account-email stub mailbox (EP-04-S4); the test session path is not used on staging. Staging data is a fixture seed with made-up customers, never production data.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** consumed: "Tag saved on a shared parcel", "Karigar job status changed", "Parcel handed over by karigar", "Parcel stopped (mismatch or raised problem)", "Edit applied", "Piece billed by one staff member" and "Metal pool changed", observed in the browsers under test.
- **Audit entry written:** No by the suite. Flows write their normal entries in staging.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Resets the staging database to the fixture seed before each run (EP-02-S13).
- **UI reference:** Routes `today`, `decisions`, `leads`, `lead-create`, `lead-convert`, `order-copy`, `k-jobs`, `parcels`, `parcel-arrival`, `parcel-tag`, `parcel-qc`, `parcel-match`, `parcel-clear`, `stock`, `edit-propose`, `edit-apply`, `stock-out`, `scrap-decision`. Acceptance references: `04-parcel-match.svg`, `05-edit-propose-apply.svg`, `06-stock-out.svg`, `22-owner-clear-mismatch.svg`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: screen load under 2 seconds and live events within about 1 second (epic section 13). Personal data: made-up customers only. Availability: tests limited to the main flows to stay stable (epic section 16 risk). Open question: which flows are required before launch and which can follow. Open question: which tooling drives the web app and the karigar web app. D4 is decided: the first flow uses phone and password after activation.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S5, EP-01-S12, EP-02-S13, EP-04-S4, EP-04-S5, EP-08-S9, EP-19-S2, EP-20-S4, EP-20-S6, EP-21-S2, EP-21-S6, EP-21-S8, EP-23-S4, EP-23-S11, EP-24-S3, EP-24-S9, EP-25-S2, EP-25-S7, EP-26-S7, EP-27-S6, EP-28-S2, EP-30-S6, EP-37-S8

## EP-40-S13: System can block a merge or deploy when any test fails

- **Story ID:** EP-40-S13
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can block a merge or deploy when any test fails
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** CI to run the unit, API, permission, concurrency, live-event, rendering and security suites on every push, the end-to-end suite before every staging promotion to production, and to block the merge or deploy on any failure
- **So that:** a change that breaks a gold rule cannot reach main or the shop (FR-40-14, BR-40-2)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a pull request with one failing unit or API test, when CI runs, then the run is red and the merge into main is blocked, naming the failing suite (epic acceptance criterion 5).
  2. Given every per-push suite passes, when the run ends, then the merge is allowed by the branch protection of EP-01-S11.
  3. Given a green main build deployed to staging, when the end-to-end suite fails, then promotion to production is blocked and production keeps its current build.
  4. Given a deploy configuration with Create Test session enabled for staging or production, when the deploy runs, then the configuration test fails it.
  5. Given a CI run, when its result is read, then each suite's test run record (commit, suite, passed, failed, duration) is shown.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** The git host and CI enforce the block; it cannot be skipped by the developer (EP-01-S11). Each suite is a required status check by name. A skipped required suite counts as failed.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None
- **Audit entry written:** No. Merge and deploy history is kept by the git host and CI service.
- **Data changes:** None in the product database. Adds the suites as required checks in the CI pipeline and branch protection.
- **UI reference:** No screen
- **Non-functional checks:** Performance: per-push suites within the agreed CI time; end-to-end on deploy only (epic section 16 risk). Security: the test sign-in path is checked absent from production configuration. Open question G24: whether "EP-03 onwards" includes EP-41 to EP-43; the required suites cover EP-03 to EP-39 until it is answered.
- **Depends on:** EP-40-S1, EP-40-S5, EP-40-S6, EP-40-S7, EP-40-S8, EP-40-S9, EP-40-S10, EP-40-S11, EP-40-S12, EP-01-S8, EP-01-S11, EP-01-S12, EP-01-S13
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

# EP-41: Launch and data migration · stories

Epic document: [EP-41 Launch and data migration](../epics/EP-41-launch-and-data-migration.md)

Role note: this is a layer E launch epic. Most stories are the Owner's, because the Owner provides the real lists, approves each import and signs go-live. Stories use "System" for the import runner and the figure calculations acting on their own, and "Developer" for the operator who rehearses imports on staging and runs the technical checklist items (the "Operator" in the epic's API table). No import, comparison or checklist page is designed yet, so screen labels in criteria are proposed. Real names, phones and weights are not known yet; criteria use the seed names Sanjay Seth (Owner), Rajesh Verma and Deepak Rao (Staff), and Lakshmi Devi, Mahesh Soni and Vijay Kumar (Karigar) as stand-ins. All weights are integers in units of 0.0001 g and shown to 4 decimals. No price, budget or invoice amount is imported (EP-42).

## EP-41-S1: System can record import runs with loaded and refused rows

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S1
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** System can record import runs with loaded and refused rows
- **As a:** System
- **I want:** an `import_runs` table and an `import_row_errors` table, and a shared import runner that reads an uploaded list for one kind, checks every row with that kind's own create rules, loads the good rows, and records each refused row with its row number, field and reason
- **So that:** every launch import leaves a record of who ran it, on which file, how many rows loaded and how many were refused and why (FR-41-9, BR-41-8)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the migration has run, when `import_runs` is inspected, then it has `id`, `kind` (one of `karigars`, `customers`, `stock`, `scales`, `users`, `opening_pool`, `karigar_holdings`), `file_id`, `run_by`, `environment`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `rows_loaded`, `rows_refused` and `status` (`validating`, `loaded`, `failed`), and `import_row_errors` has `import_run_id`, `row_number`, `field` and `reason`.
  2. Given Sanjay Seth uploads a 20-row karigar list in which row 7 has an allowance of 1.5%, when the run finishes, then it has status `loaded`, `rows_loaded` 19, `rows_refused` 1, and one row error with row number 7, field `wastage allowance` and reason "The wastage allowance is between 0.6% and 1.2%." (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  3. Given a run is in progress, when one good row fails at the database (for example a unique index clash), then that row is recorded as refused with the mapped sentence and the other rows still load, each row in its own transaction.
  4. Given a finished run, when Sanjay reads it with Read Import run, then he gets the counts, the file name, his name, the server start and end times in Asia/Kolkata, and the list of refused rows with reasons.
  5. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) or Lakshmi Devi (Karigar) calls Create Import run or Read Import run, when the server checks the permission, then it is refused and no run is written.
  6. Given a loaded row, when its audit entry is read, then the reason names the import run id.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Create and Read Import run are owner only (EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2). Each row goes through the same service function the kind's create screen uses; the importer never writes a table directly. One transaction per row with its audit entry (EP-03-S6, EP-06-S2). `run_by` comes from the session and times from the server clock (EP-03-S3). The uploaded file is stored with restricted access and deleted when the run finishes (EP-09-S1, EP-09-S6). A run is deduplicated by idempotency key so a resubmitted upload does not load twice (EP-03-S8).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Imports run before go-live, when no screens are in use; events from the services a row passes through are emitted by those services.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: one entry per loaded row from the kind's service, with actor, time, entity, action, after, and reason "import run <id>"; plus one entry for the run with actor, time, entity (import run), action (`import_run_finished`), after (counts and status).
- **Data changes:** New tables `import_runs` and `import_row_errors` with a migration. Adds Create Import run and Read Import run to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. An owner import page is needed (epic section 12).
- **Non-functional checks:** Audit: every imported row is audited with the import run as the reason (epic section 13). Security: owner only; import files kept with restricted access and removed after use. Personal data: the file is deleted after the run, and row errors hold the field name and reason, not the full row. Time: times shown in Asia/Kolkata (EP-10-S10). Open question: which file format the lists come in (not settled in the epic).
- **Depends on:** EP-02-S1, EP-03-S1, EP-03-S2, EP-03-S3, EP-03-S6, EP-03-S8, EP-05-S1, EP-05-S2, EP-06-S2, EP-09-S1, EP-09-S3, EP-09-S6, EP-10-S10
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-41-S2: Owner can import karigars from a list

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S2
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can import karigars from a list
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to upload the shop's karigar list with name, phone, email, workshop location, specialties, language and wastage allowance, and have each row created through the same rules as Add a karigar
- **So that:** every karigar I issue gold to exists in the app before the first real job, with the allowance their work is judged against (FR-41-1, BR-41-1, BR-41-7, BR-41-10)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a list with Lakshmi Devi (Temple, Tamil, 0.7%), Mahesh Soni (Hindi, 0.8%) and a third row at 1.5%, when Sanjay Seth imports it, then two karigars are created with the next `KG-NN` codes and `wastage_bp` 70 and 80, and the report names row 3 with "The wastage allowance is between 0.6% and 1.2%." (epic acceptance criterion 1).
  2. Given a row with an empty name, when it is imported, then it is refused with "Add the karigar name."; given a row with no specialty, then it is refused with "Pick at least one thing they are best at."
  3. Given a row whose specialty is not an active entry in the specialties list, when it is imported, then it is refused with the reference-list sentence and the other rows load (EP-15-S4).
  4. Given a row with language "Tamil", when it loads, then the language is stored on the karigar and changes nothing on screen, because the app is English only in v1.
  5. Given a row whose phone is already used by another karigar, or a row with no email (every karigar has one, D4), when it is imported, then it is refused with the same sentence the add screen shows, and no second karigar is created.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Each row goes through the Create Karigar service from EP-16-S3, so the owner-only check, the 0.6% to 1.2% allowance check in whole basis points, the name and specialty checks and code assignment all apply unchanged. Specialties must be active list entries (EP-15-S4). The importer adds no rule of its own beyond mapping columns.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: per karigar created, from EP-16-S13: actor (Sanjay), time, entity (karigar), action (`karigar_created`), after (code, name, specialties, allowance), reason (import run id).
- **Data changes:** Inserts rows into `karigars` through the existing service; one `import_runs` row of kind `karigars` with its row errors. No migration.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (owner import page). Fields follow `docs/ux/mockups/24-onboard-karigar.svg`, route `karigar-new`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Security: owner only. Personal data: karigar phones are personal data; the file is deleted after the run. Open question: in which spoken language each karigar is trained (affects training, not the stored field).
- **Depends on:** EP-41-S1, EP-16-S1, EP-16-S2, EP-16-S3, EP-16-S13, EP-15-S4
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-41-S3: Owner can import customers with their consent status

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S3
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can import customers with their consent status
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to upload the customer list with name, phone, birthday, anniversary and group, and for each row either a record of WhatsApp consent with the date it was given, or nothing
- **So that:** staff find real customers at the counter on day one, and the shop only messages customers whose consent it can show (FR-41-2, BR-41-5)

  3. Given a row whose phone matches an existing customer after normalising, when it is imported, then it is refused with the duplicate-phone reason and no second customer is created (EP-17-S4).
  4. Given a row with a budget or past spend column, when it is imported, then those values are ignored, the value sockets stay null, and the report says the column was skipped.

- **Audit entry written:** Yes: per customer, from EP-17-S14: actor, time, entity (customer), action (`customer_created`), after (fields without the full phone in clear text where EP-17-S14 masks it), reason (import run id); and per consent event: action (`consent_recorded`), after (kind, source `import`, original date).
- **Data changes:** Inserts rows into `customers` and `consent_events` through existing services; one `import_runs` row of kind `customers`. A nullable `given_at` (original consent date) on `consent_events` if EP-17-S2 does not already hold it; migration only if missing.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (owner import page). Fields follow `docs/ux/mockups/23-onboard-customer.svg`, route `customer-new`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Personal data: the customer list is personal data; the file is deleted after the run, and refused rows are reported by row number and field, not by copying names into the report. Audit: consent events keep their source and original date. Open question: which customer records have proof of WhatsApp consent. Open question G13: whether past purchase history is imported and from where; this story imports no history.
- **Depends on:** EP-41-S1, EP-17-S1, EP-17-S2, EP-17-S3, EP-17-S4, EP-17-S11, EP-17-S14, EP-39-S1, EP-39-S6

## EP-41-S4: Owner can import existing stock as in-stock pieces with integer weights

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S4
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can import existing stock as in-stock pieces with integer weights
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to upload the showroom stock list with tag number, HUID, name, kind, purity, gross weight and stone weight, and have each row created as a piece with source "import"
- **So that:** the stock list, the stock-out flow and gold on the floor match the showroom from the first day (FR-41-3, FR-41-4, BR-41-2, BR-41-9)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given a row with tag TAG-8841, gross "48.6500" and stones "7.0600", when it is imported, then a piece is stored with gross `486500`, stone `70600`, source `import`, `imported_at` set and the value socket null, and it reads 41.5900 g pure gold.
  2. Given the register's stock totals 1,847.0000 g pure gold, when the stock import finishes, then gold on the floor shows 1,847.0000 g to four decimals, and the sum of imported net units equals 18,470,000 exactly (epic acceptance criterion 2).
  3. Given a row whose tag number is already used on another piece, when it is imported, then it is refused with "TAG-8841 is already used on another piece." and the other rows load (FR-41-4).
  4. Given a row with stones heavier than gross, when it is imported, then it is refused with "Stones cannot weigh more than the piece."; given a weight with 5 decimals such as "12.34567", then it is refused as a validation error and never rounded.
  5. Given a row with a HUID of the wrong format, when it is imported, then it is refused with the HUID format sentence from EP-15-S8.
  6. Given a loaded piece, when Rajesh Verma opens `stock`, then it appears in the in-stock list and can be stocked out like any other piece.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Weights are parsed from text into integer units with the shared helper (EP-02-S2), with no float step. Gross greater than 0, stones from 0 up to gross. Tag number unique across all pieces (EP-15-S7) and HUID checked (EP-15-S8). Purity and kind must be active list entries (EP-15-S4). The entry state follows the open decision: by default the piece enters `in_stock` through a dedicated import transition recorded in `piece_state_transitions` with from empty and reason "import"; if the owner decides imported stock passes an owner check first, it enters `with_owner` instead. No price or value column is read. Owner only.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None. Imports run before go-live.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: per piece, from EP-22-S11: actor (Sanjay), time, entity (piece), action (`piece_imported`), after (tag, HUID, gross and stone in integer units, state), reason (import run id).
- **Data changes:** Adds `source` (`tagged` or `import`, default `tagged`) and nullable `imported_at` to `pieces` with a migration; allows the import transition in the state table. Inserts pieces and `piece_state_transitions` rows; one `import_runs` row of kind `stock`.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (owner import page). Imported pieces show on `stock` and in "Gold on the floor" on `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg`, route `decisions`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: totals after import equal the source totals exactly (epic section 13). Performance: a list of 5,000 pieces imports without timing out, run as a background job (EP-10-S1) if needed. Open question: whether existing stock enters as in-stock directly or passes the match gate or an owner check first. Open question: whether existing stock is re-weighed at import or register weights are trusted; register weights with fewer decimals are imported as recorded (for example "12.35" stored as `123500`).
- **Depends on:** EP-41-S1, EP-02-S2, EP-22-S1, EP-22-S2, EP-22-S11, EP-15-S4, EP-15-S7, EP-15-S8, EP-22-S10, EP-10-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-41-S5: Owner can register the real scales with true readabilities

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S5
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can register the real scales with true readabilities
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to register each real scale in the shop with its name, true readability and capacity from its documentation, and retire the seed scales that do not exist, before the first real parcel is weighed
- **So that:** the match ceiling for every real parcel is computed from the scale that actually weighed it (FR-41-5, BR-41-3, BR-41-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the real bench balance reads to 0.001 g up to 220 g, when Sanjay Seth registers it, then the scale is stored with readability `10` and capacity `2200000`, and the ceiling for a parcel with one parcel weighing and 12 tag weighings on it is 13 half-steps of 0.001 g, which is 0.0065 g (epic acceptance criterion 3).
  2. Given the seed "Bench balance" (0.0001 g, 600 g) does not exist in the shop, when Sanjay retires it, then it no longer appears in the picker on `parcel-arrival`.
  3. Given a production go-live checklist, when the scale item is checked, then every active scale has a readability taken from its documentation, recorded in the scale's note, and none still carries a seed value unchecked.
  4. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) tries to register or edit a scale, when the server checks the permission, then it is refused (EP-14-S4).
  5. Given a scale list file with the scales, when it is imported as kind `scales`, then each row goes through the Create Scale rules, and a readability with more than 4 decimals is refused as a validation error.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Scales are created through the Create Scale service from EP-14-S3 and retired through EP-14-S7, owner only. Readability and capacity are integers in units of 0.0001 g. The ceiling is computed on the server from the registry (EP-14-S10).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: per scale, from EP-14-S12: actor, time, entity (scale), action (`scale_created` or `scale_retired`), before, after (readability and capacity in units), reason (import run id or the owner's note).
- **Data changes:** Inserts and retires rows in `scales` through existing services; one `import_runs` row of kind `scales` if a file is used. No migration.
- **UI reference:** `docs/ux/mockups/14-match-rule-any-parcel.svg`, route `scales`.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: readability stored as integer units; a 0.001 g step is `10`. Open question: the real readabilities and capacities of the shop's scales (App. E). Open question G10 (from EP-40): the ceiling's half-step unit when readability is 0.0001 g.
- **Depends on:** EP-41-S1, EP-14-S1, EP-14-S3, EP-14-S4, EP-14-S7, EP-14-S10, EP-14-S12
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-41-S6: Owner can record the opening pool balance

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S6
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can record the opening pool balance
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to record the pool's opening balance at launch, once, using the Create Opening entry from EP-18-S2 with the agreed figure and a reason that names the launch
- **So that:** the ledger starts from the gold the shop actually holds at go-live, and the parallel run compares like for like (FR-41-6, BR-41-4)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given production has no pool entries, when Sanjay Seth records 812.5800 g with the reason "Opening balance at launch, from register page 214", then the ledger shows one `opening` entry with delta `8125800`, Sanjay as actor, the server time and the reason (epic acceptance criterion 4).
  2. Given an opening entry exists, when a second one is tried, then it is refused with code `opening_exists` and nothing changes.
  3. Given the shop's books have no pool figure, when the owner decides the pool starts at zero, then no opening entry is posted and the checklist item records that decision instead.
  4. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) tries to record the opening balance, when the server checks, then it is refused.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** All rules from EP-18-S2: owner only, allowed only while the pool has no entries, amount greater than 0 with at most 4 decimals, deduplicated by idempotency key, entry and audit in one transaction.
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** emitted: "Metal pool changed" (through EP-18-S12), if any screen is open.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: actor, time, entity (metal pool), action (`pool_opening_recorded`), before (balance 0), after (balance and delta in integer units), reason.
- **Data changes:** One row in `pool_entries` and the balance on `metal_pools`, through EP-18-S2. No migration.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed. The pool ledger page is undrawn; the action is the one built in EP-18-S2.
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: the typed figure is parsed with the EP-02-S2 helper. Audit: the entry holds the integer delta. Open question (App. B sub-question 1): whether the pool already exists in the shop's books and what its opening balance is.
- **Depends on:** EP-18-S2, EP-18-S12, EP-41-S1
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed

## EP-41-S7: Owner can record the gold each karigar holds at launch

- **Story ID:** EP-41-S7
- **Status:** Not started
- **Title:** Owner can record the gold each karigar holds at launch
- **As a:** Owner
- **I want:** to record, for each karigar, the grams of gold they hold at launch, either as an open job carried over from the register or as an opening holding with no job, through Create Karigar holding
- **So that:** "Gold with karigars" on Decisions and "Gold with me" on the karigar's phone match the paper register on day one (FR-41-7)
- **Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then):**
  1. Given the register shows Vijay Kumar holding 152.4000 g on one temple necklace job and 34.0000 g with no job, when Sanjay Seth records both, then one open job with 152.4000 g issued and one opening holding of 34.0000 g exist for KG-04, and gold with Vijay reads 186.4000 g.
  2. Given the holdings are recorded, when Vijay signs in on `k-jobs`, then "Gold with me" shows 186.4000 g, and the open job appears in his job list.
  3. Given holdings are recorded for all karigars, when Sanjay reads the custody summary, then "with karigars" equals the register's total exactly, compared in integer units.
  4. Given a holding is recorded, when the pool balance is read, then it is unchanged, because this gold already left the pool before launch.
  5. Given a holding of 0 g, a negative amount, or a karigar that does not exist or is inactive, when it is recorded, then it is refused with a validation error and nothing is stored.
  6. Given Rajesh Verma (Staff) calls Create Karigar holding, when the server checks, then it is refused.
- **Rules enforced on the server:** Owner only. Grams greater than 0 with at most 4 decimals, stored as integer units. Karigar must be active (EP-16-S7). A carried-over job is created in an open state through the EP-19 job service with a flag that posts no `issued` pool entry; an opening holding with no job is stored as a holding row. Both count in gold with karigar (EP-18-S11). Allowed only before go-live is signed (EP-41-S13).
- **Live events emitted / consumed:** None of its own. Imports run before go-live.
- **Audit entry written:** Yes: per holding: actor, time, entity (karigar holding or job), action (`karigar_holding_recorded`), after (karigar code, grams in integer units, linked job id), reason (import run id or the owner's note).
- **Data changes:** New table `karigar_holdings` (karigar id, grams held as integer, linked job id nullable, recorded by, recorded at) with a migration; a `carried_over` flag on jobs so no pool entry is posted. The custody read from EP-18-S11 adds opening holdings to gold with karigar. Adds Create Karigar holding to the shared contract.
- **UI reference:** Not yet designed (owner import page). Totals show on `docs/ux/mockups/08-owner-home.svg`, route `decisions` ("Gold with karigars"), and `docs/ux/mockups/09-karigar-phone.svg`, route `k-jobs` ("GOLD WITH ME").
- **Non-functional checks:** Precision: holdings summed in integer units. Open question: the epic allows "open jobs or opening ledger entries"; this story records them without moving the pool balance, and how an opening holding is later closed (returned gold or settled job) follows EP-18-S7.
- **Depends on:** EP-41-S1, EP-16-S7, EP-18-S7, EP-18-S11, EP-19-S1, EP-19-S2, EP-20-S9
- **Definition of done:** code reviewed · tests pass · deployed to staging · acceptance criteria demoed
